headline: Not 24x7 entertainment channel: SC bars sharing of hearing videos without prior nod
full_text:
Not 24x7 entertainment channel: SC bars sharing of hearing videos without prior nod
Taking note of the misuse of audio and video recordings of court proceedings, the Supreme Court barred their unauthorised posting, editing, sharing and uploading on social media and digital platforms without prior court approval.
Observing that courts can't be a 24x7 entertainment channel, the Supreme Court on Friday passed an interim order prohibiting the extraction, editing, dissemination, reposting, uploading or monetisation of audio and video recordings of judicial proceedings on social media and other digital platforms without prior permission from the concerned court.
A Bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi and Justice V Mohan passed the interim direction while hearing a public interest litigation filed by journalist Harshita Grover seeking guidelines to regulate the clipping, editing, dissemination and monetisation of audiovisual recordings of court proceedings.
"There shall be no extraction, modification, dissemination, posting, re-posting, uploading or monetisation of audio/video recordings of the judicial proceedings on social media or other digital platforms without the prior permission of the Registrar General of the concerned High Courts or the Secretary General of the Supreme Court," the Bench said.
According to a report in Live Law, the court, however, clarified that the interim order would not affect fair news reporting of judicial proceedings.
The Bench issued notice on the petition and impleaded all High Courts in the matter. It also directed the Union government to place before the court a proposal identifying the nodal ministries that could implement the reliefs sought in the plea.
The High Courts have also been asked to submit reports on the adoption of the Supreme Court's model livestreaming guidelines and explain the impact of continuous livestreaming of proceedings.
Notices were also issued to social media intermediaries, including Meta and X.
During the hearing, senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, clarified that the plea was not against livestreaming of court proceedings but against the misuse of selectively edited clips circulating online.
"I personally don't see any problem with livestream," Singh submitted, adding that snippets of hearings were often taken out of context and went viral. Referring to a recent incident, he said a clip from proceedings before Justice Viswanathan had become viral, making "the judiciary a joke before the lay people".
Singh relied on the Supreme Court's Model Rules for Live-Streaming and Recording of Court Proceedings, which prohibit any unauthorised recording, sharing, reproduction, modification or republication of livestreamed proceedings without prior written approval of the court, and sought an interim order enforcing those provisions.
Justice Joymalya Bagchi observed that regulating digital data had emerged as "one of the biggest challenges" and suggested that livestreaming should become "an exception rather than a norm."
"Regulating data is one of the biggest challenges in digital space... so we should ensure limited access and therefore restrict livestream itself. Parties must expressly make a prayer that they want to see. It can't be a 24/7 entertainment channel by court," Justice Bagchi remarked, while expressing concern over virtual hearing links being shared indiscriminately.
"It can't be a 24x7 entertainment channel by the court," the bench observed, adding that there was a need to ensure limited access.
Solicitor General Tushar Mehta supported the plea for interim protection and cautioned against the misuse of artificial intelligence to manipulate courtroom videos.
"Suppose your lordships are saying something to me and I am responding. There are AI tools. With the same lip movement, my and your lordships' words can be changed in our respective voices," Mehta submitted.
He also argued that selectively edited clips were often used to create misleading narratives about court proceedings.
The Chief Justice agreed that distorted reporting posed a growing challenge, saying he had personally experienced his remarks being misrepresented.
"In the print forum, I have already experienced. What I never said was thrust upon me by these people," CJI Kant observed, referring to media reports on an earlier plea concerning student protests.
The petition contends that while livestreaming was introduced to promote transparency and the principle of open justice, the absence of a regulatory framework has enabled courtroom recordings to be clipped, edited and circulated with misleading captions, sensational commentary and clickbait content, often for commercial gain.
Filed under Article 32 of the Constitution, the plea argues that isolated courtroom exchanges and oral observations are routinely taken out of context, exposing judges, lawyers and litigants to trolling, reputational harm and distorted public narratives.
It seeks guidelines governing the recording, clipping, redistribution and monetisation of audiovisual recordings while preserving the principles of open justice and fair reporting.
The petition also cites multiple instances of alleged misuse of judicial recordings, including controversies involving judges' remarks, and misleading social media content featuring courtroom exchanges.
The plea also highlights international practices such as the United Kingdom Supreme Court's copyright framework governing audiovisual recordings.

headline: Fresh bid to end Cauvery deadlock as CMs plan talk
full_text:
Fresh bid to end Cauvery deadlock as CMs plan talk
A proposed meeting between Karnataka Chief Minister, his Tamil Nadu counterpart has opened a fresh political channel to address the long-running Cauvery dispute
A proposed meeting between Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar and his Tamil Nadu counterpart C Joseph Vijay has opened a fresh political channel to address the long-running Cauvery dispute, with both governments indicating a willingness to discuss water sharing and Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir amid worsening drought conditions across the basin.
Tamil Nadu minister for agriculture and farmers’ welfare R Vinoth said on Friday that Vijay would travel to Karnataka in the first week of August to raise the Mekedatu issue, reiterating the state’s opposition to the project.
“The chief minister is set to visit Karnataka next month. Right from the beginning, we have been saying that the Government of Tamil Nadu will not permit Karnataka to construct the dam. The chief minister is going regarding this matter in the first week of August,” Vinoth said.
He said Vijay would also seek Tamil Nadu’s share of Cauvery water after Karnataka informed the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) that it could not release additional water for June and July because of deficient rainfall.
“The chief minister will demand Tamil Nadu’s share of water for the sake of establishing our rights,” Vinoth said.
Responding to reports of the proposed meeting, Shivakumar said Karnataka was willing to resolve inter-state issues through dialogue and was prepared to engage with Tamil Nadu.
Speaking after attending the CEOs’ Breakfast Meeting ahead of the Bengaluru Tech Summit, he declined to disclose details of a letter sent by the Tamil Nadu chief minister, saying the state government had been occupied with Cabinet expansion and other official work.
“I don’t want to disclose now. I’m very busy next week with my Cabinet expansion and all those things. We are ready to speak with everyone, share things with everyone and work with everyone,” Shivakumar said.
According to officials familiar with the matter, Tamil Nadu sought the meeting and Shivakumar subsequently invited Vijay for talks in Bengaluru, with August 3 being considered as a tentative date. There is no confirmation yet on whether Vijay has accepted the invitation.
The discussions are expected to focus on Cauvery water releases and Karnataka’s proposal to build the Mekedatu balancing reservoir in Shivakumar’s Kanakapura Assembly constituency. Tamil Nadu has opposed the project for nearly 15 years, arguing that it would adversely affect farmers, particularly in the Cauvery delta.
Earlier this week, Vijay chaired a consultation with legal experts who have represented the Tamil Nadu government in the Mekedatu litigation over the past 15 years. State minister for natural resources and law R Nirmal Kumar said the government would decide its next course of action after examining the recommendations made during the meeting.
Political parties in Tamil Nadu have also sharpened their stand ahead of the proposed talks.
BJP spokesperson Narayanan Thirupathy said, “Vijay during the meeting should very categorically and clearly state that the Mekedatu dam cannot be built without Tamil Nadu’s consent. I think since Congress is also in the government in Tamil Nadu, he has to say it very, very clearly that they cannot play games.”
On July 23, AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K Palaniswami urged the Tamil Nadu government to press Karnataka to release the state’s allocated share of Cauvery water for June and July. He said Karnataka had released 2.91 tmcft against the 9.19 tmcft mandated under the Supreme Court’s verdict.
The Tamil Nadu Assembly unanimously adopted a resolution on July 19 opposing Karnataka’s plan to construct the Mekedatu reservoir. Vijay led the resolution, with opposition parties, including the AIADMK and Leader of Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, extending support. The Tamil Nadu Congress also backed the government’s stand despite the Congress being in power in Karnataka.
The proposed meeting comes days after Karnataka told the CWMA that it could not release additional Cauvery water to Tamil Nadu under the Supreme Court-mandated monthly schedule because of deficient rainfall and drought-like conditions.
Karnataka informed the Authority that storage in its four Cauvery basin reservoirs stood at 48.979 tmcft against the 30-year average of 81.528 tmcft. Tamil Nadu, meanwhile, said it had received 3.442 tmcft between June 1 and July 19 against its scheduled allocation of 28.337 tmcft, leaving 24.896 tmcft yet to be released.
Karnataka told the Authority that below-normal rainfall over the past five weeks in Kodagu, Hassan, Mysuru, Bengaluru Urban, Bengaluru Rural, Ramanagara and neighbouring districts had sharply reduced inflows into reservoirs. The Authority said the Cauvery basin was entering a distress year and advised basin states to prioritise drinking water over irrigation while continuing to follow the water-sharing framework laid down under the Cauvery award for years of deficient inflows.
(With inputs from Arun Dev in Bengaluru)

headline: NEW DELHI: Opposition rebuffed PM Narendra Modiâs late-night video and proposed law on fast-track courts for paper leaks, as it reiterated that education minister Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation is a must for restoration of normalcy in Parliament. T...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Opposition rebuffed PM Narendra Modiâs late-night video and proposed law on fast-track courts for paper leaks, as it reiterated that education minister Dharmendra Pradhanâs resignation is a must for restoration of normalcy in Parliament. The aggressive stance has put a question mark on if introduction of the new bill in Parliament Monday would bring the opposition bloc back to proceedings after a week of washout.
The hostile tone was set late last night when Rahul Gandhi reacted to Modiâs video statement, saying students are demanding Pradhanâs resignation and âdonât insult their intelligence with this pathetic midnight videoâ. Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said opposition is ready for a âdetailed discussion on the education systemâ after Pradhanâs resignation.
TMC MP Sagarika Ghose mocked Modiâs video as âan oh-so-imperious PM who has contempt for Indiaâs public...forced to mumble something in a midnight Insta reel. Sadly, too little, too lateâ.
The anti-BJP parties will meet Monday morning to take a final stand on the issue, but a flurry of statements from opposition leaders Friday suggested that they are unlikely to relent.
CPM MP John Brittas said the opposition is united that the ministerâs resignation has to precede any other business. 
Asked if blocking the bill would not be politically risky, Brittas said the main issue is not the legislation but the intent of govt which is not coming through in its actions. âThe govt resolve for studentsâ cause is lacking,â he said.
There is likely to be more drama as TMC chief Mamata Banerjee will Monday visit the protesters at Jantar Mantar.
Senior members of the bloc said they are not bothered about the legislation which is âirrelevantâ to the debate, even though they cannot oppose it for the simple reason that it is propagated as targeting the âpaper leakâ menace. That has raised a strong possibility of the opposition intensifying its protests to force a washout. Leader of a minor INDIA constituent said BJP will try to project any disturbance that blocks the bill as opposition working against the reforms.
Congress accused the govt of hyping the fast-track court bill as a pioneering move when these courts can be set up under existing laws. âIt is an attempt to show responsiveness when there is none,â AICC spokesman Jairam Ramesh said.
Ramesh said Fast Track Courts only work when investigations are time-bound and there is a political will to see the investigations through. In contrast, he said the Modi govt over 12 years chose to deny paper leaks, like in 2026 and 2024. He said the govt called Sanjeev Mukhiya the âkingpinâ of the 2024 leak, but the CBI is now calling him innocent.

headline: ‘Thanks for calling us cockroaches’: Abhijeet Dipke's message for CJI Surya Kant as Modi govt gives in, minister resigns
full_text:
‘Thanks for calling us cockroaches’: Abhijeet Dipke's message for CJI Surya Kant as Modi govt gives in, minister resigns
CJP traces origin, name to May hearing at which CJI Kant used "cockroaches" and "parasites" for jobless youth and later clarified he meant fake degree holders
“Thanks for calling us cockroaches.” That was Abhijeet Dipke's message on Saturday to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, delivered from the stage at Jantar Mantar, minutes after Dharmendra Pradhan resigned as Union education minister under pressure from the movement that owed its origin and name to a remarks by India's top judge.
“I would like to thank CJI Surya Kant,” the Cockroach Janta Party founder told supporters, “If he hadn't called us cockroaches, I wouldn't have come to India. This movement would not have started.”
The comment traces the movement's arc back to its origin point, a May 15 Supreme Court hearing on Senior Advocate designation, during which the CJI remarked that “there are youngsters like cockroaches, who don't get any employment and don't have any place in the profession”. Kant later said the remark was directed only at holders of fake law degrees, not at unemployed youth broadly.
He has since reiterated that sections of the media misquoted him. The clarifications did little to stop the remark from going viral.
Dipke, then a Boston-based student who had previously worked as a communications strategist with the Aam Aadmi Party, posted a witty response on X the following day. On May 16, he announced the launch of the Cockroach Janta Party, describing it as a platform for “all the 'cockroaches' out there”, with eligibility criteria listed as being unemployed, lazy, chronically online, and able to rant professionally.
The satirical post gathered momentum through late May as anger built over the NEET-UG paper leak, and Dipke flew back to India in early June to lead protests near Jantar Mantar in person.
The movement's central demand — Pradhan's resignation over the exam irregularities — gained further weight when educator-activist Sonam Wangchuk joined with an indefinite hunger strike on June 28. Wangchuk's fast ran 26 days before he ended it earlier this week, after the Centre gave written assurances that no cases would be registered against peaceful protesters, that Parliament would take up examination reforms and accountability, and that compensation for the families of students who died by suicide following the alleged paper leak would be considered.
The CJP held firm on Pradhan's resignation even after Wangchuk's fast ended, despite a July 20 lathicharge on protesters and a rigid government position that slowly cracked.
Pradhan, in his resignation letter to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, said he was acting “keeping the future of students in mind”, and claimed the decision around ensuring “anti-national elements are not benefitted by the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the country”.

headline: CJP protest ends, what's next? Ashutosh Ranka, Neha Bora reveal plan to India Today
full_text:
CJP protest ends, what's next? Ashutosh Ranka, Neha Bora reveal plan to India Today
After Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, Ashutosh Ranka and Neha Bora said the protest leaders would first return home and rest. They said the movement would now press for accountability and structural reforms in education.
After nearly 50 days of protests, a 23-day hunger strike and weeks away from their families, the leaders of the movement that forced Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation have a surprisingly simple immediate plan: go home and sleep.
But the rest of their answer is more complicated.
“The only thing we have planned for now is to go home and sleep, meet our families,” said Ashutosh Ranka, spokesperson of the Cockroach Janta Party, after Pradhan's resignation.
Ranka said the core team had spent nearly two months away from their families and was now dealing with infections and fever after the prolonged protest.
But the break, he made clear, is not the end of the movement.
“Stay rest assured, the cockroaches are just getting started,” Ranka said.
The nearly 50-day protest may have achieved its immediate demand - Pradhan's resignation - but the leaders of the movement say they now want to push for accountability and structural reforms in India's education system.
“This has not ended. This is just getting started. We will not stop till the education system of this country is fixed, and that's a promise,” Ranka said.
He said the movement had already submitted a five-point demand charter to the government and that another round of discussions with ministers had been agreed for a month later.
“The idea is not agitation. The idea is to bring back accountability in the system. The idea is to push structural reforms in the system, and whatever it takes, we'll do,” Ranka said.
AISA president Neha Bora, who spent 23 days on hunger strike during the protest, also said the movement had achieved more than it had initially set out to do.
“We had set out to take Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, and instead what we also achieved, along with Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation, was a young people, a young nation, that has learnt to fight its battles,” she said.
Bora said the movement had brought together anger over paper leaks, unemployment, the National Education Policy, the National Testing Agency and what she described as the wider “bulldozing” of India's education system.
“This is a country of unemployed people, where even if you have a degree, even if you complete your higher education, it is almost impossible for us to get a job,” she said.
The leaders also rejected the idea that the movement had ended with Pradhan's resignation or that the Education Minister was merely “collateral damage” in a wider anti-BJP campaign.
“I wouldn't make the mistake of calling Dharmendra Pradhan collateral damage,” Bora said.
Ranka described the protest as a movement for accountability rather than simply an anti-BJP agitation.
“It is a movement for accountability in the system, which has gone missing in the last few years in this country,” he said.
The next phase could also take the movement beyond street protests. Asked whether the Cockroach Janta Party could become a political party, Ranka did not rule it out.
“The only thing I've learnt in my short career in public life and politics is never say no. Never say no,” he said.
So, for now, the protesters are going home to sleep.
But if their own leaders are to be believed, the “cockroaches are just getting started.”

headline: 'Amit Shah directly responsible': Rahul attacks HM after 'pellet guns used against students' during CJP protest
full_text:
'Amit Shah directly responsible': Rahul attacks HM after 'pellet guns used against students' during CJP protest
Rahul Gandhi said the protest was “a warning” from students and the opposition to the government.
Rahul Gandhi, the leader of the opposition in Lok Sabha, on Saturday reacted to the Narendra Modi government accepting all the demands put by the Cockroach Janta Party, saying it was “one step in a very deep problem” and directly attacking home minister Amit Shah over the alleged use of pellet guns on protesters.
Addressing his second press conference of the day, the Congress leader said the protest was “a warning” from students and the opposition to the government.
“This is a warning from the students and opposition that you cannot run the country the way you have been running. This is not your personal fiefdom,” Gandhi said.
“We hold Amit Shah directly responsible for the violence inflicted on our students. He authorised the firing on our students, authorised the use of lethal weapons, and authorised the use of pellet guns against them. That's a fundamental issue. We do not accept our security forces shooting at the future of India. This is going to be a major issue in Parliament,” he further said.
The Delhi police have denied the use of pellet guns on protesters in Delhi, though Gandhi brought a person forward on Friday who alleged that he was hit by pellets during the students' march to Parliament on Monday.
Rahul on Dharmendra Pradhan
Rahul Gandhi called Dharmendra Pradhan, who resigned as education minister earlier in the day due to massive protests, “a symbol of corruption, incompetence, and the destruction of the education system”.
“It's good that this symbol has been removed. But now, to reform the education system, the government will have to take strict measures. Students have two more demands, which we must not forget. Strict action must be taken against those who brutalised students. Narendra Modi must apologise to all the students of the country,” he said.
This comes after two major announcements were made during a joint press conference held by union ministers Jitendra Singh and JP Nadda, and Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) spokespersons Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das. CJP withdrew its agitation “in good faith”, and the government agreed to withdraw all cases against student protesters and accept all of CJP's demands.

headline: Here's the last time a Union minister resigned under Modi govt because of protests
full_text:
Here's the last time a Union minister resigned under Modi govt because of protests
To even draw a remote parallel, one has to rewind the clock all the way to 2018, when MJ Akbar stepped down from his post as Union minister.
It's rare for the Narendra Modi government to bow to public pressure. Even rarer is a sitting minister resigning. This is why education minister Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation is such a big event.
To even draw a remote parallel, one has to rewind the clock all the way to 2018, when MJ Akbar stepped down from his post as Union minister of state for external affairs at the height of the #MeToo movement.
Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation
Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on Saturday, marking a major victory for the Cockroach Janta Party-led protests against alleged paper leaks. The protesters refused to budge without his resignation despite the government assuring that it would accede to their other demands, including compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after the NEET paper leak and no legal action against those who took part in the march to Parliament earlier this week.
The CJP also said that the third round of talks with the government would take place only if Pradhan resigned. Just hours before the talks were supposed to be held (which later happened), the resignation came.
Pradhan said he took full responsibility for the NEET paper leak and "never turned away from the situation", but "individuals holding responsible positions attempted to create obstacles and mislead students".
"Considering the situation at Jantar Mantar and across the country-with the aim of preventing anti-national forces from exploiting it, preserving national unity, ensuring that not a single Indian student's future gets entangled in legal complexities, and allowing our children to devote their time to studies and focus on building their careers - I have submitted my resignation to the Honourable Prime Minister," the 57-year-old wrote in a letter that he posted on X.
Parallels to Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation since 2014
The Opposition has long accused the Narendra Modi government of "arrogance", and alleged ministers don't step down even after several controversies. Their claim is that it became a trend since PM Modi came to power in 2014.
Back in 2015, Rajnath Singh fueled the fire of such claims, which the opposition still quotes. “This is the NDA government. Resignations don't happen here,” he had said back then. And it has mostly held true. Well, mostly.
The last and only other time something similar - yet very different in terms of the kind of allegations levelled - had happened was in 2018, when MJ Akbar resigned.
Akbar, who had been the minister of state for external affairs since 2016, was accused of sexual harassment by multiple women amid a growing #MeToo movement in the country. Most of these women had worked or interacted with him when he was the editor of several leading newspapers. There were protests against him, but nowhere near as intense as those against Dharmendra Pradhan.
Several reports at the time said the decision to step down was Akbar's, and that he would remain in the BJP. "This will not set a precedent," the BJP leaders were quoted as saying at the time.
Akbar himself said he was quitting to fight the charges “in a court of law in my personal capacity” and to “challenge false accusations”.
Some others held on despite sustained calls for their removal
Ajay Kumar Mishra Teni, the minister of state for home, faced opposition demands for his resignation after an SUV registered in his name ran over farmers and a journalist in Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri in 2021. Mishra’s son was accused of driving the SUV.
Teni remained in office until he lost his Lok Sabha seat in the 2024 general election.
Before that, in August 2017, railway minister Suresh Prabhu offered to resign after two train derailments in five days, tweeting that he had met PM Modi to take “full moral responsibility” for the accidents. Modi asked him to wait, and Prabhu was moved from Railways to commerce and industry in a cabinet reshuffle days later.

headline: New bill against paper leaks will have stricter punishments, faster trial
full_text:
New bill against paper leaks will have stricter punishments, faster trial
Minister for DoPT Jitendra Singh, who is also the government interlocutor along with union health minister JP Nadda, is set to introduce the bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday
The Centre’s new bill against exam paper leak that will be tabled on Monday, aims for stricter punishment, increasing the minimum jail term and higher fines, and speedy trials by setting up fast track courts that will complete the trial within three months from the filing of the chargesheet.
Overhauling the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024, the government will introduce on Monday a series of amendments in the wake of surging protests in Delhi and across the country by students and the Cockroach Janta Party. It allows formation of a Special Task Force, time-bound probe and daily proceedings during trial.
According to the proposed law, anyone resorting to “unfair means and offences”, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term not less than “five years but which may extend up to ten years and with fine up to fifty lakh rupees.”
Similarly, the service provider can be punished with fine of ₹5 crores and proportionate cost of examination shall also be recovered from such service provider and he shall also be barred from being assigned with any responsibility for the conduct of any public examination for a period of eight years.
In the current bill, the jail term for unfair means and offences was three to five years with ₹10 lakh fine. Similarly, service providers’ fine was one crore with a ban for four years.
The proposed legislation increases the minimum jail term to five years from three, and the fine to ₹5 crore from ₹2 crore for any director, senior management or the persons in-charge of the service provider firm who are found guilty during the investigation.
For organised crime resulting to paper leaks, a person or a group of persons shall be punished with a minimum jail term of seven years which may extend to ten years and they have to pay a fine of ₹10 crore.
Minister for DoPT Jitendra Singh, who is also the government interlocutor along with union health minister JP Nadda, is set to introduce the bill in the Lok Sabha on Monday.
The statement of objects of the bill said, “In recent years, there have been some incidents of question paper leakages and malpractices in examinations conducted by public examination authorities, which tend to affect the transparency and fairness of the public examinations system. Hence, in order to further strengthen the fairness, to enhance the credibility of the public examinations system and to facilitate speedy trial and ensure time bound investigations of offences under the said Act, it is necessary to make amendments in the said Act...”
The proposed bill inserts two new sections— 12A and 12B— for speedy probe and trials. The current bill stipulated investigation by federal agencies. The new bill allows the government to set up a Special Task Force for the same purpose. The new sections add that be it a Central Investigating Agency or a SIT, shall complete the probe “within a period of two months from the date of a reference made to it by the Central Government.”
Making specific provisions for the fast track courts, the bill said, “For the purposes of providing a speedy trial on day-to-day basis, every State Government and Union territory Administration shall, in consultation with the Chief Justice of the concerned High Court, by notification, designate a Court of Session, to be a Special Fast Track Court to try offences under this Act.”
It also imposes strict timelines for trial. “In every trial of an offence under this Act, the proceedings shall be continued on day-to-day basis, until all the witnesses in attendance have been examined, unless the Special Fast Track Court, for reasons to be recorded in writing, finds that adjournment of the same beyond the following day is necessary: Provided that such trial shall be completed within a period of three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet,” the new provisions of the legislation said.
In a bid to cut down judicial delays, the bill says that an appeal shall lie from any judgment, sentence or order, not being an interlocutory order, of a Special Fast Track Court to the High Court and “Every appeal under sub-section (1) shall be heard by a bench of two Judges of the High Court and shall, as far as possible, be disposed of within a period of three months from the date of admission of the appeal.”
“Except as aforesaid, no appeal or revision shall lie to any Court from any judgment, sentence or order including an interlocutory order of a Special Fast Track Court” and “an appeal shall lie to the High Court against an order of the Special Fast Track Court granting or refusing bail.”
The bill also tightens provisions for appeals. “Every appeal under this section shall be preferred within a period of thirty days from the date of the judgment, sentence or order appealed from: Provided that the High Court may entertain an appeal after the expiry of the said period of thirty days if it is satisfied that the appellant had sufficient cause for not preferring the appeal within the period of thirty days: Provided further that no appeal shall be entertained after the expiry of the period of ninety days,” it said.
It is, however, not clear if the government would manage to pass the legislation as the Opposition, adamant for education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s ouster, had washed out the first week of the monsoon session. Many Opposition lawmakers have told HT that unless Pradhan resigns, they don’t want to give the government any leeway to debate or discussion students’ related issues.

headline: 17 people get life for 2014 Dalit man’s murder in Karnataka's Yadgir
full_text:
17 people get life for 2014 Dalit man’s murder in Karnataka's Yadgir
A dispute over banners during a village festival in Yadgir district that turned into a caste-driven killing over a decade ago came to a close on Thursday
A dispute over banners during a village festival in Karnataka's Yadgir district that turned into a caste-driven killing over a decade ago came to a close on Thursday, with sessions court convicting 20 people in the 2014 murder of Dalit leader Devendrappa Bhimappa Dalapati, sentencing 17 of them to life imprisonment.
The court found that the prosecution had established the case through eyewitness testimony, medical evidence and material objects recovered during the investigation. One accused was sentenced to seven years’ imprisonment, while two others received six months in prison. The court also imposed a collective fine of ₹4.25 lakh, directing that it be paid to the victim’s legal heirs, and advised the family to seek additional compensation through the District Legal Services Authority.
According to investigators, the violence began during the annual Sri Chowdeshwari Devi Jatra Mahotsava in Kanyakolur village on January 15, 2014, when banners displaying photographs of leaders from the Scheduled Caste and upper caste communities were torn.
“The incident dates back to January 15, 2014. As in previous years, the annual Sri Chowdeshwari Devi Jatra Mahotsava was being held at Kanyakolur village under Shahapur Police Station limits,” Yadgir Superintendent of Police Pruthvik Shankar said.
“During the festival, tensions flared between members of the Scheduled Caste community and members of the upper caste community. The reason: tearing of cut outs and banners that carried photographs of their respective community leaders.”
The disagreement continued into the next day before erupting into violence on January 17. “What started as a dispute over symbols and banners would, within 48 hours, turn into a brutal murder,” the Superintendent of Police said.
Police said villagers had gathered near the Anjaneya Temple to resolve the dispute while a group of accused had also assembled nearby. The confrontation later shifted near the old Gram Panchayat building, where Devendrappa had gone with other villagers for talks.
Principal public prosecutor Gurulingappa Shrimant Teli said the discussions quickly descended into violence after the accused allegedly abused Devendrappa using caste slurs. “The accused allegedly hurled caste based abuses at Devendrappa, accusing him of interfering in every matter,” Teli said.
According to the prosecution, Devendrappa ran towards the Jumma Mosque in an attempt to escape. “The accused chased him, armed with axes, clubs and stones. With the intention to murder him, they knocked him down and attacked him repeatedly,” Teli said.
Court records showed that he suffered multiple injuries to his head, abdomen, shoulders, knees, back and feet. His left arm was twisted and, according to the prosecution, he was dragged by his legs after the assault. The prosecution also told the court that when he asked for water, he was abused again. A person who tried to rescue him was struck with a club and injured. Devendrappa died at the scene.
Following the attack, Shahapur police registered a case and later filed a chargesheet against 32 accused under provisions relating to unlawful assembly, rioting, murder, attempt to murder, intentional insult and the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act.
During the trial, the prosecution cited 68 witnesses, of whom 37 testified before the court. The defence argued that several accused had been falsely implicated because of village rivalry, but the court rejected those submissions.
“The court has accepted all arguments put forth by the prosecution. Thirty seven witnesses were examined and the medical evidence supported our case of murder with common intention. The fine amount will now go to the victim’s family and we have also suggested they apply for DLSA compensation,” Teli said.

headline: NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.

NEW DELHI: Amid the ongoing student protest, Delhi police have deployed around 3,000 police personnel to maintain law and order for nearly 10,000 people present in and around Jantar Mantar.
Police sources said around 130 police personnel have been injured and 15 FIRs have been registered in connection with the agitation, according to Delhi Police sources. The police also said around 65 students sustained injuries during the demonstrations.
The Delhi Police further said it is using Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras to identify "anti-social elements" visiting Jantar Mantar.
According to police sources, more than 2,000 people with criminal records who had visited the protest site have been identified so far, as cited by ANI.
This is not the first time the Delhi Police has deployed Facial Recognition System (FRS) cameras.
The force has previously used the technology as part of security arrangements during Republic Day, Independence Day, Holi, Diwali, Eid, Ramlila celebrations and several other major public events across the city.
Meanwhile, Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke on Saturday said he has been diagnosed with typhoid but asserted that the nationwide protests demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan would continue without interruption.
On Friday, Dipke welcomed activist Sonam Wangchuk's decision to end his 26-day hunger strike but reiterated that the movement would continue until its demand for accountability over the examination irregularities is met.
"Our demonstration will go on until Dharmendra Pradhan steps down. Any meeting must take place at a neutral location or venue. Nothing less than the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan will be accepted," he said.
Meanwhile, activist Sonam Wangchuk responded to criticism over his decision to end his 26-day hunger strike held in support of students protesting the alleged NEET paper leak.
In a video message shared on social media, Wangchuk questioned why his commitment to the cause required a "character certificate".
Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike after receiving a written assurance from the Union government on the NEET examination issue and broader systemic reforms to the country's competitive examination framework.
The activist said he had earlier been offered verbal assurances but insisted on a written commitment, which delayed the end of his fast by two days.

headline: NEW DELHI: Digital rights advocacy group Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) has termed govt's order directing GitHub to remove the source code repositories of Bluetooth-based messaging app BitChat "unconstitutional and authoritarian".
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Digital rights advocacy group Internet Freedom Foundation (IFF) has termed govt's order directing GitHub to remove the source code repositories of Bluetooth-based messaging app BitChat "unconstitutional and authoritarian".
In a statement Friday, IFF said the order, issued by Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) under the home ministry, directed GitHub to disable access to three BitChat repositories, including the Android application and release files, within three hours. It added that the order warned the platform of loss of safe harbour protection and possible criminal prosecution for non-compliance.
It argued govt relied on Section 79(3)(b) of the Information Technology Act and Rule 3(1)(d) of the IT Rules, 2021, instead of the dedicated blocking framework under Section 69A of the IT Act and the Blocking Rules, 2009, that require procedural safeguards such as recorded reasons and an opportunity for hearing.
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
IFF also contended that the order did not identify any specific unlawful content in the repositories and instead objected to BitChat's ability to function during internet shutdowns through Bluetooth mesh networking. It said anticipating potential misuse of a communications tool was not a sufficient legal basis for ordering its removal.
The foundation criticised the three-hour compliance window, saying it effectively denied GitHub meaningful legal recourse, and demanded that govt withdraw the notice.

headline: Dharmendra Pradhan a small sacrifice for BJP's bigger goals?
full_text:
Dharmendra Pradhan a small sacrifice for BJP's bigger goals?
The BJP is a party which obsesses over the future. That a resignation would create precedence was one of the key reasons it didn't want Dharmendra Pradhan to go. But then, the BJP has bigger Parliament plans, and Pradhan was but a tiny sacrifice.
Hearts and messages are generally carved on the wooden desks of colleges. "Today's a gift, that's why it's called present" is one of the cheesier ones. The BJP didn't study in one of those small-town colleges. A big part of its education came from the streets of competitive post-Independent India, where survival was the primordial instinct, and tomorrow was always the concern.
Millions in India believe Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan should have gone long before the crowds swelled at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar seeking his head. There was the NEET-UG paper leak, followed soon after by the CBSE online marking scheme fiasco.
There was neither action nor communication from the party and the government as India's higher education looked like the crumbled blocks of Jenga on a table.
With the Opposition missing, the cockroaches turned up on the table. Sonam Wangchuk fed the fledgling movement with his hunger strike. But what they might have failed to achieve was done by Delhi Police and the RAF. The brutal use of force on July 20 on protesters, thousands of whom were minors, pushed the BJP into the proverbial cul-de-sac.
With 'what if tomorrow...' on its mind, the BJP tried to delay what was destiny. That Pradhan's resignation might create a precedence was one of the key reasons why the brass tried to save him.
However, the more the delay in packing off Pradhan, the more it presented itself as a rigid regime, showing no flexibility to accommodate people's demands.
With the monsoon session of Parliament about to begin, political activity in the capital intensified. Leaders from Opposition parties started streaming into Jantar Mantar to be seen with a fasting Wangchuk.
The monsoon session began on July 20 and the first week was a washout.
Rahul Gandhi, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, protested both in the House and in front of the PM's house and got detained. The Opposition was in no mood to let Parliament function. It knew what the government was aiming for. The government knew what the Opposition was striving for.
Two senior ministers — JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh — succeeded in getting Wangchuk to end his fast, toning down his demand for Pradhan's resignation. But by then, the protest had become way bigger than Wangchuk or the Cockroach Janta Party. The fire had spread and it needed a sacrifice made.
No stringent laws or fast-track courts or portrait-mode videos would satiate the leaping flames. It needed Pradhan, who had become the face of the crumbled Jenga blocks.
The BJP now thought, and thought seriously about tomorrow. About the future. Precedence can be taken care of, and the bigger goals, thus, took precedence.
The crucial delimitation bill, sources have revealed, might be introduced in the monsoon session. Though it wasn't among the five bills listed by the government, reports suggest the landmark bill could be brought in the session that would continue till August 13.
The Bill is special, and in April, the Modi government convened a special session to tie it with the women's reservation bill and get it passed. It was defeated as the treasury couldn't muster the support of two-thirds majority.
That was the first time that a constitutional amendment bill moved by the Modi government had been defeated. But the political landscape has changed since April.
Recent defections, inner-party feuds, lack of Opposition cohesion and political realignments have given the government hope that it could try and get the delimitation bill passed.
After the 2024 Lok Sabha election, the NDA had 293 MPs, including the BJP's 240. Its tally rose to 318, mainly because 20 rebel Trinamool MPs aligned with the NDA and six Shiv Sena (UBT) MPs merged with the Shinde Sena faction.
In the Rajya Sabha in mid-June 2024, the NDA had 101 members. The number has now increased to 152.
The growth wasn't a miracle. They have been managed shrewdly and painstakingly towards the one big delimitation goal. Other than the engineering, it needed Sharad Pawar and MK Stalin to be persuaded. No mean task.
Consequently, this monsoon session was going to be all about the BJP's guts, guile and the splintering of the Opposition, especially of the Congress. But the CJP agitation consumed every other issue. The Congress had seized the opportunity to derail the BJP's parliamentary agenda. The government couldn't have brought its agenda up as long as Jantar Mantar remained combustible. Pradhan thus became the offering.
So, it was a choice between prestige and Pradhan on one hand, and hard work and big goals on the other. So, the Modi government tapped out to save the situation, and fight a bigger fight, on another day.
The optics had already gone bad. Senior leaders Nadda and Singh negotiating with rookies Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, both seated with crossed arms, wasn't the best image for the veteran duo.
But the Modi government has been known, though rarely, to make a tactical retreat when it becomes an absolute necessity. The withdrawal of the three farm bills after the prolonged farmers' agitation is one such example.
That protest too, like the one at Jantar Mantar, was taking an altogether different shape. No government wants a protest to be hijacked and turned into an inferno that goes beyond its control.
The stakes in Parliament were already very high and Pradhan was a small sacrifice. Though everyone knows what parampara, pratishtha and anushasan mean for the party steeped in tradition and aiming for civilisational goals, what would remain a question is why the BJP let the issue fester. Why didn't the BJP, which is always planning for tomorrow, not sacrifice Pradhan yesterday itself? Why can't a party on the climb get rid of the dog Nietzsche named 'Ego'?

headline: In the 11th phase of excavations currently underway in Keeladi, continuous brick structures and over 1,300 artefacts have been discovered.
full_text:
In the 11th phase of excavations currently underway in Keeladi, continuous brick structures and over 1,300 artefacts have been discovered.
The Tamil Nadu State Department of Archaeology (TNSDA) is conducting the 11th phase of excavation at the Keeladi archaeological site, located near Madurai in Sivagangai district. While the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) conducted the first three phases, subsequent phases have been carried out by the TNSDA.
This 11th phase of excavation began on March 18 of this year, south of the area where the on-site museum is located. A total of nine quadrants were dug in this area. Ramesh Masethung, Director of Keeladi Excavations, told The Hindu that continuous brick structures were found across all nine quadrants. He mentioned that these structures, extending towards the west and north, stretch beyond these nine quadrants.
“Brick structures were previously found in the area where the on-site museum is located. In the adjacent area excavated later, no structural remains were found. However, structural remains have been uncovered once again now,” says Mr. Masethung.
Apart from these brick structures, several other important features have come to light during the current excavation. In one quadrant, a terracotta pipeline and a closed drainage system were discovered. In addition to the structural remains, more than 1,300 artefacts have been recovered. These include clay hopscotches, terracotta beads and spindles, iron knives, chisels, swords, and nails, as well as semi-precious stones such as amethyst, carnelian, agate, banded agate, and ivory dice.
Furthermore, tiny gold ornaments measuring less than a centimeter have been found. In addition, intact pots were discovered in four locations, one of which includes a handle. One of these pots features a fish symbol inscribed on its shoulder portion.
“Since an open drainage system was also found in one quadrant, this might have been an industrial area as well. However, this can only be confirmed after the studies are completed,” says Mr. Masethung. He also added that organic materials found here will be sent for carbon dating.
Depending on the rain, this 11th phase of excavation may continue until September.

headline: NEW DELHI: Aiming to ensure faster disposal of exam paper leak cases, govt has proposed a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts, unlike other cases where no such fixed timeli...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Aiming to ensure faster disposal of exam paper leak cases, govt has proposed a three-month deadline for respective high courts to dispose of appeals against orders of special fast-track courts, unlike other cases where no such fixed timeline for deciding appeals exists. This converts an open-ended investigation and judicial process into a time-bound one.
According to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill circulated to Lok Sabha MPs Saturday, individuals, service providers and organised gangs involved in paper leaks would face longer jail terms, steeper fines, and time-bound investigation and disposal of trials and appeals.
What changes in New Bill
As per the bill, which would be introduced in Lok Sabha Monday, the minimum jail term for offences committed by individuals, as well as directors, senior management personnel or persons in charge of service providers conducting public examinations, has been increased to five years. 
CJP Jantar Mantar Protest Updates
In cases involving organised crime, the minimum imprisonment has been proposed at seven years from the current provision of five years. In all these cases, the maximum jail term would be 10 years.
For speedy investigations, the bill proposes govt may constitute a central investigation agency or a special task force (STF). Where an STF has been constituted, it would carry out the investigation. The bill also seeks to insert a new provision mandating that every investigation be completed within two months.
The bill provides for day-to-day proceedings and empowers states to establish special fast-track courts in consultation with the chief justice of the respective HC.
It mandates that such trial proceedings shall continue until all witnesses in attendance have been examined. These courts would be required to dispose of cases within three months from the date of filing of the chargesheet. All pending trials will be shifted to the special court, and these must also be disposed of within three months.
It proposes that any appeal against an order of a fast-track court shall be heard by a division bench of HC. It proposes that every appeal be filed within 30 days from the date of the fast-track court's order and not after a maximum of 90 days under any circumstances.

headline: The story so far: Madhya Pradesh police personnel went to the banks of the Barana river stream in Kupi village of Chhatarpur district on July 19 and cleared a protest site where hundreds of villagers, mostly tribal people, had been demonstrating for ...
full_text:
The story so far: Madhya Pradesh police personnel went to the banks of the Barana river stream in Kupi village of Chhatarpur district on July 19 and cleared a protest site where hundreds of villagers, mostly tribal people, had been demonstrating for two weeks against the Union government’s ₹44,000 crore Ken-Betwa Link Project, India’s first river-linking project, and two irrigation projects of the State government.
The police took local activist Amit Bhatnagar, founder of the Jai Kisan Sangathan, who had been on an indefinite hunger strike for 14 days, and admitted him to a government hospital. They also picked up nearly 150 protestors, most of them from neighbouring Panna district, in buses and dropped them off at their villages.
On July 23, he suspended his 18-day fast after the government’s assurance that people left out of the rehabilitation process will be included.
What is the Ken-Betwa river linking project?
The Ken-Betwa River Linking Project is the first of 30 proposed river-linking projects under the National Perspective Plan (NPP). Formulated in 1980 by the then Union Ministry of Irrigation and the Central Water Commission, the NPP aims to transfer water from rivers with a perceived surplus to those facing water deficits. The NPP is divided into two components — Himalayan Rivers Development that proposes 14 links and Peninsular Rivers Development that plans 16 links, as identified by the National Water Development Agency.
The foundation stone for the project was laid by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in December 2024, in Khajuraho, where he also laid the foundation stone for the construction of the Daudhan Dam during a public event.
The project aims to transfer the declared surplus water of the Ken River to the Betwa River by constructing the Daudhan Dam on the Ken and a 221-kilometre canal, including a 2-km tunnel. In addition, the project is expected to generate 103 MW of hydropower and 27 MW of solar power. It also aims to address water scarcity in the drought-prone Bundelkhand region by providing drinking water to about 4.4 million people across 12 districts of Madhya Pradesh and more than 2 million people across 10 districts of Uttar Pradesh.
Why are tribal people protesting and what are their key demands?
According to the Union government, 7,193 families of 14 villages in Chhatarpur and eight villages in Panna district are facing displacement under the project. According to Divya Ahirwar of Jai Kisan Sangathan, the key demands regarding the Ken-Betwa project are that each adult be treated as an individual beneficiary — rather than as part of a family — for the ₹12.5 lakh rehabilitation package, and that the eligibility cut-off date be revised from February 16, 2024, to the present date.
The protests also oppose the State government’s Majhgaon and Runjh irrigation projects. For these projects, the protesters are demanding rehabilitation and compensation on par with the package offered under the Ken-Betwa project. In both cases, they have also alleged serious irregularities in the survey and selection process and claim that several people who have no connection with the villages or have moved years ago have been included in the rehabilitation plan, while many genuine residents have been left out.
Speaking from the hospital, Mr. Bhatnagar claimed that the police action came on the day he was planning to “reveal the details of an alleged ₹400-crore corruption scheme” involving the inclusion of fake beneficiaries in the compensation process.
Protesters have also alleged irregularities in the gram sabha proceedings in tribal villages, claiming that the process of securing consent for the Ken-Betwa project was flawed.
How did the government respond?
The State government has approved an additional ₹300 crore for the rehabilitation packages of the Majhgaon and Runjh irrigation projects, increasing compensation from ₹5 lakh to ₹12.5 lakh per eligible beneficiary.
Chhatarpur Collector Parth Jaiswal said that a new survey had identified around 750 additional families, who have now been included in the rehabilitation plan for the Majhgaon and Runjh projects. He described the protesters’ remaining demands as “invalid” and alleged that some people were “misleading” the villagers.
What are the environmental concerns surrounding the project?
Several environmental concerns have also been flagged, especially as a large part of the project falls inside the Panna Tiger Reserve. Apart from displacement, the primary concern revolves around the proposed felling of trees. As per the Jal Shakti Ministry, approximately 17,101 trees had been identified for felling to facilitate the execution of the Daudhan Dam and allied infrastructure until July, 2025. Of these, 12,404 trees have been felled within the Reserve Forest.
There is worry that the project may hurt the tiger reintroduction programme in the reserve which revived the feline population after it had locally gone extinct in 2009. Apart from tigers, species such as endangered vultures, mahseer fish, and gharials in the Ken Gharial Sanctuary are also feared to be impacted.
The Central government is yet to release hydrological data of the two basins claiming that they are sensitive by virtue of being subsets of the international Ganga basin.

headline: After nearly a decade since it got administrative sanction (in 2018), work to construct ₹8.5 crore Tangedco 33/11 KV sub-station in Yelagiri Hills in Tirupattur district has commenced.
full_text:
After nearly a decade since it got administrative sanction (in 2018), work to construct ₹8.5 crore Tangedco 33/11 KV sub-station in Yelagiri Hills in Tirupattur district has commenced.
Officials of Tangedco, which executes the work, said that a new sub-station was a long-standing demand of residents in the hills. Of the total 5,286 consumers, 1,400 are commercial establishments, mostly hotels, restaurants, and resorts. “Power shutdowns and fluctuations have been common in hamlets in the hills. The new sub-station will end the ordeal of residents, especially students, who can study under better lights,” said G. Somu, a tribal.
Around 200 consumers are farmers. . “Civic works for the substation have commenced. Thereafter, installation of transformers, feeders, and other electrical equipment will be done. The new facility will be ready in 2027,” Rajan Murugesan, Assistant Engineer (AE), Tangedco (Yelagiri Hills), told The Hindu.
At present, permanent sub-stations in Jawadhu Hills are located in Kavalur and Pudur Nadu village near Yelagiri Hills. The sub-station in Kavalur village was established in 1960s to operate Vainu Bappu Astronomical Observatory, which was relocated from Kodaikanal in 1968.
The Pudur Nadu substation was opened in 2020 after bifurcation from the Vaniyambadi power station.
Against this backdrop, Tangedco proposed to set up a sub-station at Yelagiri Hills mainly to promote domestic tourism as the hill station has more than 150 hotels and resorts. Initially, the project got its nod for a budget of ₹3.5 crore in 2018.
However, Tangedco officials said that project was halted since then before it was revived with a revised estimate of ₹8.5 crore in January 2026. A ceremony to lay the foundation stone was held in March. After polls, work to construct the new facility was expedited.
Bifurcated from the Vaniyambadi 110 KV sub-station in April 2022, the Tangedco office at Yelagiri Hills was functioning as a section office with meager staff. Daily power supply was monitored by officials at Vaniyambadi office, around 30 km away in the plains. It resulted in delay in attending complaints and repair of power lines on the route which is lined with forests.
Tangedco officials said that the new sub-station will help attend to power faults immediately. Power fluctuations will be prevented as power supply will be given directly from the sub-station in the hills. The new facility will lessen dependence on diesel-run generators in the hills and prevent pollution.

headline: Cops await Centre's orders on withdrawing FIRs against CJP protesters after Dharmendra Pradhan's exit
full_text:
Cops await Centre's orders on withdrawing FIRs against CJP protesters after Dharmendra Pradhan's exit
Officers had maintained that intelligence inputs initially estimated a crowd of 10,000 to 15,000 people, but the turnout was significantly higher.
Hours after Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned and the government assured the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) that the first information reports (FIRs) registered in connection with the protest and related violence would be withdrawn, Delhi Police said that they will wait for the official communication from the government for further action.
“As of now, we will wait for the government for any official communication on how to proceed with the cases already registered in connection with the July 20 violence and other cases registered on July 22,” a senior police officer, who did not wish to be named, said.
Union minister JP Nadda said the discussions with the CJP included cases registered during the agitation, compensation for affected families and the CJP’s broader charter of demands.
Also Read | What's 'pending' after Dharmendra Pradhan resigns: CJP lists updated demands
“We discussed these issues in detail. After the discussion, the first point was that no action should be taken and no FIR should be filed. If any FIRs have already been registered, whether by the Delhi Police or in BJP-ruled states, it will be withdrawn,” he said.
However, a second officer explained that FIRs are never “withdrawn” and the term was used only to explain to the public. The officer said that an FIR is an official record. “There are only three ways an FIR can be treated. One is to file a charge sheet and prosecute further. The second is to file a closure report or cancellation after probe. The third is for the state to withdraw prosecution,” the officer said.
The officer said that when the government officially communicates to them that they have withdrawn the prosecution, no investigation will be conducted.
A CJP spokesperson said that they will be given the same in writing on Tuesday.
Police had, until Friday, described the incidents that unfolded on July 20 as a “larger conspiracy”. The Delhi Police, until Friday, registered 15 FIRs in connection with the violence that accompanied the CJP’s “Chalo Sansad” march between July 20 and July 23. Police said the clashes on July 20 left at least 129 security personnel and over 60 protesters injured, while 11 officers were injured in subsequent clashes.
One of the FIRs, accessed by Hindustan Times, was registered at Kartavya Path police station on the complaint of an inspector and includes Section 109(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (attempt to murder), along with charges related to rioting, unlawful assembly, assault on public servants, mischief causing damage to public property and disobeying prohibitory orders.
According to the complaint, the officer was deployed near Kartavya Path’s C-Hexagon from 5 am on July 20 in view of the proposed protest. Around 11.30 am, after receiving wireless messages that protesters were marching towards the Parliament, he and his team moved to the barricades near Rail Bhawan on Rafi Marg.
The FIR stated that despite repeated announcements that prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita were in force, protesters ignored directions to disperse, delivered “instigating speeches”, attempted to breach barricades leading to the Parliament, assaulted police personnel, pelted stones and damaged public and private property. It stated that police resorted to a “mild lathicharge” and tear gas shelling to disperse the crowd.
Separately, senior officers said four more FIRs were registered later, taking the total to 15, while the special cell took over the first FIR to investigate what police termed a “larger conspiracy” behind the violence.
Investigators had said they were examining more than 15 terabytes of video footage, scrutinising speeches delivered from the main stage at Jantar Mantar, and probing the role of alleged “handlers” and social media influencers suspected of coordinating the protests. Police also claimed to be investigating alleged funding channels, logistical support and the circulation of a purported “toolkit”, instructing participants to carry pepper spray, chilli powder and blunt objects.

headline: The West Bengal Legislative Assembly on Saturday (July 26, 2026) passed the West Bengal Panchayat ( Second Amendment), 2026 Bill depriving elected representatives of panchayats of financial powers.
full_text:
The West Bengal Legislative Assembly on Saturday (July 26, 2026) passed the West Bengal Panchayat ( Second Amendment), 2026 Bill depriving elected representatives of panchayats of financial powers.
The bill was passed with 169 votes polled in favour of the bill, while 13 MLAs voted against it. 32 MLAs did not participate in the voting process.
The proposed legislation seeks to amend several provisions of the West Bengal Panchayat Act, 1973, with the stated objective of ensuring administrative stability, uninterrupted public service delivery and smoother functioning of rural local bodies.
The statement of objects and reasons of the legislation says that the bill was brought to ensure the stability of panchayat bodies for the time bound delivery of services to the public at large.
The bill provides for the prescribed authority to appoint an extension officer, or an officer of a higher rank, as Administrator for a maximum period of 30 days if both the pradhan and the deputy pradhan remain absent for more than 15 days and no elected member is willing to discharge the responsibilities.
The bill also addresses situations where no gram panchayat meeting is held for two consecutive months due to the absence of the pradhan and deputy pradhan. In such cases, the panchayat secretary, with the approval of the Block Development Officer (BDO), will be authorised to convene the meeting.
Participating in the discussion, Panchayat Affairs and Rural Development Minister Dilip Ghosh said the Bill does not intend to curtail the constitutional powers of elected panchayat heads.
“Rather, it is aiming at curtailing the authority for corruption and commission against rural civic services. Henceforth, the elected panchayat heads will only approve any proposal. But the Bill will be cleared and sanctioned by the bureaucrats,” he said.
The State Panchayat Minister alleged that in many instances where pradhans have refused to sign work-related documents due to issues regarding alleged ‘cut-money’ (kickbacks). He stated that the objective of the amendment is to curb such irregularities. Mr. Ghosh claimed that among all States in the country, it is only in West Bengal that panchayat pradhans possess such financial powers, and that economic interests have been a major factor behind the violence witnessed during panchayat elections.
A few days ago, the State government issued a notification depriving panchayat pradhans and elected representatives of powers to issue birth and death certificates.
Despite the change in the regime in West Bengal, most of the panchayats and local bodies are administered by the Trinamool Congress. The Bharatiya Janata Party government in West Bengal argues that most of the panchayat pradhans have stopped performing their duties and thus such legislative changes were necessary.

headline: 5 of family arrested in UP over law student's suspected honour killing

5 of family arrested in UP over law student's suspected honour killing
According to a complaint by the law student's boyfriend, her family claimed she had died due to illness and cremated her before the matter could come to the notice of the authorities.
A 20-year-old law student was allegedly killed in Uttar Pradesh's Aligarh district by her family in a suspected case of honour killing after she refused to end her relationship with a young man, and five of her family members have now been arrested in connection with the death.
The case came to light after the woman's boyfriend, Harshit, approached the police on Friday with a written complaint alleging that her family had killed her, according to the police.
According to the complaint, the family claimed that the woman, Himanshi, had died due to illness and cremated her on Thursday night before the matter could come to the notice of the authorities.
The police launched a probe following the complaint and arrested five people by Friday night on charges of homicide. Those arrested include Himanshi's mother, her two brothers and two maternal uncles, Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Neeraj Kumar said.
In his complaint, Harshit claimed he and Himanshi had been in contact for nearly one and a half years, and that the latter's family had consistently opposed their relationship as they were from different castes.
He alleged that both of them were repeatedly given death threats by Himanshi's family. A CCTV video related to the case has also surfaced.
The footage reportedly shows the moment when Himanshi ran away from her home and reached a shop where Harshit was already present. Reports suggest that the woman's family members arrived at the scene and thrashed the duo.
While demanding justice for Himanshi, Harshit also said that he fears for his own life now. Police said further investigation into the case is underway.

headline: Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who toured Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh’s Drass on Saturday (July 25, 2026), said the intentions of the enemies have not changed, and the proxy war remains a security challenge in the region.
full_text:
Union Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who toured Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh’s Drass on Saturday (July 25, 2026), said the intentions of the enemies have not changed, and the proxy war remains a security challenge in the region.
Without naming Pakistan, Mr. Singh, while speaking at Shaurya Bhoj in Drass, said, “As we celebrate the Kargil War victory, we have to remind ourselves of the challenges. The intention of our enemy remains the same. Proxy war is still used as a tactic. Our Army is ready to foil these nefarious designs,” said Mr. Singh.
The Defence Minister arrived in Srinagar on Saturday (July 25, 2026) morning on a two-day tour of the region. He was received by J&K Lieutenant-Governor Manoj Sinha. Officials said they discussed the current security situation in J&K, especially in the wake of the Anantnag attack that left one policeman dead three days ago.
Later, Mr. Singh visited the war memorial at Ladakh’s Drass on the eve of the 27th Kargil Vijay Diwas. He paid tributes to the soldiers who laid down their lives in the line of duty in the 1999 Kargil War against Pakistan, as he attended the ‘Shaurya Sandhya’.
“It’s these sacrifices that make people of India feel safe. When oxygen levels dropped in 1999, the guns of our soldiers did not fall silent till the Tricolour was unfurled as a mark of victory. We are proud of the valiant soldiers and their degree of courage,” said Mr. Singh.
He said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had ensured that the morale of soldiers remains high. “We are investing in modernisation of equipment and training. We are hopeful to see the Indian Army among the leading forces in the world,” he said..
Mr. Singh said the Indian armed forces were fully prepared to face every challenge posed by the country’s adversaries. “India’s military remains vigilant, battle-ready, and capable of protecting the nation’s sovereignty,” he said.
He said no one dares cast an evil eye on India as long as the patriotism and determination of the country’s soldiers remain unshaken, adding that their sacrifices ensure every Indian can pursue dreams without fear.
Ten families of Kargil War bravehearts were felicitated on the occasion. Commemorative events were held at ‘Yudh Sansmaran’ at Lamochen View Point, where the Kargil War veterans and families of fallen soldiers remembered the sacrifices made during Operation Vijay. A documentary and special presentations highlighting the valour of 40 war heroes were screened during the event.
Mr. Singh will be the chief guest at the national homage ceremony on July 26. He is expected to lay a wreath at the war memorial, interact with Veer Naris and Veer Maas, inaugurate a virtual walkthrough portal, and flag off the Shaurya Vijay Yatra motorcycle rally.

headline: Rajnath Singh honours Kargil heroes in Ladakh on Operation Vijay anniversary
full_text:
Rajnath Singh honours Kargil heroes in Ladakh on Operation Vijay anniversary
At Dras, the Army held Shaurya Sandhya to honour soldiers killed in the 1999 Kargil war. The commemoration underscored Operation Vijay's legacy as families, veterans and top leaders paid tribute.
The Army on Saturday held a Shaurya Sandhya at the Kargil War Memorial in Dras to honour the Indian soldiers who died in the 1999 Kargil conflict, as part of a two-day commemoration marking the 27th anniversary of Operation Vijay. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh took part in the event and handed a ceremonial kalash (sacred metal pot) to some family members of the personnel who made the ultimate sacrifice in the war.
The programme began on the eve of Kargil Vijay Diwas and will conclude on Sunday with a wreath-laying ceremony and the flag-in of the Shaurya Vijay Yatra from the National War Memorial in Delhi to the Kargil War Memorial in Dras. Singh, who arrived in Dras on Saturday, will be the chief guest at the Shradhanjali Samaroh on Sunday.
Saturday evening's ceremony was attended by Ladakh Lieutenant Governor VK Saxena, Army Chief General Dhiraj Seth, General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Northern Command, Lieutenant General Pratik Sharma, other senior Army officers and several military veterans.
A band of the Ladakh Scouts played patriotic songs, including AR Rahman's "Maa Tujhe Salaam", after which guests lit candles near the obelisk of the main memorial. As night fell, hundreds of neatly placed stones in rows in the Veer Bhoomi cenotaph zone were illuminated.
Earlier in the day, the Army held several events to mark the anniversary of Operation Vijay, which falls on July 26. The two-day commemoration began with Yudh Sansmaran at the Lamochen viewpoint overlooking the Kargil battlefield. Officials said the occasion marks the victory in which Indian soldiers, braving snow-clad peaks and firing by Pakistani troops, reclaimed the heights of Kargil.
The event opened with a 33-minute video on the Kargil war and India's triumph under Operation Vijay, followed by a 17-minute commemorative clip honouring 40 Kargil bravehearts whose next of kin will be present. Major General Amit Prakash Singh, General Officer Commanding, Forever in Operations Division, senior Army officers, Kargil war veterans, Veer Naris and Veer Matas attended the programme.
Murti Devi Dahiya, whose son, Sep Ravinder of 4 Jat unit, died in the war, said she was overcome with emotion at the event. "When I see other soldiers in uniform, I feel they are like my sons too. And standing here watching the peaks we reclaimed in the Kargil war, I feel very proud of my son and his service to the nation," she told PTI.
In the afternoon, a Gauravmaya Sanskriti event was organised at Vishwanathan Stadium in Dras, with the General Officer Commanding-in-Chief, Northern Command, in attendance. The cultural programme celebrated patriotism, India's cultural heritage, and the courage and professionalism of the Army.
It included a motorcycle display by the Shwet Ashw Motorcycle Riders, a display of India's combat drone capabilities, and the participation of robotic mules. The Army also hosted a Vijay Bhoj at the 16 Grenadiers Officers' Mess to mark the success of Operation Vijay.
The events are being held to commemorate India's victory in the battles fought on the icy heights of Kargil during the nearly three-month conflict and to pay homage to the fallen soldiers. Sunday's programme will also include the Shradhanjali Samaroh, where Singh and the Army chief will pay tribute in the presence of senior officers, Kargil war veterans, next of kin, civil dignitaries and serving soldiers.
