headline: EC extends electoral roll revision deadlines in Odisha, Telangana
full_text:
EC extends electoral roll revision deadlines in Odisha, Telangana
The SIR exercise is aimed at updating electoral rolls through extensive field verification, scrutiny of voter records and the settlement of claims
The Election Commission of India (ECI) has extended the schedule for the ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Odisha and Telangana after the two states sought additional time to complete different stages of the exercise, according to official communications issued on Friday.
In Odisha, the ECI has pushed back the deadline for filing claims and objections by 15 days to August 19 from the earlier August 4, while the disposal of claims and objections will now continue until September 17. The final electoral roll will be published on September 21.
The ECI said it revised the schedule after considering a request from the Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) of Odisha, conveyed through a letter dated July 30. The extension applies to the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls with July 1, 2026, as the qualifying date.
A separate notification issued by the ECI said the extension was granted under the proviso to Rule 12 of the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960. The draft electoral roll in Odisha had been published on July 5, and the claims and objections window originally ran from July 5 to August 4.
In Telangana, the ECI revised the entire revision calendar after the state election machinery requested additional time. House-to-house visits by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) have been extended until August 10, while the rationalisation and rearrangement of polling stations will also be completed by that date. The draft electoral roll will now be published on August 17.
Also Read:SIR clears a legal hurdle
The period for filing claims and objections in Telangana will run from August 17 to September 16, while their disposal has been scheduled until October 15. The final electoral roll will be published on October 19. The revision in Telangana is being carried out with October 1, 2026, as the qualifying date.
The ECI said the revised schedule followed a request from the Telangana CEO made through a letter dated July 30 and referred to its earlier orders issued on May 14 and July 15 regarding the revision programme.
The SIR exercise is aimed at updating electoral rolls through extensive field verification, scrutiny of voter records and the settlement of claims and objections before the rolls are finalised. The revision is part of the ECI’s broader effort to improve the accuracy of electoral rolls ahead of future elections.
The extension is expected to provide election machinery in both states additional time to complete door-to-door verification and other preparatory work without altering the overall timeline for publication of the final electoral rolls in early October.

headline: I am back: Taslima Nasrin renews free speech call in first public appearance
full_text:
I am back: Taslima Nasrin renews free speech call in first public appearance
Taslima Nasrin returned to Kolkata for her first public address in the city since 2007. She used the occasion to defend free speech, secularism and equal rights while reflecting on exile.
Bangladeshi author Taslima Nasrin returned to Kolkata after a gap of 19 years on Friday, describing the moment as the recovery of "a chapter of my lost life" while delivering a forceful defence of free speech, secularism, women's rights and the right to criticise religious ideologies.
The event, attended by West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari, marked Nasrin's first public address in Kolkata since leaving the city in 2007. During her speech, she thanked Adhikari and the West Bengal government for ensuring her security, while stressing that her gratitude should not be mistaken for political allegiance.
Speaking at a public event in Kolkata, Nasrin reflected on decades of exile from both Bangladesh and West Bengal, saying her return was more than a personal milestone. She called it a reminder that "closed doors do not remain closed forever" and said the day represented a victory of free thought over fear and censorship.
"I have not just returned to a city. I have returned to a chapter of my lost life," she said, adding that she was overwhelmed by the welcome she received after nearly two decades away from Kolkata.
Nasrin thanked Secular Mission chairman Osman Gani Mallick for inviting her to the city and expressed gratitude to Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari for facilitating her return and ensuring her security.
"I have not come here to speak for any political party. I have come to speak for equal rights of women, human rights, secularism, rationality, free thought and freedom of speech," she said.
RECALLING YEARS OF EXILE
The author recounted how she was forced to leave Bangladesh on August 8, 1994, after facing threats over her writings, and later had to leave Kolkata in 2007 despite not being convicted of any crime.
Describing exile as both a personal and political experience, she said the state had failed to protect writers from extremist threats.
"The state removed me from the country, but it could not remove the country from within me," she said, describing the Bengali language as her "portable homeland."
Nasrin recalled discovering Kolkata through literature, radio broadcasts and correspondence long before she first visited the city. She said poetry and literature had connected the two Bengals even when political borders divided them.
She also spoke about finding a home in Kolkata during her years in exile before being forced to leave in 2007 following threats from fundamentalist groups.
'FREEDOM OF SPEECH BELONGS TO EVERYONE'
A major part of Nasrin's address focused on freedom of expression and the dangers of governments yielding to threats from extremist groups.
She argued that exiling writers does not create lasting peace but instead strengthens those who seek to silence dissent.
"In a civilised society, the answer to one argument is another argument, the answer to a book is another book," she said, urging people to challenge ideas through debate rather than violence or censorship.
Nasrin said freedom of speech must extend even to unpopular opinions, arguing that the strength of a democracy is reflected in how safely dissenting voices can express themselves.
She also expressed hope that writers would one day no longer require police protection simply to attend events or publish their work.
CRITICISM OF RELIGIOUS FUNDAMENTALISM
Nasrin reiterated her long-held criticism of religious fundamentalism, saying she opposed all forms of extremism but had spoken most extensively about Islamic fundamentalism because it was the ideology she had experienced firsthand.
She rejected the suggestion that criticism of Islam amounted to hatred of Muslims, arguing that people deserve protection while ideologies should remain open to scrutiny.
According to Nasrin, reform within Muslim societies requires open discussion on issues including women's rights, freedom of belief and equal citizenship.
She also criticised governments that, in her view, prioritise religious pressure over constitutional rights and warned that compromising with threats only emboldens extremists.
CALLS FOR EQUALITY AND SECULARISM
The author devoted a significant portion of her speech to advocating equal rights for women and a secular state.
She argued that no religious law should deny women equality and called for legal systems to be guided by constitutional values rather than religious identity.
Nasrin also supported the idea of a common civil code based on human rights and gender equality rather than the principles of any particular religion.
She maintained that true secularism requires separating religion from state institutions, politics and education while ensuring equal rights for believers and non-believers alike.
HOPE DESPITE EXILE
Despite recalling decades of persecution, threats and displacement, Nasrin said she remained optimistic about the future.
She expressed hope that Bangladesh would one day separate religion from the state, guarantee equal rights for women and minorities, and allow writers and free thinkers to express themselves without fear.
Concluding her address, Nasrin became emotional as she reflected on returning to Kolkata after nearly two decades.
"No one can give me back those 19 years," she said. "But today's opening of the door proves that injustice can last a long time, but it is not eternal."
Calling her return a victory for freedom of speech, free thought and the affection of ordinary people, she ended with a message of gratitude to the city she once considered home.
"Today, you did not just bring me back to Kolkata," she said. "You brought me back to my lost life."

headline: Dehradun teacher dowry death: Husband, sister-in-law arrested amid outrage
full_text:
Dehradun teacher dowry death: Husband, sister-in-law arrested amid outrage
Police arrested government school teacher's husband and sister-in-law after a video allegedly detailing dowry harassment surfaced before her death in Dehradun.
Dehradun: The husband and sister-in-law of a government school teacher who was found dead under suspicious circumstances at her matrimonial home in Dehradun were arrested on Saturday in connection with her alleged dowry death, police said.
"On the basis of evidence, police arrested state secretariat official Saurabh Khatri, 36, and his sister, Surbhi Khatri alias Charu, 37, on Saturday," said Dehradun Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP) Pramendra Dobhal.
Police said the accused were arrested from their residence in Laxman Enclave in Harrawala, in Doiwala block of Dehradun.
The SSP said the incident triggered widespread outrage and drew national attention.
"During the investigation, police recorded the statements of the complainant and other witnesses. We also obtained a video that the deceased had sent to her mother before her death, in which she stated that she had been facing continuous harassment by her in-laws since her marriage," the SSP said.
"Our investigation into the matter is underway. Strict action will be taken against all culprits," he said.
Dobhal said they will request the court to ensure a speedy trial in the case.
The arrests came four days after the woman was found hanging under suspicious circumstances at her matrimonial home in Harrawala, Doiwala, on July 29.
Before her death, she recorded a video message addressed to her mother. In the video, she is heard saying through tears, "Sorry, Mummy, I am leaving like this... everything has become strange... I have been enduring this for the last six months... I cannot bear it anymore... their mindset will never change... they keep calling me cursed."
A first information report (FIR) in this regard was registered against the deceased's husband, mother-in-law Praveena Devi, and sister-in-law at Doiwala police station on July 29 under Section 80(2) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) on a complaint filed by the victim's mother, a native of Shrikot in Pauri Garhwal.
In her complaint, the deceased's mother alleged that her daughter had married Saurabh Khatri in November 2025 and was subjected to continuous mental and physical harassment by her husband, mother-in-law Praveena Devi, and sister-in-law Charu over dowry demands. She alleged that the three were responsible for her daughter's death.
Following the registration of the FIR, SSP Dobhal formed a special investigation team under Doiwala Circle Officer Vandana Verma and directed the immediate arrest of the accused.
Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA from Devprayag, Vinod Kandari, on Friday urged Chief Minister Pushkar Singh Dhami to order a high-level probe into the case.
Meanwhile, Uttarakhand State Commission for Women chairperson Kusum Kandwal has taken cognisance of the alleged harassment and the suspicious death of the newly married government school teacher, saying every effort would be made to ensure justice and that those found guilty would not be spared.
Kandwal spoke to SSP Pramendra Dobhal and Doiwala Circle Officer Vandana Verma over the phone and directed the police to conduct a fair and thorough investigation into every aspect of the case.
She said videos circulating on social media and other available evidence prima facie indicate that the victim was subjected to severe mental and physical harassment, and said that stringent legal action should be taken against all those responsible.
Kandwal also spoke to the victim's family and assured them that the commission stands with them in their fight for justice.
She said the commission would closely monitor the investigation and seek periodic progress reports from the police.
Kandwal asked women across the state not to remain silent if they face domestic violence or any form of harassment. "Enduring injustice is also a crime. Come forward and lodge a complaint without fear. The commission stands with every woman, and ensuring strict action against the guilty remains our priority," she said.

headline: Four killed in landslides as heavy rain triggers floods across Kerala
full_text:
Four killed in landslides as heavy rain triggers floods across Kerala
Idukki/Kottayam , Four people were killed while several others were rescued following separate landslides in Idukki and Kottayam districts on Saturday, as incessant heavy rain triggered floods and fresh landslides across Kerala, officials said.
The deceased was identified as Sumathi , a resident of the Adoormala area near Kudayathoor in Idukki district. Debris from a landslide struck her house in the early hours of Saturday, the district administration said.
Neighbours managed to rescue her husband, Ravi, and the couple's son, Ratheesh.
Both sustained injuries and were admitted to a hospital in Thodupuzha.
Authorities said the family's house was destroyed in the landslide.
Sumathi's body was recovered after a search operation carried out by personnel of the National Disaster Response Force , Fire and Rescue Services, police and revenue officials.
A youth died, and his mother was buried under debris in a landslide at Payyanithottam in Poonjar in Kottayam district.
The deceased is identified as Josephine , son of Johny, and his mother Rejina Johny , who were trapped under debris, officials said.
Even though Josephine was rescued, he succumbed to injuries while being shifted to the hospital.
The body of Rejina was recovered by around 10.30 am.
In another incident, a person identified as Prabhakaran Nair died after a landslide hit a house in the Vagamon area of Idukki district.
Officials said that Nair, a native of Vaikom in Kottayam, was sleeping in one of the bedrooms of his relative's house when the landslide took place.
Following an hours-long search, his body could be recovered, officials said.
Landslides and flooding were reported in various parts of the Idukki district.
At Upputhara, a parked police jeep was damaged in a landslide.
With the Pullakayar river overflowing, the Kokkayar low-level crossing has been submerged. Around six houses were inundated in the surrounding area, and the affected families were shifted to safer locations, officials said.
Heavy rain disrupted traffic at multiple locations as well.
The road between Kattappana and Vazhavara was blocked following a landslide, while rising water levels in the Chottupara stream at Vandiperiyar led to waterlogging on National Highway 183.
The road at Nellimala was also blocked, affecting vehicular movement.
Authorities have announced the opening of the shutters of minor dams in the district,
In the neighbouring Kottayam district, heavy rain triggered widespread flooding in Erattupetta, Kanjirappally, Koottickal and Erumeli, inundating residential areas, disrupting traffic and prompting large-scale rescue operations.
Four houses were damaged at Teekoy village following the landslide but residents managed to escape unhurt, officials said.
Erattupetta town witnessed a sudden rise in water levels overnight, forcing authorities to halt vehicular traffic.
Several houses in Erattupetta, including those in Nadakkal and Murikkoly, were inundated.
Rescue personnel, assisted by locals, evacuated people stranded on the upper floors of their homes to safer locations. Traffic in the area remained completely disrupted, according to officials.
In Koottickal and Mundakkayam, water levels continued to rise after the Manimala and Pullakayar rivers overflowed. The Koottickal causeway and low-level crossing were submerged, while water entered several houses.
Traffic was also affected after the Mundakkayam causeway went underwater.
More landslides were reported from the hilly areas of Pathanamthitta district.
Ranni MLA Pazhakulam Madhu, in a social media post, said heavy flooding had been reported in Ranni and adjoining areas. He urged people to remain cautious as river water levels had risen to dangerous levels and said floodwaters had entered several houses and shops.
Several parts of Ranni and nearby areas are cut off following the flood, and the district administration has deployed boats to rescue people trapped in their houses, officials said.
Authorities said heavy rain, accompanied by landslides, caused a sudden rise in the water level in the Pampa river.
Relief camps have also been set up in Pathanamthitta district, officials added.
Apart from central Kerala, heavy rain was reported in the hilly areas of Kollam district.
Also, floods and minor landslides were reported in Kozhikode, Malappuram, Kannur and Palakkad districts.
Engapuzha town in Kozhikode was completely inundated following heavy rain, with water from the river overflowing into the area.
Traffic on the Wayanad ghat road has been regulated considering the possibility of landslides in the area.
A four-year-old died after falling into a waterbody in Malappuram.
The India Meteorological Department has forecast continued heavy rainfall in parts of Kerala, prompting authorities to keep rescue teams on alert and advise people in vulnerable areas to remain cautious.
The IMD issued a red alert predicting very heavy rain in Pathanamthitta, Kottayam, Idukki, Malappuram, Kozhikode, Wayanad, Kannur and Kasaragod districts.
An orange alert has been issued for Ernakulam, Thrissur and Palakkad districts.
District administrations announced holidays for educational institutions in several districts, considering the forecast of heavy rain on Saturday.

headline: NEW DELHI: A 52-year-old BSF constable who recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of an Indian UN peacekeeping contingent has been admitted to the isolation ward at the Ebola Nursing Home of Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospita...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: A 52-year-old BSF constable who recently returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo as part of an Indian UN peacekeeping contingent has been admitted to the isolation ward at the Ebola Nursing Home of Dr Ram Manohar Lohia (RML) Hospital after developing fever during mandatory quarantine, triggering Ebola surveillance protocols.The constable, who arrived in India on July 11, had been under a 21-day quarantine at the Airport Health Organisation (APHO) facility following his return from Congo, an Ebola-endemic region. On the evening of 20th day of quarantine, he developed a fever along with body aches.
As per protocol, he was shifted to the designated Ebola isolation facility at RML Hospital. His blood sample has been sent to the National Institute of Virology (NIV), Pune, for confirmatory testing. The test report is awaited.Officials said the patient is being managed in strict isolation while health authorities continue to monitor the situation. At present, the case remains suspected, and Ebola infection has not been confirmed.India follows enhanced screening and quarantine measures for personnel returning from Ebola-affected regions. Suspected cases are isolated immediately and samples are tested at designated reference laboratories before a diagnosis is confirmed.

NEW DELHI: Venture capitalist, political analyst and consultant Tehseen Poonawala has alleged that the Delhi Police has enforced a house arrest on him in relation to his protest against E20 fuel.Poonawala had previously announced that on the 1st of August he would undertake a solo walk to Gandhi Smriti, followed by maun vrat and a hunger strike to protest against the mandatory E20 ethanol policy.

The government needs to examine where the lapses are occurringâhow militants managed to come in and kill two unarmed individuals despite the presence of the Army, CRPF and police," she added.

headline: Tehseen Poonawalla claims house arrest ahead of hunger strike over E20 petrol: ‘Nitin Gadkari is scared’

Tehseen Poonawalla claims house arrest ahead of hunger strike over E20 petrol: ‘Nitin Gadkari is scared’
Tehseen Poonawalla shared a series of posts on social media showing police personnel outside his residence and claimed he had been confined to his home.
Tehseen Poonawalla, who describes himself as a political analyst and consultant, claimed on Saturday that Delhi Police had placed him under house arrest ahead of his planned protest march and hunger strike against the government's E20 petrol policy. On Friday, Poonawalla announced that he would walk to Delhi's Gandhi Smriti, where he would hold a silent protest and a hunger strike against the policy.
On Saturday, he shared a series of posts on social media showing police personnel outside his residence and claimed he had been confined to his home, while also criticising Union transport minister Nitin Gadkari.
Tehseen Poonawalla ‘put under house arrest’
In one of the videos shared on X, Poonawalla is seen questioning a police officer about how he could be detained without any official paperwork.
“Guys, Delhi Police has detained me!!! They have put me under house arrest with NO PAPERS!!” he wrote in an X post.
In another post targeting Gadkari, he wrote, “An entire battalion of Delhi Police, including women officers, has put me under house arrest! Nitin Gadkari is scared of ethanol.”
‘Orders from top’
In one post on X, Poonawalla claimed that a Delhi Police officer informed him that the force had received “orders from top to house arrest” him.
In another video he shared, the police officer can be heard saying there were “chances of law being broken” if large numbers of people gathered and joined the activist during the protest against the E20 policy.
Row over E20-blended petrol
After the Cockroach Janta Party's agitation over exam paper leaks, which led to the resignation of education minister Dharmendra Pradhan, Poonawalla has attempted to channel the outrage over E20 petrol.
The government's introduction of E20 petrol, which contains 80% petrol and 20% ethanol, has drawn strong criticism from opposition parties as well as consumer groups.
One of the main demands raised by Poonawalla and his Team Bharat, which has been leading the campaign against E20, is that 100% petrol, E5 and E10 fuel should remain available so motorists have the freedom to choose.
Nitin Gadkari defends E20 policy
On Thursday, the Union minister informed Parliament that petrol blended with 20 per cent ethanol (E20) could lower fuel economy by 2 to 6 per cent, depending on the type and age of the vehicle.
In a written reply in the Lok Sabha, Gadkari said E20 offers better acceleration, improved ride quality and around 30 per cent lower carbon emissions than E10 fuel.
Protests over E20-blended petrol
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) had earlier announced a campaign against the policy beginning this month. At the same time, transport unions in Delhi are preparing to hold a protest march against the programme.
AAP national convenor and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal said last month that the party would hold a 'National Town Hall Against E20' at the Constitution Club of India in Delhi on August 1.
"We are inviting people to join in large numbers on this platform, where we will discuss how to create pressure on the central government to withdraw E20 petrol. Experts and people who have faced problems with their vehicles are all invited," he said, adding that those willing to join virtually can send a message to 85-88-833-212.
Delhi-based transport organisations have also announced a march to Parliament on August 4 to protest against the E20 policy.
“We want to give a wake-up call to the Members of Parliament who have been sleeping on this issue, as the problems in vehicles caused by ethanol blending are being reported from across the country," Sanjay Samrat, president of the Delhi Taxi and Tourist Transporters and Tour Operators Association, said, as quoted by news agency PTI.
Meanwhile, Uttar Pradesh Congress chief Ajay Rai has reportedly written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, urging him to remove Union ministers Nitin Gadkari and Hardeep Singh Puri from their respective portfolios over the issue.

headline: The Karnataka High Court has ruled that a special provision in the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, which excludes certain estates of former royal families from the purview of being partitioned under the Act, remains valid despite abolition of privy purse...
full_text:
The Karnataka High Court has ruled that a special provision in the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, which excludes certain estates of former royal families from the purview of being partitioned under the Act, remains valid despite abolition of privy purses and royal privileges more than five decades ago through the amendments to the Constitution of India.
“Articles 291 (privy purse sums of rulers) and 362 (rights and privileges of rulers of Indian States) were only with respect to guarantees and assurances made by the Dominion of India with regard to payment of privy purse, personal rights, privileges, dignities and titles of erstwhile rulers of princely States of India and not with respect to their personal private properties and Gaddi, impartible estate,” the court said.
Justice M.G.S. Kamal passed the order while dismissing the petitions filed in 2015 by Chaduranga Kantharaj Urs, a grandson of Jayachamarajendra Wadiyar, who was the last ruler of the princely State of Mysore, and Venkatrao Y. Ghorpade and Gayatri Ghorpade, son and daughter, respectively, of Yeshwantrao Ghorpade, the erstwhile Maharaja of Sandur.
On Section 5(ii)
The petitioners had sought the deletion of Section 5(ii) from the statute book while contending that this provision has lost its relevance with the passage of time and due to the abolition of Articles 291 and 362. It has no nexus with the object which was initially sought to be achieved. Further, the very concept of Gaddi has lost its meaning and purport, the petitioners had claimed.
The petitions arose from the issues in the civil suits between members of the erstwhile Mysore and Sandur royal families over property partition as some family members, including Pramoda Devi Wadiyar, invoked Section 5(ii) to argue that certain estates inherited by a sole heir under pre-Independence agreements were impartible.
Rejecting these contentions of the petitioners, the court held that the deletion of Articles 291 and 362 and insertion of Article 363-A by the 26th amendment to the Constitution has no bearing on the validity or otherwise of Section 5(ii) of the Hindu Succession Act.
Section 5(ii) states that “provisions of the Act are not applicable to any estate which descends to a single heir by the terms of any covenant or agreement entered into by the ruler of any Indian State with the Government of India or by the terms of any enactment passed before the commencement of this Act”.
The court examined the merger agreements of the former States of Mysore and Sandur with the Government of India, and found that they separately dealt with three issues — privy purses, private properties and succession to the Gaddi. While the Constitution removed guarantees relating to privy purses and privileges through Article 363-A, it did not disturb arrangements concerning private properties or succession to the ceremonial throne, that is, the Gaddi.
Customary perspective
On relevance of Section 5(ii) of the Act, the court said that “determination of issue with regard to succession to private properties as well as to impartible estate is still a relevant subject. It may be that purport and object of Gaddi has lost its relevance but from the customary practical perspective it is still a relevant subject”.
Referring to the apex court’s verdicts, Justice Kamal made it clear that after the signing of the merger agreement and notification of certain properties as the personal private properties of rulers, only the perceived throne would devolve according to the rule of primogeniture, and not the personal private properties of the ruler.

headline: West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (August 1, 2026) said eggs would be provided twice a week to schoolchildren through a separate arrangement while inaugurating an ISKCON community kitchen that will supply mid-day meals in Kolkat...

West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari on Saturday (August 1, 2026) said eggs would be provided twice a week to schoolchildren through a separate arrangement while inaugurating an ISKCON community kitchen that will supply mid-day meals in Kolkata.
The kitchen, operated by the ISKCON Annamrita Foundation, is expected to extend its services to around 2.5 lakh students across nearly 1,800 schools under the Kolkata Municipal Corporation (KMC) within the next three months.

Opposition parties, however, have claimed that the government decided to retain eggs in the scheme only after facing public pressure and the possibility of protests.

headline: Pak terror groups had Bengal CM on hit list, tried to infiltrate CJP protest: Cops
full_text:
Pak terror groups had Bengal CM on hit list, tried to infiltrate CJP protest: Cops
The investigation has also thrown up a possible link to the recent student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. According to the STF, Mondal was allegedly asked to procure police uniforms as part of an attempt by Pakistan-based operatives to create disturbances during the agitation.
West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari was on the target list of Pakistan-based operatives, the Bengal Special Task Force (STF) said on Saturday, after arresting two people over suspected links to handlers across the border.
The STF said Hamim Mondal, arrested from Burdwan, had been repeatedly asked to gather information about the Chief Minister's movements, including occasions when his security may have been lighter.
The probe has also revealed a possible link to the recent student protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. According to the STF, Mondal was asked to procure police uniforms as part of a plan to create disturbances during the agitation.
"Our state's Honourable Chief Minister was on their target list," West Bengal STF IG Gaurav Sharma said, adding that attempts had been made to gather details about Adhikari's movements.
The STF has arrested Mondal and his associate Arpita Sarkar, alleging that both were in contact with Pakistan-based handlers linked to the Shahzad Bhatti gang.
CM ADHIKARI ON TARGET LIST
According to the STF, an examination of Mondal's phone and online communications showed repeated attempts by Pakistan-based handles to obtain information about the Chief Minister.
Sharma said Mondal was asked to track Adhikari's movement patterns and identify occasions when he might be relatively unguarded.
Investigators also found references to police personnel, political leaders and other prominent individuals as possible targets, but the STF has not disclosed their identities.
"The matter is extremely sensitive, and we cannot disclose more," Sharma said, adding that further arrests could follow.
HONEY-TRAP PLOT LED STF TO THE NETWORK
The investigation began with an alleged plot to extort money from a senior politician in Howrah and honey-trap and kidnap his son.
"A few days ago, we received information about a plan to extort money from a senior politician from Howrah and abduct his son through a honey-trap," an STF officer said.
Investigators traced a suspicious social media handle to Sahibganj in Jharkhand. The handle was allegedly operated by Arpita Sarkar.
Police alerted local authorities and secured the potential targets before examining the account's communications.
The probe then led investigators to Mondal, who had earlier lived with his family in Howrah before moving to Burdwan a few months ago.
According to the STF, Sarkar and Mondal had known each other for around four years after first connecting on Instagram and later meeting in person. The agency said the two were in a relationship.
Investigators are examining whether Sarkar was to be used to lure the minister's son as part of the alleged honey-trap.
"Our investigation has revealed a specific plan to lure the minister's son into a honey-trap, followed by kidnapping and blackmail. The conspiracy was directed by Pakistan-based handlers," a senior STF officer said.
PAKISTAN HANDLERS, ENCRYPTED APPS
The STF said Mondal was in contact with several Pakistan-based handles using the aliases 'Rana', 'Uzair', 'Abid Jatt 333' and 'Hamad'.
Investigators suspect the handles are linked to the Shahzad Bhatti gang, which the STF alleged is involved in radicalisation, narco-terror activities and recruitment for extremist operations.
"After verifying them, we found out that all these handles were operating from Pakistan," Sharma said.
According to the STF, Mondal first came into contact with the handlers on Instagram before shifting conversations to encrypted messaging platforms.
"During the investigation of his mobile phone and social media chat history, we found some very serious information. He was in touch with several Pakistan-based handlers through encrypted platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram," Sharma said.
The agency said Element X and Session were also used for communication.
Investigators further claimed that Mondal had been radicalised through social media before coming into contact with operatives linked to the Shahzad Bhatti group.
FOREIGN SIM CARDS RECOVERED
The STF also said it recovered SIM cards issued in the United Kingdom and Mexico from the accused.
Investigators suspect the cards were used to communicate with handlers abroad.
"The SIM cards are suspected to have been used for encrypted communication with handlers operating from abroad and to facilitate the strengthening of sleeper cells and the terror network in different parts of the country," Sharma said.
The STF is now examining the communication trail to determine the wider extent of the alleged network and whether others in India were in contact with the same handlers.
JANTAR MANTAR PROTESTS UNDER LENS
The investigation has also turned to the recent student protests at Jantar Mantar.
According to Sharma, Mondal was asked by Pakistan-based handlers to procure police uniforms in connection with a plan to create disturbances during the agitation.
"We also noticed that in order to create some disturbance during the recent student protest at Jantar Mantar, Hamim Mondal was being asked to procure police uniforms," Sharma said.
The STF has not said whether Mondal actually obtained the uniforms or whether the alleged plan moved beyond the communication stage.
TWO ARRESTED, PROBE CONTINUES
Mondal was taken into custody on the intervening night of July 30 and 31, while Sarkar was arrested on Friday night.
Both were produced before a court in Burdwan and are being questioned over their alleged links to the Pakistan-based handlers.
Investigators are now trying to establish the role of each accused, identify others who may have been part of the network and trace its cross-border links.
Sharma said the investigation remained sensitive and indicated that more arrests could follow.

Heavy rain triggered widespread disruption across the hilly regions of Kannur district on Saturday (August 1, 2026), damaging roads, inundating houses, forcing evacuations, and prompting the authorities to impose travel and tourism restrictions.
Eight families comprising 26 people were shifted to a relief camp after floodwaters entered houses at Peratta Thottipalam in Ulikkal grama panchayat. Fire and rescue services, assisted by residents, rescued those stranded in their homes and relocated 19 adults and seven children to the relief camp.
Two persons were reported missing in separate rain-related incidents. Hanifa, 40, of Kottamchuram in Manthana village, was swept away in the Kunhirapuzha at Peravur. In another incident, Rajesh, a swimming instructor from Thiruvananthapuram, was swept away while trying to rescue a person who was stranded on a river island at Meenthulli in Pullingome village. A search is on for the two missing persons.
Traffic ban imposed

A woman, Sumathi, stranded on a river island at Thuruth in Pullingome-Kozhichal, was rescued by Fire and Rescue Services personnel and residents.

headline: Revenue Minister says Kerala prepared, situation under control despite rain havoc
full_text:
Revenue Minister says Kerala prepared, situation under control despite rain havoc
Malappuram , Kerala Revenue Minister A P Anilkumar on Saturday said the government was fully prepared to deal with landslides, flooding and other rain-related emergencies as heavy rain continued to lash several parts of the state.
Addressing reporters here, Anilkumar said relief camps had already been opened in vulnerable areas and authorities had been instructed to shift people living in high-risk locations as a precaution.
"We have already opened relief camps wherever required. Even if the intensity of rain decreases, people living in high-risk areas will be shifted to camps as a precautionary measure," he said.
The minister said weather forecasts indicated that rainfall was likely to ease in the southern districts by around noon, although heavy rain was expected to continue in northern Kerala.
"From this morning onwards, rainfall is expected to be concentrated in the northern districts. Red alerts have been issued and there is also a forecast of winds reaching up to 50 kmph. All departments have been instructed to remain on alert," he said.
Anilkumar said, on the directions of Chief Minister V D Satheesan, Civil Supplies Minister Anoop Jacob had been deputed to coordinate relief operations in the landslide-hit areas of Idukki and Kottayam.
"The Chief Minister directly instructed Minister Anoop Jacob to visit the affected areas. Following a request from Kottayam district, directions were also issued to deploy NDRF personnel immediately," he said.
The minister said the government had begun advance preparations after receiving weather forecasts two days ago warning of five days of continuous rain.
"Based on the forecast, meetings of district collectors, the Revenue Secretary and disaster management officials were convened. Instructions were issued to identify vulnerable areas, keep relief camps ready and ensure that rescue teams remained on standby," he said.
Another meeting of district collectors was scheduled on Saturday to review the evolving situation, he added.
The minister said minor landslides and traffic disruptions had been reported from several districts, including Malappuram, where debris had fallen near the Koodoor Nooradi bridge.
"The road has been cleared and traffic restored. District administrations have been instructed to remove mud and debris immediately wherever roads are blocked so that traffic can resume without delay," he said.
Anilkumar said the government was treating every rain-related incident with utmost seriousness and had taken all possible precautions to prevent further loss of life.
Giving an update on casualties, the minister said two deaths had been confirmed in Idukki district.
"The victims are 65-year-old Sumathi of Kudayathoor, who died in the Adoormala landslide, and 77-year-old Prabhakaran of Kolahalamedu near Vagamon, who was killed after the earth caved in on him," he said.

headline: The lifting of trawling ban off the Kerala’s coast has failed to bring the much-anticipated cheer in the fishing sector as the shores remained inactive, thanks to inclement weather.

The lifting of trawling ban off the Kerala’s coast has failed to bring the much-anticipated cheer in the fishing sector as the shores remained inactive, thanks to inclement weather.
Though hundreds of trawlnet boats and workers, including migrant workers, had geared up to venture out into the deep sea for fishing after the 52-day break in the early hours of Saturday (August 1, 2026), most vessel operators had to postpone their plans following a warning from the India Meteorological department (IMD). The IMD had warned fishers against venturing out into the sea off Kerala, Karnataka, and Lakshadweep on Friday (July 31, 2026) and Saturday in view of possible gusty winds and inclement weather.
A section of boats went to the sea from harbours in Kochi despite the warning. However, a few of them returned soon as the weather was not favourable. A few large vessels, around 20 metres long, which proceeded to sail were yet to return.
“More boats will go to the sea in the coming days from Kalamukku harbour at Vypeen. In the initial days, we are expecting a good catch of pink perch,” P.P. Gireesh, secretary, Trawlnet Boat Owners Association, said.
The traditional fishing sector, meanwhile, remained disappointed as the trawling ban period did not help it much. Traditional and artisanal fishers expect the ban period to bring a bounty to them as only they are legally permitted to fish in nearshore waters while mechanised trawlers remain ashore.
“This time, the catch was visibly poor, mainly due to dry weather conditions. The lack of expected income has pushed the traditional fisherfolk into a financial crisis as it has affected their financial plans, including repaying loans availed to mend their boats,” Yesudas Parappilly, district secretary, Matsyathozhilali Union (CITU), said. He urged the government to conduct a detailed study into the traditional fisherfolk’s plight and announce a package for them.

headline: DKS defers talks with Vijay amid Cauvery protests; Tamil Nadu to move Supreme Court

DKS defers talks with Vijay amid Cauvery protests; Tamil Nadu to move Supreme Court
DKS said the current atmosphere was not conducive for talks and that he would seek another date for discussions.
Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar on Friday announced the postponement of his August 3 meeting with his Tamil Nadu counterpart, C Joseph Vijay amid protests in the state over the Cauvery water-sharing dispute. He said the current atmosphere was not conducive for talks and that he would seek another date for discussions. The meeting had been scheduled at Vijay’s initiative.
“I had requested to visit Tamil Nadu, but the [previous] DMK [Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam] government had not given permission. Later, elections took place, and the government changed. Now Vijay has said that he will come to Karnataka with his team. In such a situation, the developments around the protests are not giving us confidence,” Shivakumar said.

He said the meeting should take place in a more cordial environment. “We should create an opportunity to resolve this issue through cordiality. If the problem is resolved, it will benefit them as well as us. The atmosphere is not good now, so I will discuss requesting the Tamil Nadu chief minister to postpone our meeting for a few days,” he said.
The decision came as farmers and Kannada organisations staged protests against the Cauvery Water Management Authority’s (CWMA) rejection of Karnataka’s appeal against an order directing it to release 3,500 cusecs of water daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.
Protesters tore posters of Vijay’s film Jananayagan and forced some theatres to stop screenings. BJP leaders, including state president B Y Vijayendra, were taken into preventive custody while marching towards the Krishna Raja Sagar (KRS) dam, officials aware of the matter said.
The party also threatened to boycott the all-party meeting convened by Shivakumar on August 2 if the state government did not assure that Cauvery water would not be released to Tamil Nadu. Leaders of Opposition R Ashoka and Chalavadi Narayanaswamy, along with MLC C T Ravi, were among those detained, the officials said.
Meanwhile, Tamil Nadu law minister R Nirmal Kumar said the state would move the Supreme Court to secure its share of Cauvery water. “Legally, we need to get the required water through the Supreme Court,” he said, adding that Karnataka had repeatedly failed to release water despite directions from the authority.
Kumar said Vijay was consulting legal experts and stakeholders and would announce the state’s legal strategy within a week. “The government is currently evaluating multiple avenues, which include approaching the apex court, pushing for a tribunal, conducting inter-state negotiations, or exerting pressure on the Union government,” he said.
Shivakumar said both states were trying to protect their interests and should work towards a solution through dialogue. “If they want to protect the interests of their state, we also want to protect the interests of our state. We are discussing whether this can be resolved through cordiality,” he said.
He said Karnataka had requested CWMA to reduce the quantity, defer the decision and give the state more time, but its appeal was rejected. “An all-party meeting has been called on August 2 to decide what should be done next. A decision will be taken after the meeting,” Shivakumar said.
Shivakumar said Tamil Nadu sought 9.94 TMC of water, while the recommendation was roughly half that quantity. He added that drinking water supplies would remain protected. “There will be no problem with drinking water. It requires 40 TMC of water, of which 36 TMC is required for drinking and 4 TMC may be lost through evaporation. Any remaining surplus water during a distress situation will be distributed based on the water sharing formula.”

Mumbai, NCP leader Supriya Sule on Saturday demanded a time-bound SIT probe into irregularities in competitive examinations and the use of police force against protesting students, calling for an all-party meeting or a joint parliamentary committee to discuss reforms in the education system.

headline: New Delhi: Challenged by BJP MPs to authenticate his claim that the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh supported the Emergency, Congress MP Jairam Ramesh has submitted to the Rajya Sabha Chairperson three letters written in 1975 by then Sangh chief Balasahe...
full_text:
New Delhi: Challenged by BJP MPs to authenticate his claim that the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh supported the Emergency, Congress MP Jairam Ramesh has submitted to the Rajya Sabha Chairperson three letters written in 1975 by then Sangh chief Balasaheb Deoras—which, he claims, vindicate his stand.
“…The ban on RSS may be lifted and the RSS and its volunteers may participate in the development of plans which are being implemented in all the spheres in the country,” reads an appeal made by Deoras in one of the letters.
Ramesh has submitted three letters by Deoras—two to then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi and one to Acharya Vinoba Bhave.
Deoras had appealed to Gandhi to lift the ban on RSS. He had also congratulated Gandhi after the Supreme Court had upheld the validity of her 1971 election, writing: “Let me congratulate you as five judges of the Supreme Court have declared the validity of your election.”
The letters indicate that the tone and tenor of the correspondence was accommodative towards the government. Deoras had repeatedly appealed for the ban on RSS to be lifted, for its jailed volunteers to be released, and for the organisation to be allowed to contribute to government programmes.
The RSS was banned after Emergency was declared in 1975 as the Indira Gandhi government accused the organisation of opposing it and threatening law and order. The RSS had supported the Jayaprakash (JP) movement, which had called for nationwide protests and demanded Gandhi’s resignation after she was found guilty of electoral malpractice by the Allahabad High Court—a ruling that was later overturned by the Supreme Court.
Congress has cited the letters to argue that they reflect an accommodative approach by RSS leadership towards the Indira Gandhi government. The BJP and the RSS have, however, maintained that the letters were written to seek the release of jailed volunteers and the withdrawal of the ban on the organisation, rather than as an endorsement of the Emergency itself.
Ramesh, Congress general secretary (communications), Friday submitted to Rajya Sabha Chairman Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan what he described as “authenticated historical documents” after BJP MPs challenged him to substantiate his assertion that the then RSS chief had written to former Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in “support” of the Emergency.
In a covering letter dated 31 July, Ramesh wrote that the issue had arisen during an exchange in the House the previous evening. “Yesterday evening I had made a response to a statement made by the Union Minister of Parliamentary Affairs. BJP MPs challenged me to authenticate my assertion that the RSS Chief had written to Indira Gandhi in support of the Emergency. I attach herewith my authentication for the records—2 letters to Indira Gandhi and 1 letter to Acharya Vinoba Bhave.”
The documents include authenticated extracts from Five Headed Monster: A Factual Narrative of the Genesis of Janata Party, a 1978 book by Brahm Dutt reproducing three letters attributed to Deoras during the Emergency. The pages attached by Ramesh carry his signature certifying them as authenticated copies.
The first letter, dated 22 August 1975, was written from Yerwada Central Jail after RSS’s ban. Referring to Indira Gandhi’s Independence Day address, Deoras had described it as “suitable for the occasion and well balanced”. Defending the RSS against the allegations levelled, he had written, “The work of RSS lies extended to every nook and corner of the whole of India, it is necessary to properly utilise such power of the Sangh for the upliftment of our country.”
He had also appealed for the ban on the RSS to be lifted and written that if Gandhi thought it proper, “my meeting with you will be a source of pleasure to me.”
In the second letter, dated 10 November 1975, Deoras had congratulated Gandhi after the Supreme Court had upheld the validity of her election. He had again appealed for withdrawal of the ban on RSS, seeking to distance the organisation from the Jayaprakash Narayan movement, and saying that the Sangh had “no connection with these movements”.
The third letter, addressed to Acharya Vinoba Bhave, urged him to remove the prime minister’s “wrong impression” of the RSS, so that “the ban on RSS may be lifted and the RSS and its volunteers may participate in the development of plans which are being implemented in all the spheres in the country”.

headline: E20 petrol saved consumers nearly ₹30 per litre during crude price spike: Govt
full_text:
E20 petrol saved consumers nearly ₹30 per litre during crude price spike: Govt
The clarification comes as the Centre introduced the use of E20 petrol, a move that has faced criticism from opposition parties and consumer groups.
The use of E20 petrol resulted in savings of nearly ₹30 per litre for consumers at the height of the global crude oil crisis, the petroleum ministry said in an official release issued on Friday.
It also said that petrol prices in Delhi could have risen to ₹125 per litre if oil marketing companies had not mixed ethanol with petrol when global crude oil prices climbed to nearly US$135 per barrel.
The clarification from the petroleum ministry comes as the Centre introduced the use of E20 petrol, which contains 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent petrol, a move that has faced criticism from opposition parties and consumer groups.
ALSO READ | How FCI rice is driving govt’s ethanol push
₹30 per litre in savings, says govt
The government said the use of E20 petrol not only helped prevent a steeper increase in retail fuel prices during the surge in crude oil prices but also resulted in savings of nearly ₹30 per litre for consumers at the height of the crisis.
The ministry also dismissed claims that foodgrain meant for poor families was being diverted for ethanol production, or that subsidised rice supplied by the food corporation of India (FCI) was being used for the programme.
"The purpose of ethanol blending is to reduce India's dependence on imported crude oil, which still meets nearly 88 per cent of the country's oil requirement. It is an insurance policy against global oil shocks and not a day-to-day price competition," the release said.
ALSO READ | In Lok Sabha, Centre backs E20, says no proof of adverse impacts
Petrol prices in Delhi would have climbed to ₹125/litre: Govt
The petroleum ministry said in the release that the ethanol-blended petrol (EBP) programme aims to improve “India's energy security, reduce dependence on imported crude oil and support farmers while safeguarding food security”.
It said that when the Indian crude oil basket touched around US$135 per barrel, the estimated price of petrol in Delhi, without ethanol blending, would have been close to ₹125 per litre.
The ministry said consumers instead paid ₹94.77 per litre because one-fifth of every litre consisted of ethanol produced within the country and purchased at fixed prices agreed in advance.
Outrage over ethanol-blended petrol
The rollout of E20 petrol, made up of 80 per cent petrol and 20 per cent ethanol, has received backlash from opposition parties and several consumer groups, who have expressed concern about its effect on older vehicles not built to run on fuel containing 20 per cent ethanol.
Those opposing the policy have questioned whether every vehicle can safely use E20 fuel. They have also raised concerns about lower fuel efficiency and increased maintenance costs, and asked who would be responsible if engine or fuel-system issues occur.
The Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) began a campaign against the policy on Saturday. Meanwhile, transport unions in Delhi are planning a protest march against the programme.
AAP national convenor and former Delhi chief minister Arvind Kejriwal, while addressing the 'National Town Hall Against E20' at the Constitution Club of India in Delhi on Saturday, demanded that petrol pumps offer both E20 and pure petrol, E20 be sold at a lower price than pure petrol, and the price of petrol be brought below ₹84/litre.

The vibrancy of Telugu language, culture and traditions came alive in Baltimore, Maryland, on Friday as thousands of Telugu people from across the United States gathered for the 19th American Telugu Association (ATA) conference, celebrating their shared heritage while strengthening ties with their roots.
The three-day convention is bringing together Telugu families settled in the U.S. along with their children born and raised in America, offering them an opportunity to reconnect with their cultural identity through traditional dance, music and authentic Telugu cuisine.
The conference was inaugurated in the presence of Maryland Lieutenant Governor Aruna Miller, a Telugu born in Hyderabad, lending a special connect to the celebrations.
A host of dignitaries from India attended the inaugural session, including Telangana Legislative Council Chairman Gutta Sukhender Reddy, Tourism Minister Jupally Krishna Rao, MLAs T. Rammohan Reddy, Yennem Srinivas Reddy and Manohar Reddy, besides Telangana BJP president N. Ramchander Rao.
The event also witnessed the presence of noted film personalities, including veteran actor Rajendra Prasad and playback singer Sunitha Upadrashta, who added glamour to the opening ceremony. Organisers said several more film personalities would participate in the remaining sessions of the conference.
Telangana Deputy Chief Minister Mallu Bhatti Vikramarka is scheduled to join the celebrations on Saturday.
Addressing the gathering, Mr. Sukhender Reddy lauded the Telugu diaspora for preserving their language and culture despite living abroad and for contributing to the development of both Telugu States.
The ATA also presented Lifetime Achievement Awards and other honours to distinguished individuals for their contributions in diverse fields, including community service, science and technology, performing arts, sports, medicine, entrepreneurship, business and journalism. Among the awardees was Ravikanth Reddy Ramasayam, who was honoured for excellence in journalism.
Other recipients included Kiran Chukkapalli, Sashi Gundala, Dr. Ravinder Regatte, Dr. Ramamohana Reddy Appannagari, Sudheer Rao, Raghunandan Nallanchakravarthula, Ashok Chintakunta, Madhavi Soleti, Akshara Devalua, Nitish Reddy Sudini, Sai Teja Reddy Mukkamalla, Esha Nagireddy, Dr. Ramya Chitrangada, Bala Reddy Indurthi, Dr. Vandana Devalapalli, Yennem Srinivas Reddy, Narsimha Reddy Koppula, Ram Matiapalli, Bhanu, Ram Annadi and Goutham Amarneni.
ATA president Jayanth Challa, national coordinator Sharath Vemula, co-coordinator Zeenath Kundar, convenor Sridhar Banala and several past presidents attended the inaugural session.
Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Sharath Vemula said ATA’s contribution to the Telugu community in the United States over the last 38 years had been unparalleled. He said the association had played a vital role in bringing together Telugu families while helping younger generations born in the U.S. reconnect with their language, culture and traditions.

headline: Faridabad woman kills lover after he refuses to marry her
full_text:
Faridabad woman kills lover after he refuses to marry her
The accused, Anita, who is from Satna village in Madhya Pradesh's Rewa district, was produced before a city court on Saturday and sent to two days of police custody. Police said she told them during questioning that she had been asking Sadaqat to marry her, but he kept delaying it.
A 33-year-old woman has been arrested for allegedly killing her lover, a house painter in Faridabad, after he resisted her pressure to marry her, police said on Saturday. The man’s decomposed body was found in her rented room in Anangpur village a day before her arrest.
The accused, Anita, who is from Satna village in Madhya Pradesh’s Rewa district, was produced before a city court on Saturday and sent to two days of police custody. Police said she told them during questioning that she had been asking Sadaqat to marry her, but he kept delaying it.
According to police, Anita allegedly called Sadaqat to her room on July 25 and gave him alcohol. Late that night, when he was drunk and asleep, she allegedly slit his throat with a knife, killed him, locked the room from outside and fled.
Police said Anita and Sadaqat worked in a gated residential society in Faridabad. He worked as a house painter and she as a cleaner. Both had been married earlier, and Anita had been abandoned by her husband.
The two had earlier been sharing a room in Anangpur village, but the landlord asked Anita to vacate it after he learnt about their relationship. Around 15 days ago, she rented another room in Domka Mohalla of Anangpur village, where Sadaqat would often visit her.
In the complaint, Sadaqat’s brother Nazakat Ali said he suspected Anita of being behind the murder. He alleged that on July 23, Sadaqat left home saying he was going to Aligarh but did not return, and his mobile phone later became unreachable. When Nazakat contacted Anita, she allegedly denied that Sadaqat had visited her.
Police said they received information on Thursday about a body lying in a house in Domka Mohalla. When a team reached the spot, it found the body of Sadaqat, who was from Rampur Shahpur in Uttar Pradesh’s Aligarh district.
The investigation found that he had been murdered after his throat was slit with a sharp-edged weapon.
Based on Nazakat’s complaint, an FIR for murder was registered against Anita at Surajkund police station, and she was arrested on Friday night. "Our police team cracked the case within hours and arrested the accused woman. We are questioning the accused woman after taking her on police remand," a Faridabad Police spokesperson said.
Police are continuing their investigation into the case after arresting Anita, who they say confessed that the alleged murder followed a dispute over marriage.

headline: Unable to eliminate extortion despite being in power: Bengal BJP chief's admission
full_text:
Unable to eliminate extortion despite being in power: Bengal BJP chief's admission
BJP state president Samik Bhattacharya said West Bengal could reverse the flight of capital only if partisan politics was kept out of business, and announced that the government would soon hold consultations before finalising a new industrial policy.
The BJP has not yet been able to eliminate extortion in West Bengal despite coming to power in the state, the party's state president Samik Bhattacharya said on Saturday, while admitting that a section within his own party was showing the same tendencies.
He said the government had been in office for only two months and that not everything had changed with the change in power.
Bhattacharya also warned party workers, supporters and newly inducted leaders against hurling eggs at opposition leaders, saying such acts could rebound on those now indulging in them. He said Bengal could reverse the flight of capital only if partisan politics was kept out of business, and announced that the government would soon hold consultations before finalising a new industrial policy.
Addressing the 'Udyami Samagam' event at the IIT Kharagpur Research Park in Rajarhat on the outskirts of Kolkata, Bhattacharya said, "Our government has come to power only two months ago. We have not been able to solve all problems. If I say on behalf of my party that we have been able to eradicate extortion from everywhere, then I will be making a false claim. There are deviations. People had become accustomed to passing through a system of making easy money through syndicates. Not everything has changed with the change in state power."
He added, "Some joined the ruling party within four hours, others had dormant wishes that have now surfaced. We are trying to control such tendencies within the party. Our CM Suvendu Adhikari is also trying to apply strict brakes on such tendencies." Bhattacharya said a section of workers in the party was trying to enter every sector, from education and health to business, with political flags.
Stressing the need to clean up the business environment, he said Bengal was at a point where it could move away from its difficult industrial past.
"We must keep partisan politics out of this system. We have become residents of a political society in West Bengal. We need freedom from it. Till such time Bengal is able to come out of the culture of infiltration of politics in every sphere of life, no government can bring about its effective change and attract investment," he said.
"We are making an earnest effort to build a government for West Bengal and not a BJP government," he added.
Bhattacharya said the party had achieved only partial success. "We haven't been able to provide you with an error-free atmosphere, but we have largely been able to deliver an investment climate that is fear-free. To set up a company, you can now buy your own brick, cement and sand. If someone approaches you, use the phone. He will either leave your premises or find himself inside lock up," he said.
Calling the BJP government in Bengal one that had "stepped into its adolescence", he said the business community should point out mistakes directly and protest if needed. "No system can function or be made to live for long by quashing protests. All autocracies across the world inevitably fall. If someone from our side sports a body language of having 207 MLAs and hits the road, then the consequence will be disastrous," he said.
He added, "The unwarranted egg-therapy we see now can turn on its head and start falling on the other side as well. All, including those in my party, must understand that. Those Sanatanis who have suddenly found a place in our party and are harbouring aspirations for influence and advantage must also remain careful because the trajectory of those eggs can change in no time."
Referring to the government's move to scrap the Urban Land Ceiling Act to unlock developable land and attract large-scale industrial and real estate investment, Bhattacharya said the next step would be wider consultation. "
Within the next few weeks, the government will sit in a meeting with the investors in this state, those who have set up start-ups, professors in different universities and our industrialists before drawing up our new industrial policy," he said.
Bhattacharya said the government was trying to curb extortionary practices, keep politics out of commerce and build conditions for investment, while also warning his own party against excesses.

headline: Supreme Court judge's 'ant' remark during discussion on judicial transparency
full_text:
Supreme Court judge's 'ant' remark during discussion on judicial transparency
Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said that not giving reasons for judicial appointments did a disservice to outstanding judges whose work and achievements deserved to be in the public domain.
Supreme Court Justice Ujjal Bhuyan has called for greater transparency in the collegium system, arguing that withholding reasons for judicial appointments not only denies deserving judges due recognition but could also allow individuals who make "wholly unconstitutional" remarks to enter the judiciary.
Speaking during a panel discussion to mark the launch of the Judicial Transparency Index by the Vidhi Centre for Legal Policy, Justice Bhuyan said the collegium should explain the reasons behind its recommendations and questioned why judicial appointments should be insulated from informed public debate.
"By withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as 'ants' and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional and contrary to the values of the Constitution," he said during the panel discussion.
Justice Bhuyan said that not giving reasons for judicial appointments did a disservice to outstanding judges whose work and achievements deserved to be in the public domain.
He argued that greater disclosure and discussion around appointments could help prevent the elevation of individuals whose views may be at odds with constitutional values.
"To prevent the elevation of such individuals, there should be discussion. There should be reasons explaining what happened. What harm is caused if there is informed public debate on such decisions?" Justice Bhuyan said.
'NEED GREATER TRANSPARENCY IN APPOINTMENTS'
Separately, in his address to the gathering, Justice Bhuyan made a broader case for greater transparency in the process of appointing and transferring judges.
He pointed out that deliberations over the elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential, reasons for rejecting or deferring recommendations are rarely disclosed in full, and the criteria applied by the collegium are not codified in any publicly accessible document.
Justice Bhuyan also drew attention to what he described as a recent shift in Supreme Court collegium statements.
"I have seen that the last three statements of the Supreme Court collegium do not contain any reason at all for recommending elevation as opposed to the earlier statements where each of the recommendations were supported by some reason," he said.
Justice Bhuyan described this as a "reflexive gap", pointing to the contrast between a judiciary that has embraced greater openness in its adjudicative role and one that remains more guarded about its own institutional processes.
"Deliberations over the elevation and transfer of judges remain confidential; reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full; and the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly accessible instrument comparable to the Memorandum of Procedure's own limited disclosure," he said.
Justice Bhuyan also raised the broader question of accountability within the judiciary.
"Every legal system that claims to administer justice rather than merely dispense power must answer an old and uncomfortable question: who watches the watchmen?" he said.
WHY THE COLLEGIUM SYSTEM HAS BEEN CONTROVERSIAL
The Supreme Court collegium system remains one of the most debated aspects of India's judiciary.
Under the system, the Chief Justice of India and a group of senior Supreme Court judges recommend appointments and transfers in the higher judiciary. The government can seek reconsideration of a recommendation, but its role in the process is limited.
Critics have long argued that the collegium lacks transparency, with little public information available on why particular candidates are selected, rejected or deferred. Questions have also been raised over the absence of clearly codified and publicly accessible criteria governing appointments.
The judiciary, however, has consistently defended the system as necessary to protect judicial independence and insulate appointments from executive interference.
The issue has also repeatedly led to friction between the judiciary and the government. Parliament sought to replace the collegium with the National Judicial Appointments Commission (NJAC), but the Supreme Court struck down the law in 2015, holding that it undermined judicial independence.
Former Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud had also defended the collegium system in 2024, saying efforts were being made to improve transparency in the appointment process.
In an interview with PTI, he said it was easy to criticise the system, but maintained that the collegium made every effort to ensure that the required process of consultation was followed before a judge was appointed.

Nathula pass border trade resumes after 6 years; traders seek expansion of goods list
