Nathula Border gate (ANI image)
Border trade through the Nathula Pass in East Sikkim, a key segment of the ancient Silk Route connecting India and China, resumed on Saturday after remaining suspended for nearly six years. A formal reopening ceremony was held at Nathula, with officials from both countries participating in the event.The trade route had remained closed since 2020 due to the Covid-19 pandemic and subsequent border tensions between India and China.Welcoming the resumption of trade, Anil Gupta, General Secretary of the Indo-China Nathula Border Traders Welfare Association, thanked Sikkim Chief Minister Prem Singh Tamang for his efforts in facilitating the reopening.
"I extend heartfelt thanks to our Chief Minister, Prem Singh Tamang. This has become possible today solely due to his efforts. For traders who had outstanding dues or stocks stranded on the other side, this is a time of great joy, and everyone is happy," Gupta said.
Traders seek expansion of trade list
While welcoming the resumption of trade, Gupta said the existing list of goods permitted through Nathula needs to be updated to reflect present-day commercial needs.
"The current trading list includes items like horses, sheep and general goods. We believe industrial products relevant to today's times should be included. We have submitted a formal request to the department, and we are hopeful that the government will take a very positive view of this," he said.
Under the existing arrangement, only a limited list of traditional goods is allowed to be traded through the border route. Traders have long been seeking the inclusion of industrial and other commercially relevant products.
Around 300 traders await passes
Gupta said preparations for the resumption of trade were underway, with authorities verifying applications submitted by traders."Around five hundred traders collected forms, and approximately three hundred have submitted them. Verification is underway, and we hope all traders will receive their passes very soon," he said.
The reopening is expected to revive economic activity in the border region and provide relief to traders whose businesses had been affected by the prolonged suspension of cross-border trade. Nathula, located in East Sikkim, is one of the few officially designated border trading points between India and China and has historically served as an important corridor on the ancient Silk Route.

headline: PM Modi has failed, says Shehzad after dropping BJP from X bio. There's a twist
full_text:
PM Modi has failed, says Shehzad after dropping BJP from X bio. There's a twist
Instead of behaving like a dictator, PM Modi appealed to society, the police and everyone else to forgive the students who used abusive language against him, Shehzad Poonawalla said as he spoke of the PM's "failure".
BJP leader Shehzad Poonawalla on Saturday took a swipe at Prime Minister Narendra Modi's critics, saying the Prime Minister had "failed" to become a dictator, and contrasted PM Modi's response to the recent NEET protest controversy with what he called the Congress's and opposition-ruled states' record on dissent. His remarks came just a day after he updated his X account and dropped "BJP national spokesperson" from his bio.
In a video posted on X, Poonawalla said he was "totally disappointed" with PM Modi, adding sarcastically, "Twelve years have passed, and he is a failure. He doesn't even know how to become a proper dictator."
The remark came a day after Prime Minister Modi released a video message urging people to forgive the students who had allegedly used abusive language against him and his late mother during the NEET protests at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
Instead of behaving like a dictator, Poonawalla said, PM Modi had appealed to society, the police and everyone else to forgive the students.
"Last night he released a video and, regarding the children who used abusive language against constitutional authorities and his late mother, he said, 'They are mischievous children, forgive them.' He appealed to society, to the police and to everyone to forgive them," Poonawalla said.
The BJP leader then targeted Congress leader Rahul Gandhi, saying, "Rahul Gandhi is a descendant of Indira Gandhi and Jawaharlal Nehru. Learn from them what a real dictatorship is, what a real Emergency is, Modi ji."
He alleged that while the Modi government had withdrawn cases against student protesters after accepting their demands, Congress governments were registering cases over social media posts and protests.
Referring to recent incidents, Poonawalla claimed that cases had been registered in Kerala against Instagram users for allegedly insulting Rahul Gandhi. He also referred to police action in Karnataka over a poster and against a rap artist.
Poonawalla went on to invoke the Congress's political history, alleging that it was Jawaharlal Nehru who curtailed freedom of speech and that Indira Gandhi imposed the Emergency, jailed opposition leaders and suppressed dissent.
He also referred to the Assam movement, the Navnirman movement and the Anna Hazare-led anti-corruption agitation, alleging that thousands of protesters had been jailed during those periods.
Addressing PM Modi again, Poonawalla said, "Today, the children are using abusive language and you're saying, 'They are kids, mistakes happen. We should help them get to the right path.' But Rahul ji, like a real dictator, is getting cases filed over an Instagram post."
He ended his remarks with another jibe at the Prime Minister's critics: "Modi ji, it has been 12 years. You are unable to become a dictator. You have dashed the hopes of all these Left liberals. You have failed."
PM'S APPEAL TO FORGIVE STUDENTS
In a late-night video on Friday, Prime Minister Modi said it pained him that even his late mother had been subjected to "filthy abuses" during the NEET protests, but urged society not to punish the students.
Calling them "misguided children", Modi appealed to people to forgive them and help them "learn from their mistakes".
"The children are ours. It is our responsibility to show them the correct path," the Prime Minister said, adding that dragging them to court or publicly shaming them would not solve the problem.
The remarks came days after the 36-day agitation led by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) ended following the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan and the government's acceptance of the protesters' key demands.
The protests over alleged irregularities in the NEET examination had drawn nationwide support from opposition parties, many of whose leaders repeatedly accused the Modi government of acting in a "dictatorial" manner over the police crackdown on demonstrators. Several Opposition leaders including AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi, Shiv Sena (UBT) president Uddhav Thackeray, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge had used the term "dictator" while criticising the government's handling of the agitation.
Shehzad Poonawalla’s remark on Saturday was in response to the Opposition’s criticism of the PM-Modi led government.

headline: Delhi High Court transfers six judges to newly set up exclusive NIA courts
full_text:
Delhi High Court transfers six judges to newly set up exclusive NIA courts
The Delhi High Court has transferred 151 judicial officers and posted 13 judges to newly created special courts at Rouse Avenue. The move shifts all NIA trials from Patiala House and reshuffles several high-profile judicial assignments.
The Delhi High Court on Saturday transferred 151 judicial officers across the capital, including 13 judges who will take charge of newly established Special Exclusive Courts for National Investigation Agency (NIA), Maharashtra Control of Organised Crime Act (MCOCA) and Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act cases at the Rouse Avenue Court Complex.
According to the High Court's transfer order, six judges—Anu Grover Baliga, Vikas Dhull, Prashant Sharma, Amit Bansal, Kiran Bansal and Pulastya Pramachala—have been posted as Special Exclusive NIA judges. They will assume charge from August 4.
The newly constructed NIA courtrooms at Rouse Avenue are scheduled to be inaugurated on Monday, marking the shift of all NIA trials from Patiala House Courts to the new judicial complex.
In addition to the NIA courts, dedicated MCOCA and NDPS courts have also been established at Rouse Avenue. Four judges—Sandeep Yadav, Anuradha Shukla, Devendra Kumar Sharma and Bhupinder Singh—have been posted as Special Exclusive NDPS judges, while Gaurav Rao, Gagandeep Singh and Surbhi Sharma Vats have been appointed as Special Exclusive MCOCA judges.
CHANGES IN JUDICIAL ASSIGNMENTS
The restructuring also brings changes to several high-profile judicial assignments.
Additional Sessions Judge Prashant Sharma, who has been hearing NIA cases involving Hafiz Saeed, leaders of the Popular Front of India (PFI), and cases related to Ukrainian and US nationals, will now continue as a Special Exclusive NIA judge at Rouse Avenue.
Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga has been transferred from the recently constituted paper leak court to the Special NIA Court. Her place in the paper leak cases will be taken by Special Judge Ajay Gupta.
Among other notable transfers, Special CBI (MP-MLA) Judge Jitendra Singh has been shifted to the Family Court at Tis Hazari. Singh had discharged former Delhi Chief Minister Arvind Kejriwal and other accused in the alleged Delhi Excise Policy CBI case in February 2026. He had taken charge of the court in October 2024 and has been transferred before completing two years in the post.
Special Judge (MP-MLA) Vishal Gogne has been transferred from Rouse Avenue to the Family Court at Dwarka as Additional Principal Judge.
Meanwhile, Additional Sessions Judge Sheetal Chaudhary Pradhan has been moved from Saket Court to the Labour Court at Rouse Avenue, while ASJ Ekta Gauba Mann has been appointed Registrar (Judicial) of the Delhi High Court from the office of the Principal District and Sessions Judge (HQ), Tis Hazari.

headline: Zee's Subhash Chandra, Punit Goenka fined by SEBI, barred from markets for one year
full_text:
Zee's Subhash Chandra, Punit Goenka fined by SEBI, barred from markets for one year
ZEEL has also been fined ₹3 million and barred from the securities market for two months.
Market regulator SEBI has cracked the whip on Zee Entertainment Enterprises (ZEEL) over securities law violations, with the company, Chief Executive Punit Goenka and Founder-Chairman Emeritus Subhash Chandra facing penalties totalling ₹14.8 million, news agency Reuters reported.
Goenka faces a fine of ₹5.8 million, while Chandra faces a penalty of ₹6 million after the SEBI's 150-page order issued naming Goenka, Chandra and ZEEL on Friday.
Also read: ‘First and last mistake… I am just 15’: Girl booked for PM Modi remarks apologises in viral video
The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) also barred Goenka and Chandra from the securities market for one year.
ZEEL has also been fined ₹3 million and barred from the securities market for two months.
The trouble for the company stems from a SEBI investigation which found that the company had used its land in Hyderabad as security for loans taken by large shareholder-linked entities without proper approvals.
The market regulator found that ZEEL's property was deployed for the benefit of related entities and the arrangement was not disclosed to the company's board, audit committee, shareholders or investors.

SEBI in its order said that four entities of Essel Group had availed four separate loans aggregating to ₹726 crores from Indiabulls Housing Finance Limited (“IHFL”) on December 13, 2016.
“As on March 31, 2019, Essel Home held the entire share capital of each of the four borrowing entities. Though the ownership of Essel Home was held through multiple corporate layers, the investigation traced its ultimate ownership and control to Ms. Sushila Goenka, Noticee No.2 and Essel International Limited,” SEBI said.

headline: Supreme Court asks states to stop cattle straying on roads, compensate victims of accidents
full_text:
Supreme Court asks states to stop cattle straying on roads, compensate victims of accidents
The court said that the presence of cattle on roads must be prevented, adding that this is only possible if states enact laws or enforce regulations.
The Supreme Court on Friday asked states and Union territories to amend their laws to prevent stray cattle on roads and frame schemes to compensate pedestrians and motorists killed or injured in bovine attacks and accidents.
A bench of justice Sanjay Karol and justice N Kotiswar Singh said, “It is commonplace to see reports in newspapers regarding bovine-related incidents and accidents…accidents with a direct and proximate bovine cause are not few and far between.”
Dealing with a 2007 incident in Sangrur, Punjab, where a stray bull attacked a man who sustained head injuries and later died, the bench directed the state to award a lump sum compensation of ₹15 lakh to the widow, holding that the order shall not be treated as a precedent. The bench said, “While this case presents a particular instance before us, we are of the view that the larger issue of these incidents must also be addressed,” offering several suggestions for the Centre and states to act upon.
“Necessary amendments may be carried out or rules promulgated, as is deemed fit by the competent authority, to develop a mechanism for payment of compensation in accidents caused as a result of bovine/cattle, in both categories of cases i.e., pedestrian or vehicular,” the bench said.
The court noted that the presence of cattle on roads and highways must be prevented, adding that this is only possible if states enact laws or enforce existing regulations to hold owners accountable when cattle are left to graze in the open.
Justice Karol, authoring the judgment, said, “We live in a deeply flawed, human world. Perhaps it is a feature of this flawed world that, on the one end, we let them (cattle) roam about without caring for their safety, and, on the other, find it deeply offensive if an individual uses them to secure a full stomach for himself or his family.”
Noting that 24 states have enacted laws regarding the protection and preservation of bovines, the court asked all such states to take steps to ensure complete and immediate implementation of the law in letter and spirit.
In the case before the court, the bench noted the plight of the victim, who had filed a police complaint after being injured by the bull. While still alive, he wrote to the Municipal Council, Sangrur, demanding compensation of ₹1 crore. The council replied that it received no funds to provide such compensation. He then moved the Punjab and Haryana high court, where a single judge in 2019 calculated compensation by applying the scheme under the Motor Vehicles Act. However, a division bench of the high court set aside this decision in November 2025, directing the widow to file a suit before a civil court.

The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders. (Generative image)
NEW DELHI: The Bombay high court on Friday came down heavily on Indians who litter public places at home but follow cleanliness rules abroad, saying the same people who "throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid" in India ensure to put "even a small chocolate wrapper" in the dustbin abroad.The court stressed that maintaining cleanliness is a fundamental duty and called for strict action against offenders.A bench of Justices G S Kulkarni and Aarti Sathe made the observations while hearing a batch of petitions over pollution, foul odour, gas emissions and health hazards linked to the Kanjurmarg dumping ground in Mumbai.The judges said public participation was essential to keeping the city clean and urged civic authorities to enforce the rules without hesitation."If a person wants a clean environment, then he or she has a corresponding fundamental duty towards society to maintain cleanliness. We want the civic officials to be ruthless in taking action," the court said according to news agency PTI.Expressing concern over people's attitude towards public cleanliness, the bench said citizens often behave differently once they leave India."We have to sensitise our citizens. Here, a person will throw garbage on the road without batting an eyelid, but these same people, when abroad, will strictly avoid such behaviour.
Even a small chocolate wrapper they will throw in the dustbin," the high court said.The bench then questioned, "Is this the price of liberty and democracy?"The court also voiced concern over the large quantity of plastic waste strewn across public places, observing that even Mumbai's beaches are littered with plastic. It questioned whether such conditions reflected the standards of "a civilised society".The judges noted that garbage dumped on roads and in narrow lanes poses serious health and hygiene risks to residents every day.Referring to the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai's slogan 'Swachch Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai, Aapli Mumbai, Sundar Mumbai', the court said the civic body's intention was commendable but was being undermined by irresponsible behaviour from citizens and inadequate enforcement by the municipal machinery.
"It is in these circumstances the role of MCGM's cleanliness machinery wardwise becomes significant, to take all effective steps so that public streets are not used by the citizens as dumping places," the bench observed.The court said failing to enforce the rules would defeat the objective behind the civic body's cleanliness campaign and urged authorities to implement the existing regulations strictly.It also raised concerns over the handling of garbage near heritage landmarks such as Rajabai Tower and the Bombay high court building. The bench observed that tourists, including foreign visitors, often encounter garbage on roads because of poor waste handling by municipal collection vehicles.The high court directed the civic body to take corrective steps within a week, warning that it would otherwise be compelled to pass further orders.

headline: New Delhi: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticised the decision to replace the Indian hockey team’s traditional blue jersey with a saffron-coloured kit for the upcoming FIH Hockey World Cup, alleging that the move reflected an attempt to imp...
full_text:
New Delhi: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge criticised the decision to replace the Indian hockey team’s traditional blue jersey with a saffron-coloured kit for the upcoming FIH Hockey World Cup, alleging that the move reflected an attempt to impose a political ideology on national sporting symbols.
The controversy erupted after Hockey India unveiled a new saffron primary jersey for the men’s and women’s teams. The federation has said that the redesign was meant to improve player visibility against blue synthetic turfs and that saffron was chosen as one of the colours of the Indian tricolour.
But this has raised questions over the decision and has drawn criticism from opposition leaders and some former players such as Olympic gold medal-winning captain Vasudevan Baskaran and former India captain Viren Rasquinha.
In a post made in Hindi on X, Kharge said the issue was “not merely a sporting decision” but one that was linked to the emotions of millions of Indians and the country’s sporting tradition. He added that Indian teams have long been recognised as the “Men in Blue”, “The Blues” and the “Blue Tigers”, calling the blue jersey a legacy of Indian sport.
भारतीय हॉकी टीम की जर्सी का रंग बदलने का फैसला केवल एक खेल संबंधी निर्णय नहीं है, बल्कि करोड़ों भारतीयों की भावनाओं और हमारी खेल परंपरा से जुड़ा विषय है।
भारतीय खिलाड़ी वर्षों से दुनिया भर में “Men in Blue” और “The Blues” “ The Blue Tigers” के नाम से पहचाने जाते रहे हैं। यह…
— Mallikarjun Kharge (@kharge) August 1, 2026
Questioning the rationale behind the move, the Congress president wrote, “Today it is difficult to understand why there was a need to change this historic identity.”
“The question is not about any colour, but about the decision-making process, transparency and respect for public sentiment,” he said. Kharge elaborated that his objection was not with the colour saffron itself. “Saffron, white and green are all colours of our national flag and are also represented with equal respect in the Indian National Congress flag.”
The Congress chief also accused the Bharatiya Janata Party-Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (BJP-RSS) ideological ecosystem of attempting to leave its mark on national institutions and symbols. “It is unfortunate that those whose ideological tradition had no contribution to the freedom movement are today in a hurry to leave their ideological imprint on every national symbol and every public institution.”
“History knows that the RSS had fiercely opposed the Tricolour and Sardar Patel had also warned them.”
Kharge also claimed that the jersey issue was part of a larger pattern of changes to public institutions and symbols.
“From road pavements to Parliament staff uniforms, from the Doordarshan logo and now the players’ jerseys — all without broad public consensus,” he wrote. Calling for the decision to be reversed, he said, “National symbols, sports and players should not be made instruments of narrow political experiments.”
He urged the government to “immediately reconsider this decision” and asked why Hockey India’s Executive Board was not consulted before the decision to change the jersey colour was changed. The federation has denied any political motive behind the change. The issue has sparked a wider political debate, with the Congress accusing the government of attempting to reshape national sporting symbols.

headline: A gang of five persons was arrested by Thanrampattu police in Tiruvannamalai on Saturday for allegedly assaulting a commuter in a government bus a few days ago.

headline: 360-degree cameras, 8-member monitoring team: Ram temple trust starts videography of donations
full_text:
360-degree cameras, 8-member monitoring team: Ram temple trust starts videography of donations
Every stage of donation, from collection boxes inside the temple to the counting room, will be videographed, according to a senior Ram Temple trust official.
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust has rolled out a new surveillance system to make donations at the Ram Temple more transparent and accountable even as investigation into the alleged embezzlement of devotees’ offerings continues.
From July 25, every stage of donation handling — from the collection boxes inside the temple to the counting room — is being videographed, according to a senior official of the Trust. An eight-member monitoring team has been deployed to oversee the process.
According to the senior official of the Trust, 360-degree cameras and SLR cameras are being used to document each step, ensuring a visual record is maintained from the moment a donation box is moved till the money is counted.
Officials said the objective is to bring in transparency, credibility and accountability at every level of the donation chain.
How the new process works
The Trust has also changed the way the temple’s 40-odd donation boxes are emptied. Earlier, multiple boxes were opened together. Now, they are being emptied on different days to allow closer scrutiny.
To manage this, two professional videographers have been appointed. Each exercise is carried out in the presence of two bank officials, two Trust representatives and two security personnel.
Once the box reaches the counting room, officials of the State Bank of India formally seal it after the counting.
The tighter monitoring comes weeks after an alleged theft of donations at the Ram temple triggered a Special Investigation Team (SIT) probe.
Police have arrested multiple accused in the case and the investigation is underway.
Also Read: ‘Attack on Hindu society’: Poonawalla slams Rahul Gandhi over Ram Temple theft skit in Parliament
The combination of videography, multi-agency presence, and bank involvement is aimed at removing any scope for manipulation and reinforcing public trust.
Officials said the new system will also help in quick audits and in addressing any complaints from devotees regarding the donation process.
Firm registered in name of accused's wife
The business operations and financial transactions of a firm registered in the name of Poonam Devi, the wife of key donation theft accused Ram Shankar ‘Tinnu’ Yadav, is being probed to trace any link with the alleged embezzlement.
Ashutosh Tiwari, the circle officer and the investigating officer, has written to the state tax department seeking complete details of the firm — Saundarya Construction and Suppliers.
Following a letter from the officer, the department concerned has begun collecting records.

headline: No GenZ disconnect, PM responded with action: Smriti Irani on NEET protest row
full_text:
No GenZ disconnect, PM responded with action: Smriti Irani on NEET protest row
Smriti Irani said the Centre answered the NEET paper leak protests with legislation, a task force and direct outreach by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. She said the response showed engagement with students while drawing a line against violence during dissent.
Senior BJP leader and former Union Education Minister Smriti Irani has dismissed claims that the NEET paper leak protests exposed a widening disconnect between Generation Z (GenZ) and the Narendra Modi government. She asserted that the Centre responded swiftly through legislation, dialogue and direct communication by the Prime Minister.
In an exclusive interview with India Today, Irani said the passage of the anti-paper leak legislation in Parliament, coupled with Prime Minister Modi's recent appeal to students through an Instagram video, demonstrated that the government was responsive to the concerns of young people rather than indifferent to them.
'NO DISCONNECT BETWEEN GENZ AND GOVT'
Asked whether the student-led protests reflected a growing gap between the youth and the government, Irani rejected the premise, arguing that the government's response proved otherwise.
She said Parliament had passed the anti-paper leak Bill after extensive deliberations and described the Prime Minister's message to protesting students as evidence of constructive engagement.
"It is a great insult to Parliament when you say the issue has merely been papered over," she said, adding that the government had acted proactively by setting up a task force, passing the legislation and directly communicating with young citizens.
Irani also accused sections of the media of disproportionately focusing on the Jantar Mantar protests while ignoring similar student movements elsewhere, particularly in Jharkhand.
DEFENDS EDUCATION REFORMS, ANTI-PAPER LEAK BILL
Responding to concerns over whether previous reform committees had yielded tangible results, Irani said the new legislation "speaks for itself" and argued that examination-related challenges had existed long before the Modi government came to power.
Drawing on her tenure as Education Minister, she said the National Education Policy was framed after one of the most extensive consultation exercises in independent India's history.
According to her, the government consulted more than 2.25 lakh village education councils, district education officers, state education ministers, parent-teacher associations and student bodies before finalising the policy.
She also defended the composition of the newly constituted task force on examination reforms, saying it reflected the Prime Minister's willingness to involve experts and individuals across political and ideological lines rather than limiting participation to supporters of the government.
'RIGHT TO DISSENT, NOT TO ANARCHY'
Irani strongly defended the police response during the protests, saying democratic dissent was a constitutional right but violence against security personnel could not be justified.
She questioned why images of injured Delhi Police and paramilitary personnel had received relatively little attention and pointed to reports that individuals with criminal backgrounds had participated in the demonstrations.
"You have the right to debate, deliberate and dissent. You do not have the right to anarchy," she said, urging that conclusions be drawn only after official investigations are completed.
Rejecting attempts to portray the issue as a conflict between the government and GenZ, Irani argued that many young Indians serve in the armed forces, police and other public institutions, and should not be grouped together based solely on age.
"Don't bring age as a new division," she said, adding that patriotism and respect for democratic institutions transcended generational identities.
CREDITS PM MODI'S LEADERSHIP
Responding to criticism over the government's handling of the protests, Irani credited Prime Minister Narendra Modi's leadership for maintaining a balance between protecting students and preserving law and order.
She said then Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan stepped down to prevent student protests from being "usurped by criminal forces" and described the government's actions as sensitive and timely.
Concluding the interview, Irani maintained that the Centre's response to the protests reflected a willingness to engage with students while ensuring that democratic dissent did not descend into violence or attacks on public institutions.

headline: Ex-army chief General Sharma dies at 96
full_text:
Ex-army chief General Sharma dies at 96
Former army chief General Vishwa Nath Sharma passed away on Friday at the age of 96
Former army chief General Vishwa Nath Sharma passed away on Friday at the age of 96. He served as the army chief during 1988-90.
Sharma was the younger brother of Major Som Nath Sharma, the first soldier to be awarded the Param Vir Chakra, India’s highest wartime honour, posthumously. An alumnus of Indian Military Academy, Dehradun, General Sharma was commissioned into the 16 Light Cavalry in June 1950.
Offering his condolences on the former chief’s demise, defence minister Rajnath Singh said on X, “Deeply saddened by the passing of former Chief of the Army Staff, General Vishwa Nath Sharma. A distinguished military leader, General Sharma served the Nation with unwavering dedication, courage and honour. He carried forward the illustrious legacy of his family, including that of his elder brother, Major Som Nath Sharma, PVC, with great distinction.”
Major Sharma was among the four army heroes awarded the PVC for their uncommon courage in the 1947-48 Kashmir operations; the others were Lance Naik Karam Singh, Second Lieutenant Rama Raghoba Rane and Naik Jadunath Singh (posthumous).
The Indian Army also extended its condolences to his bereaved family and loved ones. “A distinguished soldier and visionary military leader, General Vishwa Nath Sharma dedicated his life to the service of the Nation. The younger brother of Major Som Nath Sharma, PVC, Independent India’s first Param Vir Chakra awardee, he upheld his family’s extraordinary legacy of courage and selfless service with distinction. His exemplary leadership, unwavering commitment and enduring legacy of honour, duty and military excellence will continue to inspire future generations,” it wrote on X.

Amit Shah presented Lokmanya Tilak award to Ajit Doval and hailed his role in India's national security
NEW DELHI: Union home minister Amit Shah on Saturday lauded National Security Advisor (NSA) Ajit Doval for his contribution to India's national security and foreign policy, saying the veteran intelligence officer has played a crucial role behind every major national security decision taken by Prime Minister Narendra Modi since 2014.Speaking at a function in Pune after presenting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award 2026 to Doval, Shah said the NSA's advice and strategic inputs have been instrumental in strengthening India's security architecture and defence preparedness.He also said Doval's contribution to India's internal and external security had been so significant that history would reserve "a golden page" for him.
"NSA Ajit Doval has played a great role in strengthening India's foreign policy. In every decision of PM Modi for national security, Doval has had a 'role and advice' in the background," Shah said."Whenever history is written, if anyone analyses internal security and external security, then clearly, for Ajit Doval ji, a golden page will have to be kept reserved; there is no doubt about this," he added.
'First selection' after Modi became PM
Shah said one of the first decisions taken by PM Modi after assuming office in 2014 was appointing Doval as the National Security Advisor, a move he said transformed India's strategic posture.
"Today, India's foreign policy has become a foreign policy with a backbone of steel; no one can deny this. We have, along with self-respect, strengthened our position in the world," Shah said.Praising Doval's decades-long career in the Intelligence Bureau, Shah said India has emerged as a stronger and more confident nation under Modi's leadership, with Doval making a significant contribution to that transformation.
"After becoming NSA in 2014, Doval helped implement many strategic ideas on the ground and played a major role in modernising India's armed forces, strengthening technology, enhancing operational capability and improving the country's defence preparedness," Shah said.He added that the Modi government has fundamentally transformed both the defensive and offensive capabilities of the armed forces over the past 12 years, with Doval playing a key role in the process.Shah also noted that much of Doval's contribution can never be made public because of the confidential nature of intelligence operations.Recalling his tenure as Gujarat's home minister, Shah narrated how he first interacted with Doval following the Ahmedabad serial bomb blasts. He said then chief minister Narendra Modi had advised Gujarat Police to consult Doval while investigating the attacks."I remember Ajit ji had come to my house. The tips he gave resulted in Gujarat Police resolving not just the Ahmedabad bomb blast, but 13 bomb blasts across the country all at once. This was a very great achievement," Shah said.
Shah invokes Lokmanya Tilak's legacy
The Union home minister also paid tribute to Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, calling him one of the foremost architects of India's freedom movement.He said Tilak's iconic slogan, "Swarajya is my birthright, and I shall have it," gave a new direction to India's freedom struggle and inspired generations of freedom fighters.
Shah added that the slogan made Indians realise that self-rule was their right and not a favour bestowed by anyone.Describing Tilak as a fearless journalist, Shah said one could truly understand courage in journalism only by reading the articles published in Kesari, the newspaper founded by the freedom fighter."How fearless a journalist can be can only be experienced by reading the articles of Kesari," he said.
Referring to Tilak's role in mobilising people through the public Ganesh and Shivaji festivals, Shah said they laid the foundation for cultural nationalism and that India continues to follow the path envisioned by the freedom fighter."India is now moving firmly on the path of cultural nationalism laid down by Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak, and no one can reverse that journey," he said.Shah further added that Tilak's ideas on nationalism, self-rule and social awakening continue to guide the country and remain relevant for nation-building, particularly for the younger generation.
Shah said honours such as the Lokmanya Tilak National Award are not merely ceremonial but recognise those who dedicate their lives to the country and inspire future generations."When such individuals are honoured, the feeling of gratitude of society towards them is discharged... Today, the Tilak Award that has been conferred upon Ajit Doval ji... for those who live for this country and work for this country, it will become a place of great inspiration," he said.
Doval accepts award with humility
Accepting the Lokmanya Tilak National Award, Doval thanked the organisers and said he was honoured to receive an award named after Lokmanya Tilak."I am thankful for this award named after Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and accept it with humility," Doval said.Doval also praised the country's leadership, saying, "We are very fortunate to have leaders like PM Modi and Amit Shah".

headline: BSF reservation benefits extend to ex-Agniveers
full_text:
BSF reservation benefits extend to ex-Agniveers
The Centre on Thursday issued a notification extending reservation benefits to ex-Agniveers in the Border Security Force
The Centre on Thursday issued a notification extending reservation benefits to ex-Agniveers in the Border Security Force.
According to the existing reservation policy for constable (General Duty) posts in central armed police forces(CAPFs), 15% seats are reserved for Scheduled Castes, 7.5% for Scheduled Tribes(ST), 27% for other back backward classes(OBCs).
The selected ex-Agniveers, upon completion of their service in the armed forces, will be joining as Constables(General Duty) in the different CAPFs.
“The provisions of reservation shall also apply in the case of ex-Agniveers,” the July 30 notification said.
The Union Home Ministry also notified the government’s announcement made in Parliament last week regarding 50% reservation in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and exemption for ex-Agniveers from the written exam, physical standards and physical efficiency tests. HT first reported on April 14 that retired Agniveer soldiers would be exempted from all the three tests during their induction in the central armed police forces(CAPFs). To be sure, the government has yet to announce how merit will be determined among the ex-Agniveers applying for recruitment to the CAPFs and Assam Rifles. People aware of the matter said the home ministry is working on this and is holding regular discussions with chiefs of CAPFs.
On July 21, minister of state for home affairs, Nityanand Rai said informed the Parliament that former Agniveers will be entitled to 50% reservation in the recruitment of Constable (General Duty) and Rifleman posts in the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPFs) and Assam Rifles, besides being exempted from the Physical Standards Test (PST), Physical Efficiency Test (PET) and the written examination.
The first batch of 2,600 Agniveers inducted into the Navy, who began training in November 2022, is likely to retire before November 2026. Subsequently other batches will retire and become eligible to join the different CAPFs. Many state police forces such as Haryana and Delhi, have also reserved 20% of posts for the young soldiers post their retirement.
India had on June 14, 2022, announced the Agnipath scheme replacing the military’s decade old system of recruitment, which will lower the age profile of the armed forces, ensure a fitter military and create a technically skilled war fighting force capable of meeting future challenges. The Agnipath scheme seeks to recruit soldiers for only four years, with a provision to retain 25% of them in the regular cadre for 15 years after another screening round. At least 3,000 Agniveers — barely 20 years old and recruited during the last three years — manned critical weapons and systems integral to the army’s hardy air defence (AD) shield activated during Operation Sindoor, which Pakistan couldn’t penetrate despite launching wave after wave of missile and drone attacks on multiple Indian military installations, airbases and cities during the May 7-10, 2025, clash between the two nuclear-armed neighbours.

full_text:
Rajasthan teacher booked for abducting, raping Class 11 student during lunch break
Rajasthan police launched a search for a government school PTI accused of abducting and raping a 16-year-old Class 11 student during lunch break.
A 35-year-old physical training instructor (PTI) at a government school in Rajasthan’s Churu district was booked for allegedly abducting and raping a Class 11 student during the school’s lunch break on Friday, police said.
The physical training instructor is absconding, and multiple police teams have been deployed to trace and arrest him, a police officer said.
What the FIR revealed
According to an FIR lodged by the 16-year-old’s father, the accused threatened the minor during the lunch break, forced her onto his motorcycle, and took her to his residence, where he allegedly raped her, Circle Officer (CO) of Sujangarh, Darjaram, who is investigating the case, said.
Also Read | 15-yr-old girl ‘gang-raped’ after being lured for car ride; 3 held
The girl later returned home and informed her family, following which her father approached the Sandwa police station and filed a complaint, he added.
Case registered against accused
Based on the complaint, police registered a case against the accused under the relevant provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act.
Also Read | MP woman raped after masked men break into house in MP, wooden object inserted into private parts
Darjaram said the survivor has undergone a medical examination, while a Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL) team has inspected the alleged crime scene and collected evidence. He added that the student’s statement is yet to be recorded before a magistrate under the relevant legal provisions.
Incident triggers protests
The incident triggered protests by local residents and the girl’s family outside the government school. The protesters locked the school’s main gate and demanded the immediate arrest of the accused teacher, along with strict action against him.

Police personnel reached the school, held talks with the protesters, and persuaded them to call off the agitation after assuring them that the accused would be arrested at the earliest. Further investigation is underway.

headline: Pappu Yadav attacked with shoe in Delhi, MP claims attacker pulled out knife
full_text:
Pappu Yadav attacked with shoe in Delhi, MP claims attacker pulled out knife
Independent MP from Bihar's Purnea, Pappu Yadav, was attacked after a man identified as Sumit from Bulandshahr allegedly hurled a shoe at him during a press conference in Delhi, sparking chaos and a scuffle.
Independent MP from Bihar's Purnea, Pappu Yadav, was targeted after a person threw a shoe at him during a press conference in Delhi, triggering a commotion and a scuffle between his supporters and the attacker.
According to the information provided, the protest was linked to Yadav's statement on the law related to the theft of donations meant for the Ram Temple.
The incident led to chaos at the venue, with pushing and shoving breaking out between Yadav's supporters and the protester after the shoe was thrown. Police have started an investigation into the incident.
According to sources, the person who entered the venue and thrown the shoe at Yadav identified himself as Sumit, a resident of UP's Bulandshahr. He was overpowered and detained immediately after the incident.
Police are currently verifying the sequence of events at the press conference, including whether the accused had come armed with a knife.
According to police, when Sumit was handed over by Pappu Yadav's supporters, a knife was also handed over along with him. Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the recovery of the knife.
Sources further said that Sumit told police he was upset over the alleged insult to saints, which he cited as the reason behind his actions.
Pappu Yadav claimed that the accused had come to kill him. "He came to kill me with a knife," Yadav alleged. The MP further alleged that there was a conspiracy to kill him.
"Every day, some religious figures are saying, 'Burn him, we will give Rs 51 lakh.' Everyone is saying, 'Kill him.' There was a conspiracy to kill me," Yadav said.
Pappu Yadav's media convenor, who was present at the spot, alleged that the attack escalated after the shoe was thrown.
"They first took off a slipper and threw it. When the knife was drawn to attack, our supporters and associates tried to restrain the assailant. I stepped forward and positioned myself between the attacker and Pappu Yadav, and I was beaten severely as a result," he said.
Following the incident Pappu Yadav alleged that the attacker had political links and sought an investigation into who was behind the alleged attack.
In a post on X, Yadav addressed Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union Home Minister Amit Shah, asking, "Prime Minister and Home Minister, tell me who gave him the contract to kill me? This youth was seen with the Chief Minister and Deputy Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, and he carried out a murderous attack on me."
Yadav further alleged that people associated with the BJP were protecting the accused and demanded action.
"Tell me who is protecting such killers in your party. Do they have your direct patronage? If not, then action should be taken," he wrote.
One of Pappu Yadav's supporters also alleged that the attacker had pulled out a knife during the incident.
"Pappu Yadav is constantly serving the public. The moment he pulled out a knife from behind, we immediately acted together and overpowered him. Had we not restrained him at that moment, it is possible that our Pappu-ji might not have been with us today," the supporter said.
The media convenor further alleged that the Delhi Police failed to protect the MP despite prior warnings.
"I tried to help Pappu Yadav escape the scene. The Delhi Police stood by and allowed the beating to happen. The police seemed to be shielding the goons. These people had come to stage a 'Prayagraj Part Two'—they came to replicate the Atiq Ahmed incident today," he alleged.
Claiming that he was injured in the scuffle, he said, "I was beaten so badly while facing two or three individuals that I lost consciousness. My associates carried me away from the spot. The Delhi Police took the attackers away, so they would know the exact number."
He also claimed that he had alerted the police in advance about threats to the MP.
"I personally met the DCP this morning and filed a formal complaint stating that the MP was arriving today and has been receiving constant threats on social media. Despite knowing all this, they deployed only three or four police personnel here," he alleged.
The media convenor further claimed that no police personnel helped Pappu Yadav during the attack.
"Not a single policeman stepped forward to help Pappu Yadav escape. When the assault was taking place, they focused solely on saving the goons and whisked them away from the scene. There were people hiding behind the cameras, three or four of them. Suddenly, someone pulled out a knife, another a slipper. The MP was the target, no one else," he alleged.
Congress leader Pawan Khera also reacted to the incident, criticising the Delhi Police.
"The Delhi Police seems remarkably efficient when it comes to repressing students peacefully demanding their constitutional rights. But when it comes to protecting a vocal Opposition leader – even a sitting Member of Parliament – at his own residence, it suddenly falls short," Khera said in a post on X.
He further said, "Ever since Anurag Kumar took charge as Delhi's Police Commissioner, the force's record has gone from bad to worse."
Police are verifying the facts surrounding the incident, including the alleged use of a knife, and the investigation is underway.

headline: Educated but unemployed: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed up
full_text:
Educated but unemployed: Inside India's broken jobs market and why the 'cockroaches' are fed up
Kanchan Yadav / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 02, 2026, 21:05 IST
Comments
Share
AA
Text Size
Small
Medium
Large
India's un-employment crisis and helplessness of modern life. (Representative image)
Franz Kafka's The Metamorphosis transformed an ordinary man into a giant insect to explore alienation, helplessness and the dehumanising pressures of modern life.More than a century later, India's self-styled Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) has adopted a similarly unsettling symbol, not to tell a work of fiction, but to express the frustrations of a generation increasingly unsure whether years of education, expensive coaching and relentless competition will ever translate into a stable job.What began as a social media sensation with a strong and straightforward satirical structure, quickly evolved into one of the country's biggest youth-led movements in recent years.Calling itself the "voice of the lazy and unemployed," the movement grew from memes mocking joblessness, paper leaks, inflation and the political establishment into street protests.The protest may have become a trigger for a generation already grappling with shrinking employment opportunities, rising educational costs and growing uncertainty about the future.And at its heart lies a simple question. What happens when an economy produces millions of graduates every year but fails to create enough quality jobs?According to veteran economist Arun Kumar, a retired professor at JNU, "This unemployment crisis has created a huge gap between expectations and reality.""Young people earn degrees believing they will secure good jobs, but when those jobs do not materialise, they continue preparing for competitive examinations year after year. Many take these exams four, five or even six times because they still hope to secure an organised sector job.
Their parents also encourage them because they know such jobs offer stable salaries and social security," he said."But the increasing privatisation of education has intensified competition. Coaching institutes want to showcase high success rates because that is their biggest selling point. That creates incentives for unethical practices, including paper leaks. The greater the privatisation, the greater the pressure to resort to illegal methods to ensure students succeed. Fake degrees, cheating and question paper leaks are all symptoms of a much deeper problem. They are linked to unemployment and the shortage of quality jobs in the organised sector," he added.
India's employment challenge
India has spent decades expanding access to higher education. Universities have multiplied, enrollment has surged and millions of families have invested heavily in degrees, viewing education as the surest path to upward mobility.The numbers tell a remarkable story. According to the State of Working India 2026 report by Azim Premji University, the number of young graduates in India increased nearly 13-fold, rising from around 5 million in 1983 to 63 million in 2023.But while the supply of graduates has grown rapidly, employment opportunities have not kept pace.The report estimates that graduate unemployment among people below the age of 25 is now close to 40%, while graduates accounted for nearly two-thirds of India's unemployed population in 2023.Even more striking is the rise in the number of unemployed graduates, which has increased from less than one million in 1983 to around 11 million in 2023, a 16-fold increase over four decades.The mismatch between education and employment has widened steadily since the mid-2000s as higher education expanded much faster than the creation of quality jobs. For millions of families, earning a college degree no longer guarantees stable employment or financial security.Recent government data suggest that the challenge is becoming even more severe.According to the government's flagship Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), unemployment among Indians aged 15 to 29 rose to 16.2% in June, the highest level recorded since monthly estimates became available in April 2025. At that time, youth unemployment stood at 13.8%.The ministry of statistics and programme implementation (MoSPI) has cautioned that monthly figures may fluctuate because of seasonal factors, academic cycles and the increased frequency of surveys. Even so, the latest numbers are significant because they fit into a broader pattern rather than representing an isolated spike. Youth unemployment has increased across all six categories tracked by the survey, urban and rural areas, men and women alike, during the 15 months for which monthly data are available.At the same time, the Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) among young people has declined from 42.7% to 40.3%. In simple terms, fewer young people are actively looking for work.Ordinarily, such a decline would be expected to reduce unemployment because fewer people are participating in the labour market. Instead, unemployment has continued to rise, suggesting that the economy is not generating enough opportunities even for the shrinking pool of job seekers.Annual PLFS data reinforce the same trend. Between 2022 and 2025, youth unemployment increased in 13 states and Union Territories, including Andhra Pradesh, Delhi, Telangana and West Bengal.The situation appears even more challenging for young women, with unemployment rising across 16 states and Union Territories during the same period.Taken together, the figures suggest that youth unemployment is becoming a structural challenge rather than a temporary fluctuation.
The problem isn't just unemployment, it's job quality
Headline unemployment figures often fail to capture the deeper challenges within India's labour market. Many graduates do find work, but not necessarily the kind of work they expected after spending years in higher education.Economist Arun Kumar said that the root of the problem is the sharp divide between India's organised and unorganised sectors."When unemployment rises, it inevitably leads to greater conflict because there are too few jobs for too many people. In India, this problem is even more pronounced because the unorganised sector employs around 94% of the workforce, while the organised sector employs only about 6%. The difference in wages and job security between these two sectors is enormous. A courier delivery worker may earn around Rs 10,000-12,000 a month, whereas a postman can earn around Rs 70,000. Naturally, nobody wants to lose an organised sector job, and everyone wants to secure one. That intense competition creates immense pressure," he added.
An analysis of India's Periodic Labour Force Survey illustrates this disconnect. Out of every 100 graduates aged between 15 and 29, only 50 are employed, 15 remain unemployed while actively searching for work, and the remaining 35 are outside the labour force altogether.Some continue their education. Others perform unpaid domestic work or have simply stopped looking for employment after repeated disappointments.Even among those who are employed, the quality of jobs remains a major concern. Only 26 out of every 100 graduates have regular salaried jobs. More strikingly, just four hold formal jobs that provide written contracts, paid leave and social security benefits.The remaining graduates are spread across self-employment, unpaid family work, casual labour and small household enterprises. Many earn irregular incomes and lack job security despite years spent pursuing higher education.The figures highlight a growing reality in India's labour market: employment alone is no longer an adequate measure of economic well-being. The challenge is increasingly about the availability of secure, productive and reasonably paid jobs.
Why educated youth feel left behind
The employment crisis begins long before students enter the labour market. Competition for limited seats in prestigious colleges has transformed education itself into an expensive investment.Government survey data show that Indian households now spend a significantly larger share of their education budgets on private coaching than they did seven years ago.The sharpest increase has been among higher secondary students preparing for engineering, medical and university entrance examinations.Families now spend nearly one-fourth of their higher secondary education budgets on coaching, compared with about 18% in 2018.Private coaching expenses have also increased steadily across primary, middle and secondary education, reflecting a growing belief that classroom teaching alone is no longer sufficient to compete in high-stakes entrance examinations.The pressure becomes particularly visible in engineering education. India had around 4.4 million undergraduate engineering students during the 2023-24 academic year. Yet the country's top 100 engineering institutions together offered only about 500,000 seats.
In effect, only one in nine engineering students can study at an institution widely regarded as offering strong placements and better career prospects.Students who fail to secure admission to elite institutions often graduate from colleges with weaker placement records, making it significantly harder to obtain well-paying jobs.The widening gap between educational aspirations and employment outcomes has created growing frustration among young people. The traditional promise that more education automatically leads to better employment is becoming increasingly uncertain.According to the State of Working India 2026 report, fewer than 7% of male graduates secure a permanent salaried job within one year of graduating. The figure is even lower, just 3.7%, when it comes to white-collar jobs.Using data from the PLFS and the earlier Employment-Unemployment Survey, the report estimates that 1.1 crore out of India's 6.3 crore graduates aged between 20 and 29 were unemployed in 2023.Graduate unemployment itself is not a new phenomenon. The report estimates that unemployment among graduates below the age of 25 increased from 35.02% in 1983 to 39.33% in 2023.What has changed, however, is the scale of the problem. India now produces far more graduates than ever before, while simultaneously entering the most important phase of its demographic transition.The country's median age currently stands at around 29 years and is expected to rise to 38 years by 2050.This is the period during which India's working-age population is expected to drive economic growth. If the economy fails to generate enough productive employment during this demographic window, the much-discussed demographic dividend could gradually turn into a demographic challenge.
India's employment paradox
India today is one of the world's fastest-growing major economies. Even amid geopolitical tensions, volatile oil prices and slowing global trade, the country has continued to post robust GDP growth and position itself as a manufacturing and investment hub.The government has invested heavily in highways, airports, railways, ports and digital infrastructure. Global technology companies such as Apple have expanded manufacturing in India, electronics exports have surged and semiconductor investments are beginning to gather pace. Policymakers increasingly see manufacturing as the sector that can absorb millions of workers and turn India's demographic advantage into sustained economic growth.Yet for many young Indians entering the labour market, this optimism feels distant. The central contradiction facing the Indian economy is that rapid economic growth has not translated into an equivalent expansion in quality employment. Economists often describe this phenomenon as "jobless growth", an economy that continues to grow without creating enough secure and productive jobs.India's challenge is especially daunting because nearly eight million graduates enter the labour market every year. Generating employment for such a large number of educated young people has become one of the country's biggest economic challenges.This gap between economic growth and employment opportunities lies at the heart of the frustration that has fuelled recent youth protests.
Is India creating enough jobs?
Whether India is creating enough jobs depends largely on which dataset is examined. The Reserve Bank of India's KLEMS database estimated that the economy generated 4.7 crore jobs during 2023-24, the highest annual increase in more than four decades.However, labour economists caution against looking at headline employment numbers alone.Employment estimates differ across official surveys because they use different methodologies. More importantly, the definition of employment itself often masks the underlying quality of jobs being created.For instance, India's labour surveys classify a person as employed if they have worked even for a few days during the reference period. Likewise, unpaid family workers and subsistence self-employed individuals are counted as employed despite earning little or no regular income.As a result, headline employment figures may paint a healthier picture than what many young workers experience in reality. Increasingly, economists argue that the more important question is no longer how many jobs India is creating, but what kind of jobs they are.
The informal sector is slowing too
For decades, India's informal economy acted as a safety valve for the labour market. Workers unable to secure formal employment often found opportunities in small businesses, family enterprises, retail trade or self-employment.However, even this safety net appears to be weakening.According to the ministry of statistics and programme implementation's latest Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE), the informal sector generated around 74.5 lakh jobs in 2025, significantly lower than the 1.1 crore jobs created during the previous survey period ending September 2024.Wage growth has also slowed sharply. Average wage growth in the sector declined to 3.9%, compared with 13% previously, suggesting that even workers who manage to find employment are seeing slower improvements in earnings.The figures reinforce concerns that employment opportunities are weakening across both formal and informal sectors, making it increasingly difficult for young people to find stable livelihoods.
India's employment quality lags behind peers
India's labour market also differs from many comparable economies because of the quality of employment available.International comparisons reveal another structural weakness: the quality of employment. Labour market studies show that around 93% of employed workers in Russia hold regular jobs. The share is about 68% in Brazil, 54% in China and 42% in Bangladesh, the PLFS 2022-23 & Jan-Mar 2024 data reported.In India, by contrast, only about 23% of workers are in regular salaried employment.This means that nearly three-fourths of Indian workers remain outside the formal sector, without written contracts, paid leave, provident fund benefits or social security.The shortage of secure employment also explains the extraordinary demand for government jobs. Whether it is railways, banking, the armed forces, civil services or state recruitment examinations, millions of candidates compete for relatively few vacancies because government employment still offers something much of the private sector cannot consistently provide stability.A government job often brings predictable salaries, pensions, housing allowances, healthcare benefits and long-term security.For many young Indians, particularly those from middle- and lower-income households, these jobs represent far more than employment. They represent financial stability for entire families.According to Kumar, the desperation is visible in the jobs educated Indians are willing to apply for.
The real issue is the lack of decent employment opportunities. We saw this clearly in Uttar Pradesh in 2017, when more than two lakh people applied for peon posts. Many applicants held qualifications such as PhDs, MTech, BTech, MCom and BCom degrees. When highly educated people apply for peon jobs, it shows they are unable to find work that matches their qualifications.
Arun Kumar
AI adds a new challenge
Even as India grapples with creating quality jobs, technological change is reshaping the employment landscape. A government-backed research group estimates that artificial intelligence could displace around three million managerial and coding jobs by the end of this decade.Automation is expected to reduce demand for routine white-collar work at a time when India is producing record numbers of engineering and technology graduates.Overseas opportunities are also becoming more limited. Tighter immigration policies in countries such as the United States, the United Kingdom and Australia have reduced opportunities for skilled Indian professionals.For decades, migration acted as a safety valve for India's educated workforce. That pathway is becoming increasingly uncertain."Many young Indians even leave the country in search of better opportunities. Some spend lakhs of rupees to migrate, while others take illegal routes because they see very few prospects at home. In many cases, they still end up doing low-paying or menial jobs abroad. That reflects the level of desperation created by the lack of opportunities in India,"Kumar noted on the brain-drain situation in India.
India's demographic dividend at a crossroads
India possesses one of the world's youngest populations, a demographic advantage that economists have long viewed as one of the country's greatest strengths.A growing working-age population has the potential to accelerate economic growth, boost productivity and expand domestic consumption.But demographic dividends are never automatic. They depend on whether an economy can generate enough productive employment for the millions entering the labour market every year.Research suggests that India's employment intensity of growth, the ability of economic expansion to generate jobs has steadily declined over the past four decades.
When NEET became the tipping point
Against this backdrop, the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak became much more than an examination controversy. Millions of students spend months and often years preparing for the country's most competitive entrance examinations.Families invest heavily in coaching classes, relocate to education hubs and, in many cases, students take gap years in pursuit of a medical seat.When allegations emerged that the examination paper had been leaked and sold before the test, the issue struck at the heart of a system that already demanded enormous financial and emotional investment.The government cancelled the examination, handed the investigation to the Central Bureau of Investigation and ordered a re-examination.For lakhs of aspirants, particularly those from middle- and lower-income households, the cancellation meant far more than repeating a test. It meant another year of uncertainty after months of preparation and considerable financial sacrifice.Some students performed worse in the re-examination. Others worried they had lost their best chance of securing admission. Reports of severe psychological stress and alleged student suicides linked to the controversy further intensified public anger.What began as protests against examination irregularities gradually evolved into a wider movement about education, unemployment and shrinking opportunities.It was in this atmosphere that the Cockroach Janta Party found resonance among young Indians. Initially known for satirical social media posts, the movement soon expanded into organised protests questioning paper leaks, unemployment, inflation and what participants described as the growing disconnect between educational aspirations and employment opportunities.The group's unusual symbol, the cockroach, captured widespread attention.The insect represented resilience, survival and invisibility, mirroring how many young people felt overlooked despite years of education and preparation. Eventually, the protests became one of the biggest youth movements witnessed in recent years.The protests exposed far more than frustration over one examination. They revealed a widening disconnect between education, employment and economic expectations.Economist Arun Kumar says unemployment extends far beyond those who are officially counted as jobless. "Youth unemployment, particularly among those aged 15 to 29, is extremely high, and the situation is especially difficult for women. There are different forms of unemployment. First, there are those actively looking for work but unable to find it. Second, there are people who are technically employed but only in low-paid, part-time or menial jobs that do not provide a decent livelihood," he said."Third, there is disguised unemployment, where people appear to be working but contribute little to productive economic activity. Finally, there are those who have stopped looking for work altogether because they have lost hope. Women are disproportionately represented in this last category. Female labour force participation in India remains much lower than in many other major economies, which means many women are no longer even counted among active job seekers," he added.Over the past few decades, India has dramatically expanded access to higher education, produced record numbers of graduates and remained one of the world's fastest-growing major economies.But the growth in quality jobs has failed to keep pace with the growing pool of educated youth. For many young Indians, securing a degree no longer guarantees a stable career or upward social mobility.
That gap between aspirations and opportunities lies at the heart of the growing frustration. For millions of students, the question is no longer just whether examinations are conducted fairly. It is whether years of education, expensive coaching, repeated attempts at competitive exams and immense financial sacrifices will eventually lead to a secure, well-paying job. Without that, the frustrations exposed by such protests are likely to persist long after the headlines fade.
Kanchan Yadav is a writer at The Times of India, where she covers business, politics, international affairs and social issues. Her reporting also focuses on policy, governance and economic developments, with a close lens on how decisions in corridors of power affect everyday lives and community well-being.

headline: In another round of potential name changes, the Tamil Nadu government has in official communications dropped the name Chief Minister’s Thayumanavar Scheme, under which essential commodities supplied through ration shops are delivered to the doorsteps...
full_text:
In another round of potential name changes, the Tamil Nadu government has in official communications dropped the name Chief Minister’s Thayumanavar Scheme, under which essential commodities supplied through ration shops are delivered to the doorsteps of senior citizens aged above 65 and persons with disabilities.
Instead, official releases from the State government refer to it as the scheme for doorstep delivery of Public Distribution System commodities for senior citizens and persons with disabilities. The scheme was launched by the previous DMK government headed by M.K. Stalin.
The State government also appointed Guru, founder of an online Vijay fan club, to head the Tamil Nadu Fact Check Unit, which was formed by the previous DMK government to combat fake news and disinformation, particularly on social media platforms.
It is learnt that the Fact Check Unit has been renamed the Information Integrity Desk. However, no Government Order or official notification had been made public in this regard as of Sunday, and the unit continues to retain its original name on X.
Renaming spree
The new government has already renamed several schemes introduced by its predecessor, including renaming the free bus travel scheme for women from Magalir Vidiyal Payanam to Magalir Payanam, and the Chief Minister’s Breakfast Scheme to the Perunthalaivar Kamarajar Breakfast Scheme.

headline: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.He said achieving the goal of a dev...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday launched the 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan', calling on the country's youth to stay physically and mentally fit and remain away from drug abuse.He said achieving the goal of a developed India requires a healthy, confident and drug-free younger generation. During his address, PM Modi also highlighed how the drugs affect one's family and career.Launching the campaign through video conferencing, PM Modi said the initiative is not only for individuals, families and society but also for the nation. He added that the next 100 Sundays would represent 100 strong steps towards a drug-free India.
"Next 100 Sundays will mark 100 strong steps towards drug-free India," he said.PM Modi also warned that drug trafficking was part of a larger strategy by hostile forces to weaken India and called for greater public vigilance. "Hurting India's interests by supplying drugs part of enemy nations' terror plan," he said.
"Today, all countrymen have come together for a great and important resolve. The campaign we are witnessing is meant for individuals, families and society, but above all, it is for the nation. The campaign, 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat', clearly reflects this resolve. As the country moves towards the goal of a developed India, it is essential that our youth remain physically and mentally healthy and stay away from drugs and other such harmful substances."
"The campaign we are witnessing today is for the individual, the family, and society; above all, it is for the nation. The very name of this movementâthe 'Drug-Free Youth' initiative under the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan â clarifies its resolve. As the nation sets its sights on becoming a Viksit Bharat, it is essential that our youth be healthy in body and mind, brimming with self-confidence, and forever free from the deadly habit of drugs. This is the objective of the campaign... This campaign was launched last year as a pilot project from Kashi... Over 125 spiritual organizations have joined us today for the welfare of crores of our fellow citizens."
"By being addiction-free, you need to protect your potential. You need to be aware that drugs get you high for a short time, but take your career and family to a new low/bottom.
From Varanasi to nationwide campaign
"As the MP from Kashi, I am happy that this campaign was launched last year from the sacred land of Kashi as a pilot project. Along with scientific clarity, it also carries spiritual energy. Social organisations and NGOs have joined this initiative for the welfare of crores of Indians. Together, they have prepared a roadmap through the Kashi Declaration. Today, we are witnessing how the welfare-oriented idea that emerged from Kashi has become a national project. From today, the Nasha Mukt Yuva campaign is being launched across the country."
"The 'Nasha Mukta Yuva Abhiyaan' is launching across the country today... There is immense power in collective action, and today, driven by that very strength, this campaign is set to touch the heart of every young person. Lakhs of youths across the nation took a pledge to stay free from drugs... The pledge taken today will continue to move forward steadily over the next hundred weeks."
"Drug use disturbs focus, takes you away from dreams. If a youth gets addicted to drugs, his aspirations take a hit, family gets shattered."
Govt's anti-drug drive and national campaign
"Today, the government stands firmly with the youth in the campaign against drugs. Strict action is being taken in the country against drug traffickers and drug abuse; there have been many times more arrests compared to before, and drugs worth thousands of crores of rupees have been seized. This shows how tough our government is against drugs."
"Today, thousands of students from schools, colleges and universities are connected online to this programme. Even lakhs of volunteers of MY Bharat are also connected. The NSS jawans too have joined us. People from different sectors, institutions and backgrounds--more than 1 crore youths are together today. I congratulate all of you for this big movement."
Youth key to Viksit Bharat, drugs part of enemy agenda
"You are India's Amrit Peedhi. You will shape your lives over the next 20-25 years, and you will lead the country to the goal of a Viksit Bharat in 2047, and you will be at the helm. You will be the ones to reap its full benefits."
"The country needs your energy, your imagination, and your talent, so staying drug-free is crucial for the country and for your own lives."
"When a young person falls prey to drug addiction, it is not just that individual who loses; a dream is lost. Hostile nations conspire and leave no stone unturned to drag our youth into the trap of addiction. Profiting from the supply of drugs while aiming to destroy a country like ours is part of their terror-driven agenda."
Parents, teachers and society must lead the fight
"We must always keep this in mind: if any child from our home has become a victim of addiction, do not hide it under the guise of social prestige. Seek help from whoever is needed."
"Make efforts to free your child from addiction with medical help."
"We should also foster a culture of open communication with children in the family, so that you can hold their hand before they get caught in such a whirlpool."
"Along with teaching the courses, please also discuss the dangers of drugs with the students. Launch a movement against addiction on your campus. Your efforts can bring big results."
"The support of society, the power of yoga and meditation--these strengthen our inner resolve against addiction. And today, we also have facilities like rehabilitation centres to help quit drugs." "I appeal to all of you that you are all the leaders of this great movement. You have further strengthened my belief that the youth of India is so aware, so sensible, and so serious about their duties."
The 'Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat Sankalp Abhiyan' aims to encourage young people to stay away from substance abuse and become ambassadors of positive social change in their communities.
The launch marks the beginning of a 100-week nationwide Jan Bhagidari campaign, under which awareness programmes will be organised every Sunday across the country.Activities will include sports events, walkathons, meditation sessions, cultural programmes, street plays, discussions, art competitions and community engagement initiatives.The campaign brings together educational institutions, youth organisations, civil society groups, industry bodies and more than 125 spiritual organisations to build a collective movement against substance abuse.Youth from over 10,000 locations across the country are participating through schools, colleges, universities, MY Bharat volunteers, NSS volunteers, youth clubs, NGOs and industry associations.
