headline: IIT Guwahati student dies in Brahmaputra drowning, another rescued: Police
full_text:
IIT Guwahati student dies in Brahmaputra drowning, another rescued: Police
Local sailors immediately came to the rescue, followed by the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team
A third-year BTech student of the Indian Institute of Technology Guwahati (IIT-G) died after accidentally falling into the Brahmaputra near Guwahati’s Lathia Bagicha Ghat on Saturday evening, police said on Sunday.
Another student who fell into the river with her was rescued shortly after the incident, officers said.
Local sailors immediately came to the rescue, followed by the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) team.
“One of the students was rescued within around 20 minutes, while the body of the other student was recovered after nearly three hours of searching,” an NDRF official said.
“It is with profound grief and deep sorrow that IIT Guwahati informs of the untimely demise of a BTech 3rd Year student of the Department of Electronics and Communication Engineering (ECE), who tragically lost her life in a drowning incident near Lathia Bagicha Ghat yesterday evening,” the institute said in a statement.
The authorities informed the student’s parents and asked them to visit the campus.
Also Read:IIT Guwahati Convocation 2026: 2265 degrees awarded, Saptarshi Mukherjee receives gold medal
“Police authorities are presently conducting a formal investigation into the circumstances of the incident. The institute remains in close communication with her parents and is extending full cooperation and assistance,” IIT-G said.
Additional superintendent of police (Kamrup), Kalyan Pathak, said police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the incident. “We are investigating the matter further,” Pathak told HT on Sunday evening.
IIT-G urged students, faculty and staff to exercise caution around water bodies and avoid hazardous locations, particularly during the monsoon.
The institute said it would strengthen its safety communication and issue frequent advisories cautioning students against going to the river and other unsafe water bodies during the monsoon.

headline: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Sunday came under sharp criticism from the Opposition over flood management as well as his participation in private functions during the floods. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat said i...
full_text:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Sunday came under sharp criticism from the Opposition over flood management as well as his participation in private functions during the floods. The Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)] State secretariat said in a statement on Sunday that the Chief Minister, who also heads the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, should not stand aside and delegate responsibility to Ministers.
“The primary duty of an administrator is to protect the lives and property of the people. Not fulfilling that can only be seen as a defiant attitude towards the public. Pathanamthitta and Idukki districts, which received the most rainfall, had only an orange alert until Saturday morning. The fact that many areas were under water by the time the red alert was announced is evidence of mismanagement. No steps were taken to relocate people to safe places and evacuate them from danger-prone areas,” said the CPI(M).
The CPI(M) alleged that the Coastal Police arrived 13 hours late to rescue the fishermen whose boat capsized near Muthalapozhi in Thiruvananthapuram. A video shared by Muslim Youth League vice-president Faisal Bafaqui Thangal of Mr. Satheesan participating in a lunch at his house in Ponnani on Saturday as well as the reports of the Chief Minister using the government’s helicopter for private purposes also invited criticism from the Opposition.
“The fact that the helicopter rented by the government was used for a private purpose and that a feast was being held when the people were suffering has led to severe public criticism of the Chief Minister. The State rented the helicopter to use it for disaster-relief activities and in times of need. The then Leader of the Opposition who criticised the LDF government when it rented the helicopter and called it wasteful expenditure is now using it for private purposes,” said the CPI(M).
Don’t politicise: MLA
Congress MLA C. Noushad Ali of Ponnani said such issues should not be politicised to target the Chief Minister during times of disaster. “Shouldn’t the Chief Minister go anywhere or have food during the rainy season? Such campaigns against him are politically motivated,” he told press persons. Contrasting Mr. Satheesan’s conduct during the flood with that of Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan during his term as the Chief Minister, the CPI(M) said Mr. Vijayan and his office had stayed vigilant round-the-clock, coordinating rescue efforts.
“When journalists asked Mr. Satheesan about the flood situation on Saturday, he took an indifferent approach and said that his office would brief them. It is worth recollecting that during the LDF’s tenure, Mr. Vijayan used to interact constantly with the press during such crisis situations. Through this, it was possible to give confidence to the people and also make them alert,” said the CPI(M).
‘No warnings’
In a separate statement, Mr. Vijayan said it is unacceptable that the negligence and lack of coordination on the part of the government has worsened people’s sufferings amid the floods. “It is being alleged that proper warnings were not issued before the opening of a dam near Ranni. Traders did not even get time to secure the goods in their shops. The negligence in the relief camps is also worrying. The government agencies themselves have admitted that there was a lapse in food distribution. Due to the lack of coordination by the officials, volunteers, local people and political activists had to prepare and distribute the food. The government should also examine the lapses and prevent them from recurring,” said Mr. Vijayan.

headline: Rs 700 crore worth of drugs seized, 84 traffickers arrested in Rajasthan crackdown
full_text:
Rs 700 crore worth of drugs seized, 84 traffickers arrested in Rajasthan crackdown
The operation targeted major opium trafficking routes linked to Manipur, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. More than 360 kg of opium has been recovered so far.
Rajasthan’s Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) has seized drugs worth more than Rs 700 crore over the past 10 months, marking what officials described as a record crackdown on narcotics trafficking in the state.
ANTF Inspector General Vikas Kumar said Rajasthan Police had seized narcotics worth around Rs 850 crore under the NDPS Act last year, while the total this year is expected to cross Rs 1,000 crore. The task force alone has accounted for seizures worth Rs 700 crore.
The operation targeted major opium trafficking routes linked to Manipur, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. More than 360 kg of opium has been recovered so far.
The ANTF also uncovered and dismantled 34 units allegedly manufacturing MD drugs across Rajasthan, seizing more than 185 kg of the synthetic narcotic. Officials said action was also taken against the illegal cultivation of opium and cannabis.
Working with agencies in five states and five central bodies, the task force arrested 84 alleged major drug traffickers. Several of them were wanted criminals who had been on the run for years, police said.
Officials claimed that sustained action across different supply routes had disrupted several trafficking networks and weakened the narcotics supply chain in the state.
Kumar appealed to the public to share information about drug trafficking and related crimes with the ANTF control room or through its WhatsApp helpline, assuring that the identities of informants would remain confidential.

headline: The water level in the KRS and Kabini reservoirs in the Cauvery basin continued to rise on Sunday as the dams recorded heavy inflows following widespread rainfall in their catchment areas.
full_text:
The water level in the KRS and Kabini reservoirs in the Cauvery basin continued to rise on Sunday as the dams recorded heavy inflows following widespread rainfall in their catchment areas.
While the water level in the KRS reservoir was inching towards the 100-ft. mark, reaching 98.8 ft. against its Full Reservoir Level of 124.8 ft. on Sunday evening, the reservoir was receiving an inflow of 31,583 cusecs. The Kabini reservoir, meanwhile, had almost reached its maximum level.
According to a bulletin issued by the authorities, the water level in the Kabini reservoir stood at 2,282.43 ft. (above mean sea level) against its maximum level of 2,284 ft., with an inflow of 27,217 cusecs on Sunday.
Discharge from Kabini
The authorities were releasing 25,000 cusecs of water into the river through the four crest gates of the Kabini dam on Sunday. About 2,000 cusecs of water is being released into the canal system, the bulletin said.
The increased discharge from the reservoir submerged a low-level bridge near the dam while cutting off connectivity to a few villages in the vicinity.
The Irrigation Department had issued a flood warning on Saturday, advising residents of low-lying areas downstream of the river to take precautionary measures in view of the increased discharge from the dam.
Meanwhile, the rainfall in Kodagu district, the catchment area of the KRS reservoir, which had received heavy showers on Friday and Saturday, showed signs of easing on Sunday.
However, with the Cauvery in spate, the road connecting Karigodu and Chikkanahalli villages in Ammathi hobli of Virajpet taluk was submerged. The authorities cautioned the public against using the road and advised them to take alternative routes.
The water level at the Triveni Sangama in Bhagamandala also rose, the authorities said.
The water level in the Harangi reservoir stood at 2,856.72 ft. (above mean sea level) against its maximum level of 2,859 ft., with an inflow of 10,440 cusecs. The authorities had reduced the discharge from the reservoir from 14,470 cusecs at 8 a.m. to 9,500 cusecs at 8 p.m. on Sunday.

headline: The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) has recently decided that the criteria for bidders to procure medical supplies for the three major hospitals here.
full_text:
The Tirumala Tirupati Devasthanams (TTD) has recently decided that the criteria for bidders to procure medical supplies for the three major hospitals here.
The TTD governs the administration of the Sri Balaji Institute of Surgery, Research, and Rehabilitation for the Disabled (BIRRD), the Sri Venkateswara Institute of Medical Sciences (SVIMS), and the Sri Padmavathi Children’s Heart Centre (SPCHC), all located in Tirupati, and offers exclusive, specialised medical care.
While reviewing the tender process, the TTD authorities found that the existing eligibility for procurement of medicines, injections, medical and surgical consumables, in terms of the minimum annual turnover for manufacturers, authorised distributors and importers has been on the higher side. The authorities also found the criterion to be restrictive, due to which the number of participants from eligible bidders remained “limited”, thus affecting competition and efficiency.
Revised cap
The committee was reconstituted to review the criteria met on July 3 under the Chairmanship of the BIRRD Director. The committee unanimously recommended revising the eligibility criteria for the minimum average annual turnover, currently capped at ₹100 crore, to ₹25 crore for the procurement of medicines and injections, and ₹15 crore for surgical and medical consumables for the laboratories and blood bank.
The panel recommended to the TTD trust board to continue the multi-vendor procurement system, which enables procurement from the willing L2 and L3 bidders at the rates quoted by and approved for the L1 bidder. This system provides relief to the TTD in case of a supply failure by the L1. The committee’s proposals were approved by the TTD’s trust board at its meeting held on July 14.

headline: Tiger grabs woman by head, drags her 300 metres to death in Madhya Pradesh
full_text:
Tiger grabs woman by head, drags her 300 metres to death in Madhya Pradesh
A tiger entered Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat village and fatally attacked a woman sleeping in her hut. The killing has triggered fresh safety measures and renewed concern over repeated big cat incursions.
A woman in her 30s died after a tiger attacked her in Madhya Pradesh's Balaghat district in the early hours of Sunday, officials said. The woman, identified as Sugni Bai Dhurve, suffered grievous head injuries and was taken to a hospital in Baihar, where she died, Block Medical Officer Dr Anant Lilhare said.
The attack took place in Parrapur Baigatola village under the Khapa range of the Kanha National Park. Assistant Director of the Sijhora Buffer Zone Ashish Pandey confirmed the incident and said a detailed report would be prepared after an inquiry, while police said a case of accidental death has been registered and further investigation is under way.
According to villagers, Dhurve was sleeping in a hut when the tiger entered the village, around 80 km from the district headquarters, at about 1.30 am. They said the animal grabbed her by the head and dragged her away.
After hearing the family's cries for help, local residents rushed to the spot with torches. The tiger dragged her for about 300 metres before leaving her and disappearing into the forest, they added.
Forest officials said the village has seen several instances of tigers and leopards entering human habitations in recent months. They said the victim's family would be given financial assistance as per government norms.
The forest department also said it would install a cage in the area, step up patrolling, and urged residents to keep house doors shut at night, avoid going into the forest, and not leave children and elderly people unattended.
Local representatives claimed the woman's family lives in a hut without a door and alleged that it has not benefited from a central government scheme aimed at the socio-economic development of the most backward and vulnerable tribal groups.
The attack has prompted fresh measures in the area as officials investigate the incident and prepare assistance for the family.

headline: Protests over paper leaks: SC to hear on Monday pleas relating to police action
full_text:
Protests over paper leaks: SC to hear on Monday pleas relating to police action
New Delhi, The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear on Monday a batch of pleas alleging police brutality during the recent protests against irregularities in exams and the NEET paper leaks.
A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana will be hearing the pleas in which the court had indicated that it might constitute an SIT headed by a former Supreme Court judge for a probe into the allegations made by protestors, pellet gun victims and to ascertain whether the attacks on policemen were carried out by students or some "miscreants".
On July 28, the top court had restrained states from taking any coercive action against protesters and directed them to release those under 18 on the condition that none should have any criminal antecedents.
The top court had observed that a fair and independent probe in the matter was required and whosoever committed excesses, took law into their hands should be taken to task.
It had directed, "All states are hereby instructed to release children under the age of 18, who have been reported to be arrested or detained in connection with the ongoing protests and who do not possess any criminal antecedents."
The top court had said if necessary, these children shall be released upon the execution of a simple bond by themselves or their family members, especially if such a requirement is insisted upon for surety.
It had taken note of allegations such as the use of pellet guns, lathis embedded with nails, rubber bullets and electric batons on protestors resulting in severe life threatening injuries to several students and young women.
The top court had directed that Delhi government and other states may proceed with the investigation of the FIRs registered but no coercive measures shall be taken against the protesting students.
"Such protection, nonetheless, shall not be extended to the persons with criminal antecedents," it had clarified.
Noting that the bench is mulling an independent, a transparent and thorough probe into all allegations by a task force, the bench had said a probe is also required to ascertain the attacks on policemen and whether they were by students or some "miscreants".
"Be that as it may, the allegations made by the petitioners, prima facie, establish a compelling case for an independent and impartial investigation into the incidents of violence. Such an investigation will adequately address the allegations presented by the family members of the police personnel, as well as the issues raised by the Solicitor General of India," it had said.
While posting the matter for further hearing, the top court had said in the interest of justice an opportunity was given to the Centre and the states concerned to place their versions on record before it considers constituting an independent committee or a Special Investigation Team .
The top court had issued notices to Maharashtra, Bihar, Assam, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, West Bengal and Kerala and asked their advocates general to appear online on the next date of hearing.
It had issued a slew of interim directions to states where protests were held to preserve CCTV footage, drone recordings, body-camera footage, wireless communication records, PCR logs and other digital evidence pertaining to the protests.
"Although it has already been stated at the bar by the Solicitor General of India, on instructions, we also, as an abundant precaution, direct that all CCTV footage, drone footage, body-worn camera recordings, videography, wireless communication records, and PCR lodge collections related to the students' protest be preserved," it had directed.
The top court had also ordered the police authorities to ensure that the personal information and digital data of the protestors, collected during the students' protests, are preserved and are not disclosed to the public domain for the time being.
It had emphasised that the authorities may not publish any public data/details of the protestors, especially students.
"The NCT of Delhi and other states may proceed with the investigation of the FIRs registered; however, no coercive measures shall be taken against the protesting students. Such protection, nonetheless, shall not be extended to the persons with criminal antecedents," it had ordered.
The Cockroach Janta Party -led march on July 20 in Delhi witnessed clashes between protesters and security personnel, who used lathis and teargas shells to disperse crowds attempting to move towards Parliament. The protests escalated and spread to several other states.
The protesters were demanding the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET paper leak issue.
The agitation ended on Saturday with Pradhan's resignation and the government agreeing to the demand for compensation to the families of those who had ended their lives and no FIRs against the protesters.

headline: Fake identities, phone numbers: How 5 men impersonated deceased owners in ₹2.29 crore land fraud in Navi Mumbai

Fake identities, phone numbers: How 5 men impersonated deceased owners in ₹2.29 crore land fraud in Navi Mumbai
As per police, Shinde got his father and brother-in-law to impersonate the dead brothers by using fake identity documents.
A five-month manhunt in Navi Mumbai led to the arrest of five people accused of impersonating dead owners. As per the police, the five accused, led by mastermind Suraj Vasudev Shinde, faked their identities to carry out a land fraud of ₹2.29 crores.
As reported by HT earlier, the accused allegedly targeted a plot in Karanjade belonging to brothers Nathan Eliyahu Chincholkar and Shalom (Selim) Eliyahu Chincholkar, who had migrated to Israel and later died in the country.
Fake documents, new phone numbers
As per police, Shinde got his father and brother-in-law to impersonate the dead brothers by using fake identity documents.
Using these fake documents, Shinde and his accomplices managed to execute the sale of the plot for ₹2.29 crores.
Police added that the arrests came after a five-month manhunt for the accused as they kept changing their phone numbers, identities and hideouts to evade the police.
Shinde had lived in the states of Maharashtra, Goa, Gujarat, Rajasthan, Uttarakhand, Delhi, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh while trying to evade arrest. As per officials, Shinde fled with his relatives who were also involved in the scam.
Accused tracked using intelligence inputs
Suraj Shinde was tracked to Thivim in Goa, where he was arrested with his uncle, Satish Namdev Shinde, 41, and cousin, Tejas Pramod Surve, 26, using technical surveillance and intelligence inputs.
Police added that Manish More was arrested by Mapusa police in an unrelated theft case and was lodged in Colvale Central Jail, and Vasudev Shinde was arrested from Dombivli on July 27.
Following their arrest, police also recovered the forged PAN and Aadhaar Cards in the names of the deceased landowners.

headline: Stating that the water situation in the Cauvery is “slightly better” in view of the rain, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday (August 2, 2026) reiterated his appeal to the Kannada organisations to withdraw their State-wide bandh plan o...
full_text:
Stating that the water situation in the Cauvery is “slightly better” in view of the rain, Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar on Sunday (August 2, 2026) reiterated his appeal to the Kannada organisations to withdraw their State-wide bandh plan on August 13.
However, Kannada Chaluvali leader Vatal Nagaraj, who is leading the protest, said the bandh will be held as planned.
At an all-party meeting, the Chief Minister said Karnataka is carefully assessing the Cauvery situation, including the petition of the DMK in the Supreme Court. A limited quantity of water is being released from the reservoirs in the light of rain, he said.
The meeting had been convened to address the concerns over the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA)’s directive to the State to abide by the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee’s order to release 3,500 cubic metres daily to Tamil Nadu for 15 days. The order set off protests in parts of Karnataka.
“(Four) reservoirs in the Cauvery basin are cumulatively receiving about 68,000 cusecs of water. Our dams were not full since there was no rain. There has been some rain (now) and the situation has become slightly better. Kabini (reservoir) is full,” he told presspersons here after the all-party meeting.
The data shared by the Water Resources Department shows that Karnataka was releasing water at the rate of 25,000 cusecs from the Kabini reservoir and 1,819 cusecs from the Krishna Raja Sagar on Sunday to Tamil Nadu.
The Chief Minister said: “We are releasing a limited quantity of water through canals only to fill lakes and tanks meant for drinking water purposes, and not for irrigation.”
‘Mekedatu is the solution’
Reiterating that the proposed Mekedatu project on the Cauvery is the long-term solution to the problems faced by both the States, he said, “Karnataka will respect the law and orders of the Supreme Court while protecting the State’s interest.”
On the petition filed by the DMK in the Supreme Court, Mr. Shivakumar said: “We are closely watching the situation. Individual petitions of political parties and organisations are treated differently. We have to utilise our experience and be careful.” He also said that a legal and technical team would fight the State’s case.
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister Joesph Vijay has agreed to postpone his visit to Bengaluru to discuss the Cauvery issue on the request of the Karnataka government, he said. “Mr. Vijay intended to hold talks, but the meeting has been deferred. I requested from him that we meet later when a cordial atmosphere prevails. I do not want anyone shouting slogans against my friends. We should respect each other. We have to live together and work together. Ultimately, India is one,” said the Karnataka Chief Minister.
Asked if he would be able to convince Mr. Vijay of the situation, he said: “We will make him understand (the situation) and he will understand. Though he is new to politics, he is courageous. Whatever our political differences may be, he wanted to come to Karnataka.”
He said he will speak to the protesting farmers, Kannada organisations, and Opposition leaders. “Our Ministers will also speak. When the government is standing with you and nature is also with you, bandh is of no use. It will affect our schools and businesses. Ultimately, it will not help us. We are committed to farmers’ welfare and bound to protect the State's interest,” the Chief Minister said. “They [Opposition leaders] have pledged their support to the Government and have provided valuable suggestions. We will take the suggestions that will be discussed with the legal team before moving forward.”
However, in Mysuru, former MLA Vatal Nagaraj said the bandh had not been called on one issue. “More than 2,000 Kannada organisations have extended support to the bandh. Educational institutions, film chambers and hotel industries, among others, have extended support. Bandh is for various issues, including the Mahadayi river water dispute, employment for Kannadigas, and the development of the Mysuru-Hyderabad-Karnataka region, North Karnataka, Belagavi, Hubballi-Dharwad, and border areas. There is no question of withdrawing the bandh.”

full_text: Shivamogga/ Honnali/ Chikkamagaluru: Heavy rain continued in the Malnad region on Sunday. As widespread rain lashed the catchment areas, the Tunga and Bhadra rivers and the Malati stream near Thirthahalli are flowing above the danger mark..After 48 hours of continuous rain, Ram Mantap in the Tunga River submerged on Sunday morning. Floodwaters from the Tunga have entered fields and plantations in and around Thirthahalli town. .Houses were damaged in Jambetallur, Mrugavadhe, and Biluve villages of Thirthahalli taluk. Rainwater gushed onto the National Highway 169. The intensity of the downpour reduced after Sunday noon. .The Varahi project catchment area in Hosanagar taluk recorded a downpour over the past 24 hours. Chakranagar recorded 32 cm, Mani 28.6 cm, and Yadur and Hulikal 28 cm each, while 27 cm was recorded at Mastikatte. Agumbe received 24.6 cm of rain..Inflow rises.The Tunga reservoir at Gajanur, Bhadra reservoir at Lakkavalli and Linganamakki reservoir at Kargal recorded their highest inflow of the monsoon season for the first time..The Tunga reservoir at Gajanur was receiving 94,000 cusecs of water on Sunday evening. Around 92,500 cusecs of water was being released into the river..The inflow into the Bhadra reservoir jumped to 31,874 cusecs. The reservoir has a storage capacity of 186 feet and had 160.3 feet of water on Sunday. .The inflow into the Linganamakki reservoir at Kargal reached 77,580 cusecs. The reservoir has a storage capacity of 1819 feet and currently has 1781.85 feet of water. .In Honnali.The river water level in the Bhadra reservoir, which was around five metres a week ago, rose to seven to eight metres by Saturday. The level jumped to nine metres on Sunday morning and further to 9.7 metres by evening. .Good rainfall in Nyamati and Honnali, twin taluks, is expected to benefit ragi sowing, maize crops in the growth stage, cotton, red gram, groundnut and other crops, Agriculture Officer Vishwanath said..On August 1, an average rainfall of 1.56 cm was recorded in the twin taluks. Honnali recorded 0.76 cm, Savalanga 3.02 cm, Belagutti 2.84 cm, Haralahalli 1.32 cm, Govinakovi 1.42 cm, Kundur 0.72 cm and Sasvehalli 0.84 cm..In Chikkamagaluru.Continuous deluge since Friday has caused flooding across Sringeri, Koppa and NR Pura taluks. The Tunga River overflowed at Kerekatte and Kigga, inundating roads, fields and low-lying areas..National Highway 169 at Nemmar was submerged, disrupting the Sringeri–Mangaluru route, while several roads in Sringeri town were flooded. Bharathi Theertha Road, Gandhi Maidan and Kurubakeri Road in Sringeri town were also inundated. .The weekend flooding caused major inconvenience to devotees and tourists visiting the Sharada Peeta. Unaware of the worsening weather conditions in the Malnad region, many visitors had to park their vehicles nearly two kilometres away and walk through flooded roads..Waterfalls, including Narasimha Parvatha, Barkana, Sirimane and Sutanabbi, were overflowing. In Koppa, fallen trees blocked highways and roads, while Tunga backwaters flooded routes near Haranamakki and Narve. headline: TN minister rejects demand for all-party meeting to discuss Cauvery water issue
full_text:
TN minister rejects demand for all-party meeting to discuss Cauvery water issue
Chennai, Tamil Nadu Minister C T R Nirmal Kumar on Sunday rejected the demand for an all-party meeting made by various political parties in the state to discuss the ongoing Cauvery water row with Karnataka.
He said a detailed resolution was already passed unanimously in the Assembly with the support and participation of all political parties.
The DMK, AIADMK, PMK and VCK have demanded for an all-party meeting.
The minister also alleged that DMK President M K Stalin and Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar were working in tandem to undermine Tamil Nadu's interests in the ongoing Cauvery water dispute.
"In our Legislative Assembly, a resolution was passed unanimously with the support and participation of all political parties. They all nodded along and supported the resolution unanimously," he told reporters here.
"Everything regarding that resolution was debated right there. If there was opposition to be voiced, it could have been raised right then. They supported only after listening to everything, didn't they? Wasn't everyone given an equal opportunity to speak? Everyone spoke," he said.
"Then why, just four days ago, did they file a petition in the High Court challenging the very resolution they had supported? The moment they filed a case in the High Court, the DMK filed a petition in the Supreme Court two days later. Who ultimately suffers because of all this? It is the people of Tamil Nadu. Under the guise of creating trouble for the chief minister, they are acting against the interests of the public," he said.
"Under such circumstances, how can you expect us to invite these very people to an all-party meeting," he asked.
Kumar also said that the DMK's "hasty" petition in the Supreme Court has created undue confusion.
"Yesterday morning, after completing consultations with various stakeholders, the CM decided that we must file a case in the Supreme Court regarding this issue. By afternoon, our Supreme Court counsel, Umapathy, announced the decision, outlined the filing strategy after concluding all discussions, and initiated the process."
"While it was being processed, the DMK hastily filed their petition after 5 PM. It creates confusion when multiple petitions on the same issue are filed from the same state. What have they done over the last five years? Has the DMK filed even a single petition on this matter before this," he questioned.
"In Karnataka, everyone remains united on a single stance. They are adamant about not releasing water to us, and there are no two opinions on that among them. However, when it comes to our approach, how are we going to reclaim our rights? On one hand, there is the court, on the other, there are diplomatic channels. Yet, beyond all this, political parties here remain divided on the exact strategy to pursue," he said.
With regard to the reported release of 12,000 cusecs of water to Tamil Nadu from the Kabini reservoir, the minister said it was not enough for the state. "We need to get 17 TMC water from Karnataka", he added.
The CWMA on Thursday rejected the Karnataka government's plea and upheld the CWRC recommendation ordering the release of 3,500 cusecs of Cauvery water daily to Tamil Nadu for the next 15 days.
Kumar alleged a long-standing alliance between the DMK and Shivakumar, claiming the latter routinely prioritises Stalin's leadership.
Claiming that the DMK maintains a close, cordial relationship with Shivakumar, the minister said, "Their political stances appear closely aligned."
The minister further leveled serious allegations regarding political horse-trading, saying, "Bengaluru served as a financial safe haven for DMK to orchestrate MLA buyouts."
"Regarding the case involving the purchase of our MLAs, most of the money was seized in Bengaluru, and the majority of the funds originated from there," he said.

headline: Social media has erupted with pleas from users asking YouTube India to restore the account of Mohammad Irfan, a resident of a Delhi slum, whose channel gained a substantial following overnight before being taken down by the video-hosting platform.

Mr. Irfan went viral for reciting the Preamble to the Constitution during the recent Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protest at Jantar Mantar.

After his YouTube channel was taken down, Mr. Irfan took to X, saying the termination was “some kind of mistake” and urging the platform to rectify it.
“My channel was completely new, and I have honestly followed all of YouTube’s guidelines,” Mr. Irfan said in his post on X. “People really liked my content, which is why my subscribers increased. It seems like there was a mistake by your automatic system. Please review my channel again and restore it.”
Mr. Irfan’s channel found a vocal supporter in veteran journalist Ajit Anjum, who posted several times on X in support of the page while it was active, and after it was taken down.
“A young man named Mohammad Irfan, who lives in a slum in Delhi, started his YouTube channel just yesterday with our support,” Mr. Anjum posted on X on Sunday (August 2, 2026). “From yesterday evening until this morning, his channel gained more than 70,000 subscribers.”
“Suddenly this morning, his YouTube channel was terminated,” he added. “How did a working-class young man manage to gain so many subscribers in such a short time? That in itself is an extraordinary achievement. So why did YouTube terminate his channel so abruptly?,” the post said.
Several other social media users also posted in support of Mr. Irfan’s page, saying that the content and the channel were genuine, and that its termination was the result of a mistake by Google-owned YouTube’s automated systems. They urged the platform to rectify the issue.

headline: 3 states, 3 bypolls: All eyes on PK, Ashutosh Tiwari as Bankipur, Datia, Manjalpur await verdict on Monday

3 states, 3 bypolls: All eyes on PK, Ashutosh Tiwari as Bankipur, Datia, Manjalpur await verdict on Monday
Both Bankipur and Datia have become prestige battles for the Bharatiya Janata Party, with both being traditional strongholds of the saffron party.
The results of three assembly by-elections in three states will be declared on Monday, with the spotlight on Bihar's Bankipur and Madhya Pradesh's Datia.
The third seat is Gujarat's Manjalpur. Voting for all three bypolls was held on July 30.
Both Bankipur and Datia have emerged as prestige battles for the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), as both are considered traditional saffron party strongholds. Bankipur was previously represented by BJP national president Nitin Nabin, while Datia is the political bastion of former Madhya Pradesh home minister Narottam Mishra.
Datia assembly bypoll
Mishra did not get a ticket for the by-election for the seat he lost in the 2023 assembly polls to Congress candidate Rajendra Bharti.
The bypoll was necessitated after a Delhi court in April this year sentenced Bharti to three years' imprisonment in a cheating case, leading to the termination of his assembly membership.
Violence erupted in the aftermath of the ticket denial, with Mishra's supporters clashing with the police. The former minister later shed tears as he promised full support to the BJP candidate, Ashutosh Tiwari.
The outcome of the Datia assembly bypoll may not alter the stability of the BJP government in the state, but political observers believe it carries wider implications, coming against the backdrop of recent student protests and the resignation of Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan.
According to analysts, the closely watched result, slated for Monday, could significantly shape the political standing of both the ruling BJP and the Opposition Congress in the state ahead of the 2028 assembly elections.
The main contest is widely seen as being between Tiwari and Congress nominee Ghanshyam Singh.
District Election Officer Swapnil Wankhede said counting would begin at 8 am on Monday with postal ballots, followed by votes polled through electronic voting machines (EVMs).
The Bankipur battle
The high-stakes assembly bye-election in Bihar's Bankipur-182 constituency concluded with a moderate turnout, recording approximately 34.16 per cent total voter participation on Thursday, according to the Election Commission.
The Bankipur seat fell vacant after BJP leader Nitin Nabin resigned as MLA following his election to the Rajya Sabha. The BJP has fielded Neeraj Kumar Sinha, while Jan Suraaj Party founder Prashant Kishor has thrown his hat in the contest.
What would have been a straightforward election for the BJP, which recently made Samrat Chaudhary its first-ever chief minister in the state, has been complicated by the entry and relentless campaigning of Prashant Kishor.
Kishor has claimed that he would defeat the BJP in the election, which, if it happens, would be a major embarrassment for the ruling party.
The BJP has fielded Neeraj Kumar Sinha from the seat, while RJD’s Rekha Kumari is also in the fray.
The Manjalpur election
The Manjalpur Assembly by-election in Gujarat was also held on July 30, recording a voter turnout of approximately 37.5 per cent. This high-stakes bypoll was triggered by the death of veteran Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) MLA and former minister Yogesh Patel on June 2, 2026, who had held the consecutive legislative seat for decades.
The election is a direct face-off between BJP’s Satish Govindbhai Patel and Congress’s Bhikhabhai Rabari.

headline: Climate change shifts malaria risk to southern, East Africa: Study
full_text:
Climate change shifts malaria risk to southern, East Africa: Study
The southern and East African regions expected to be hit the hardest in the future are also regions that aren’t accustomed to needing to fight the disease today
Climate change has increased childhood malaria and could continue to do so in southern and East Africa where communities are less experienced at tackling the disease, while reducing the risk in today’s hotspots as temperatures become too high for mosquitoes, according to a new study published in Nature.
The study— The past and future impact of climate change on childhood malaria in Africa— quantifies climate change’s historical and future impact in sub-Saharan Africa’s children, where most cases and deaths occur. It finds that climate change has slightly increased malaria overall.
Looking ahead, rising temperatures could increase the malaria risk in southern and East Africa while reducing it where it is most rampant today as it becomes so hot that even mosquitos struggle to survive.
“Climate change isn’t just making malaria worse or better—it’s moving it,” said co-author Tamma Carleton, faculty head of Research for the Climate Impact Lab and an assistant professor at the University of California, Berkeley, in a statement. “Whether a place sees elevated malaria risks or reduced burdens under climate change depends on how hot it is today. We see relief in the current hotspots and new risk nearly everywhere else.”
The study finds that climate change has slightly suppressed the spread of the disease in the warm, malaria hotbeds of today, and will continue to as it gets too hot for the disease to flourish—posing other human health threats. This is especially the case in many large West African nations (Nigeria, Burkina Faso, Mali), where climate change will reduce cases by 5 percent. In extremely hot Sahelian countries (Niger, Gambia, Guinea-Bissau, Somalia) the disease may actually be fully eliminated.
The opposite is true for cooler regions where malaria isn’t a significant problem today, such as southern Africa and high-elevation east Africa. In these areas, climate change is slowly making the temperature more suitable for mosquitoes to spread malaria, increasing cases by 5 percent in the Ethiopian highlands (Kenya, Burundi) and by similarly large increases in Angola, Zambia, and northeast South Africa. By 2100, the risk could increase by 20 percent in regions like the Rift Valley and coastal southern Africa, creating new malaria challenges.
But efforts to reduce emissions can change this trajectory. If the world is able to meet the 2°C warming threshold, this would avert 5 excess cases per 1,000 children in southern Africa and more in the east African highlands. It would also reduce the other widespread climate impacts that will be felt in central and western Africa as the planet continues to heat up. Further, while mitigation is crucial, so is adaptation. The southern and East African regions expected to be hit the hardest in the future are also regions that aren’t accustomed to needing to fight the disease today.
“Governments, health systems and communities must adapt to the evolving malaria threat,” said co-author Christopher Trisos, director of the Climate Risk Lab and Principal Research, Officer at the African Climate and Development Initiative at University of Cape Town. “That means getting ready now to implement more aggressive anti-malaria programs in cooler regions of sub-Saharan Africa where malaria risk is growing, and which can be less experienced at tackling it. Inclusive economic development, and global health financing of effective surveillance, disease control, and better healthcare will be crucial to help confront increased malaria rates caused by climate change in eastern and southern Africa.”
The authors make clear that both climate mitigation and adaptation actions, including malaria elimination strategies, will be needed.
“Malaria was one of the first health outcomes linked to climate change, but it’s taken a quarter century to be sure which direction things are headed,” said co-author Colin Carlson, assistant professor of Epidemiology at Yale University. “The big story here is the opportunity for action: so far, elimination efforts have counteracted climate change impacts by nearly 200-fold. Malaria elimination within a generation is not only possible, but one of the best ways to protect frontline populations from climate change impacts.”

headline: West Bengal to fine builders for dumping materials on roads from September 1
full_text:
West Bengal to fine builders for dumping materials on roads from September 1
Agnimitra Paul announced fines from September 1 for anyone storing construction materials on public roads. The warning broadens West Bengal's civic discipline drive to vacant plots, parking violations and footpath encroachment.
West Bengal Urban Development and Municipal Affairs Minister Agnimitra Paul said on Sunday that people who leave construction materials such as sand, bricks and stones on public roads while building houses will face penalties from September 1. She said roads cannot be used to store such materials and property owners must keep them within their premises.
Paul also said owners of vacant plots would be responsible for keeping their land clean, and warned of strict action against illegal parking. She urged hawkers not to occupy entire footpaths, but said no eviction drive against them would be carried out until the end of the Durga Puja festivities.
Speaking to reporters on the sidelines of a programme at the Siliguri Municipal Corporation, Paul said, “People cannot leave stones, sand and bricks on the road while constructing houses. We will impose fines. Roads are not anyone's private property.”
She said landowners cannot leave vacant plots overgrown with bushes or clogged with drains and waterbodies for years, as such conditions could contribute to mosquito breeding and increase the risk of diseases such as dengue.
Maintaining vacant land, like maintaining one's house and its surroundings, is the responsibility of the owner, she said. Reiterating the government's recent measures to improve civic discipline, Paul said vehicles must be parked only in designated parking spaces and reminded people that the state government is introducing a dedicated parking app.
Those parking cars or motorcycles on footpaths would also face hefty fines, she added. Paul also urged hawkers occupying entire footpaths to move back and leave adequate space for pedestrians.
In summary, Paul announced fines from September 1 for keeping construction materials on public roads, said vacant plot owners would have to keep their land clean, warned of action against illegal parking and asked hawkers to leave space on footpaths, while saying no eviction drive against them would be carried out until the end of the Durga Puja festivities.

headline: Maharashtra’s anti-conversion law takes effect
full_text:
Maharashtra’s anti-conversion law takes effect
The gazette was published after the legislation was approved by President Droupadi Murmu on July 17, paving the way for its implementation in the state.
Maharashtra became the 13th Indian state to notify an anti-conversion law, with the controversial Maharashtra Freedom of Religion Act taking effect after the state government published the legislation in its official gazette on July 30.
The gazette was published after the legislation was approved by President Droupadi Murmu on July 17, paving the way for its implementation in the state.
Also Read | Basic structure touchstone for anti-conversion laws
What is the law?
The law criminalises religious conversions carried out through force, allurement, fraud, inducement or marriage by making it a cognisable offence. This includes interfaith marriages where conversion is alleged to have taken place through such means, particularly if objections are raised by the families of either party.
The law makes unlawful religious conversion a cognisable and non-bailable offence punishable with imprisonment of up to seven years.
Among its most controversial provisions is the requirement that a person intending to convert must give 60 days’ notice to the designated authority.
The act also places the burden of proof that the religious conversion was voluntary on the person accused of carrying out the conversion, as well as on anyone alleged to have assisted or aided it.
The legislation has been widely opposed by civil rights groups as a violation of an individual’s right to freedom and personal privacy. It is seen as an attempt to curb interfaith marriages, particularly instances involving a Hindu woman marrying a non-Hindu man, where conversion to the latter’s faith may take place. Civil liberties groups believe the legislation could be misused in various ways, especially to harass interfaith couples.
Also Read | UP anti-conversion law doesn’t bar interfaith couples from live-in relationships: HC
When was the bill passed?
The Bill was passed by both houses of the Maharashtra legislature earlier this year, with governor Jishnu Dev Varma giving his assent on April 6. It was published in the state’s official gazette on July 30 after it received presidential assent.
“Legal action may now be initiated in cases involving unlawful religious conversions in the state, strictly in accordance with the provisions of the new act,” said a senior official from the state home department.
Provisions of law
The legislation is expected to make interfaith marriages difficult. Once an individual provides notice, the designated authority is required to make it public and invite objections within 30 days. They must then conduct a police inquiry into the intention, purpose and circumstances of the proposed conversion. If the inquiry concludes that the conversion is unlawful, criminal proceedings may be initiated.
Under the act, any religious conversion carried out through allurement, coercion, force, misrepresentation, fraud, deceit or other unlawful means is illegal. It also treats as unlawful any religious conversion carried out through the solemnization of a marriage or a relationship on the promise of marriage if such means are used.
The legislation further mandates that the individual or institution conducting the conversion must submit a declaration to the designated authority within 21 days of the ceremony. Failure to do so will render the conversion null and void.

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Sunday expressed deep sorrow over the devastation caused by heavy rains in Kerala, offering condolences to the families of eight people who lost their lives and urging party workers to assist in relief and recovery operations."Deeply saddened by the devastation caused by heavy rains across Kerala. My heartfelt condolences to the families of the eight people who have lost their lives. May those still missing be found safe, and the injured make a swift recovery," he said in a post on X.
The Congress leader also added that the state government was making every possible effort to support affected families and coordinate relief operations. "I urge all Congress workers and volunteers to assist these efforts in every possible way," he said, urging people to remain vigilant, especially in hilly regions, and follow authorities' guidance.
"Kerala stands united in this difficult hour. I stand firmly with every affected family," Rahul Gandhi added.Kerala chief minister V D Satheesan confirmed that eight people have died, an equal number are missing and 13 others injured in the heavy rains that triggered landslides, waterlogging and property damage across the state. In a statement, he said 27 houses were completely destroyed, 196 homes partially damaged and 5,792 people have been shifted to 209 relief camps.
Satheesan said that despite a reduction in rainfall, people should remain vigilant, especially in hilly areas. He said the government would ensure assistance to families of the deceased and those who lost homes and livelihoods.Revenue minister A P Anilkumar told reporters the situation was improving and was under control. He said damaged roads had been restored in many areas, though some restrictions on vehicular movement remained. He added that alerts had been issued for several districts and preparations were in place.According to the Kerala State Disaster Management Authority, the state received up to 320 mm of rainfall in some parts on Saturday, with Ayyankunnu in Kannur district recording the highest. The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services warned of huge waves of 2.7 to 3.5 meters along the northern Kerala coast and advised fishermen and coastal residents to be vigilant.On Sunday morning, while rains subsided, water had not receded from flooded areas, with people seen travelling using small boats. Karnataka BJP chief reaches out to CM Vijay over water-sharing dispute
NEW DELHI: Karnataka BJP president BY Vijayendra has written to Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay, urging him to adopt a cooperative approach to the long-running Cauvery water dispute and support the proposed Mekedatu reservoir project, saying the river should 'unite our people, rather than divide them.'The appeal comes amid renewed tensions between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu after the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) directed Karnataka to release 3,500 cusecs of water per day to Tamil Nadu for 15 days.
The direction has triggered protests in Karnataka, while the DMK has moved the Supreme Court seeking implementation of the water release order and clearance of the accumulated shortfall.In his letter, Vijayendra said differences between neighbouring states were natural but should be resolved through dialogue and statesmanship."As neighbouring states, differences are inevitable. What matters is how we resolve them," he wrote.
Referring to the earlier resolution of the dispute over the Thiruvalluvar statue in Bengaluru, Vijayendra said former Karnataka chief minister BS Yediyurappa and former Tamil Nadu chief minister M Karunanidhi had demonstrated that difficult issues could be settled when larger public interest prevailed."Their maturity demonstrated that even difficult issues can be resolved when the larger interests of our people prevail.
That is the spirit in which I appeal to you today," he wrote.The Karnataka BJP chief said the Cauvery was a lifeline for crores of people in Bengaluru and several towns across the Cauvery basin, including both Kannadigas and Tamilians living in Karnataka."At a time when inadequate and erratic monsoons have placed enormous stress on farmers and citizens alike, their concerns cannot be overlooked," he said.Vijayendra also urged Vijay to reconsider Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu reservoir project, saying it would help meet Bengaluru's drinking water needs without affecting Tamil Nadu's legitimate share of Cauvery waters."I also appeal to you to view the Mekedatu project in the spirit of cooperation. Let the Cauvery unite our people, rather than divide them," the letter said.
The Cauvery water dispute is one of India's longest-running inter-state river disputes involving Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry. It centres on the sharing of the Cauvery river, which is a major source of drinking water and irrigation for millions of people.The Supreme Court's 2018 judgment largely upheld the Cauvery Water Disputes Tribunal's water-sharing formula and led to the creation of the Cauvery Water Management Authority (CWMA) and the Cauvery Water Regulation Committee (CWRC) to oversee implementation.
However, disagreements frequently resurface during years of low rainfall, with Karnataka arguing it needs water for its own drinking and irrigation requirements, while Tamil Nadu insists on releases as mandated by the tribunal and the Supreme Court.The latest flashpoint is Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu reservoir project, which the state says is intended to improve Bengaluru's drinking water supply and generate hydroelectric power.Tamil Nadu has opposed the project, arguing that it could affect its allocated share of Cauvery waters and violate the existing water-sharing framework.

Sources, however, said candidates who left the examination hall carrying question papers and OMR sheets had violated Karnataka Examinations Authority rules and were therefore not allowed to re-enter.
Similar problems were reported at a few other centres, though most candidates resumed writing the examination after supervisors explained the prescribed procedure.
Deputy Commissioner K Anand, Superintendent of Police Laxman Nimbargi and other senior officials visited the Tikota centre to assess the situation.

headline: Researchers at the Central University of Kerala (CUK) have secured an Indian patent for a novel multifunctional catalyst preparation technology that could help convert biomass and petrochemical feedstocks into cleaner fuels and other value added chem...

Researchers at the Central University of Kerala (CUK) have secured an Indian patent for a novel multifunctional catalyst preparation technology that could help convert biomass and petrochemical feedstocks into cleaner fuels and other value added chemicals more efficiently.
The patent was granted for ‘Method for the Preparation of ITQ-2 Metal Oxy-Hydroxide Composite Material Thereof’ (Indian Patent No. 596368). The innovation was developed by Prof. A. Sakthivel along with researchers Soumya B.N. and Nimisha N.P.
Prof. Sakthivel said the team had developed a multifunctional catalyst, a specially engineered synthetic material known as zeolite, that can speed up chemical reactions required to convert biomass and petroleum-based raw materials into useful products.
“The main innovation is the preparation of the material itself. It is a multifunctional catalyst that combines acidic and redox (reduction-oxidation) properties in a single material, making it more efficient than conventional catalysts,” he said.
According to the researchers, conventional catalysts generally perform only one function, limiting their efficiency. The newly developed catalyst integrates multiple functions enabling chemical reactions to proceed more effectively while improving access to active sites within the material.
The technology is expected to find future applications in the petroleum and petrochemical industries, particularly in the production of cleaner fuels, fuel additives, polymers and other value-added chemicals. Prof. Sakthivel said the research had so far focused on developing and patenting the catalyst material, and commercial fuel production using the technology was yet to begin.

headline: Birbhum police raid aides of absconding stone quarry kingpin Tulu Mondal
full_text:
Birbhum police raid aides of absconding stone quarry kingpin Tulu Mondal
The operation against Mondal started on Wednesday when police seized 15kg of gold bars and ₹28.05 crore from his cousin’s home
The Birbhum district police in Bengal on Sunday raided the homes and offices of several people associated with Md Nazibuddin alias Tulu Mondal, the absconding kingpin of an illegal stone quarry and sand business.
Officials aware of the probe said the investigation focused on his modus operandi which deprived the state of revenue worth hundreds of crores during the Trinamool Congress (TMC) regime.
“Closure notices were sent to eight stone quarries because they were operating without a valid licence. Mondal’s nephew SK Wasim was arrested from Siliguri on Friday while trying to flee to Nepal. Police raided the homes and offices of more relatives and associates of Mondal on Saturday and Sunday,” a Birbhum district police officer said, requesting anonymity.
The operation against Mondal started on Wednesday when police seized 15kg of gold bars and ₹28.05 crore from his cousin’s home, whose husband, a retired state bus driver, was arrested.
After that, the police froze ₹93 crore found in Mondal’s bank accounts and seized 242 vehicles, including over 100 dumpers and some expensive Audi and BMW cars. At least 21 properties, including farm houses, were also sealed.
“Mondal started his career in around 2010-11 as a common labourer who carried stones from quarries to trucks. By 2015, he became the owner of several stone quarries because of his proximity to powerful politicians. By 2020, his company was collecting toll tax from around 2000 trucks that left Birbhum every day carrying stones and sand. He gave only a fraction of the collected tax to the government,” the police officer said.
On Sunday, police searched the home of Ijajul Sheikh, who worked as a manager in Mondal’s quarry business. “We are also on the lookout for Md Mohim, a man who rose fast under Mondal’s guidance,” a second police officer said.
“From the records we seized, it appears that besides his illegal quarry business, Mondal charged ₹2,500–3,000 from each truck loaded beyond the government-regulated limit. Around 1500-2000 trucks passed through the toll booths every day. Mondal used to give only around ₹22 lakh a day to the government,” the officer added.
Police suspect that Tulu Mondal invested in several properties in Dubai and may have fled there. On Thursday, the state told a Birbhum court that the seized gold bars were smuggled from Switzerland, Dubai and Malaysia.
West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari targeted his predecessor on Friday saying, “None of this would have been possible without the direct support of ex-chief minister Mamata Banerjee. Nobody can amass so much money and buy such properties and vehicles in one day.”
Adhikari told the state assembly on July 23 that revenue was stolen in Birbhum.
“The revenue from stone and sand in Birbhum used to be ₹65 crore a year. We collected ₹82 crore in the first month after coming to power. During the former regime the actual revenue was ₹1200 crore but only around ₹100 crore reached the state exchequer,” Adhikari said in his July 23 address before the assembly.
Since most of the TMC leaders from Birbhum, including former district unit president Anubrata Mondal have joined the rebel camp, the Mamata Banerjee faction said the police must take action against the politicians behind Tulu Mondal.
“If Tulu Mondal amassed such wealth then police must act against the politicians behind him,” TMC MLA Kunal Ghosh said.

headline: In India, a towel draped over an office chair often became a symbol of power, associated with a govt job.
full_text:
In India, a towel draped over an office chair often became a symbol of power, associated with a govt job.
Long ago, my father told me a story about a certain âSunil ji. Nobody ever addressed him by his first name, it was always succeeded by a âjiâ, because his office chair was covered with a towel.He would often wear a safari suit & a stiff-upper lip at family weddings. The guy with a govt job, an Afsar (officer), top billing in the arranged marriage market, despite having the lowest basic pay. At one such wedding, his wife blurted out an issue they were facing. Due to some clerical mistake, the details of their salary account was not updated, and Sunil ji wasnât receiving his salary for over 2 years. They found this anomaly just last month. My family was grudgingly impressed, and hoped one of their kids turned out to be a towel-chair guy like Sunil ji.
For much of modern Indiaâs history, there wasn't enough. Jobs. College seats. Telephones. Gas cylinders. Batsmen with a good strike rate. We were short of everything. As if our nation came out of British rule like some of the TV reporters came out of the NEET protest, Gasping for breath, barely surviving the violence with almost all of the valuables stolen, but their morality, virtue and the associated pride intact.
This was India in 1947.Such was the muscle memory of the rule, that we kept presenting our Annual budget at 5 PM IST, so that our British overlords could tune-in after having their breakfast. This tradition continued till 1999, more than 50 years after independence, until the Finance minister Yashwant Sinha, changed it to 11 AM. Imagine. The trauma of British rule never went away, it showed up in our metabolic wiring, in our insulin resistance, in our early onset of diabetes. Primarily due to the British administered famines. The bodies of our ancestors rewired to store fat. When the Brits eventually went back, they left behind quite a few problematic things like bureaucracy, Pakistan & monumental scarcity.When our leaders took over, they knew our demand vastly exceeded the supply, so they had to control the access of resources. And who do you trust to do that?Another British inheritance - The Collectorate. A regiment of people specifically trained to extract from the population, to collect revenues and give it back to the overlords, for whom serving people was optional, a hobby. A lot of them were corrupt too, In contrast there was barely any corruption among British officers, because they were paid almost 70 times the Indian officers. Hence, the Indians had to compensate with corruption. As we know, they continued compensating beyond independence as well. This coterie was assigned to allocate resources to Indians.No wonder, they acquired tremendous power. People began paying to jump the queue. When the government decided who could manufacture, import or expand a factory, permissions themselves became valuable commodities. British raj was eventually succeeded by Inspector Raj. And the underpaid inspectors lived in the same bungalows the British lived in.Economist Robert Klitgaard famously summarized it as:Corruption = Monopoly + discretion - accountabilityWhenever one person has monopoly over a decision, wide discretion, and little accountability, corruption happens.Accountability was like Vitamin-D for the country. We were always deficient. Add to that a lethargic judiciary. Some even justified corruption saying it's an essential lubricant for files to move without friction. A tool to facilitate ease of doing business. Many of the Indian billionaires today, exist due to their ancestors greasing their file-folders with this lubricant generously.Corruption is a chronic illness, it has been embedded in the DNA of a drought-coded, resource starved nation like ours. A government comes to power riding a wave of public anger. The previous regime is portrayed as irredeemably corrupt. Files are opened. Committees are formed. Raids happen. People are content. Finally, someone is cleaning the system.For a while, it genuinely feels different. Time passes, Power stops feeling temporary. The government begins winning elections. The public approval remains high. Loyalists become more confident. Criticism starts sounding less like feedback and more like conspiracy. Every institution gradually fills up with people who think alike.Corruption creeps up again. Like a virus - a parasite that needs a host - like a mosquito or a bat or a pigeon.Parasites don't advertise themselves. They attach themselves to something stronger. In India's case, this host is often identity - caste, religion, language. Every political movement needs an emotional engine. That engine mobilises voters, creates loyalty and builds political capital. Most of the time these issues are legitimate and deeply important. But once emotions become intense enough, they also become excellent camouflage. People stop asking uncomfortable questions because larger battles appear to be underway.
If my religion is under threat, why discuss the waterlogged street near my house?If my caste is finally receiving justice, why focus on procurement irregularities?Not saying, Identity is not important. But we often forget to see whatâs lurking behind it. The virus keeps growing, and one day it becomes bigger than the host, voters can see it, and it gets overthrown. Exit pollsters get shamed. The power of democracy is lauded. Until a new host emerges. The cycle continues. Elections just change the wrapper of the age-old system.Corruption will go away when we make it high-risk and low-reward. High salaries & high conviction rate. A Singaporean minister earns more than a top investment banker. And their corruption watchdog has a conviction rate of 99%. Our ED has at ~1%. This is the crux, until we fix it - another Sunil ji will discover they have a salary account a decade later.

headline: Stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra has cancelled his scheduled shows from Monday to Thursday at a venue in Whitefield and shifted them to another venue in Koramangala.
full_text:
Stand-up comedian Kunal Kamra has cancelled his scheduled shows from Monday to Thursday at a venue in Whitefield and shifted them to another venue in Koramangala.
The development comes after a Hindutva outfit, Hindu Rashtra Samanvaya Samiti, petitioned the Whitefield police, demanding that Mr. Kamra should not be permitted to perform.
They had contended that Mr. Kamra had disrespected Hindu deities.
A senior police official from the Whitefield Division told The Hindu that Mr. Kamra and the organisers of the shows visited the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday and informed that they had decided to cancel the shows. The decision, they said, was taken as the event had become controversial. No law and order incident was reported in connection with the scheduled performance.
Taking to social media platform X, Mr. Kamra on Sunday announced: “Shows for Monday - Tuesday - Wednesday - Thursday shifted to Underground Comedy Club in Koramangala.”
He further said that amount would be refunded to those who had already booked tickets for the Whitefield shows and requested them to book shows at the Koramangala venue afresh.
On Saturday, responding to the Hindutva activists objecting to his shows in Whitefield, Mr. Kamra gave an open invite on X that he would be at the Whitefield Police Station on Sunday to seek permission to perform and any objectors were free to join him to debate on “comedy and culture”. He later said only senior journalist Aakar Patel turned up.
Meanwhile, Mohan Gowda, spokesperson, Hindu Janajagruti Samiti, said that Mr. Kamra shifted the shows after facing strong opposition and appealed to the Koramangala police not to allow him to perform in their jurisdiction.

headline: The Bombay High Court, on Friday (July 31, 2026), refused to grant urgent bail to Ramesh Mhatre, the corporator accused of assaulting a doctor at a municipal hospital in Dombivli. Mhatre is a member of the Shiv Sena, led by Chief Minister Eknath Shin...
full_text:
The Bombay High Court, on Friday (July 31, 2026), refused to grant urgent bail to Ramesh Mhatre, the corporator accused of assaulting a doctor at a municipal hospital in Dombivli. Mhatre is a member of the Shiv Sena, led by Chief Minister Eknath Shinde.
A division bench of Acting Chief Justice Ravindra Dhuge and Justice Gautam Ankhad made the decision after considering the stage of the police investigation. The court noted that the original complainant, Dr. Vaibhav Salunkhe, has not yet conducted the identification parade to confirm the identity of the accused. Additionally, the police are required to record statements from more witnesses and collect further evidence.
The court has directed the state government to provide protection to the victim, Dr. Salunkhe, and other witnesses involved in the case. The bench clarified that the bail application will be heard next on August 6.
In court, Senior Counsel Aabad Ponda, representing Mhatre, argued for bail. He stated that since his client is currently in custody, there is no possibility of pressuring the victim or witnesses. He also submitted that the investigation is largely complete. Ponda informed the court that Mhatre is willing to stay outside Maharashtra for four to six weeks, if necessary, to prevent any influence on the ongoing inquiry. He requested the court grant bail during the remaining investigation period.
Opposing the bail plea, Senior Counsel S.U. Kamdar, representing the Dodian Medical Association, made a strong case against the relief. Kamdar argued that Mhatre’s actions have created a sense of fear among doctors at the municipal hospital. He further alleged that the accused has a history of securing acquittals in multiple cases by pressuring witnesses. Kamdar also claimed that attempts to exert pressure on the complainant and witnesses are still ongoing.
Meanwhile, Advocate General Milind Sathe, appearing for the State Government, provided the court with the current status of the investigation. He stated that a Deputy Commissioner of Police is now leading the probe following a court order. The investigation has so far recorded statements from 26 individuals. Sathe informed the bench that critical procedures, including recording additional witness statements, collecting voice samples of the accused, and sending the victim’s video evidence for forensic analysis, will be completed in the next two weeks. He also gave an assurance that the identification parade for Dr. Salunkhe will be conducted under police security.

headline: Gurugram man, 36, found dead after wife seeks divorce; police probe video recorded by 7-year-old son

Gurugram man, 36, found dead after wife seeks divorce; police probe video recorded by 7-year-old son
The deceased's sister alleged that he had been facing marital discord and claimed that his wife had sought a divorce
A 36-year-old man was found dead at his residence in Gurugram on Thursday, with police launching a probe after his family alleged that his wife had sought a divorce and that the couple had been facing marital disputes.
The deceased, who worked as an associate operator at a multinational company, was originally from Amritsar, lived with his family in Surat Nagar, Gurugram, news agency PTI reported.
Investigators are examining a mobile phone video recorded by the couple's seven-year-old son after the incident.

The incident came to light when the man's wife informed relatives about his death. At the time of the incident, only the couple and their seven-year-old son were present at home, the report added.
The deceased's sister alleged that he had been facing marital discord and claimed that his wife had sought a divorce. She alleged that the circumstances surrounding his death were suspicious and demanded a thorough investigation.
His father also alleged foul play and urged police to investigate all possible angles.
Wife detained
Based on a complaint filed by the family, police have detained the man's wife for questioning and registered a case. Investigating officer Mahender Singh said police are awaiting the post-mortem report to ascertain the exact cause of death.
"We are awaiting the post-mortem report to ascertain the exact cause of death. Action will be taken as per law," the officer said according to PTI.
The couple, who married in 2018 after meeting at their workplace, have a seven-year-old son. Police said further investigation is underway.
Earlier in July, in another case from Gurugram, a missing person's complaint led police to the body of a 25-year-old woman inside a paying guest (PG) accommodation in Sector 55.

headline: 'Threw slipper, carried a knife': What we know about attack on Pappu Yadav
full_text:
'Threw slipper, carried a knife': What we know about attack on Pappu Yadav
Edited by: Prisha Patnaik / TIMESOFINDIA.COM / Updated: Aug 02, 2026, 20:09 IST
