headline: दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर का आंदोलन पूरे देश में चर्चा में रहा था. अब झारखंड की राजधानी रांची में चल रहे छात्र आंदोलन को लेकर भी सियासी हलचल तेज होती दिख रही है. JPSC और JSSC भर्ती परीक्षाओं में कथित गड़बड़ी के खिलाफ धरने पर बैठे छात्रों को अब कॉकरोच जनता ...
full_text:
दिल्ली के जंतर-मंतर का आंदोलन पूरे देश में चर्चा में रहा था. अब झारखंड की राजधानी रांची में चल रहे छात्र आंदोलन को लेकर भी सियासी हलचल तेज होती दिख रही है. JPSC और JSSC भर्ती परीक्षाओं में कथित गड़बड़ी के खिलाफ धरने पर बैठे छात्रों को अब कॉकरोच जनता पार्टी (CJP) का भी साथ मिल गया है. पार्टी के संस्थापक अभिजीत दिपके ने आंदोलन कर रहे छात्रों से बात करने की जानकारी दी. उन्होंने कहा कि CJP झारखंड के छात्रों के सपोर्ट में है और उनकी मांगों का समर्थन करती है.
बता दें कि रांची के जयपाल सिंह मुंडा स्टेडियम में करीब एक हफ्ते से छात्र अनिश्चितकालीन सत्याग्रह पर बैठे हैं. झारखंड पब्लिक सर्विस कमीशन (JPSC) और झारखंड स्टाफ सिलेक्शन कमीशन (JSSC) परीक्षाओं में कथित गड़बड़ी के आरोपों को लेकर हजारों युवा सड़कों पर उतर चुके हैं. इसी सिलसिले में छात्रों ने रविवार को हाथों में जलती मशालें लेकर विशाल मार्च निकाला. अभ्यर्थियों का साफ कहना है कि जब तक पूरे मामले की CBI जांच का फैसला नहीं होगा, तब तक यह आंदोलन जारी रहेगा.
दिपके ने क्या कहा?
छात्रों को अपना समर्थन देते हुए अभिजीत दिपके ने सोशल मीडिया पर लिखा कि उन्होंने झारखंड में आंदोलन कर रहे अभ्यर्थियों से बात की है. उन्होंने कहा कि CJP इस लड़ाई में पूरी तरह छात्रों के साथ है और उनकी सभी जायज मांगों का समर्थन करती है. वहीं, CJP के प्रवक्ता आशुतोष रांका ने भी सोशल मीडिया पर पोस्ट शेयर की. उन्होंने लिखा कि उनका संगठन झारखंड के युवाओं के साथ मजबूती से खड़ा है.
यह भी पढ़ें: रांची के 'जंतर-मंतर' की मांग कब सुनेगी सरकार? JPSC मामले पर सड़कों पर छात्र
क्यों आंदोलन कर रहे हैं छात्र?
पूरे विवाद की मुख्य वजह 14वीं सिविल सर्विसेज परीक्षा का प्रीलिम्स रिजल्ट है. छात्रों का कहना है कि पासिंग मार्क्स (कट-ऑफ) तय करने में भारी गड़बड़ी हुई और मेरिट लिस्ट पर जिम्मेदार अफसरों के दस्तखत तक नहीं थे. साथ ही, OMR शीट में भी हेरफेर के आरोप लग रहे हैं. सबसे चौंकाने वाली बात यह है कि परीक्षा कराने का ठेका लखनऊ की जिस 'TDPL' कंपनी को दिया गया, उसे महज एक महीने पहले ही राज्य में ब्लैकलिस्ट किया गया था. हालांकि सरकार के कहने पर CID मामले की जांच कर रही है, लेकिन छात्र केंद्रीय एजेंसियों से निष्पक्ष जांच कराने पर अड़े हैं.
धरने पर बैठे युवाओं का कहना है कि सिर्फ सीआईडी जांच से न्याय नहीं मिलेगा. उनका दावा है कि पहले भी ऐसे मामलों में जांच हुई, लेकिन कोई ठोस नतीजा सामने नहीं आया. बड़ी संख्या में आंदोलन में शामिल युवा किसान और साधारण परिवारों से आते हैं. उनका कहना है कि वे किसी की दया नहीं, बल्कि अपनी मेहनत के दम पर निष्पक्ष मौका चाहते हैं. इसके अलावा, छात्र OMR शीट में 'Not Attempted' (अटेम्प्ट नहीं किया) का पांचवां विकल्प जोड़ने की मांग भी कर रहे हैं. उनका कहना है कि इससे भविष्य में OMR शीट से छेड़छाड़ की आशंका कम होगी.
मुद्दे पर राजनीति भी तेज
छात्र आंदोलन के बीच झारखंड की राजनीति भी गरमा गई है. मुख्यमंत्री आवास पर 'इंडिया' गठबंधन के विधायकों की बैठक हुई. बैठक के बाद प्रदीप यादव ने कहा कि सभी विधायक एकजुट हैं और सीएम हेमंत सोरेन के नेतृत्व पर भरोसा जताया है.
दूसरी तरफ बाबूलाल मरांडी ने छात्रों का समर्थन करते हुए सरकार से CBI जांच कराने की मांग की है. उनका कहना है कि युवाओं के भविष्य से जुड़े इस मामले में निष्पक्ष जांच होनी चाहिए.

headline: Police detained office-bearers of the Maharashtra Youth Congress and Pune City Congress from their residences shortly after midnight on August 1. The action preceded the visit of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval ...
full_text:
Police detained office-bearers of the Maharashtra Youth Congress and Pune City Congress from their residences shortly after midnight on August 1. The action preceded the visit of Union Home Minister Amit Shah and National Security Advisor Ajit Doval to the city.
The detentions took place on the day of the visit. Police personnel reached the residences of the office-bearers around midnight. The individuals were taken into custody. The police described the action as a preventive measure. The measure was intended to maintain order during the visit of the Union Home Minister and the National Security Advisor.
Mr. Shah arrived in Pune on Thursday (July 30, 2026) night for a two-day visit. He presented the Lokmanya Tilak Memorial National Award to Mr. Doval at a function on Friday (July 31). The day marked the death anniversary of Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak and the birth anniversary of Lokshahir Annabhau Sathe. The state held programmes to commemorate these occasions. Mr. Shah paid floral tribute at the memorial of Annabhau Sathe after the award ceremony.

The Youth Congress condemned the action. The organisation stated that peaceful protest and dissent are rights protected under the constitution. headline: 70,000 drug smugglers arrested in Punjab's 500-day anti-drug drive: Bhagwant Mann
full_text:
70,000 drug smugglers arrested in Punjab's 500-day anti-drug drive: Bhagwant Mann
Bhagwant Mann said Punjab's anti-drug campaign has completed 500 days and will continue unabated. He said arrests, rehabilitation and village volunteers have turned it into a people's movement.
Punjab Chief Minister Bhagwant Mann on Sunday said his government’s anti-drug campaign, ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’, will continue until the menace is wiped out from the state. He said the drive has completed 500 days and asserted that the government has taken strict action against smugglers while also focusing on treatment, rehabilitation and public awareness.
Speaking at a meeting with Village Defence Committee volunteers, Mann said 70,000 drug smugglers have been arrested during the campaign and that 1.25 lakh volunteers across 13,000 villages have become the backbone of the movement. He said the fight against drugs would go on until Punjab becomes completely drug-free.
Addressing the gathering, Mann said, “Yudh Nashean Virudh has completed 500 days and our Village Defence Committees have completed one year.” He added, “I thank the people of Punjab for turning both these initiatives into a people’s movement. The day is not far when together these two movements will completely eradicate the menace of drugs from Punjab.”
The chief minister said he was indebted to all those serving Punjab in the true spirit and that their determination showed any challenge, however big, could be overcome through collective resolve. “The problem that once appeared insurmountable is steadily coming to an end within 500 days. Many people believed that this curse could never be eliminated, but with the active support of the people we have broken the backbone of this menace,” he said.
Mann said the AAP government had ensured treatment for those caught in drug addiction by taking them to de-addiction and rehabilitation centres so they could live with dignity and self-respect. He also said Punjab, once branded as ‘Udta Punjab’, was now changing into “Padhta Te Tandrust Punjab” as reflected in the state’s top ranking in school education, record JEE and NEET success, and merit-based employment.
On education, Mann said Punjab had emerged as the top-performing state in primary and middle-school education because of the state government’s sustained efforts over the last four years. He said the government had upgraded primary and middle-school education, strengthened the overall system, introduced smart classrooms and ensured advanced training for teachers.
“Punjab has surpassed Kerala, Maharashtra, and Delhi to secure the number one position in primary and middle-school education. The latest figures released by NITI Aayog confirm that Punjab now ranks first in the country in this sector,” he added.
Mann said the anti-drug campaign and the village committees had together become a people’s movement, and reiterated that the government would continue its crackdown, rehabilitation efforts and awareness drive until Punjab is free from drugs.

headline: Though Wayanad has witnessed heavy rain over the past few days, cumulative southwest monsoon rainfall in the hill district remains around 50% below normal after the first two months of the season.
full_text:
Though Wayanad has witnessed heavy rain over the past few days, cumulative southwest monsoon rainfall in the hill district remains around 50% below normal after the first two months of the season.
Data released by the Hume Weather Lab of the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology shows that Wayanad received only 802 mm of average rainfall between June 1 and July 31, against the India Meteorological department (IMD) normal of 1,600 mm for the period.
This year, the onset of the southwest monsoon was delayed, a phenomenon experts attributed to the combined influence of global climate change and the El Niño phenomenon.
“The recent spell of heavy rain has, however, brought some relief. Between July 27 and 31 (five days), Wayanad recorded 199 mm of rainfall, accounting for nearly 25% of the total rainfall received during the past two months. The prevailing wet spell is expected to continue until August 4,” said C.K. Vishnudas, executive director of the Hume Centre for Ecology and Wildlife Biology.
Rainfall distribution across the district has remained highly uneven. Lakkidi recorded the highest rainfall at 2,548 mm, while Muthanga received the least at just 228 mm. Among local bodies, Thondernad grama panchayat registered the highest average rainfall of 1,990 mm, whereas Noolpuzha grama panchayat recorded the lowest average of 277 mm.
The late July rain has also brought down temperatures across Wayanad. The average daytime temperature has dropped to around 25°C over the past five days, ending the unusually warm conditions that prevailed during the early weeks of the monsoon when rainfall remained scarce.

headline: The discharge of water from Maharashtra slightly increased after continued rains in Maharashtra and Belagavi on Sunday (August 2). The discharge was at around 1,23,238 cusecs, 704 cusecs more than the discharge on Saturday (August 1).

The inflow into the Malaprabha dam was 4,862 cusecs while the outflow was 1,194 cusecs. It has around 12 tmcft of water against the full capacity of 37 tmcft.

Live storage is 226.44 tmcft, against 376.16 tmcft capacity — around 60.2%, said another officer.
Inflow into Bhadra dam, Tungabhadra, Ghataprabha and Almatti dam have increased, while inflow into Malaprabha and Narayanapura dams have recorded a marginal decline.

headline: Grey monsoon clouds hang low, almost touching the white domes and arched gateways of the Shiromani Shri Guru Ravidass Mandir.
full_text:
Grey monsoon clouds hang low, almost touching the white domes and arched gateways of the Shiromani Shri Guru Ravidass Mandir.
The religious complex, spread across 11.5 acres, marks the skyline along the Grand Trunk Road in Chak Hakim village, Phagwara, in Punjab’s Kapurthala district.
The Guru Ghar, as it is known among followers, is dedicated to the 15th-century saint-poet Guru Ravidass. It serves as a place of worship but has also become a symbol of the Dalit community’s rising economic, religious and political assertiveness, reflecting its gradual shift from historical marginalisation.
Punjab has an agrarian economy, with Jat Sikhs, the dominant landowning community, and Scheduled Castes (SCs) constituting a significant share of its population. According to the 2011 Census, SCs account for nearly 32% of Punjab’s population, the highest proportion among all States. Yet, historically, land ownership has remained concentrated among Jat Sikhs. Most SCs have traditionally worked as agricultural labourers for Jat Sikh landowners, the economically dominant community that has over the years exercised considerable influence over State politics.
For generations, the social hierarchy was reflected in religious and residential architecture, particularly in rural areas. While large gurdwaras were built by the dominant landowning Jat Sikhs at central locations, Dalit communities, historically landless and marginalised, often constructed smaller places of worship. Their homes, too, were typically located on the fringes of villages.
Today, complexes such as the one at Chak Hakim are changing that pattern. Davinder Kultham, president of the Shiromani Shri Guru Ravidass Mandir Prabandhak Committee, which manages the gurdwara’s affairs, says that small landholdings were among the factors that prompted people to migrate in search of better livelihoods. Over time, migration by members of the SC community to Dubai, the U.K., the U.S. and Canada played a significant role in improving the community’s socio-economic status, particularly in Punjab’s Doaba region.
Punjab is broadly divided into the Malwa, Doaba, and Majha regions, and the Dalit population is unevenly distributed across these regions. Its largest concentration is in Doaba, the region between the Beas and Sutlej rivers. Guru Ravidass was born near Varanasi into a Chamar family, a community traditionally engaged in leather work and historically regarded as “untouchable” within the Hindu caste hierarchy. After Independence, the community was accorded SC status as part of the country’s affirmative action policy in education and public employment.
On the land of a guru
“Today, the third and fourth generations of our community are living abroad. Money sent home by non-resident Indians (NRIs) has brought about a marked change in how Dalit families see themselves and what they aspire to,” says Kultham.
He says the Guru Ghar at Chak Hakim has largely taken shape thanks to contributions from NRIs, with nearly 70% of the funds coming from members of the Dalit community settled overseas. Although construction began in the 1960s, it gathered pace only after 2005.
“The land for this gurdwara was donated decades ago by a Dalit NRI who owned a textile factory in England. We run a school up to Class 10 for underprivileged children, where the fee is nominal,” Kultham says. The complex also has a charitable dispensary, a community kitchen and accommodation for travellers. “Years ago, this would have been unimaginable,” he says, pointing to a section of the complex where a sarovar (sacred pool) is under construction.
Chak Hakim holds deep religious significance for the Ravidassia community. Followers believe Guru Ravidass stayed here for about 70 days and held spiritual gatherings. Across the road from the Guru Ghar stands an older shrine, whose foundation was laid in 1845. Devotees believe it marks the exact spot where Guru Ravidass stayed. It was only in the 19th century that the ascetic Mahant Baba Hira Das, revered as a saint, identified the site as the place where the guru had stayed.
The power of money and mobilisation
Forty-five-year-old Gian Sheel from Dhaddey village near Phagwara traces his family’s story to his grandfather, who worked in the leather industry when it was still thriving in the Doaba region. As larger businesses entered the trade and local units began to decline, his grandfather migrated to England in 1952.
“My grandfather moved to England, where he worked as a factory labourer. Over the years, his earnings helped the family establish a financial footing back home. With that money, he bought around 26 acres of land in Narur village near Hoshiarpur,” says Sheel.
His grandfather also purchased a tractor, sowing and harvesting machinery, and livestock. While Sheel’s uncles and their children eventually settled abroad, his father stayed back to manage the family’s farm and household.
Sheel, who now runs a spice business and is a social activist associated with an informal organisation called Volunteer Indian Social Integration of Nationhood, says that while remittances from the NRI diaspora have contributed, albeit modestly, to the socio-economic empowerment of Dalits, government welfare programmes, both at the Centre and in the State, have largely failed to achieve the same objective.
“These initiatives fall into two categories. One comprises party-specific policies. The other consists of constitutional obligations, which must be fulfilled regardless of which party is in power. These include ensuring representation and implementing reservations in education, employment and politics,” he says.
In Punjab, he adds, the issue of promotions under the 85th Constitutional Amendment remains unresolved. Successive governments have also failed to create awareness among SCs about welfare schemes. “Genuine sincerity is lacking, regardless of which party comes to power.”
Sheel says the Dalit community has long been politically conscious in Punjab, particularly in the Doaba region. “The Ad Dharm movement, which sought dignity and a distinct identity for the “untouchable” castes, began in the Doaba region under Mangoo Ram Mugowalia in the 1920s. Around the same period, Dr. B.R. Ambedkar’s emergence in public life also contributed to the political mobilisation of Dalits,” he says.
However, he argues that divisions within the SC community have limited its political empowerment. According to him, the fragmentation of Dalit votes among the major political parties has prevented the community from emerging as a unified political force.
With the Punjab Assembly election due in early 2027, the Congress, the Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD), the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) and the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) are all courting Dalit voters, underlining the community’s growing political significance. Leaders across party lines have been making frequent visits to various deras — socio-religious institutions that have long served as important centres of social and spiritual life, particularly for marginalised communities.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s visit to Dera Sachkhand Ballan in Ballan village, Jalandhar, on February 1 this year, to mark Guru Ravidass’s 649th birth anniversary, and his subsequent meeting with dera head Sant Niranjan Dass on July 17 are seen as part of the BJP’s outreach to Dalit voters. Leaders of the ruling AAP, the SAD and the Congress have also been visiting various deras to seek the blessings of their heads.
Poverty behind under-representation
Yash Barna, chairperson of the Guru Ravidass Tiger Force, an organisation that works on issues affecting the Dalit community, recalls how, in the past, hardworking members of the community were often denied fair wages in villages and towns.“During my childhood, I saw this in our village. They were either given basic daily meals by members of the Jat community in exchange for their labour or paid with a small share of the agricultural produce,” he says.
Barna says that while the Dalit community had intellectuals, poverty remained a major constraint. “As our people gained access to education and employment, those who went abroad also realised the importance of political and religious representation. Today, with the support of intellectuals, working professionals and the NRI diaspora, we feel politically and religiously stronger,” he says.
However, despite the community’s economic and political progress, Barna believes social barriers persist. “The Sri Guru Granth Sahib is installed at the Guru Ghar. Yet, the majority of those who visit are from our community. It is still seen as an SC space,” he says.
On July 25, members of the SC community gathered at Ambedkar Bhawan in Phagwara, which houses a gurdwara and a cultural and literary centre run by the Shri Guru Ravidass Sabha Trust. Most of those present were retired government employees living in the Urban Estate locality. Many have close relatives settled abroad, and a majority of the trust’s nearly 200 members also have children living overseas. Through the trust, they run a dispensary, a charitable laboratory and a computer centre for children. They see these initiatives as a way of giving back to society.
“Most of us are retired government employees. Our parents’ generation lived in nearby villages, and as our economic condition improved, we moved to the town. Many members of our older generation and many of our children and relatives have settled abroad. They help us financially in running these social initiatives,” says Ghanshyam, general secretary of the Sabha.
He says the trust’s expenditure broadly falls into two categories: recurring monthly expenses and infrastructure development. “These efforts have benefited not only the SC community but other marginalised sections of society as well.”
Sharing his experience, Parvinder Raju, who retired earlier this year as a senior manager at a public sector bank and now lives next to Ambedkar Bhawan, recalls how support from relatives abroad made a significant difference during his childhood. “My maternal uncle moved to England in 1977. My father worked in a government job and was particular about our education. There were five siblings, and all of us graduated. But those were difficult times. Whenever there was a need, whether for education or family weddings, my uncle would help us,” he says. Even during periods of illness, he adds, the family knew there was someone they could turn to for financial support.
Socially mobile
The impact of emigration is most visible in Jalandhar, Hoshiarpur, Kapurthala and Shaheed Bhagat Singh Nagar (Nawanshahr), the districts in the Doaba region, where an estimated one in three families has at least one member working abroad. Remittances from the Dalit diaspora have contributed to a marked change in the community’s self-image and aspirations.
Dr. Amanpreet Kaur, an Assistant Professor at Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, who has extensively researched Dalit issues in Punjab, says international migration among Punjabi Dalits, particularly from the Doaba region, has played an important role in their social mobility.
“They have settled across the world and constitute a significant section of the Punjabi diaspora. They advocate achieved status rather than ascribed status. A large number are employed in the Gulf countries, and their remittances have significantly benefited their families,” she says.
In her 2019 study, Role of Dalit Diaspora in the Mobility of the Disadvantaged in Doaba Region of Punjab, Kaur argues that these developments have made the community more socially, politically and religiously assertive.
Varun Bangar, the sarpanch of Chak Hakim, where about 80% of the population belongs to the SC community, says the village has prospered over the years. “While the diaspora’s contribution to village development has been limited, remittances have significantly improved the living standards of individual families. The village’s overall development, however, has been driven largely by contributions from residents and government funding,” he says.
Pyare Lal, a former member of the Chak Hakim Block Samiti, agrees.
“At the personal and religious levels, the financial contribution of the SC diaspora has been significant. However, there is scope for greater support for village development,” he says.
Jaswinder Singh, a Phagwara-based social activist, says, “When marginalised communities build institutions of this scale, they send a clear message that their faith, history and identity deserve equal dignity and recognition. However, with a section of the community still disadvantaged, it is important that both the NRI diaspora and governments continue to support efforts to ensure they can live with dignity.”
Punjab Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema, who belongs to the SC community, says the State government is implementing several welfare measures for marginalised communities.
“For the first time, the Punjab Government has reserved posts for Scheduled Castes in the appointment of law officers,” he says. He also cites the Mukh Mantri Mawan Dhian Satkar Yojana launched this year, under which women aged 18 and above from the general category will receive ₹1,000 a month, while those belonging to the SC category will receive ₹1,500.
As Punjab prepares to mark Guru Ravidass’s 650th birth anniversary on February 20, 2027, the grand entrance gate at Chak Hakim stands as a symbol of the Dalit community’s growing religious, social and political assertion, and of its continuing quest for an equal place in Punjab’s social fabric.

headline: J&K Cabinet Minister Javed Ahmed Rana, who holds the Forest, Ecology and Environment and Tribal Affairs portfolio, on Saturday (August 1, 2026) announced that the Tribal Affairs department would be the nodal agency to implement the Forest Rights Act ...
full_text:
J&K Cabinet Minister Javed Ahmed Rana, who holds the Forest, Ecology and Environment and Tribal Affairs portfolio, on Saturday (August 1, 2026) announced that the Tribal Affairs department would be the nodal agency to implement the Forest Rights Act (FRA) 2006, and warned against the issuance of eviction notices to forest dwellers without following the set procedure.
“No notices will be served by the J&K Forest Department to any member of forest dwellers, whether a Schedule Tribe or any other traditional forest dwellers living for decades. These dwellers will not be disturbed or evicted from the forest under occupation till the process of recognition and verification is complete,” said Mr. Rana.
The announcement comes months after the Lok Bhavan and the elected government were at loggerheads over the eviction drive in Jammu’s Sunjwan, Bathindi, Raika, and Sidhra areas in Jammu. The drive had triggered protests by BJP legislators, with the elected government accusing the Forest department of functioning under the directions of the Lok Bhavan.
Mr. Rana said the Tribal department, and not the Forest department will be the nodal department for implementing the FRA in J&K.
“A three-member Project Monitoring Units has been established. No one will be evicted till a set procedure is followed. All the deputy commissioners will speed up the pending cases under the FRA,” he said.
According to the 2011 Census, Jammu and Kashmir has a Scheduled Tribe population of 12.75 lakh, including 8.10 lakh in the Jammu division and 4.64 lakh in the Kashmir division.
The Government is pushing hard to implement the Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006 (FRA) and has expedited the process of receiving, verifying and settling claims through the statutory three-tier mechanism.
An official circular said the Gram Sabha is the statutory authority responsible for initiating the process of determining the nature and extent of individual and community forest rights under the provisions of Section 6 of the Act.
“The Gram Sabha is mandated to receive, scrutinize and verify claims, prepare maps of the recommended claims and forward its recommendations to the Sub-Divisional Level Committee (SDLC) for further examination and decision,” an official spokesman said.
Separately, J&K Legislative Assembly Speaker Abdul Rahim Rather held a public outreach camp at Kanidajan in the Charar-i-Sharief Constituency. An official spokesman said a major concern was raised by the villagers pertaining to the alleged harassment caused by the eviction notices issued by the Forest Department and the obstruction of agricultural activities on lands, “which have been under their possession and cultivation for generations”.
“No one would be allowed to act in violation of the provisions of the FRA. The rights of all eligible beneficiaries under the Act would be protected in letter and spirit adding that no undue harassment of villagers would be tolerated,” said Mr. Rather.
The Speaker cautioned that no individual should attempt to misuse the Act as a pretext for fresh encroachments on forest land or government property. “The law must be implemented fairly and transparently while safeguarding the rights of genuine beneficiaries,” he added.

headline: Honeytrap gang posing as cops, journalists busted in UP; 2 arrested
full_text:
Honeytrap gang posing as cops, journalists busted in UP; 2 arrested
Two accused have been arrested, while a search is underway to arrest two more members of the five-member gang.
A gang that allegedly impersonated police personnel, senior police officers and journalists to run a honeytrap-based extortion racket has been busted in Uttar Pradesh's Meerut, police said on Saturday.
Two accused have been arrested, while a search is underway to arrest two more members of the five-member gang.
The case came to the fore after a resident named Neeraj Pal alleged that he was lured into a honeytrap through a fake female profile, threatened with fabricated criminal charges and forced to transfer money.
Social media posts also claimed that the gang had been running a fake police outpost. However, police have rejected the claim, saying the accused operated from a rented office and not a police station.
VICTIM LURED THROUGH FAKE WOMAN PROFILE, FORCED TO PAY MONEY
According to police, the accused, Shashank Sharma, Rahul Pal and Akash, posed as a woman online and struck up a conversation with Neeraj. Over time, they established an intimate rapport and exchanged photographs with him.
After gaining his trust, they asked Neeraj to meet the woman in person. However, when he reached the designated location, two men approached him instead and demanded money to facilitate the meeting.
The accused then identified themselves as police personnel and journalists, threatened Neeraj with legal action and demanded Rs 2 lakh to settle the matter. They also forced him to transfer Rs 10,000 through Google Pay.
As per the complaint, they also recorded videos of Neeraj and further used them for deepfake purposes to blackmail him.
Following the incident, Neeraj approached the local police and lodged a complaint. Acting on the complaint, a special team constituted on the directions of the Senior Superintendent of Police launched an investigation and arrested Rahul Pal and Akash. Police said efforts are underway to trace the remaining accused.
During the investigation, the accused told investigators that they followed the same modus operandi for other targets. They identified targets through Instagram by creating fake female profiles, called them for a meeting, and then threatened them by impersonating fake police personnel and journalists.
FAKE POLICE EQUIPMENT, WALKIE-TALKIES, AND DOCUMENTS SEIZED
Police recovered a handful of items used by the accused to impersonate law enforcement officials and lend credibility to their operation.
The seized articles include a Maruti Alto car without a registration plate, a separate number plate, two mobile phones, a telephone set, a laptop, a tablet, a calculator, walkie-talkies, a PhonePe receiver box, a baton, a beat book, official-looking seals, nameplates, complaint applications, files and several other documents.
Police suspect these materials were used to convince people that they were dealing with genuine police officials before extorting money from them.
POLICE DENY REPORTS OF FAKE OUTPOST
Addressing speculation surrounding the case, senior cop Vinayak Gopal Bhonsle said the accused were not operating a fake police outpost.
"There was no fake police chowki. It was an office with 'Karyalaya' written outside it. Claims circulating on social media that a fake police outpost was being run are incorrect," he said.
Bhonsle said police registered an FIR immediately after receiving Neeraj Pal's complaint regarding the forced transfer of Rs 10,000.
"The accused created fake female identities to honeytrap people. Neeraj was called to their office, where he realised there was no woman. They recorded videos to blackmail him using fabricated allegations and demanded Rs 2 lakh. Two accused have been arrested, while two others remain absconding. They will be arrested soon," the officer said.
Police said the investigation is continuing to identify other possible survivors and determine whether the gang was involved in similar cases elsewhere in the region.

headline: NEW DELHI: More than 2.7 lakh medical graduates have registered for NEET-PG 2026, an increase of over 12.5% over last year, as the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences rolls out enhanced authentication measures and candidate-friendly in...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: More than 2.7 lakh medical graduates have registered for NEET-PG 2026, an increase of over 12.5% over last year, as the National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences rolls out enhanced authentication measures and candidate-friendly initiatives for the Aug 30 exam.Candidates will undergo Aadhaar-based authentication during registration and on the exam day, while iris-based biometric verification will be used wherever fingerprint authentication is unsuccessful. They will also have to indicate three preferred states for allotment of exam centres, with their correspondence state as mandatory first preference. The test city information will be issued nearly three weeks before the examination, enabling candidates to plan travel and accommodation in advance.
The exam will comprise 180 questions that have to be answered in 210 minutes, giving candidates more time per question while retaining the overall exam duration.Union health minister JP Nadda reviewed preparations for the examination Saturday and directed officials to ensure its smooth, transparent and technology-enabled conduct while maintaining the highest standards of security and integrity.
He urged candidates not to fall prey to rumours or fraudulent claims regarding question paper leaks, saying the final paper is selected through a highly encrypted, time-bound process shortly before the exam, making any claim of prior access entirely false.
Officials said the exam will be conducted under a multi-layered securityframework, which includes CCTV surveillance, biometric authentication, candidate frisking, signal jammers, dynamic computer allocation, live monitoring through central and regional command centres, and independent observers. More than 60,000 exam personnel will be deployed to oversee the process. The end-to-end question paper preparation and delivery process has been reinforced through multiple layers of encryption, secure offline preparation, time-bound finalisation of the paper shortly before the exam and controlled digital decryption at the scheduled commencement of test.NBEMS has also operationalised a dedicated email address to report impersonation, touting and other unfair practices while issuing regular advisories to candidates.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

headline: Injured worker succumbs, Kulgam terror attack toll rises to 2
full_text:
Injured worker succumbs, Kulgam terror attack toll rises to 2
Terrorists had attacked two brick kiln workers in Kelam area, where one of them died on the spot, while Bhupendra Bhaina (28) succumbed to his injuries later.
A labourer from Chhattisgarh, who was injured along with another worker from the state in a terrorist attack in Jammu & Kashmir’s Kulgam district, succumbed to his gunshot wounds on Saturday, officials aware of the development said. The other worker succumbed on Friday.
Terrorists had attacked two brick kiln workers late on Friday in the Kelam area of the south Kashmir district, where one of them — identified as Deepak Ratre (24) — died on the spot, while Bhupendra Bhaina (28) succumbed to his injuries later. A senior doctor at SKIMS said that Bhaina had received bullets in his chest and all efforts by doctors failed to revive him.

Ratre, a resident of Sakti district in Chhattisgarh, and Bhaina, who belonged to Sarangarh-Bilaigarh district of the state, had migrated to J&K this year in search of work, people aware of the matter said.
The attack follows closely on the heels of another incident less than 10 days ago, in which terrorists allegedly shot and killed a police officer deployed on Amarnath Yatra security duty in Anantnag.
J&K LG chairs security review meeting
J&K lieutenant governor Manoj Sinha on Saturday chaired a high-level security review meeting in Srinagar, where he directed all the deputy commissioners and SSPs to conduct a comprehensive review of the Standard Operating Procedures (SoPs) established to protect labourers from outside Jammu & Kashmir.
“We must intensify precise, high-impact anti-terror operations to neutralise the terrorists,” Sinha said, instructing the authorities to ensure dignified last rites for the victims. The meeting also discussed the security arrangements in place for the ongoing Amarnath Yatra and strengthening of the security grid. During the day, security forces conducted several operations across south Kashmir to trace the killers of two labourers.
Also Read | 3 dead in 10 days: Two terror attacks rock J&K despite high security alert
Chhattisgarh government announces ex gratia
The Chhattisgarh government, too, announced an ex gratia of ₹20 lakh each for the families of two migrant workers. “The Chhattisgarh government stands firmly with the bereaved families in this hour of grief,” chief minister Vishnu Deo Sai said.

Political controversy erupts
Meanwhile, a political controversy erupted on Saturday after National Conference president and former chief minister Farooq Abdullah questioned the timing of the Kulgam terror attack.
He called for an investigation into the killing of two migrant labourers in a terror attack in Kulgam, and asked why such incidents happen whenever his party demands the restoration of Jammu and Kashmir’s statehood.
“It is not even known who carried out the attack or who the perpetrators are. There must be an investigation to identify the attackers. I do not know why this happens only when we ask for the restoration of statehood,” Abdullah said.
The remarks drew sharp criticism from BJP leader Ravinder Raina, who termed Abdullah’s statement “highly controversial” and “deeply unfortunate”. “When innocent labourers are brutally murdered by terrorists, the nation expects every political leader to stand united against terrorism, not to make speculative statements, create confusion or divert attention from the perpetrators,” Raina said.
AIP chief spokesperson condemns terrorist attack
Awami Ittehad Party (AIP) chief spokesperson Inam Un Nabi condemned the terrorist attack, describing it as a barbaric act that deserves the strongest condemnation.
“The killing of innocent labourers is a crime against humanity and a direct assault on Kashmir’s age-old values of peace, hospitality and brotherhood. Such acts have no sanction in Islam, which declares the killing of an innocent person as if one has killed all of humanity,” he said.

headline: Embattled NTA floats ₹7.5 crore tender for round-the-clock security at HQ, regional offices
full_text:
Embattled NTA floats ₹7.5 crore tender for round-the-clock security at HQ, regional offices
The contract will initially be for two years and can be extended by two additional one-year terms based on performance.
The National Testing Agency (NTA) has floated a ₹7.5 crore tender to hire a professional security agency for round-the-clock security services at its headquarters on Delhi’s Minto Road, regional offices in Okhla and other notified locations, as the examination body undergoes a major overhaul following the NEET-UG 2026 controversy.
According to the request for proposal (RFP) document, seen by HT, the selected agency will provide “comprehensive security services” to safeguard NTA personnel, visitors, assets, premises, confidential examination material, server rooms, strong rooms, warehouses, record rooms and other critical infrastructure housing sensitive examination records.
Also Read | Spain builds 1,600-foot sea barrier after Ceuta migrant crisis leaves 67 dead
The contract will initially be for two years and can be extended by two additional one-year terms based on performance.
The tender was issued on July 25 and bids can be submitted until 3 pm on August 17. Technical bids will be opened the same day.
The RFP requires bidders to have at least five years of experience in professional security services, an average annual turnover of at least ₹10 crore over the past three financial years and prior experience in securing central government organisations, examination agencies, universities, airports, hospitals, metro systems or other high-security establishments.
Also Read | ‘Being a Gurkha’: Mountaineer Nirmal Purja ‘Dai’, killed by Pak avalanche, had ‘only one dream’
According to the document, the estimated value of the contract is ₹7.5 crore, excluding GST, though NTA has reserved the right to increase or reduce deployment requirements and split the work if necessary. Bidders will also have to furnish an earnest money deposit of ₹15 lakh and a performance security equivalent to 5% of the contract value.
Unlike conventional government procurement based solely on the lowest financial bid, NTA has opted for a Quality-and-Cost Based Selection (QCBS) model, saying that “the sensitive nature of NTA’s examination ecosystem and confidentiality requirements” makes quality of service paramount.
Under the evaluation process, technical quality will carry a weightage of 70% and financial bids 30%. Only agencies securing at least 70 out of 100 marks in the technical evaluation will qualify for the financial round, the document says.
The technical assessment will evaluate bidders on their experience in high-security environments, workforce strength, financial capacity, ISO certifications and a presentation on deployment strategy. Agencies will also be assessed on their proposed use of technology, including GPS patrols, biometric attendance systems and incident-reporting mechanisms.
The selected agency will be responsible for regulating entry and exit, ensuring that “only authorized persons enter restricted areas”, preventing unauthorised access, maintaining visitor records and deploying hand-held and door-frame metal detectors at entrances and confidential locations.
Security personnel will also be tasked with protecting examination material, IT infrastructure, server rooms and storage facilities, while maintaining strict confidentiality regarding examination materials and security arrangements even after the contract ends.
The RFP states that the service provider and its personnel “shall maintain strict confidentiality” regarding examination materials, IT systems, security arrangements and other information obtained during the contract, and that this obligation will continue after the contract period ends.
The document does not specify what security arrangements existed earlier or whether the facilities were guarded by an outsourced agency or in-house personnel.
Queries sent by HT to the NTA and the Union education ministry remained unanswered till the time of publication.
While the K. Radhakrishnan committee, constituted after the NEET-UG 2026 controversy, did not recommend hiring a private security agency, it had called for strengthening NTA’s security architecture, including having “in-house security analysts who will analyse the security protocol and make the necessary changes”.
The move comes days after the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) filed a charge sheet against all 13 arrested accused in the alleged NEET-UG 2026 paper leak case. The agency said it had traced the leak from paper setters to beneficiary candidates and uncovered the entire conspiracy.
Investigators found no involvement of any government official or NTA functionary and concluded that the paper had been leaked by teachers engaged to set the examination.
The alleged leak prompted NTA to cancel the original May 3 examination on May 12 after receiving an email alleging a leak and identifying overlaps between a circulated “guess paper” and the actual question paper. A re-test was conducted on June 21.

headline: DKS Cabinet likely to be finalised, but Karnataka delay among rarest in history
full_text:
DKS Cabinet likely to be finalised, but Karnataka delay among rarest in history
Karnataka CM DK Shivakumar and senior Congress leaders from the state met the party high command in Delhi to discuss the long-pending issue of Cabinet expansion. The delay is among the lengthiest for a state government operating with an incomplete cabinet in recent years.
Nearly two months after DK Shivakumar took the oath as Karnataka Chief Minister on June 3, the full expansion of his Council of Ministers remains pending, with reports indicating the list could be finalised over the weekend, around August 2, and swearing-in possibly early next week.
DKS and other state leaders met the Congress top leadership at party president Mallikarjun Kharge's residence in New Delhi on Thursday to discuss the expansion of the Cabinet.
Shivakumar was sworn in at Lok Bhavan along with Deputy Chief Minister G Parameshwara and 12 other ministers, a first batch of 13 ministers in total with him, for a 14-member team initially. Karnataka's constitutional limit is 34 ministers including the CM, so roughly 20 berths remain vacant.
Portfolio allocation for the first group happened quickly, but further expansion has been delayed by high-command consultations in Delhi over regional, caste, community, gender and generational balance, competing factional lists (involving Shivakumar and predecessor Siddaramaiah), and other political priorities.
By July 31, this amounts to about 58 days since the initial swearing-in.
Recent reports have pointed to finalisation of names by around August 2, with induction targeted for August 3 or shortly after, ahead of the monsoon session, which begins on August 13.
This is longer than some recent Karnataka precedents but does not set a new national record for the time a state government has operated with a minimal or incomplete cabinet after a CM's induction.
Indian states have seen several extended periods of limited cabinets, often one- or two-member core teams handling all departments, while leadership negotiated equations, high-command clearances, or other factors.
OTHER STATES HAVE SEEN A LONGER DELAY IN CABINET APPOINTMENT
One of the longest such instances in recent years came in Telangana, where K Chandrasekhar Rao (KCR) was sworn in as Chief Minister on December 13, 2018, along with only one other minister, Mohammed Mahmood Ali.
The council remained a two-member affair for over two months before 10 more ministers were inducted on February 19, 2019, creating a gap of around 66–68 days. The delay, attributed to administrative reorganisation and political considerations, also drew criticism from the Opposition over governance.
Maharashtra has also witnessed similar delays on multiple occasions.
After the Shiv Sena split in 2022, Eknath Shinde and Deputy Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis ran the government as the only two members of the council for nearly 40 days before the cabinet was expanded on August 9. Three years earlier, the Uddhav Thackeray-led Maha Vikas Aghadi government functioned with just a seven-member cabinet for about 40 days after taking office in November 2019, as alliance partners negotiated the distribution of portfolios.
Karnataka itself has experienced a comparable, though shorter, phase. After the collapse of the JD(S)-Congress coalition in 2019, BS Yediyurappa was sworn in as Chief Minister on July 26 and headed a one-man cabinet for 25 days before inducting 17 ministers on August 20. During this period, he even chaired cabinet meetings alone while the BJP worked through caste and regional representation and awaited the party high command's approval.
Similar, though less prolonged, episodes have unfolded elsewhere.
In Himachal Pradesh, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu and his deputy operated with a two-member council for about four weeks after taking office in December 2022 before the first cabinet expansion in January 2023.
Delays of several weeks have also been seen in Puducherry, Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and other states, particularly where coalition negotiations or consultations with party leadership have prolonged the process of balancing regional, caste and political representation.
Against this backdrop, Karnataka's current delay — of around 58 days since the initial swearing-in — stands out as one of the longer recent examples, though it remains shorter than Telangana's 2018-19 record. The Constitution does not prescribe a deadline for completing cabinet formation, but prolonged delays have often sparked criticism over governance.

headline: Day after 'forgive' remark, PM Modi praises youth for powering India's growth
full_text:
Day after 'forgive' remark, PM Modi praises youth for powering India's growth
PM Modi said the country’s transformation from the constraints of colonial rule had been made possible by the capabilities of its young people.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Saturday credited the country’s youth with driving India’s rise as the world’s fastest-growing major economy, its third-largest startup ecosystem and the nation’s emerging strength in semiconductors, artificial intelligence, deep tech and space, saying young Indians were now “giving impetus to the development of the world”.
The remarks came a day after Modi posted a video on Instagram offering to “forgive” students who had hurled expletives at him during weeks of nationwide protests led by the self-styled Cockroach Janta Party (CJP).
Triggered by a leak of the NEET-UG paper that forced a retest for around two million students, the agitation became the biggest political crisis of Modi’s third term, ending only after education minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned last week and the government accepted the demonstrators’ demands, including examination-system reforms and the withdrawal of police cases against protesters.
Also Read | Embattled NTA floats ₹7.5 crore tender for round-the-clock security at HQ, regional offices
Modi was speaking on Saturday after inaugurating the Swami Vivekananda Cultural Youth Centre — Viveka Smaraka — at the Sri Ramakrishna Ashrama in Mysuru. He said the country’s transformation from the constraints of colonial rule to the frontlines of global innovation had been made possible by the capabilities of its young people.
“Today, India is the world’s fastest-growing major economy. Who has made this possible? The capability of India’s youth. The youth of India are giving impetus to the development of the world,” Modi said.
Pointing to the recent launch of a privately built Indian rocket into space, he said the feat reflected “the growing capabilities of the country’s young innovators”, and that initiatives such as Atmanirbhar Bharat and Make in India were succeeding on the strength of the youth.
Also Read | Spain builds 1,600-foot sea barrier after Ceuta migrant crisis leaves 67 dead
What young people needed, he said, was “the right opportunities, guidance and confidence to realise their dreams”.
Modi framed the message through Vivekananda, invoking the principle “Shiva Jnane Jiva Seva” — serving humanity is serving God — and urging young Indians to place the welfare of the poor and the nation above personal interests. The Viveka Smaraka, built at the site where Vivekananda stayed during his 1892 visit to Mysuru and from where he decided to travel to the 1893 Parliament of Religions in Chicago, should serve as “a powerful source of inspiration and energy” for that mission, he said.
Opposition parties, meanwhile, attacked the PM for his video message on Friday.
The Congress said the Prime Minister owed the country’s students an apology rather than an offer of forgiveness, remarking that while the country was asking the PM to apologise, he had instead “forgiven the country”. In a post on X, Rahul Gandhi said Modi had the “audacity to speak of forgiving students” when he had not visited a single family that had lost a child to suicide over what he called a “corrupt” exam system and cancelled papers.
“Nothing is more painful than seeing a parent grieve their child,” Gandhi said after meeting affected families during a day-long visit to Tamil Nadu. “Behind every young life lost is a family carrying pain that will never leave them — and serious questions about a broken education system.”
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke turned the demand for an apology onto the police action of July 20, when demonstrators marching towards Parliament were met with tear gas and baton charges. In a video posted on X on Saturday, Dipke said he expected Modi to record a fresh message on Saturday night — this time to apologise to the girls who were “brutally beaten up” by male police officers at Jantar Mantar.
“I think Modi ji will upload a new video tonight, so I hope that he will apologise… he will apologise for the lathi-charge of July 20,” he said.
Earlier in the day, Modi inaugurated the Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport at Bhogapuram in Andhra Pradesh’s Vizianagaram district, which is inspired by the freedom fighter Alluri Sitarama Raju. PM Modi said that it reflects the pride in Indian heritage.

headline: Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies N. Uttam Kumar Reddy has stated that every effort is being made to maximise utilisation of Godavari waters for the benefit of farmers in Telangana and reiterated that the government is committed for revival ...
full_text:
HYDERABAD
Minister for Irrigation and Civil Supplies N. Uttam Kumar Reddy has stated that every effort is being made to maximise utilisation of Godavari waters for the benefit of farmers in Telangana and reiterated that the government is committed for revival of the Kaleshwaram project barrages.
Mr. Reddy along with Ministers D. Sridhar Babu, G. Vivek and A. Laxman Kumar, legislators and senior officials visited Sriramsagar, Kaddam and Yellampally projects on Saturday.
Speaking after inspecting the three projects, which were getting the first significant inflows of the season. He stated that five pumps were switched on at Nandi Medaram pump house by drawing water from Yellampally reservoir with gravity to fill Mid Manair by using Flood Flow Canal.
“Our goal is to use every drop of Godavari water optimally,” Mr. Uttam Kumar Reddy said. He reviewed inflows, storage levels and pumping operations and insisted upon hourly monitoring and coordinated operation of projects to prevent any wastage of water.
The Minister strongly rejected claims that water pumped from Yellampally was “Kaleshwaram water”. He clarified that Sripada Yellampally was a Congress-era project conceived under the Pranahita Chevella project. The water currently entering Yellampally was natural Godavari flow and not lifted from the three Kaleshwaram barrages - Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla, he said.
He highlighted that landmark projects like SRSP (foundation laid by Jawaharlal Nehru in 1963), Kaddam (1959), Nagarjunasagar, Srisailam and the Flood Flow Canal — all built during Congress regimes — continue to serve the State reliably. In contrast, he said Medigadda, Annaram and Sundilla barrages constructed between 2016 and 2019 under the previous BRS Government, developed serious structural issues by 2023.
Rehab on expert advice
The Minister asserted there was no political motive in keeping the barrages under free-flow condition and the government was strictly following National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA) and Central Water Commission (CWC) directives, which prohibit water storage until detailed investigations and repairs were completed.
A Central Technical Oversight Committee, constituted on June 30, was supervising the process. IIT Bombay and AFRY India were preparing the rehabilitation design and it was expected to be ready in 2–3 months. He explained that proposed measures include construction of a diaphragm wall and extension of the stilling basin to strengthen foundations.
Repairs would begin once designs were finalised, with efforts to restore the barrages before the next monsoon. Explaining why Kannepalli pumps were not being operated yet, the Minister said water lifted from there would need storage in Annaram and Sundilla first, both of which were under structural investigation.
He stated that experts had flagged serious defects in the secant pile foundation system, which deviated from the original Detailed Project Report.
The Minister accused BRS of running a misinformation campaign and trying to claim credit for water from the Congress-built Yellampally project. He pointed out that the previous government spent ₹1.81 lakh crore on irrigation but had created little new ayacut. Even Kaleshwaram failed to deliver stable irrigation to one-lakh acres, he alleged. Several other projects like Palamuru-Rangareddy and others remained incomplete, he said.

headline: President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent to the legislation aiming at raising the punishment for unfair means in public examinations, days after the bill was pushed through both the Houses of Parliament by voice vote earlier this week

President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent to the legislation aiming at raising the punishment for unfair means in public examinations, days after the bill was pushed through both the Houses of Parliament by voice vote earlier this week
President Droupadi Murmu gave her assent to the legislation aiming at raising the punishment for unfair means in public examinations, days after the bill was pushed through both the Houses of Parliament by voice vote earlier this week.
In a gazette notification issued on Friday, the law ministry said President Murmu has given her assent to the Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, 2026.
According to the legislation, individuals involved in paper leaks or unfair means in exams will get jail terms for a minimum of five years and a maximum up to 10 years and a fine up to ₹50 lakh. Earlier, the punishment scale was three years jail term, extendable up to five years and ₹10 lakh.
For organised crimes, the amended law proposes a minimum sentence of seven years and a fine of up to ₹10 crore. The law outlines 15 illegal acts, including leaking question papers, tampering with OMR sheets, creating fake websites and issuing fake admit cards.
The government pushed for an early passage of the Bill by Parliament amid massive protests across the country by students against the NEET 2026 paper leak.
President Murmu’s assent came within days of Parliament clearing the bill, bringing the amended penalties into force from the date of publication.

headline: A new digital medical emergency referral system being rolled out in Rajasthan is set to transform patient care during the critical initial hours. The model will enable the tertiary hospitals to make preparations for attending to the patients even bef...
full_text:
A new digital medical emergency referral system being rolled out in Rajasthan is set to transform patient care during the critical initial hours. The model will enable the tertiary hospitals to make preparations for attending to the patients even before they arrive.
Rajasthan is the first State in the country to implement the model, in which a referred patient’s medical history will reach the control room online before they arrive at the hospital. This will allow a team of medical experts to review the reports and stand ready for treatment.
Prepared and tested at Rabindranath Tagore Medical College in Udaipur, the Simplified Emergency Transfer and Urgent Referral (SETU) has already managed over 3,510 emergency cases across 15 districts in the State. The model is going to be a lifesaver for patients by eliminating the issue of “blind arrivals”.
Principal Medical and Health Secretary Gayatri Rathore said in Jaipur on Saturday (august 1, 2026) that the SETU would serve as a robust digital bridge connecting the primary health centres (PHC) and community health centres (CHC) in the remote rural areas with medical colleges and tertiary hospitals in the cities.
“The system operates using only smartphones, quick response (QR) codes, and a closed user group (CUG) network, eliminating the need for heavy investments in additional infrastructure,” Ms. Rathore said. As soon as a physician at a PHC refers a patient using the digital app, the complete digital data, estimated time of arrival and live GPS tracking will be sent to the tertiary hospital.
Before the patient reaches the hospital, the control room will alert super-specialists in the relevant departments, such as trauma, surgical, obstetrics and gynaecology, and paediatrics, via the CUG network and reserve intensive care unit or emergency beds.
Ms. Rathore said a fully prepared team of doctors would begin the life-saving treatment for the patient from “minute zero”, as soon as the ambulance doors open. Besides, every patient referred through SETU will receive a follow-up call from the control room on the following day to obtain feedback on treatment and hospital services.

headline: Hamim's aide arrested as STF probe reveals Bengal CM on Pak operatives' target list
full_text:
Hamim's aide arrested as STF probe reveals Bengal CM on Pak operatives' target list
The West Bengal STF has arrested Arpita Sarkar, alleging she worked with Hamim Mondal in a cross-border network targeting senior political figures, including West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. The investigation has also revealed that Hamim was allegedly instructed to procure police uniforms to create disturbances during the recent student protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.
The West Bengal Police's Special Task Force (STF) has arrested Arpita Sarkar, an alleged associate of Hamim Mondal, the Burdwan youth arrested over suspected links with Pakistan-based operatives. Investigators claim the duo was part of a network that was allegedly gathering sensitive information and receiving instructions from handlers across the border.
Arpita Sarkar was arrested from Sahibganj in Jharkhand and brought to West Bengal for questioning. According to STF officials, she was in regular contact with Hamim Mondal and allegedly played a role in operations aimed at trapping and abducting targets.
ARREST LINKED TO CROSS-BORDER NETWORK PROBE
The arrest comes a day after Hamim Mondal was picked up from the Renaissance residential complex near the Durgapur Expressway in Burdwan. During the investigation, STF officers uncovered communications between Mondal and several Pakistan-based online handlers.
Addressing the media, STF Inspector General Gaurav Sharma said the probe was triggered after intelligence inputs suggested that a senior minister in Howrah was being extorted and that there was a plan to honey-trap and kidnap his son. Investigators traced a key digital handle operating from Sahibganj, which eventually led them to Hamim and Arpita.
"When we verified the handle, we found that it was in regular contact with a man named Hamim Mondal. That discovery led us to expand the investigation, which subsequently revealed several other suspicious links and activities," Sharma said.
According to the STF, Hamim was in contact with multiple suspicious online accounts, including individuals identified as Rana, Abir Jat, Uzar and Had. Verification of these accounts revealed that they were being operated from Pakistan.
"We found that Hamim was in contact with several suspicious online handles, including accounts identified as Rana, Abir Jat, Uzar and Had. After verification, we established that all these handles were being operated from Pakistan. Acting on this information, we took him into custody on the night of July 30-31," Sharma added.
STF SAYS CM'S MOVEMENTS WERE SOUGHT BY PAKISTAN-BASED HANDLERS
Sharma said that during interrogation, investigators discovered that Pakistan-based operatives had repeatedly sought information about the movement patterns of West Bengal Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. He said the Chief Minister was on the target list of the handlers and that Hamim was being asked to gather details about her movements and security arrangements.
"During interrogation, we uncovered several serious findings. One of the most significant revelations was that the state's Chief Minister was on the target list of these Pakistan-based handlers. They repeatedly sought information about the Chief Minister's movement patterns, particularly any unguarded movements, and instructed him to verify and report such details," Sharma said.
The STF further claimed that Hamim was instructed to procure police uniforms to create disturbances during the recent student protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar. Investigators are examining whether any operational plans had moved beyond the planning stage.
Officials also said that certain police personnel, political figures and other prominent individuals were allegedly being surveilled or identified as potential targets, though the STF declined to disclose further details.
Both Hamim Mondal and Arpita Sarkar have been produced before a court in Burdwan. Their custodial interrogation is underway as investigators continue to probe the alleged network and its suspected links to Pakistan-based operatives.

headline: The verification of electronic voting machines (EVMs), control units, and voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT) machines used in 14 polling stations in the Kolathur Assembly constituency continued for the fourth day on Saturday.
full_text:
The verification of electronic voting machines (EVMs), control units, and voter verifiable paper audit trail (VVPAT) machines used in 14 polling stations in the Kolathur Assembly constituency continued for the fourth day on Saturday.
The exercise, which commenced on July 29 following the directions of the Election Commission (EC), covered the machines used in two polling stations on Saturday.
The verification was carried out at the electronic voting machine storage facility in Chintadripet, in the presence of Chennai District Election Officer and Greater Chennai Corporation Commissioner G.S. Sameeran.
The Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) Checking and Verification process being conducted for 14 polling stations in Kolathur Assembly constituency has so far found no evidence of malpractice, and should not be construed as a recounting exercise, Chennai District Election Officer G.S. Sameeran said on Saturday.
Addressing reporters after the fourth day of the verification process, Mr. Sameeran said the exercise was intended only to verify the reliability of the EVMs in accordance with the EC’s guidelines.
“This is not re-counting. This is EVM Checking and Verification process,” he said. “It is a 100% transparent exercise to establish the reliability of the EVMs.”
He said that in the eight EVMs verified over the past two days, the polled votes recorded candidate-wise matched the results in Form 20, while the preliminary mock poll had also been completed successfully.
During the detailed mock poll of one EVM from Polling Station 75 at Chennai Higher Secondary School in Kolathur, the VVPAT developed a technical fault after correctly recording 412 mock votes, with its indicator light failing to function.
Mr. Sameeran said the EC’s protocol permitted either replacing only the VVPAT and continuing the mock poll until the required 500 votes, or replacing the entire EVM set and restarting the exercise. However, the applicant’s representatives declined both options, following which the process was halted.
He said officials had also offered a randomly selected list of 10 EVM sets, from which the applicant could choose two for verification. “They were given one hour to select two EVMs. If they do not, we will randomly select two EVMs in the presence of other agents, videograph the entire process and complete the verification,” he said.
Responding to allegations regarding missing or incomplete seal markings on certain machines, Mr. Sameeran said, “All the machines have been properly sealed, and the seal identification is available. Their allegation is only that the seal is at the rear and not on the front. That can easily be verified by opening the machine and tallying it. In the subsequent stages, there are opportunities to verify and check the authenticity. They call it a technical issue. But that is not evidence of any malpractice or tampering with the EVM. We have explained all this to them in detail through a letter. Based on that, we have given them time.”
If they do not make a selection within that time, we will select two EVMs ourselves in accordance with the EC’s instructions and complete the procedure. The same procedure was followed in Kancheepuram by the District Election Officer and the District Collector, he said.
He added that if the applicant or chief agent chose not to participate, the EC’s guidelines authorised the District Election Officer to proceed with the verification through random selection, under videography and in the presence of officials, before submitting the report to the EC.
Additional District Election Officer and Joint Commissioner (Education) K. Karpagam, District Revenue Officer (Elections) N. Pushnadevi, and other election officials were present during the exercise.
