headline: Shame on Hemant Soren: Jharkhand students seek CBI probe into JPSC exams lapses
full_text:
Shame on Hemant Soren: Jharkhand students seek CBI probe into JPSC exams lapses
Jharkhand students have continued an indefinite sit-in in Ranchi against alleged irregularities in JPSC and JSSC exams. Their protest has sharpened pressure on the Jharkhand government for an independent probe and recruitment reforms.
Hundreds of students in Jharkhand continued their protest for the fifth consecutive day on Sunday over alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC examination, JSSC-CGL and other recruitment tests. They demanded a CBI probe into the alleged lapses and reforms in the state's recruitment agencies.
The protesters have been holding an indefinite sit-in at a stadium in Ranchi since July 29. They are seeking cancellation of the 14th JPSC Combined Preliminary Test held on April 19, an independent probe by central agencies including the CBI and Enforcement Directorate, and the introduction of a fifth option of 'not attempted' in OMR sheets.
During the protest, students raised slogans such as 'Order CBI probe in JPSC', 'Long live Students Unity' and 'Shame on Hemant Soren'.
JPSC aspirant Rahul Kumar Kranti said, "Paper leaks in JPSC have happened several times. This time, OMR sheets of candidates have been leaked. Chief Minister Hemant Soren has ordered a CID probe, but we are not satisfied." He alleged that earlier probes into the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission CGL paper leak had not led to action and claimed that the latest investigation could also be "covered up" after a few months.
Kranti said, "We have completely lost faith in the ongoing CID probe. We demand a CBI probe into all recruitment examinations conducted by the JPSC and JSSC over the past seven years. We also demand the chief minister's resignation on moral grounds."
Ankit Kumar from Giridih district said, "The careers of thousands of students and aspirants are at stake due to corruption in both agencies. Most of us come from farmers' families. We only want fair opportunities based on merit." Sneha, a tribal student from Ranchi, said the protesters wanted strict punishment for those involved in the alleged irregularities and cancellation of the 14th JPSC examination.
"I have been preparing for competitive examinations since 2023. But if an equal and fair chance is not given, how can I get a job? I urge CM Soren to listen to our demands," she said.
Archana Kumari from Palamu said the protesters would continue their agitation until the government addressed their demands and fixed accountability for the alleged irregularities. Shyam Bihari Gupta, a student from Balumath in Latehar district, said, "The state government is still in a sleeping mode. We are getting support from across the country. People from various cities are sending food items to the protest site. We are thankful to those helping us continue our protest."
The protest remained focused on demands for cancellation of the April 19 test, a wider independent investigation and changes in the recruitment process.

headline: Exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin on Sunday (August 2, 2026) called for all countries of the Indian subcontinent to implement a Uniform Civil Code (UCC), arguing that this was needed to protect women from discrimination.
full_text:
Exiled Bangladeshi writer Taslima Nasrin on Sunday (August 2, 2026) called for all countries of the Indian subcontinent to implement a Uniform Civil Code (UCC), arguing that this was needed to protect women from discrimination.
“Uniform Civil Code is a must. This is the first step for any civilised society,” Ms. Nasrin said, interacting with journalists in Kolkata. The Bengali writer said that she has been fighting for the UCC for the past 40 years and added that “if women come under religious laws, there is discrimination and persecution”. Delivering a speech in Kolkata on Saturday (August 1), she had said that India, Bangladesh, and Pakistan should have a uniform law for all their citizens.
“Due to religious laws, women are suffering. Hindus are being tortured in Bangladesh. During the Yunus regime, Hindus were tortured even more. In many madrasas and mosques, hatred is being taught against Hindus. Now we have Jamaat-e-Islami as an Opposition party. It is against women’s equality, and they want Sharia rule,” she said, reflecting on the situation in her home country.
The author’s remarks come at a time when the West Bengal government has announced plans to implement UCC in the State and has set up a committee headed by a retired Supreme Court judge to look into the provisions of a draft UCC Bill.
Return to Kolkata
Ms. Nasrin arrived in Kolkata on July 31, almost 19 years after she was forced to leave the city due to violent protests by a mob upset with her writings during the Left Front government. Prior to this, she was exiled from Bangladesh in 1994.
Her return to Kolkata was celebrated by West Bengal’s first BJP government, even as she shared the stage with Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari. Asked for her view on different governments in the State, she said, “One government had forced me out, another did not allow me to return, and one government has helped me to return,” she said.
‘Some madrasas produce jihadis’
Ms. Nasrin also came down hard against madrasas, saying that some of these “religious schools produce jihadis”. “In my opinion, madrasas should not exist. Not in all cases, but in some, it is seen that jihadis are being produced in madrasas,” the writer said. Alleging that “child abuse is going on there, rapes are happening, and imams and madrasa teachers are being held,” she opined that “there is no need for madrasas to exist.”
“No one does anything after passing out of madrasas. They beg, survive on charity. Madrasas should go, and secular schools should come up instead,” Ms. Nasrin said.
Freedom of speech
The Bengali writer also expressed anguish over an incident during Saturday’s (August 1) event, where the crowd prevented Bengali poet Joy Goswami from addressing the gathering. The poet is considered to be close to the Trinamool Congress regime. Ms. Nasrin had called Mr. Goswami to take his seat on the stage when the people gathered started shouting.
“Not only was Mr. Goswami insulted, but I was also insulted because I had invited him,” she said. “In my speech, I spoke about freedom of expression. Everyone should be allowed to speak. It is not right to stop anyone from expressing their views,” she said.

headline: As relief and rehabilitation efforts continue across flood-ravaged Pathanamthitta, the focus is rapidly shifting from rescue to accountability, with allegations of administrative lapses and poor disaster management dominating the political discourse.
full_text:
As relief and rehabilitation efforts continue across flood-ravaged Pathanamthitta, the focus is rapidly shifting from rescue to accountability, with allegations of administrative lapses and poor disaster management dominating the political discourse.
The sharpest criticism came from CPI(M) Pathanamthitta district secretary Raju Abraham, who described the deluge as a `government-sponsored flood’. He accused the authorities of failing to issue timely red alerts and opening dam shutters without adequate public warning, and demanded compensation for all those who suffered losses.
“The authorities neither issued a proper red alert nor gave advance warning before opening the dam shutters. The lack of timely information from both the government and weather monitoring agencies caused widespread anxiety among the public and resulted in losses worth crores,” he alleged.
According to Mr.Abraham,the Moozhiyar and Kariyarkayam dams were opened at 1 a.m. Under the existing protocol, the authorities are required to inform elected representatives, local self-government institutions and the Public Relations Department before releasing water. Public announcements through loudspeakers should also have been made to alert residents. However, the government failed to follow any of these procedures. Had even a public announcement been made, people would have had time to move their belongings to safety and take the necessary precautions, he pointed out.
He also claimed that DYFI volunteers had to undertake cleaning operations because the official response was delayed.
Questions have also been raised over the government’s preparedness and the coordination of relief operations. Residents and public representatives alleged that relief camps lacked basic facilities, flood-hit areas did not receive adequate support and coordination among various departments remained patchy at a time when swift action was crucial.
Taking a serious note of the situation, Aranmula MLA, Abin Varkey urged the government to extend additional assistance to the constituency, saying it was among the worst-hit regions and required greater support. Ranni MLA, Pazhakulam Madhu likened the aftermath of the floods to `a battlefield after the battle’ and said local teams were doing their best with the limited resources at their disposal while appealing for more government assistance. Complaints also surfaced over inadequate facilities at a relief camp in Aranmula.
Even in Ranni, where post-flood cleaning operations were being coordinated under the leadership of the MLA, residents alleged that official support remained inadequate and inter-departmental coordination continued to be poor.
Responding to the criticism, Revenue Minister A.P. Anil Kumar said the government would step up rehabilitation efforts and improve facilities in the coming days. District in-charge Minister P.C. Vishnunath also remained in the district to oversee the relief and rehabilitation work in the flood-affected areas.

headline: Worli MLA and Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray has written to Maharashtra Director General of Police (DGP) Sadanand Date seeking clarity over the first information reports (FIRs) registered against protesting students.
full_text:
Worli MLA and Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray has written to Maharashtra Director General of Police (DGP) Sadanand Date seeking clarity over the first information reports (FIRs) registered against protesting students.
Mr. Thackeray said that the Home Department had said on July 31 that it had decided to withdraw, in accordance with the prescribed legal procedure, the criminal cases/FIRs registered against students, youth, and other individuals who participated in protests held at various places across Maharashtra in support of the demonstration at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi.
“We are continuously being contacted by many students, parents, lawyers, and citizens across the State. There is confusion regarding how the decision will be directly implemented. Many students are still receiving police notices; investigation is underway in some cases; and in many cases, crimes are pending in the court,” Mr. Thackeray wrote in the letter on Saturday (August 1, 2026).
He asked if the benefit that Home Department of the State offered extended to all cases; if police stations would pursue suo motu charges; if the students would have to independently file applications in the court; and if a standard operating procedure had been issued to the police to make sure the cases were withdrawn.
“It is essential that the government’s decision does not remain merely on paper but is implemented uniformly and effectively throughout the State. Students who exercised their democratic right to protest should not suffer unnecessary adverse consequences in their academic, professional, or social lives on account of criminal proceedings,” he emphasised.

NEW DELHI: Commonwealth Games silver medallist and Assam boxer Lovlina Borgohain said she felt 'hurt' after noticing that the Northeast was missing from a map printed on napkins and displayed outside a popular Indian restaurant in Glasgow. The restaurant owners acknowledged the mistake and assured the Indian boxing contingent that it would be corrected.The incident took place when the Indian boxing team visited Mister Singh's India, The Home of Curry for a celebratory dinner after securing a record 10 medals, seven gold and three silver, at the Commonwealth Games.Lovlina noticed that the restaurant's branding showed an incomplete map of India without the Northeast. As someone from the North East, that really hurts us. That's all I wanted to say.
Please keep this in mind next time. Thank you so much," she said.
Boxing Federation of India (BFI) president Ajay Singh, who was present at the restaurant, said there was no confrontation and that the issue was resolved amicably."There was no confrontation. It was an aberration and we pointed that out, me and Lovlina. They accepted their mistake and assured us that it will be corrected," Singh told PTI.
The restaurant is a popular Indian dining destination in Glasgow and has hosted several visiting sports teams and dignitaries over the years.Lovlina won a silver medal in the women's 75kg boxing event at the 2026 Commonwealth Games.The Tokyo Olympic bronze medallist lost a closely fought final to Australia's Emma-Sue Greentree by a 4-1 split decision, missing out on her first Commonwealth Games gold medal.The silver was Lovlina's maiden Commonwealth Games medal after earlier exits at Gold Coast 2018 and Birmingham 2022.India's boxing team has produced its best-ever Commonwealth Games campaign, winning a record seven gold and three silver medals. headline: Karnataka boy, 5, dies after choking on toy ball found inside snack packet
full_text:
Karnataka boy, 5, dies after choking on toy ball found inside snack packet
Police sources told India Today that the plastic ball had come as a complimentary item with the Kurkure packet and that the child accidentally swallowed it while playing.
A five-year-old boy died after choking on a plastic toy ball that was found inside a Kurkure packet in Karnataka's Mysuru district, police said.
The incident took place in Karnataka's Gauripura village, where the child is believed to have swallowed the complimentary plastic ball while playing. According to police sources, the ball became lodged in his throat, causing him to suffocate.
Family members rushed the child for medical assistance, but he could not be saved.
The incident has left the family and residents of the village in mourning. The boy was the only child of his parents and belonged to a well-known family in the village.
Police sources told India Today that the plastic ball had come as a complimentary item with the Kurkure packet and that the child accidentally swallowed it while playing.
However, the police clarified that the family has not lodged any complaint regarding the incident. As a result, no Unnatural Death Report (UDR) has been registered, and no criminal case has been initiated so far.
Authorities said they are in touch with the family and that further action will depend on whether a formal complaint is filed.

headline: Participants in the Jain Summer Program pose for a group photograph at Jain Vishwa Bharati in Ladnun, Rajasthan, on July 29. Photo by Aman Dhage/The American Bazaar
full_text:
Participants in the Jain Summer Program pose for a group photograph at Jain Vishwa Bharati in Ladnun, Rajasthan, on July 29. Photo by Aman Dhage/The American Bazaar
Nestled amid the arid plains of Rajasthan, about 230 miles west of Delhi, Ladnun is the kind of town many travelers might pass without a second glance. Its narrow streets, whitewashed temples, and unhurried pace stand in stark contrast to Indiaâs bustling metropolitan centers.This summer, however, the quiet town has become an unlikely destination for seekers of one of the worldâs oldest philosophies.For more than three centuries, Ladnun has been the spiritual home of the Terapanth order of Jainism, a reformist sect known for its disciplined monastic tradition and emphasis on nonviolence, self-restraint, and spiritual inquiry. Last month, those traditions welcomed an unusual group of visitors: nearly three dozen students, scholars, and faculty members from eight countries who are spending three weeks not merely studying Jainism, but living it.The immersive summer program, which began July 20 and concludes on Friday, is the result of a collaboration among Florida International University, California State University Long Beach, the Jain Education and Research Foundation (JERF), Jain Visva Bharati Institute, and southern California philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose support made the initiative possible.Rather than treating Jainism as an academic subject confined to classrooms and textbooks, the organizers designed a program that allows participants to experience the philosophy through daily practice.
Each morning began with meditation. Students attended lectures on Jain philosophy, Prakrit â the ancient language of many Jain scriptures â and the foundational principles of âAhimsaâ (nonviolence), âAnekantavadaâ (the multiplicity of viewpoints), and âAparigrahaâ (non-attachment to possessions). They also interacted with monks and nuns, observed their disciplined routines, and experienced a lifestyle centered on simplicity, compassion, and mindfulness.âIt has been a very eventful week, and it has been a tremendous experience,â said Anne Vallely, a professor at the University of Ottawa and one of the foremost scholars of Jainism in the Western world.Describing the demanding schedule, she added, âWe have our lessons from 9:00 in the morning, and they go really into 10 oâclock, 11:00 at night.âThe program reflects months of planning by scholars in India and the United States.Florida International University, home to the first endowed chairs in Jain Studies in the United States, worked closely with California State University Long Beach, to develop the curriculum. The Jain Education and Research Foundation helped coordinate the academic and logistical aspects of the initiative, while Jain Visva Bharati opened its sprawling campus and monastic community to the international participants.At the heart of the effort is a broader mission: introducing Jain philosophy to a global audience at a time when its central teachings of nonviolence, environmental sustainability, restraint, and respect for diverse perspectives have taken on renewed relevance.Much of that vision has been championed by physician, entrepreneur, and philanthropist Dr. Jasvant Modi, whose years of support for Jain education and higher learning have helped establish academic programs across the United States. Modi, who has contributed tens of millions of dollars to educational and religious causes in the United States, India, and globally, provided the principal financial support for this yearâs summer school.âI was born in India in the Jain faith, and those principles of Ahimsa, compassion, and respect for all living beings have guided my entire life as a physician,â the La CaÃ±ada, California,-based physician entrepreneur told The American Bazaar. ââ After my medical career, I realized philanthropy allows me to heal on a larger scale, not just one patient at a time. I contribute to Jain education because I believe Americaâs young students must be exposed to this ancient wisdom of tolerance, non-possessiveness, and plurality, which is so undervalued today.âThe program also coincided with another milestone.This year marks the 300th anniversary of the founding of the Terapanth order, giving participants an opportunity to witness commemorative events while learning about one of Jainismâs most influential traditions. Established in the 18th century by Acharya Bhikshu, the Terapanth order is distinguished by its centralized leadership and disciplined monastic structure. Its monks and nuns travel extensively to spread Jain teachings rather than remaining in permanent monasteries.Throughout the three weeks, students discovered that learning extended far beyond formal lectures.Meals became lessons in mindful eating. Silence became a form of reflection. Conversations with monks and nuns often continued long after scheduled sessions ended. Participants learned not only the philosophical foundations of Jainism but also how those principles shape everyday decisions, from food and consumption to conflict resolution and environmental responsibility.For many students, the immersive setting transformed abstract ideas into lived experience.âIâm surrounded by scholars and Iâve gotten to meet with sadhvis and sadhus, and itâs just been lovely,â said Carol Rodriguez, one of the participants, who holds a Ph.D. in Jain Studies from the University of Florida.The Cuban-born scholar earned her bachelorâs and masterâs degrees in Jain Studies from Florida International University in Miami, where she translated portions of the Lilavatisara, a 13th-century work by Jain monk Jinaratnasuri.The international composition of the group further enriched the discussions. Participants brought diverse academic backgrounds and cultural perspectives, creating conversations that reflected Jainismâs emphasis on dialogue and multiple viewpoints rather than absolute certainty.Organizers hope the program will serve as a model for future international collaborations in religious studies, philosophy, sustainability, and peace education.Unlike traditional study abroad programs, the Ladnun initiative invites participants to become temporary members of a living spiritual community, where learning occurs as much through observation and daily practice as through formal instruction.
As the summer school concludes on July 7, participants will return to universities and communities around the world carrying more than lecture notes and academic credits. They will leave with firsthand experience of a philosophy that has quietly endured for millennia and memories of a small Rajasthan town where, for three weeks, Jainism was not simply studied, but lived.(Aman Dhage contributed to the report.)(By arrangement with The American Bazaar)

headline: NEW DELHI: Even as exclusive breastfeeding rates have improved globally over the past decade, India continues to lag behind, with the proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months declining from 63.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 55....
full_text:
NEW DELHI: Even as exclusive breastfeeding rates have improved globally over the past decade, India continues to lag behind, with the proportion of infants exclusively breastfed for the first six months declining from 63.7% in NFHS-5 (2019-21) to 55.8% in NFHS-6 (2023-24).Ahead of World Breastfeeding Week (August 1-7), the World Health Organization (WHO) and UNICEF called for stronger support systems for mothers, saying global exclusive breastfeeding has increased from about 37% in 2012 to over 47% today, driven by sustained investments in health systems, community counselling and maternity protection. However, the agencies said progress remains uneven and many countries continue to fall short of global targets.Responding to a question in the Rajya Sabha, the Union health ministry attributed the decline in India's exclusive breastfeeding rate to multiple factors, including socio-cultural practices, family customs, individual preferences, the use of pre-lacteal feeds and infant milk substitutes, and breastfeeding frequency.The ministry, however, highlighted improvements in other breastfeeding indicators.
Early initiation of breastfeeding within one hour of birth increased from 41.8% to 50.1%, while the proportion of infants below six months receiving any breast milk rose marginally from 95.1% to 95.6%.The Rajya Sabha question had sought to know whether the government had assessed the impact of rising Caesarean deliveries, inadequate postnatal lactation counselling and early return to work, particularly among women in the informal sector. While the ministry did not provide findings of any such assessment, it said the National Health Mission promotes exclusive breastfeeding through the Mother Absolute Affection (MAA) programme, lactation management centres, healthcare worker training, Poshan Tracker-based counselling and community awareness campaigns.
It also cited a 2025 NITI Aayog evaluation, which found that new mothers were receiving information on exclusive breastfeeding during the postnatal period.Calling breastfeeding one of the most effective public health interventions, WHO and UNICEF said it provides essential nutrition, protects children against infections, strengthens immunity, supports cognitive development and lowers mothers' risk of breast and ovarian cancers and type 2 diabetes. The agencies said scaling up proven interventions, including skilled breastfeeding support, community counselling, paid maternity leave, supportive workplace policies and stronger regulation of breast-milk substitute marketing, could prevent nearly 400,000 child deaths and 140,000 maternal deaths globally every year.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

headline: Jaish operative, his girlfriend, honeytrap, and a plan to ‘target’ CM Suvendu, CJP protest: Bengal police's big case
full_text:
Jaish operative, his girlfriend, honeytrap, and a plan to ‘target’ CM Suvendu, CJP protest: Bengal police's big case
The Bengal STF arrested the alleged Jaish operative – who had planned to target Adhikari and carry out sabotage at the recent students' protest – on Friday.
An investigation into an extortion plan and the social media handle of a Jaish operative's alleged girlfriend led the West Bengal Special Task Force to uncover an alleged plan to track chief minister Suvendu Adhikari's movements for Pakistan-based criminals, officials have claimed.
The West Bengal STF arrested the alleged Jaish-e-Mohammed operative who had planned to target Adhikari and also carry out sabotage at the recent students' protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar in the guise of a police official, news agency PTI cited a senior officer of the unit as saying on Saturday.
The accused has been identified as Mohammed Hamim Mondal, who was arrested from Purba Bardhaman district on Friday and brought to Kolkata later that night for interrogation, IG (STF) Gaurav Sharma said. The STF also arrested Arpita Sarkar, alleged to be Mondal's girlfriend, on Friday.
The STF claimed that the duo had hatched a plot to honey-trap the son of a minister of state in West Bengal, and later abduct him to extort money from his family.
How did STF unravel the Jaish operative's plot?
The probe began after investigators received inputs regarding a conspiracy to extort money from the minister and abduct his son, according to another STF officer cited by PTI. “A few days ago, we received information about a plan to extort money from a senior politician from Howrah and abduct his son through a honey-trap. We were told that an organisation was behind the conspiracy,” the officer said
A probe into that led the STF to a social media handle from Sahibganj operated by Arpita Sarkar. Investigation into Sarkar's social media account then led the officers to the Jaish operative, the IG said. Mondal and Sarkar had allegedly been in contact for the last four years after getting acquainted on Instagram and later meeting in person. The STF said the two had been in a relationship and that the officers were further probing whether Sarkar had been used to lure potential targets as part of the honey-trap plan.
‘Contacted Pak-based handlers through WhatsApp, Telegram’
IG STF Gaurav Sharma said the investigation had establised Mondal's links with Pakistan-based handlers, adding that he had been working for them. The probe further revealed that Mondal had allegedly been radicalised through social media before coming in contact with Pakistan-based operatives linked to the Shahzad Bhatti group, Sharma added.
“Hamim had been assigned by Pakistan-based handlers the task of keeping a watch on the CM's movements. He was asked to gather information on the places the chief minister could remain unguarded,” PTI cited Sharma as saying at a press conference. Sharma added that several police officers and politicians were also targets.
The accused was reportedly in contact with the Pakistan-based handlers through encrypted messaging platforms, including WhatsApp and Telegram as well as Element X and Session.
“During the investigation of his mobile phone and social media chat history, we have found some very serious information. He was in touch with several Pakistan-based handlers through encrypted platforms such as WhatsApp and Telegram,” Sharma said.
The Bengal STF sleuths said they had also recovered international SIM cards issued in the United Kingdom and Mexico from the accused. They said these SIM cards had allegedly been used “for encrypted communication with handlers operating from abroad and to facilitate the strengthening of sleeper cells and the terror network in different parts of the country.”

headline: After being on tenterhooks for the past 24 hours, Pathanamthitta finally got some respite on Sunday as floodwaters began receding from several inundated areas, offering relief to thousands affected by the deluge. However, the Upper Kuttanad region co...
full_text:
After being on tenterhooks for the past 24 hours, Pathanamthitta finally got some respite on Sunday as floodwaters began receding from several inundated areas, offering relief to thousands affected by the deluge. However, the Upper Kuttanad region continued to bear the brunt of the rain fury, with rising waters forcing more evacuations and disrupting normal life.
Water levels in major rivers, including the Pamba, Achankovil and Manimala rivers, started receding as residents in the upper reaches began returning home. In Ranni, one of the worst-affected areas in the district, the flood situation improved considerably, allowing residents and traders to begin the recovery process. Shop owners were seen removing water-damaged goods from their establishments, with traders estimating losses running into several crores of rupees.
The floodwaters in Aranmula also began to recede, while authorities continued to urge people living in vulnerable areas to remain vigilant. The storage position in major reservoirs remained comfortable, with the live storage level in the Pamba reservoir at 35.47% and the Kakki dam at 44.11%.
However, as water receded from the upper reaches, the runoff entered the low-lying Upper Kuttanad region, inundating several houses and triggering a large-scale evacuation drive. Water levels continued to rise through the day in parts of the region, even as more people were shifted to relief camps.
Floodwaters from the Pamba and Manimala rivers spilled onto the Thiruvalla–Ambalappuzha State Highway around 1 a.m., inundating roads, houses, commercial establishments and places of worship. The Nedumpram stretch, which is prone to flooding during intense rain spells, witnessed major disruption to traffic movement.
KSRTC suspended services through the waterlogged stretch at Nedumpram. Buses from the Alappuzha, Edathua and Haripad depots operated only up to Chakkulathukavu Junction, while services from Thiruvalla were curtailed at Vaikkathillam Bridge.
Traffic on the Thiruvalla–Ambalappuzha State Highway came to a standstill after nearly 1.5 km of the road, from Padarattilpadi to NC Junction at Nedumpram, was submerged.
As of Sunday evening, the district had 95 relief camps sheltering 3,568 people. Thiruvalla taluk, which includes parts of the Upper Kuttanad region, accounted for the highest number of camps at 47. A detailed assessment is under way to ascertain the extent of damage to houses and property. Authorities have also issued orders to clear flood debris. Preliminary estimates indicate that one house was completely damaged, while 42 houses suffered partial damage.
In view of the continuing heavy rain and flooding, District Collector A. Nizamudeen declared a holiday for all educational institutions in Pathanamthitta, from anganwadis to professional colleges, as well as tuition centres, on Monday. The holiday will not apply to scheduled public and university examinations.
The Travancore Devaswom Board has also issued an advisory urging Sabarimala pilgrims to exercise extreme caution, considering the prevailing weather conditions.

headline: Supreme Court's Justice Bhuyan backs more transparency in collegium’s operation
full_text:
Supreme Court's Justice Bhuyan backs more transparency in collegium’s operation
Releasing a report on the Judicial Transparency Index, Justice Bhuyan said that not giving reasons is a disservice to many genuinely outstanding judges.
Justice Ujjal Bhuyan of the Supreme Court on Saturday observed that collegium resolutions are not being forwarded with reasons, questioning whether this was a “step back” from the principle of transparency that the judiciary has always embraced.
Releasing a report on the Judicial Transparency Index at an event in the Capital, justice Bhuyan said that not giving reasons is a disservice to many genuinely outstanding judges. Conversely, he said: “By withholding reasons, we also create space for individuals to enter the judiciary who may later describe groups of people as ‘ants’ and make other remarks that are wholly unconstitutional and contrary to the values of the Constitution.”
He was apparently referring to a controversial speech made by a former Allahabad high court judge at a VHP event in 2024 in a veiled reference to Muslims.
Also Read | ‘Collegium system well-suited for India': South Korea SC judge Justice Daeyup Chun | HT Interview
Justice Bhuyan said, “A judiciary that has embraced publicity in its adjudicative function has been markedly more cautious about extending the same principle to its own constitutive processes.”
He cited three recent Supreme Court collegium statements that do not contain any reason for recommending elevations as opposed to the earlier trend when detailed reasons accompanied resolutions forwarded by the collegium. “Is this a step back from the principle of transparency,” he asked.
Also Read | Collegium recommendation review will open ‘pandora’s box’: SC
He further observed that deliberations in the collegium remain confidential and reasons for rejecting or deferring a recommendation are rarely disclosed in full and the criteria applied are not codified in any publicly accessible instrument comparable to the Memorandum of Procedure.
Batting for open courts, he said, “There is no doubt that open courts make it possible for the public to develop reasonable perceptions about the judiciary, by enabling them to directly observe judicial behaviour, the processes and outcome of cases.”
Also Read | ‘Too important to discard, too imperfect to ignore’: The collegium system is flawed but necessary
On the recent SC hearing where use of judicial proceedings on social media was sought to be regulated, justice Bhuyan said the move by the CJI-led bench does not retreat from live-streaming. “Court’s concern is precisely that decontextualised fragments of oral exchanges, observations made by judges in the course of argument, not findings, are being circulated with sensational captions, causing reputational harm to judges, advocates, and litigants...”

headline: Watch: Scuffle erupts after slipper thrown at Pappu Yadav, MP claims ‘plot to kill’ him
full_text:
Watch: Scuffle erupts after slipper thrown at Pappu Yadav, MP claims ‘plot to kill’ him
In a video of the incident, a man is heard questioning Yadav, claiming the Independent MP from Purnia had hurt religious sentiments.
A scuffle broke out during Lok Sabha MP Pappu Yadav's press conference in Delhi, in the aftermath of several police complaints against him for a protest skit inside the Parliament premises.
In a video of the incident released by PTI news agency, Yadav is seen answering media questions outside his residence when an object is thrown at him, following which chaos erupts. Before this, a man is heard questioning Yadav, claiming the Independent MP from Purnia had hurt religious sentiments.
What led to the scuffle?
While the man continues to question Yadav, the MP is seen repeatedly asking him who he is. An object is then thrown at Yadav in between this exchange, resulting in the situation getting heated. The police personnel present at the scene are seen attempting to bring the situation under control.
Pappu Yadav's media convenor, who was present at the spot, said some people allegedly “took off a slipper and hurled it” towards the MP. He claimed a knife was also drawn to attack Yadav.
The convenor further claimed that the Delhi Police “stood by” during the incident, adding that they later “took the attackers away.” “... I was the one who personally met the DCP this morning and filed a formal complaint stating that the MP was arriving today and he has been recieving constant threats on social media... Despite knowing all this, they deployed only three or four police personnel here,” the convenor told ANI news agency.
‘Plot to kill me, but I survived’: Pappu Yadav
Speaking to reporters after the incident, Yadav alleged that it was an attempt “to kill” him, claiming a bounty had been announced against him. “Babas are saying every day, ‘Kill me, burn me down; we will give ₹ 51 lakh’. We caught him and handed him over to the police. There was a plot to kill me, but I survived,” Yadav said, according to ANI. He further alleged that the person involved in the incident was carrying a knife.
Responding to the BJP's charge saying the “skit” regarding the alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple donations had hurt religious sentiments, Yadav said the Opposition leaders were protesting to “protect Sanatan.” The Vishva Hindu Parishad (VHP) also attacked Yadav and Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi, who played a brief part in the protest skit.
FIR, police complaints against LoP Rahul Gandhi, MPs Pappu Yadav and Awadhesh Prasad
BJP MP Bansuri Swaraj and other leaders filed police complaints in Delhi against the protest skit, while a separate FIR was also registered against Rahul Gandhi, Pappu Yadav and Lok Sabha MP from Faizabad and Samajwadi Party leader Awadhesh Prasad.
The Varanasi Police registered the case against the three opposition leaders based on a formal complaint submitted at Kotwali police station by seers, who claimed that they had insulted Sanatan Dharma, PTI cited Gaurav Banswal, deputy commissioner of police, Kashi zone, as saying. “In a democracy, the Constitution certainly gives you the right to protest, but it does not permit you to hurt the faith of any community....” BJP MP Swaraj said.
Yadav had, dressed in a saffron outfit, performed the skit along with other opposition MPs in front of the Makar Dwar at the Parliament complex on Friday. While the opposition leaders put money inside donation boxes, Yadav slipped money into his pockets to symbolise the alleged embezzlement of Ram Temple donations.

headline: Book Box : The addictive art of pairing books
full_text:
Book Box : The addictive art of pairing books
How pairing books reveals the truth between the lines.
Dear Reader,
Recently, I’ve taken to pairing my reading, and it feels like a compounding of pleasures. Much like combining a cappuccino with a croissant. Or food with wine.
Whether it’s two entire novels, both about the same relationship, or fiction read alongside biography, this double-dipping has become addictive.
The “He Said, She Said” Pairing
I kicked off my reading year with the ultimate marital immersion: Mr. Bridge and Mrs. Bridge by Evan S. Connell.
The two books tell the story of an upper middle-class couple, Walter and India Bridge, who live in Kansas City in the period between the two world wars. We see the Bridges live their life with their three children, doing all the humdrum little things that make up domestic life. Dinner, shopping, managing investments. The stuff we all live through. But here’s the kicker: perspective is everything.
You read Walter’s side and think, 'Okay, he’s just practical.' You read India’s side and think, 'Okay, he’s a cold robot.' And then you sit back and realise that the truth is probably somewhere in the uncomfortable middle. It makes you look at your own family and go, hmm, which is deeply unsettling but also kind of the point.
Then there’s the other “She Says, He Says” duo I devoured: Bengal Nights by Mircea Eliade and It Does Not Die by Maitreyi Devi. Oh, the audacity of white men! And men in general.
Reading these books together is basically watching one man pass off stereotype and fantasy as fact and the woman valiantly snatch it back. It made me realize more than ever, how crucial it is to tell your own story—because if you don’t, someone else will, and they will absolutely get it skewed. Also, translation matters. So much. I could go on a whole rant about that, but I’ll save it for another Sunday.
The “Who Got the Credit?” Subject Pairing
You know when two people work on something, and only one of them gets all the fame and glory? Like the entire history of the world, basically written by the victor. Our book club decided to tackle this head-on earlier this year.
We read Anna Funder’s Wifedom, which is about George Orwell’s wife, Eileen, and Marie Benedict’s The Other Einstein, about, well, the other Einstein. Both women were brilliant, both got completely written out of the narrative.
But here’s where it gets interesting: Funder writes a kind of memoir-meets-biography, weaving her own life into Orwell’s story, while Benedict goes the historical fiction route. At the end we couldn’t agree on which style was more hard-hitting. One set insisted Funder’s genre-bending approach, part biography, part memoir, part indictment, was the only way to do justice to a woman like Eileen. The other set argued that Benedict’s historical fiction allowed for more emotional intimacy, more room to imagine what Einstein’s wife actually felt. We never agreed. But it was a great discussion which got us to think about so many things.
The Armchair Traveler Pairing (Next on my list)
Up next, I’m heading to Afghanistan. Vicariously. I plan to read this year’s winner of the Women’s Prize for non-fiction, The Finest Hotel in Kabul: A People’s History of Afghanistan by Lyse Doucet, along with a travelogue called Shadow City: A Woman Walks Kabul by Taran N. Khan. Maybe I’ll add a novel like The Little Coffee Shop of Kabul as well.
Whichever route I choose, I know one thing for sure: reading one book on a subject is fine, but reading two (or three) is where the real drama lies.
Have you ever tried pairing books, or do you stick to one at a time ? Send me your recommendations—I’m always looking for my next pair.
And here’s to a year of double-dipping on stories, reading between the lines, and questioning every author’s biases and blind spots.
Sonya Dutta Choudhury is a Mumbai-based journalist and Founder, Sonya’s Book Box, a bespoke book service. For all questions about life and literature email sonyasbookbox@gmail.com.

headline: Southern Railway has dropped departmental action contemplated against motorman K. Karunakaran, who flagged a major safety issue between Ambattur and Avadi railway stations here on March 5, 2026, and rewarded him for the good work, sources in the zona...
full_text:
Southern Railway has dropped departmental action contemplated against motorman K. Karunakaran, who flagged a major safety issue between Ambattur and Avadi railway stations here on March 5, 2026, and rewarded him for the good work, sources in the zonal headquarters said.
The motorman’s name was also recommended for an award at the Railway Board level. On the day of the incident, Mr. Karunakaran stopped his train, despite the signal giving clearance to proceed, after seeing two other trains parked on the same track. He photographed the scene and alerted his superior officers about the safety issue.
The signal failure was rectified and normal train services resumed. Investigators held the motorman “blameworthy” for exceeding the permissible speed limit. The All India Loco Running Staff Association had represented to the railway authorities to drop action against Mr. Karunakaran as he had done his best in the dynamic situation.
A multi-departmental inquiry, comprising senior railway officers drawn from different departments, confirmed the signal failure. Further inquiry revealed that the particular automatic signal (S192) had failed multiple times but was reset by a local signal department technician without following the standard operating procedure. A few other automatic signals had also failed in recent times but were reset with no investigation conducted to analyse the root cause.
The inquiry committee gave a set of recommendations on the safety front. The railway officers who examined the sequence of events, circumstances that led to the incident, and technical evidence called for launching a safety drive in Chennai Division. They said the Station Masters should be counselled about the rule position in resetting the multi-section digital axle counter (MASDAC) while restoring signal failures. Since the failure buzzer that alerted the Station Master of signal failures was found disconnected on March 5, 2026, the committee wanted the authorities concerned to check and ensure the functioning of the same.
To avoid opening of the relay room randomly by the signal technicians for resetting, a double lock arrangement was recommended for access control. The diagnostic panels in MSDAC huts should be made failsafe, the report said.
The Chennai Division accepted the recommendations and directed the departments concerned to take necessary action, the sources said. There was no response from the Southern Railway spokesperson to questions sent by The Hindu on the inquiry committee’s recommendations and the reward given to the whistleblower motorman.

The YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) president and former Chief Minister Y. S. Jagan Mohan Reddy on Sunday accused the TDP-led coalition government of misusing the police machinery to target Opposition leaders and workers. He alleged that those responsible for attacks were being protected while cases were being registered against the victims.
In a post on X, referring to the arrest of Alur MLA B. Virupakshi, Mr. Jagan questioned the deployment of a large police contingent to arrest the legislator and his son, Chandrasekhar, from their residence in the early hours of Sunday. He alleged that the manner in which the arrest was carried out raised serious concerns about the rule of law in the State.
Mr. Jagan said that the episode stemmed from an attack on the residence of a YSRCP leader at Nemakallu village in Chippagiri mandal. He said the local leader had contacted Mr. Virupakshi seeking protection for his family and argued that responding to such an appeal from a party worker could not be treated as a crime.
He further alleged that TDP workers attacked the MLA when he visited the village and that the legislator’s brother, Sriramulu, sustained injuries in the incident. Instead of taking action against those responsible for the attack, the government had allegedly registered attempt-to-murder cases against the MLA and YSRCP workers, he said.
Mr. Jagan also questioned the seizure of CCTV hard disks from the MLA’s residence and alleged that the move was intended to prevent the release of footage of the police action. He further claimed that several YSRCP leaders had been booked in different cases for opposing the government.
The former Chief Minister also alleged that former Guntur East MLA Shaik Mohammed Mustafa and his son had been implicated in a kidnapping case despite having handed over the person concerned to the police.
Asserting that the YSRCP would continue to stand by its workers, Mr. Jagan said arrests, police action and criminal cases would not deter the party from fighting what he described as political vendetta and injustice.

full_text:
NEW DELHI: Want to age more slowly? The answer may lie not just in exercise and diet, but also in a trip to the theatre, museum or even the cinema.A new study by Japanese researchers has found that older adults who engage more frequently in cultural activities tend to have a lower physiological ageâa measure of how well the body's organs and systems are functioningâthan their actual age, suggesting cultural engagement may be an overlooked tool for healthy ageing.Researchers from the Institute of Science Tokyo analysed 4,207 observations from 1,899 adults aged 50 years and above in the English Longitudinal Study of Ageing. Participants who more frequently visited cinemas, museums, art galleries, theatres, concerts or the opera had lower physiological age. Every one-point increase in cultural engagement score was associated with a 0.085-year reduction in physiological age, even after adjusting for income, health status, employment, smoking, physical activity and other factors. The association persisted in a four-year follow-up analysis. Physiological age, estimated using 10 markers including blood pressure, lung function, grip strength, walking speed, BMI, haemoglobin, cholesterol and blood sugar, is considered a better predictor of disease and mortality than chronological age.The researchers said cultural engagement may promote healthy ageing by strengthening social connections, reducing loneliness and stress, improving mental well-being and encouraging healthier lifestyles.
Indian experts said the findings reinforce the importance of staying socially engaged as people age.Dr Prasun Chatterjee, Group Clinical Lead, Department of Geriatric Medicine and Longevity Sciences, Apollo Hospitals, and former professor at AIIMS, said the findings reinforce that healthy ageing depends not only on diet and exercise but also on social and cultural engagement. Social interaction improves memory and mood by boosting serotonin and dopamine, enhancing emotional well-being, memory and a sense of purpose, which encourage healthier lifestyles. In the Indian context, he said, activities such as visiting parks, cinemas, theatres or places of worship can provide similar benefits by promoting happiness, social connection and purpose.Prof Rajesh Sagar, psychiatrist at AIIMS, New Delhi, said social and cultural engagement promotes healthy ageing by strengthening emotional support networks, improving cognitive function and reducing chronic stress.
He said loneliness increases the risk of depression, anxiety and cognitive decline while reducing motivation for physical activity. He advised older adults to stay socially connected by regularly meeting friends and relatives or joining walking groups, book clubs, music classes or spiritual gatherings.The authors cautioned that the study shows an association, not causation, as healthier people may also be more likely to participate in cultural activities. headline: Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday (August 2, 2026) accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of misusing the talent of helpless and vulnerable artistes to further its own political interests. The BJP fears expression of creativit...
full_text:
Samajwadi Party (SP) president Akhilesh Yadav on Sunday (August 2, 2026) accused the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) of misusing the talent of helpless and vulnerable artistes to further its own political interests. The BJP fears expression of creativity as it will further strengthen the “anti-establishment wave”, Mr. Yadav said after making an “offering” of ₹51,000 each to two Ramlila artistes, who play Lord Ram and Lord Hanuman. The BJP stands for “bhrasht” (corrupt), “julm” (oppression), and “paap” (sin), the Opposition leader said. All major problems in Uttar Pradesh would end only after the BJP was voted out of power, he said.
Mr. Yadav took to social media platform X to address creative professionals. “Dear artistes and creators, The way the Bharatiya Janata Party misused the talent of a helpless and vulnerable artiste to further its own political interests is highly condemnable. Everyone knows that a few days ago, during the arrival of the BJP’s national president (Nitin Nabin) in Lucknow, an artiste dressed as Hanuman was made to dance in front of his (Mr. Nabin’s) chariot. This has caused deep resentment among devotees of Bajrangbali (Lord Hanuman) worldwide to this day. This is not the fault of any poor artiste forced to support their families, as there is no place for artistes in the BJP government. Negative BJP members have always been opposed to creativity as it (creativity) forges a new path against conventions and orthodoxies, which the BJP’s conservative thinking does not like at all since they fear the expression of creativity will further strengthen the ‘anti-establishment wave’. Therefore, whether it’s a writer, an honest journalist, or any artiste, these BJP members and their allies do not want them to speak out or find any platform for their artistic expression. If the BJP ever gives artistes an opportunity, it’s for its (the party’s) own respect, not for theirs (the artistes’),” Mr. Yadav said in his post, along with images of the Ramlila artistes he had awarded.
“Today, we altogether helped the artiste who is facing financial crises, and will continue to do so (support artistes) in future so that he can face the illness and misery going on in his family. Artistry refines humanity. Art promotes tolerance, harmony, camaraderie, and equality, which is why those who engage in negative divisive politics are opposed to artistes,” Mr. Yadav added.
“Today, we promise to every artiste that just as we gave every type of respect and financial support to artistes during our government even after the coming of the new government, we will take that healthy tradition of creativity forward and will felicitate the special, talented people associated with Uttar Pradesh for their social contribution by giving them the ‘Yash Bharti Samman’ and ₹1 lakh per month for life,” the SP chief said.
The BJP government in Uttar Pradesh had closed more than 26,000 government primary schools since assuming power in 2017, Mr. Yadav also alleged on Sunday, claiming this had been done to deny education to children from the PDA (Pichhda or Backward Class, Dalit, and Alpsankhyak or Minority) communities. “Uttar Pradesh had 1,13,938 government primary schools until March 2017, when the BJP came to power. More than 26,000 of them have been closed since then,” the SP leader said.

headline: The State government is likely to seek explanation from officials of the Local Self Government department as well as the Home department over a letter which was used by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Thiruvananthapuram Corporation administratio...
full_text:
The State government is likely to seek explanation from officials of the Local Self Government department as well as the Home department over a letter which was used by the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)-led Thiruvananthapuram Corporation administration to secure six months of leave for BJP councillor R. Sugathan, who was arrested under the Kerala Anti-Social Activities (Prevention) Act (KAAPA) and is currently lodged at the high-security correctional facility at Viyyur Central Prison in Thrissur.
The letter, dated July 20, 2026 and signed by an Under Secretary on behalf of the Additional Chief Secretary, was sent to Mr. Sugathan in response to his request for an escort parole to take part in the council meeting on Friday (July 31). Though the government rejected the request, the letter further goes on to detail ways in which he can avoid disqualification. It suggests submitting a leave letter to the council through the Jail Superintendent. Further, it says that if the council approves this request through voting, his councillor post will be “safe.”
Unfortunate incident
Minister for LSGs K.M.Shaji told mediapersons on Sunday that it was unfortunate that a letter which went through his department had aided a “criminal” to secure leave. An official in the LSGD had reportedly added the additional lines which suggested that Mr. Sugathan can get a leave through voting in the council. “The Minister and the Secretary had rejected the request for leave. However, it is not right for any official to add to the report we had signed on. In case such additions are made, it has to come back to us. However, in this case, the report went to the Home department after the official made the addition. Such conduct cannot be allowed. On Monday, we will take decisive action on this,” said Mr. Shaji.
Earlier, Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala had also expressed dissatisfaction at the letter, dated July 20, 2026, which was signed by an Under Secretary on behalf of the Additional Chief Secretary, Home department. The Left Democratic Front (LDF) had pointed to the letter as yet another instance of a Congress-BJP understanding.

headline: Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is in the firing line from the Opposition for using a helicopter hired by the State government primarily as an air ambulance and for other emergencies for an alleged personal visit to Kochi.
full_text:
Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan is in the firing line from the Opposition for using a helicopter hired by the State government primarily as an air ambulance and for other emergencies for an alleged personal visit to Kochi.
Mr. Satheesan reportedly flew aboard the helicopter from Golf Club in Thiruvananthapuram to Kochi on Friday to visit his father-in-law, who was undergoing treatment. However, inclement weather prevented the helicopter from landing, and it returned to Thiruvananthapuram. Reports suggest the journey was made later.
CPI(M) State committee member M.B. Rajesh slammed Mr. Satheesan for using the helicopter “for personal purposes, with prime-time actors in [his] lap remaining in silent mode”, in an oblique criticism of prime-time television anchors for not covering the issue. As Leader of the Opposition, Mr. Satheesan had criticised the then LDF government for its “extravagance” in hiring the helicopter.
Another State committee member of the CPI(M), V. Sivankutty, also mocked Mr. Satheesan’s flight as a ‘U-turn’ by the helicopter. Health Minister K. Muraleedharan defended the Chief Minister’s use of the chopper, saying modes of transport change with the times. He also contended that “nobody was criticised earlier for travelling by helicopter”.
However, social media was abuzz with criticism over the helicopter journey, with many users digging up old posts by Mr. Satheesan and other Congress leaders criticising the then State government and then Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan for hiring the helicopter. The Chief Minister’s Office did not respond to messages seeking clarification.
(With agency inputs)

headline: The 679th Foundation Day of Bahmani Empire was observed at the tomb of Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, the founder and first ruler of the Sultanate, in Kalaburagi city on Monday.
full_text:
The 679th Foundation Day of Bahmani Empire was observed at the tomb of Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah, the founder and first ruler of the Sultanate, in Kalaburagi city on Monday.
The event, organised by the Bahmani Foundation, brought together historians, artists, intellectuals and social activists, who recalled the contributions of the Bahmani Sultanate to the cultural and architectural heritage of the region during its nearly two-century rule from 1347 to 1527 AD.
Speaking on the occasion, advocate Jabbar Gola said the Bahmani rulers played an important role in promoting art, culture and architecture, leaving behind a rich legacy reflected in the monuments and traditions of the region.
Bahmani Foundation president Qazi Rizwan-Ur-Rahman Siddique said the organisation has been commemorating the Foundation Day for several years through seminars, cultural programmes and competitions aimed at creating awareness among students about the history and heritage of the Bahmani period.
Artists Mohammed Ayazuddin Patel and Rehaman Patel, Numismatist Mohammad Ismail and others were present.

headline: SC agrees to examine Madras HC order on Karthigai Deepam near dargah
full_text:
SC agrees to examine Madras HC order on Karthigai Deepam near dargah
The bench also questioned the Tamil Nadu government over the delay in actively pursuing the appeal after filing it in June.
The Supreme Court on Monday agreed to examine the correctness of Madras high court orders permitting the lighting of the Karthigai Deepam at a stone pillar near a dargah atop the Thirupparankundram hill in Madurai, while declining to suspend the operation of the judicial directions at this stage.
A bench of justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M Pancholi issued notice on the Tamil Nadu government’s appeal challenging the high court’s December 2025 and January 2026 orders, directing the respondents to file their replies within six weeks. The state was granted two weeks thereafter to file a rejoinder.
The court, however, refused the state’s request for an interim stay of the high court orders.
During the hearing, the bench also questioned the Tamil Nadu government over the delay in actively pursuing the appeal after filing it in June. “If this situation had cropped up in January 2026, when this order came, what were you doing all this time?” asked the bench.
The state attributed the delay to the time taken to translate voluminous records before the matter could be effectively pursued.
When the state expressed concern over contempt proceedings pending before the Madras high court for alleged non-compliance with its earlier directions, the Supreme Court asked it to mention the issue before the concerned division bench of the high court instead of seeking interim protection from the apex court.
The counsel appearing for the respondents opposed the appeal, contending that the state had filed the special leave petition but failed to prosecute it for nearly seven months and was now seeking urgent consideration only because of a change in the political dispensation.
According to the respondents, the state had also relied on the pendency of the Supreme Court proceedings to resist the contempt proceedings before the high court.
The appeal has been filed by the Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments (HR&CE) Department after the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam government led by chief minister C Joseph Vijay assumed office.
The state has challenged the Madras high court’s directions permitting the Arulmigu Subramania Swamy Temple Devasthanam to light the Karthigai Deepam at the Deepa Thoon, a stone lamp pillar situated about 50 metres from the Sikander Badusha Dargah atop the Thirupparankundram hill.
The controversy arose after devotee Rama Ravikumar sought permission in October 2025 to light the traditional lamp at the Deepa Thoon. After the temple administration informed him that the festival would continue to be celebrated at its customary location near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple, he and other devotees approached the Madras High Court.
On December 1, 2025, justice GR Swaminathan directed that the Karthigai Deepam be lit at the Deepa Thoon in addition to the existing venue, observing that doing so would honour Tamil tradition and reaffirm the temple’s title over the property. A division bench substantially upheld the direction on January 6, while restricting the ritual to a small official team, with the number of participants to be decided in consultation with the Archaeological Survey of India and the police. Members of the public were barred from accompanying the team.
In its appeal, the state has argued that the high court effectively created a new religious practice unsupported by any established custom, Agama prescription, temple record, inscription or historical material. It has maintained that for over 150 years the Karthigai Deepam has been lit at the Deepa Mandapam near the Uchi Pillaiyar Temple and never at the Deepa Thoon.
The petition further contends that while Article 25 guarantees the right to worship, it does not confer a right upon individual devotees to alter or introduce temple rituals, and that courts ought not to interfere in matters concerning religious ceremonies and established practices.

headline: Courts can't ‘teach or preach’ citizens on what to say: Former SC judge Abhay S Oka
full_text:
Courts can't ‘teach or preach’ citizens on what to say: Former SC judge Abhay S Oka
Justice Oka said courts are not meant to decide what citizens should or should not say. Their responsibility is to safeguard fundamental rights.
It is not the function of courts to “preach or teach” citizens on what they ought to say or not, retired Supreme Court Judge Abhay Oka said, while urging constitutional courts to quash criminal cases initiated merely to silence dissent.
Speaking at the inaugural Advocate Haroon Solkar Memorial Lecture Series in Mumbai on Saturday, Justice Oka said courts are not meant to decide what citizens should or should not say. Their responsibility is to safeguard fundamental rights, even when the views expressed by individuals may not align with those of the judges, news agency PTI reported.
Courts must protect dissent, even when they disagree with views
Justice Oka said citizens have a constitutional right to stage peaceful protests and express their grievances.
Also read | ‘Citizens need not say only what rulers like’: Justice Abhay Oka on free speech, protests
Referring to Irish writer Sir Thomas More, he said citizens cannot be expected to speak only in ways that please those in power.
“If democracy is to survive, we must guard and protect our freedoms guaranteed under Articles 19(1)(a) and 21 of the Constitution of India (dealing with fundamental rights) even if we have to pay a huge cost to protect these fundamental rights,” he told the gathering, as per the news agency.
He highlighted that people often approach courts seeking the dismissal of criminal cases filed over alleged violations of their right to freedom of expression.
Also read | 'Withdraw FIRs now': CJP to BJP after top court clarifies order on protest-linked cases
When such matters come before courts, judges must examine whether an offence has actually been committed and whether there has been an infringement of fundamental rights, Justice Oka said.
‘It is not the function of court to preach or teach’
Justice Oka said courts may not agree with the statements or opinions expressed by petitioners, but that cannot become a reason to deny protection of free speech.
“The court may not like what the petitioners have said or expressed, but still it is the duty of the court to protect the freedom of speech and expression. It is not the function of the court to preach or teach the petitioner what he or she should have said or not said,” the former Judge said.
Also read | Stone-pelting by CJP protesters happened even after Parliament march violence: Officials
He said the role of courts is limited to determining whether an offence is made out and whether constitutional rights have been violated.
Peaceful protests are constitutional right
Justice Oka said citizens have the right to put forward their demands, while the state has a responsibility to consider them.
He added that if grievances are not addressed, people have the right to hold peaceful protests as a way of expressing their dissatisfaction.
"If demands are not considered, the citizens have a right to stage a peaceful protest, because that is the only way of expressing displeasure," noted Justice Oka, who served in the Supreme Court from August 2021 until May 2025.
He said courts must remain vigilant against attempts to weaken constitutional values and ensure that freedom of speech and expression is not restricted.
"I always believe that the courts must be at the forefront to protect the fundamental rights of citizens. It is the bounden duty of the courts to ensure that the Constitution and its ideals are not trampled upon," he observed.
Justice Oka raises concern over intolerance towards criticism
Justice Oka questioned who would protect fundamental rights if courts failed to do so.
"If courts are not going to protect these fundamental rights then who is?," Justice Oka questioned.
He also reminded the government of its constitutional obligations, saying that when the state violates citizens' fundamental rights, it fails in its duties.
Justice Oka said constitutional principles such as secularism, democracy and liberty must be respected by the state.
"But in the present day, we rarely see the government respecting the ideals under the Constitution," Justice Oka said.
Disagreement should lead to dialogue, not attacks
The former Supreme Court judge also expressed concern over increasing intolerance towards criticism.
He said disagreement with a viewpoint should be addressed by presenting an alternative opinion rather than targeting the person expressing it.
Justice Oka reiterated that in a democracy, citizens have the right to raise demands and the government has a duty to engage with them.
"The government may or may not accept it (demands), but it is the government's duty to consider it, have a dialogue and discussion. But perhaps with the passage of time, we have all forgotten these golden principles," he noted.

headline: CJP to hold its first core committee meeting on Aug 5 to discuss future plans
full_text:
CJP to hold its first core committee meeting on Aug 5 to discuss future plans
CJP led the 36-day-long student protest over the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) paper leak and other alleged exam irregularities at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) will hold its first core committee meeting in Chhatrapati Sambhaji Nagar on Wednesday to discuss its future course, organisational expansion and the public issues it plans to address in the coming months.
CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke said members from across the country have been invited to attend the meeting. “This meeting has been called to decide our agenda. We will discuss how to expand the organisation, identify the issues we should take up in the interest of the people, and chart the roadmap for the outfit,” Dipke said on Monday.
He dismissed speculation that CJP could transform into a political party, asserting that it will continue to function as a people’s movement. “We have no intention of turning the organisation into a political outfit. We want it to continue as a people’s movement.”
“Given the current circumstances, I see no reason to convert CJP into a political party,” adding, “When votes are being deleted, people are losing faith in the electoral process, when they vote for someone in the morning and by the evening someone else gets elected, when they elect MLAs and MPs from one party and they switch their allegiance to another political party, and political parties are split with the help of the ED (Enforcement Directorate) and the CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation), forming a political party is not the solution.”
Also Read:‘There would have been no CJP’: Dipke ‘credits’ CJI Surya Kant for nationwide student protests
Responding to a demand by a Surat-based Right to Information (RTI) activist seeking an inquiry into his family’s finances, Dipke said he will make documents related to his educational loan, scholarship and academic qualifications public.
“If Prime Minister Modi ji is willing to make his educational degree public, I am also ready to make public all my documents related to my educational loan and scholarship. I have my original degree, and I hope the Prime Minister’s degree is genuine as well. Let him make his documents public, and I will do the same,” he said.
CJP led the 36-day-long student protest over the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) paper leak and other alleged exam irregularities at Delhi’s Jantar Mantar that led to the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan on July 25.

headline: A masked assailant dragged a 30-year-old teacher out of her class and stabbed her to death at a private school in Sikrauna in Haryana's Faridabad on Monday.
full_text:
A masked assailant dragged a 30-year-old teacher out of her class and stabbed her to death at a private school in Sikrauna in Haryana's Faridabad on Monday.
Police said the teacher was stabbed in the neck and chest at least 18 to 20 times in quick succession, resulting in her death at the spot.
The assailant masked his face with a white cloth. He entered the school premises through the main entrance between 9.30am and 9.40am and asked for the teacher after waiting inside for some time.
Inspector Kewal Singh, the station house officer of Faridabad's Sector-58 police station, said that as soon as the teacher came out, the assailant dragged her and stabbed her multiple times after pulling out a knife.
Singh said the assailant chased the teacher's colleagues away and then began stabbing her again, targeting the neck, until she collapsed, as they rushed to rescue her after hearing her screams.
Investigators said that the assailant fled as colleagues rushed the teacher to the Al-Falah Medical College and Hospital, where doctors declared her dead. Police said the teacher is a mother of two.
Police said CCTV footage of the murder has surfaced and they were trying to ascertain the assailant's identity to arrest him.

headline: As many as 3,444 students in Malappuram received allotment in the Plus One higher secondary second supplementary allotment that was published on Monday (August 3, 2026). Across the State, 9,270 students have secured allotment.

headline: A retired sub-inspector of the local intelligence unit (LIU) allegedly shot himself with his licensed single-barrel gun at his home in Uttar Pradesh's Unnao district and died while being taken to hospital, police said on Monday.
full_text:
A retired sub-inspector of the local intelligence unit (LIU) allegedly shot himself with his licensed single-barrel gun at his home in Uttar Pradesh's Unnao district and died while being taken to hospital, police said on Monday.
The deceased was identified as Ramjeet (65), a native of Rautamai village in Kannauj district's Gursahaiganj area. He had retired from the LIU in 2021 and was living with his son Abhishek in PD Nagar locality of Unnao, police said.
According to police, Ramjeet had dinner with his family on Sunday night before retiring to his room.
At around 11.30 pm, family members rushed to the room after hearing a gunshot and found him critically injured. Ramjeet was being taken to a hospital in Kanpur for treatment but succumbed to his injuries on the way, police said.
In his statement to police, Abhishek said his father had been under mental stress for some time and suspected that he had shot himself with his licensed firearm.
On receiving information, personnel from Sadar Kotwali police station and a forensic team reached the spot, collected evidence and seized the licensed single-barrel gun.
Circle Officer Vini Singh inspected the scene, while Sadar Kotwali Station House Officer Chandrakant Mishra said the exact cause of death would be established after the post-mortem examination, forensic analysis and other evidence are examined.
Police said Ramjeet's wife had died earlier and he had been living with his son's family.

headline: 'Not a single penny came from their pockets': UP CM Yogi Adityanath slams opposition on Ram temple donation case
full_text:
'Not a single penny came from their pockets': UP CM Yogi Adityanath slams opposition on Ram temple donation case
UP CM Yogi Adityanath alleged that those criticising the handling of donations for the Ram temple had earlier tried to stall the temple's construction.
Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday said those raising questions on the handling of donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya had earlier attempted to obstruct the temple's construction, and slammed their "double standards".
Talking to reporters before the commencement of the Monsoon Session of the state legislature, Adityanath also appealed to all legislators to ensure a constructive discussion in the House and said the government had brought a supplementary budget aimed at strengthening welfare measures for various categories of frontline workers.
"The Ayodhya issue is being raised by those who had fired bullets at Ram devotees. They are the same people who used to resort to lathi-charge and firing when people raised the slogan of 'Jai Shri Ram'," the chief minister said without naming any party.
Also Read | Ram Temple donation row: SP stages protests as UP assembly monsoon session begins
He alleged that those criticising the handling of donations for the Ram temple had earlier tried to stall the temple's construction by "deploying an army of lawyers" in courts.
"They talk about theft of donations meant for the Ram temple, but not a single penny for the temple's construction came from their pockets. The country and the world are watching their double standards," Adityanath said.
His remarks came amid opposition protests over the Ram temple donation issue during the opening day of the Monsoon session of the state legislature.
The chief minister said the government expects meaningful deliberations in the legislature and called upon members across party lines to contribute positively to the proceedings.
Also Read | Slipper thrown at MP Pappu Yadav over Parliament Ram temple skit, two detained
"I appeal to all honourable public representatives to maintain healthy discussion and debate in the House," he said.
Referring to the supplementary budget, Adityanath said it included provisions to enhance financial support for Anganwadi workers, ASHA workers, cooks engaged in government programmes and village chowkidars.
"The supplementary budget has been brought to ensure these workers receive a handsome honorarium and continue serving the interests of the state," he said.
Also Read | Ram temple donation probe in final stage: Trust member
Expressing confidence that the legislature would function smoothly, the chief minister urged the opposition to move beyond "negative politics" and work together for the welfare of the state's 25 crore people.
"I hope our opposition colleagues will give up negative politics, adopt a positive approach and contribute to Uttar Pradesh's changed perception, development and prosperity," Adityanath said.
