headline: TMC-turned-NCPI MP cites Muslim interests, says will not remain in NDA nor join BJP
full_text:
TMC-turned-NCPI MP cites Muslim interests, says will not remain in NDA nor join BJP
Abu Taher Khan said they are from Murshidabad, West Bengal’s Muslim-majority district, and have to protect the interests of Muslims
Member of Parliament (MP) Abu Taher Khan, who was among the Trinamool Congress (TMC) defectors who joined the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) constituent Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI) in June, on Tuesday said that he would not remain in the ruling bloc nor join the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), citing Muslim interests.
“We will not support any bill that goes against the interest of Muslims. We are from Murshidabad and have to protect the interests of Muslims,” Khan said after skipping a second NDA meeting along with two other Lok Sabha members, Khalilur Rahman and Yusuf Pathan. Khan said they were giving a message by not attending the NDA meetings.
The three were among the 20 MPs who left the TMC and joined the NCPI, an unrecognised party that contested two assembly seats in Tripura and polled a few hundred votes, after the TMC lost power in West Bengal to the BJP after 15 years. The rebels announced support for the BJP-led NDA after joining the NCPI.
Khan, Rahman, and Pathan represent West Bengal’s Muslim-majority Murshidabad district.
Sudip Bandopadhyay, the leader of the 20 MPs, separately met the Prime Minister on Monday amid speculation that they might join the BJP. The group was also due to meet West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari in Delhi on Tuesday. “Nineteen of us will attend the meeting with the chief minister. Only one is out of station,” Bandopadhyay said.
Khan said he and the two other lawmakers from Murshidabad would attend the meeting. “This is about issues relating to development projects in our constituencies,” Khan said.
In Bengal, minister Agnimitra Paul said she and her colleagues are too busy with development work to keep track of people switching sides. “We are working all day for the state’s development. We do not have the time to track who is on whose side and who is switching parties. The Prime Minister and the chief minister are there to ensure the best for our state and the nation. Nation first,” Paul said.
The Mamata Banerjee-led TMC faction said at least six of the 20 MPs are in touch with them. “The BJP is protecting them. Otherwise they would have lost their Lok Sabha membership because they won the polls on TMC tickets,” said TMC leader Kunal Ghosh.
Also Read: ‘You want me to have heart attack, I’ll live to see your end': Mamata to BJP amid TMC rebellion
Ghosh claimed at least 30 of the 60 TMC legislators who joined the rebel Ritabrata Banerjee-led faction were in touch with Mamata Banerjee and other leaders in their group. Ritabrata Banerjee dismissed Ghosh’s claim. “They should be more concerned about the rest of the MPs who are ready to leave,” he said.
The TMC won 29 of West Bengal’s 42 Lok Sabha seats in 2024. One of them died months after the election. Of the remaining 28, 20 joined the NCPI on June 14, questioning TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee’s leadership.
The Mamata Banerjee-led TMC was left with nine Rajya Sabha members after Sukhendu Sekhar Roy, Sushmita Dev and Prakash Chik Baraik resigned in June, joined the BJP and were re-elected to the upper House on July 24. A fourth TMC Rajya Sabha member, actor Koel Mallick, resigned from the Rajya Sabha in July.

headline: ‘My words had only one meaning’: Udhayanidhi Stalin rejects Trisha remark allegations, calls Vijay's TVK a ‘circus’
full_text:
‘My words had only one meaning’: Udhayanidhi Stalin rejects Trisha remark allegations, calls Vijay's TVK a ‘circus’
The DMK leader alleged that the Vijay-led government edited his speech to divert attention from the Cauvery issue.
Tamil Nadu Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin on Tuesday denied allegations that he made “double-meaning” remarks against actor Trisha Krishnan during a rally in Thanjavur. His speech was only about the release of Cauvery water for the state's farmers, he said, and accused the ruling Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government of twisting his words.
Speaking to reporters after his release, the DMK leader said he had not spoken against anyone. “I did not speak with any wrongful or malicious intent. I was arrested simply for speaking in support of farmers,” Udhayanidhi said.
ALSO READ | Udhayanidhi Stalin detained after TVK's complaint over his alleged remarks against Trisha Krishnan
Udhayanidhi also dismissed allegations that he had insulted women. "I have a wife, a sister and a daughter. I have not said anything against women," he said.
On the allegation that his remarks carried a “double meaning”, he said his words had “only one meaning”, a demand for the release of Cauvery water for the benefit of Tamil Nadu's farmers.
"My words had only one meaning. I never intended to insult anyone," he said.
What did Udhayanidhi Stalin say on Trisha Krishnan?
The controversy began during a DMK protest in Thanjavur over the Cauvery water dispute and Karnataka's proposed Mekedatu project. While addressing the gathering, Udhayanidhi Stalin criticised the Tamil Nadu government over the Cauvery issue.
During his speech, some people in the crowd started chanting Tamil Nadu chief minister and TVK chief Vijay's friend and fellow actor Trisha Krishnan's name. Udhayanidhi then made a remark in Tamil that was interpreted by some as vulgar double entendre.
ALSO READ | From Sanatana row to alleged remarks against Trisha: The many controversies of Udhayanidhi Stalin
Trisha has acted in several films with Tamil Nadu Vijay. The two have also been linked by dating rumours, though neither has confirmed them publicly.
Stalin alleges speech was edited
The DMK leader alleged that the government circulated an edited version of his speech to divert attention from the Cauvery issue ahead of the Assembly session.
“Yesterday's protest received a strong response from farmers. Since the issue had gained momentum and the Opposition was set to raise it in the Assembly, the government circulated a cut-and-paste version of my speech and falsely claimed I had made remarks that I never uttered,” he said.
He said he fully cooperated with the police during his detention and accused the government of trying to intimidate the Opposition through false cases.
ALSO READ | ‘Offensive’ remarks to detention: 6 points on Udhayanidhi Stalin's Trisha comments row
"They are trying to silence me and intimidate me, but I will not be intimidated. We are not afraid of such actions," he said.
Calling the TVK government a "circus," Udhayanidhi said, "I do not consider this to be a government in the true sense; I see it as nothing more than a circus." He alleged that the government's first response to DMK legislators was to arrest them instead of addressing public issues.
He also criticised the manner of his detention, saying he was treated "like a terrorist" despite cooperating with the police. "They treated me like a terrorist and transported me by road all the way to Thanjavur," he said.
Case against Udhayanidhi
Udhayanidhi was detained on Tuesday after police registered a case based on a complaint filed by a TVK functionary. He was released after over an hour of questioning.
He has been booked under various provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Information Technology Act and the Tamil Nadu Women Harassment Prevention Act.

Committee Chairman Radha Mohan Singh is learnt to have said that the panel would seek detailed information from the government on the role of private institutions in the management and functioning of the schools.
HOW NEW SAINIK SCHOOLS ARE SELECTED
The Union Cabinet approved the establishment of 100 New Sainik Schools under the PPP model in October 2021. Of these, 86 schools have been approved over three rounds and 79 are currently operational. Applications under the fourth round are being processed for the remaining schools.
NGOs, trusts, societies and private and government schools can apply to establish a New Sainik School under either the greenfield or brownfield category.
Applications are submitted through an online portal and first examined by a Documents Scrutiny Committee comprising five serving uniformed officers. The panel assesses whether an applicant meets requirements related to land, infrastructure, sports facilities and other basic criteria.
Schools clearing this stage are physically inspected by a School Evaluation Committee comprising the district magistrate or collector, the principal of a Navodaya Vidyalaya or Kendriya Vidyalaya in the district and the principal of the nearest Sainik School.
The committee verifies the applicant’s facilities and submits its assessment to the Sainik Schools Society.
The report is then examined by an Approval Committee comprising the honorary secretary of the Sainik Schools Society, a representative of the Department of School Education and Literacy and a Brigadier-rank officer, among others.
CRITERIA FOR APPROVAL
Defence sources said the shortlisting process considers geographical spread, district population density and the principle of approving one New Sainik School in each district.
Preference is given to existing brownfield schools over greenfield projects. Among brownfield applicants, schools with stronger academic records receive priority.
Boarding schools are also preferred over private day schools, the sources said.
New Sainik Schools may operate as day schools, residential schools or day-cum-boarding institutions. Day schools require at least six acres of land, while residential schools need a minimum of eight acres.
Defence sources said the scheme aims to mould young students into responsible citizens and maintained that the multi-stage selection process is based on objective criteria rather than political or ideological affiliation.

UP plans helicopter flower showers for kanwariyas across 7 western districts

headline: Pune auto fares to be hiked to ₹30 from September 1
full_text:
Pune auto fares to be hiked to ₹30 from September 1
Pune's autorickshaw fares rise from ₹25 to ₹30 for 1.5 km, with per-km charge increasing from ₹17 to ₹20, effective September 1.
Autorickshaw fares in Pune district will rise from September 1, with the minimum fare for travel in Pune and Pimpri-Chinchwad hiked from ₹25 to ₹30 for the first 1.5 km and the per-kilometre charge from ₹17 to ₹20, officials said on Tuesday.
The latest revision by the Regional Transport Authority (RTA) marks the fourth fare hike since 2021. In less than five years, the minimum autorickshaw fare has increased by nearly 67% from ₹18 in 2021.
The decision was taken at an RTA meeting chaired by Pune district collector Jitendra Dudi on Monday. The revised rates will apply to all licensed autorickshaws operating across Pune district.
The first fare revision came in November 2021 when the minimum fare was increased to ₹20 and the per-kilometre charge from ₹12 to ₹13 following a sharp rise in CNG prices. Less than a year later, in August 2022, the RTA approved another hike, raising the minimum fare to ₹23 and the per-kilometre rate to ₹14. Within the same month, the fare structure was revised again to ₹25 for the first 1.5 km and ₹17 for every additional kilometre. The latest increase to ₹30 and ₹20 respectively is the first revision in nearly four years.
“The fare revision has been approved after considering the recommendations of the Khatua Committee and the increase in operating costs over the past few years. All autorickshaw metres must be recalibrated, and until that process is completed, drivers will have to display the official fare chart while charging passengers,” said Swapnil Bhosale, Deputy Regional Transport Officer.
Autorickshaw unions had been demanding a fare revision, arguing that rising CNG prices, higher maintenance costs, expensive spare parts, insurance premiums and overall inflation had made it difficult to operate under the existing fares. According to transport officials, CNG prices have increased from around ₹91 per kg in August 2022 to nearly ₹96 per kg at present. The revised fares have been calculated based on the recommendations of the Khatua Committee, which prescribes a formula linked to fuel prices and operating costs.
The hike is expected to benefit nearly 150,000 autorickshaw operators across Pune district. However, it will also increase the commuting cost for thousands of passengers who depend on autorickshaws for first- and last-mile connectivity.
The RTA has made recalibration of all autorickshaw meters mandatory. Operators will have six months from September 1 to complete the process. Until then, drivers must carry and prominently display the officially approved fare chart to help passengers verify the correct fare and minimise disputes.
The decision has drawn mixed reactions from commuters, many of whom said the fare hike should be accompanied by stricter enforcement against errant drivers.
“We understand that fuel and maintenance costs have gone up, but passengers also deserve better service. Many drivers still refuse short-distance trips, don’t switch on the meter or demand arbitrary fares. Before increasing fares again, the authorities should ensure these problems are addressed,” said Raunak Birajdar, a Baner resident.
Another commuter, Priya Kulkarni, who travels daily between Kothrud and Deccan, said, “Every fare hike is justified in the name of rising costs, but there is hardly any action against drivers who refuse rides or overcharge. If we are paying more, there should be accountability and strict enforcement of the rules.”

headline: Release Udhayanidhi Stalin today, orders HC; govt says he will get station bail
full_text:
Release Udhayanidhi Stalin today, orders HC; govt says he will get station bail
The court also directed the DMK leader to cooperate with the investigation and appear before the police as and when required
The Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK) government on Tuesday told the Madras High Court that it had merely detained senior Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) leader Udhayanidhi Stalin for questioning and that the latter will be released soon.
Stalin was taken into custody by the police this morning following an FIR against him over his alleged remarks on Tamil film actor Trisha Krishnan.
Tamil Nadu advocate general (AG) Vijay Narayan told a bench of Justice GK Ilanthiraiyan that the State had “no intention” of keeping Udhayanidhi in custody and that he had been detained only for questioning.
“He will be let out today itself on station bail. State only wants to protect the interest of women,” Narayan said.
Recording the government’s Justice Ilanthiraiyan directed the police to release Udhayanidhi “today itself” after his questioning.
The court also directed the DMK leader to cooperate with the investigation and appear before the police as and when required.
The court was hearing an urgent anticipatory bail petition moved by Udhayanidhi after the Thanjavur East police registered an FIR against him over remarks made during a Cauvery protest meeting in Thanjavur on Monday.
The anticipatory bail plea was mentioned for urgent hearing by senior counsel Hasan Mohammed Jinnah on Tuesday morning. Jinnah had sought protection against arrest, saying that there was an apprehension that the police could take coercive action a day before the commencement of the state assembly’s budget session.
Justice Ilanthiraiyan agreed to hear the matter once it was numbered and listed by the high court registry. Jinnah had at the time, also sought an interim direction restraining the police from arresting Udhayanidhi, and the judge had orally asked the government counsel to issue appropriate instructions to the police until the court examined the matter.
Justice Ilanthiraiyan also sought details of the case, including whether an FIR had been registered, the allegations levelled against the Leader of the Opposition and the penal provisions invoked.
However, in the meanwhile, Udhayanidhi had already been picked up from his residence by the police.
When Udhayanidhi’s anticipatory bail plea was taken up for hearing by Justice Ilanthiraiyan at 2.15pm, the advocates informed the court that Udhayanidhi had already been detained and was being taken to Thanjavur.
The AG then clarified that the State had no intention of seeking his remand and only wanted to question him.
Senior counsel NR Elango, who appeared for Udhayanidhi, argued that the court could still consider granting anticipatory bail until the petitioner was remanded to custody. Justice Ilanthiraiyan, however, observed that since the petition was one seeking pre-arrest bail, it would cease to be maintainable.
Udhayanidhi has been booked under multiple provisions of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act and section 67 of the Information Technology Act over allegations of objectionable remarks concerning actor Trisha Krishnan and chief minister C Joseph Vijay during the rally.
The DMK has denied the allegation, maintaining that his remarks related only to the Cauvery issue.

headline: Chennai: Tamil Nadu Leader of Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin was granted bail by the Madras High Court Tuesday afternoon, hours after he was arrested in connection with an allegedly derogatory remark he made, seemingly referring to actor Trisha.
full_text:
Chennai: Tamil Nadu Leader of Opposition (LoP) Udhayanidhi Stalin was granted bail by the Madras High Court Tuesday afternoon, hours after he was arrested in connection with an allegedly derogatory remark he made, seemingly referring to actor Trisha.
The high court heard Udhayanidhi Stalin’s anticipatory bail plea after the Tamil Nadu Advocate General Vijay Narayan informed the bench that the police did not intend to seek his judicial remand.
The prosecution said that Udhayanidhi is being taken to Thanjavur police station and will be released after questioning. Justice G.K. Ilanthiraiyan stated that the DMK leader must be released Tuesday itself after the inquiry.
Udhayanidhi purportedly made the double entendre remark at a rally in Thanjavur Monday, when he was speaking about the Cauvery water dispute. The comment drew sharp criticism, with leaders from the ruling TVK and the BJP calling it “disgusting, obscene, vulgar and shameful”, demanding his arrest.
Additional Commissioner of Police Narendran Nair confirmed that an FIR had been registered against the DMK legislator. The TVK also filed a complaint with the National Commission for Women (NCW) against him.
“I see the arrest action against me as a joke and I will deal with this through the legal route,” Udhayanidhi told the media, as he was taken in the police van.
#WATCH | DMK leader and LoP Udhayanidhi Stalin detained by Police from his Chennai residence, following an FIR against him over his alleged defamatory remarks against CM Vijay. Slogans directed at actor Trisha were raised at his rally yesterday. pic.twitter.com/wTM6rABo85
— ANI (@ANI) August 4, 2026
What did Udhayanidhi say?
During a protest organised to raise farmers’ concerns over the Cauvery water issue, Udhayanidhi criticised the Vijay-led TVK government, alleging that no water had been released and that the CM was silent on the matter while focusing on filing cases against the DMK.
The demonstration demanded action to stop Karnataka’s proposed Mekedatu balancing reservoir project, full waiver of farmers’ loans, and declaration of the Cauvery delta districts as drought-affected.
He highlighted the lack of water release from the Cauvery. “Water should have come. But today, not even a single drop of water has come.”
“But is the Chief Minister opening his mouth to speak about this? No, he isn’t. His only concern is, what false allegations can be made against the DMK? What fake cases can be filed?” he said.
During the speech, a section of the crowd began chanting “Trisha! Trisha!” (a reference to actor Trisha Krishnan). It was at that moment he made the alleged remark before clarifying that he was referring to Cauvery.
TVK functionaries lodged a police complaint at the Thanjavur East police station and approached the NCW seeking action, an explanation, and an apology.
Security was bolstered outside Udhayanidhi’s residence on Monday morning before his arrest. DMK workers were detained for attempting to breach cordons.
Police registered the case and took him into custody amid the escalating political confrontation between the DMK and the ruling TVK.
Earlier, a plea was submitted before the Madras High Court seeking to restrain the police from arresting Udhayanidhi. Senior advocate Hasan Mohamed Jinnah submitted that there was an attempt to arrest Udhayanidhi to prevent him from attending the assembly.
The High Court agreed to hear an urgent anticipatory bail petition to be moved by the LoP.
Justice Ilanthiraiyan listed the LoP’s anticipatory bail plea for hearing in the afternoon, after being told Thanjavur police had filed a case. The judge also orally asked government counsel to direct police not to take any coercive steps against the LoP until the bail petition is heard. However, the arrest was made around 11 am.
DMK MP T.R.Baalu rejected the allegations against Udhayanidhi, saying that he had not referred to any individual. “He has not mentioned any word about the particular woman. It is all false,” Baalu told reporters.
This is an updated version of the report.
(Edited by Tony Rai)

headline: TMC rebels divided? 3 NCPI MPs skip NDA meet amid alliance uncertainty
full_text:
TMC rebels divided? 3 NCPI MPs skip NDA meet amid alliance uncertainty
Three NCPI MPs skipped the NDA parliamentarians' meeting despite their group's outreach to the alliance. Their absence has sharpened scrutiny of the TMC rebels' numbers and political positioning in the Lok Sabha.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union ministers and leaders of NDA allies attended the ruling coalition's weekly meeting of parliamentarians on Tuesday, but the absence of three NCPI MPs drew attention amid signs of differences within the 20-member group of TMC rebels over its association with the alliance.
The development is significant as the recognition of the 20-member NCPI group in the Lok Sabha is still pending before Speaker Om Birla. The breakaway group can seek protection under the anti-defection law only if it accounts for at least two-thirds of the TMC's original strength of 28 Lok Sabha MPs.
Khalilur Rahaman, Abu Taher Khan and Yusuf Pathan, who represent West Bengal's Jangipur, Murshidabad and Baharampur Lok Sabha seats, also stayed away from the first NDA parliamentary party "Mangal Milan" meeting attended by NCPI MPs on June 28. Speaking to reporters on the Parliament premises, Khan said, "We are not with the NDA, and neither are we going to the BJP, rest assured. There was an NDA meeting today also, and the three of us did not go. But we will attend the meeting called by the chief minister (Suvendu Adhikari) because it is about developmental works in my seat. We will not support any step that is against Muslims as well." Suvendu Adhikari also visited Parliament House during the day.
Sources said the three MPs, who represent Muslim-majority constituencies, chose to skip the NDA meeting after a section of their voters questioned their perceived association with the BJP. NCPI floor leader Sudip Bandyopadhyay attended the NDA parliamentary party meeting for the first time on Tuesday after missing the June 28 meeting. "I am one of the senior-most parliamentarians in the country. All are united in NCPI. It is a good experience," he said, dismissing suggestions of a rift among the dissident MPs.
At the meeting in the Parliament House complex, BJP president Nitin Nabin was seen sitting next to Modi, a day after the party lost the Bankipur assembly bypoll in Bihar to poll strategist-turned-politician Prashant Kishor. The bypoll in Bankipur, considered a BJP bastion, was held after Nabin vacated the seat following his election to the Rajya Sabha after taking charge as BJP president.
BJP MP Manoj Tiwari said Union Minister Mansukh Mandaviya gave a detailed presentation on sports and said the Modi government adopted a sports policy in 2014 that led to India winning several medals, including gold, in international events such as the Olympics, Asian Games and Commonwealth Games. He said a detailed presentation was also made on employment-generating avenues and parliamentarians were told that job opportunities for the youth had increased steadily. "We were told at the Mangal Milan that between 2004 and 2014, when UPA was in power, only 2.89 crore youth got jobs while between 2014 and 2026, a total of 17.1 crore youth got employment," Tiwari said. He added that a presentation was also made on various social security schemes of the government. Another BJP MP, P P Chaudhary, said, "Mangal Milan mein mangal hi hota hai."
Representatives of NDA allies including JD(U), JD(S), NCP and Shiv Sena also attended the meeting, along with leaders such as Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, Home Minister Amit Shah, Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar. The meeting brought together the NDA leadership, but the absence of the three NCPI MPs again highlighted the questions around the group's position within the alliance.

headline: UP woman leaves home with torch, found hanging from tree next morning
full_text:
UP woman leaves home with torch, found hanging from tree next morning
A woman reported missing from her home was later found hanging with a local man in a Sultanpur orchard. Police suspect suicide for now, but forensic evidence and the post-mortem will shape the final conclusion.
The bodies of a 47-year-old woman and a 46-year-old man were found hanging from a mango tree in Uttar Pradesh's Sultanpur district, with police treating the deaths as a suspected case of suicide while investigating the circumstances from all angles.
The woman, identified as Lalti, had left her home late on Sunday night after dinner, carrying a torch, but did not return. When she could not be found by Monday morning, her daughter Rani filed a written missing-person report at the Gosaiganj police station.
Later on Monday, a farmer discovered Lalti and local man Sanghiram hanging from a tree in an orchard and alerted police and villagers.
MISSING WOMAN FOUND DEAD
According to police, Lalti's family searched for her through the night after she failed to return home but could not trace her.
The bodies were found the next day when a farmer from the village went to his field to check his crops and spotted the two hanging from the tree in the orchard in the Gosaiganj area.
Circle Officer Jaisinghpur Sunil Kumar Singh said police reached the spot, brought down both bodies and sent them for post-mortem examination.
LIGATURE MARKS FOUND
Singh said both Lalti and Sanghiram had ligature marks around their necks.
A blood clot was also found on the lower part of Sanghiram's leg, which police said could have resulted from a scratch or abrasion.
The police and forensic teams recovered a torch from the spot. Gutkha and some cash were also found in the pocket of one of the deceased.
PROBE UNDERWAY
Police said the circumstances surrounding the deaths were still being examined and that the post-mortem reports and other evidence would help establish what happened.
“For now, the case appears prima facie to be one of suicide,” Singh said, while adding that the investigation was being conducted from all angles.
Police are awaiting the post-mortem findings and examining the evidence collected from the orchard as they investigate the deaths of Lalti and Sanghiram.

headline: India brings back 274 fugitives in seven years, attaches Rs 17,874 crore assets
full_text:
India brings back 274 fugitives in seven years, attaches Rs 17,874 crore assets
India has brought back 274 fugitives from 36 countries over the last seven years. The government says tougher laws, sharper coordination and technology-driven tracking accelerated extraditions.
India has repatriated 274 fugitives from 36 countries over the last seven years, averaging around 40 returns a year — nearly 10 times the annual average recorded between 2004 and 2013, the government said on Tuesday.
The Home Ministry also said assets worth Rs 17,874 crore belonging to fugitives had been attached under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act during the period, as it described the extradition of fugitives as a “national priority”.
According to the ministry, the 274 fugitives brought back between 2019 and July 2026 included nine wanted in financial crimes, 17 in terror cases, 42 for organised criminal activities, 62 for murder, robbery and violent crimes, 53 for sexual crimes and sexual crimes against children, 16 for drug peddling, 12 in smuggling and fake currency cases, 18 in human trafficking and 45 for other offences.
RED CORNER NOTICES RISE
The government said Interpol Red Notices issued against fugitive criminals had risen sharply in recent years.
According to the data, 40 Red Corner Notices were issued in 2022, followed by 100 in 2023, 107 in 2024, 112 in 2025 and 182 so far in 2026.
A total of 401 Red Notices were issued over the past three years, the ministry said.
A Red Notice is a request to law enforcement agencies worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition, surrender or similar legal action.
The Home Ministry said extradition requests were now being prepared in a more professional and standardised manner.
“Under the guidance of Union Home Minister Amit Shah, extradition requests are now being prepared in a more professional and standardised manner,” it said, adding that written assurances were provided after taking into account the documentary requirements and legal expectations of the country concerned.
The ministry said India had developed an “integrated, intelligence-based, and technology-driven model” to tackle fugitives, which had helped strengthen action against them and secure their return.
GOVT CONTRASTS RECORD WITH 2004-2013
The ministry said India secured the extradition of only about four fugitives a year on average between 2004 and 2013, while 110 extradition requests remained pending.
It said that before 2014, India had extradition treaties with 37 countries and did not have a dedicated law dealing with economic fugitives or the confiscation of their assets.
“In addition, incomplete documentation and slow processing made the extradition process highly cumbersome, often leading foreign courts to deny extradition requests,” the ministry said.
It also referred to legal and judicial hurdles, including the principles of double jeopardy and dual criminality, which it said had frequently resulted in extradition requests being rejected.
The statement further blamed the absence of effective coordination and a unified strategy among the Home Ministry and other departments for delays in information-sharing, location tracking and the issuance of Red Corner Notices.
“Previous governments lacked the political will to bring back fugitives; the Modi government has made the extradition of fugitives a 'national priority',” it said.
The ministry said the government's approach, in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's vision, focused on “global outreach, strong coordination and smart diplomacy”.
MULTI-AGENCY APPROACH
The government said the effort involves coordination among the Intelligence Bureau, Central Bureau of Investigation, Research and Analysis Wing, National Investigation Agency, Enforcement Directorate, Ministry of External Affairs, Narcotics Control Bureau, Directorate General of Goods and Services Tax Intelligence and state police forces.
The constitution of a Standing Focus Group under the Intelligence Bureau's Multi Agency Centre in January 2026 was described as a “significant institutional step”.
The group is tasked with prioritising fugitive cases, standardising dossiers, closing information gaps, following up with foreign partners and providing national-level support to cases initiated by state agencies.
“Fugitives operating from abroad are not dormant case files, they represent live operational threats that require sustained, coordinated, and proactive action,” the ministry said.
LEGAL CHANGES STRENGTHEN FUGITIVE CASES
The ministry also pointed to legal changes aimed at making it harder for fugitives to evade proceedings.
The Fugitive Economic Offenders Act was enacted in 2018 to strengthen action against fugitives, while amendments to the NIA Act and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in 2019 expanded enforcement beyond banned organisations to individual terrorists, handlers, financiers and overseas networks.
India's hosting of the 90th Interpol General Assembly in 2022 also provided further impetus to efforts to bring fugitives back, the ministry said.
The CBI's BHARATPOL platform, launched in January 2025, has connected more than 1,400 agencies by bringing together the CBI, state police headquarters through Interpol Liaison Officers and district police headquarters on a single platform.
The ministry said information sought by the CBI is now generally shared by other law enforcement agencies within 10 to 20 days, and in some cases within three to 10 days, helping speed up investigations and extradition proceedings.
The Union Home Minister has also held five important meetings on the issue, it said.
NEW OPERATIONS, TECHNOLOGY TO TRACK FUGITIVES
The CBI has set up a Special Global Operations Centre to coordinate in real time with police agencies worldwide through Interpol, according to the ministry.
“To facilitate the swift exchange of information, the CBI has also designated Interpol Contact Officers in every State as well as in all Central investigating agencies, significantly enhancing coordination and international cooperation in fugitive investigations,” it said.
The ministry also referred to Operation Trishul, under which India sought to geo-locate fugitives with Interpol's support.
Agencies used satellite inputs, surveillance and digital footprint analysis to establish the locations of fugitives, it said.
The government said some fugitives had changed their names or identities while living abroad, but Indian agencies were able to identify and trace them using technology and profile mapping.
Technology has also been used to speed up extradition proceedings, including through video conferencing for court hearings, the ministry said.
The government presented the repatriation of 274 fugitives, attachment of Rs 17,874 crore in assets, rising Red Corner Notices and the expansion of legal, technological and inter-agency mechanisms as part of its broader effort to bring offenders back to India and pursue cases against those operating from abroad.

headline: NEET paper leak case: 3 accused seek polygraph, brain mapping tests
full_text:
NEET paper leak case: 3 accused seek polygraph, brain mapping tests
Three accused in the NEET paper leak case have asked the court to let them undergo lie-detector and brain mapping tests. The move puts the focus on whether such voluntary scientific tests can aid the CBI probe and stand legal scrutiny.
Three accused in the NEET paper leak case have volunteered to undergo a lie-detector test and brain mapping, prompting a designated fast-track court to seek the CBI's response on whether such a plea can be entertained.
The court asked the agency to respond by August 6, when the matter will come up for hearing again.
The proceedings also saw a change in the judge hearing the case, with Special Judge Ajay Gupta taking over after Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga was transferred to a special NIA court. The court also deferred the bail pleas of two accused and postponed the issue of taking cognisance of the CBI's chargesheet.
POLYGRAPH, BRAIN MAPPING PLEA
The three accused — Mangal Lal Biwal, Dinesh Biwal and Vikas Biwal — moved an application seeking permission to undergo a polygraph examination and a Brain Electrical Activation Profile examination, commonly known as brain mapping.
According to their plea, the request was being made “voluntarily, without any coercion” to “demonstrate their bona fides” and assist the CBI in conducting a “fair and transparent investigation”.
“The applicants seek to assist the investigating agency by voluntarily offering themselves for recognised scientific examination, so that every lawful investigative avenue capable of aiding the search for truth may be explored,” the plea said.
The accused said the examinations could be conducted at any government-approved forensic science laboratory and in accordance with the law, subject to constitutional and procedural safeguards.
COURT SEEKS CBI'S RESPONSE
Judge Gupta, who had earlier heard the paper leak case, directed the CBI to respond to all issues concerning the application, including whether it is maintainable, by August 6.
The court also deferred the bail pleas of Vikas Biwal and Dinesh Biwal to the same date.
The question of taking cognisance of the CBI's chargesheet was also adjourned to August 6 as the court continues to examine the final report.
JUDGE CHANGE IN PAPER LEAK CASE
Special Judge Anu Grover Baliga had been appointed on July 23 after the Delhi High Court notified a designated court to hear criminal cases arising from paper leaks and other unfair means in public examinations.
The move followed Prime Minister Narendra Modi's announcement on setting up fast-track courts to ensure swift action in paper leak cases.
Baliga took charge two days later, with the first hearing in the NEET paper leak case before her taking place on July 27.
On August 1, the high court transferred her to a special NIA court to hear terror cases. Special Judge Ajay Gupta was subsequently designated to hear the NEET paper leak matter.
13 ACCUSED CHARGESHEETED
The CBI has chargesheeted 13 accused in the case, all of whom are currently in judicial custody.
The case relates to the NEET-UG examination for medical admissions, which the National Testing Agency cancelled on May 12 after the May 3 examination amid allegations of a question paper leak.
A re-examination was subsequently conducted on June 21.
The court will now consider the CBI's response to the voluntary testing plea, along with the pending bail applications and the chargesheet, on August 6.

headline: Hyderabad: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s “criminal waste” remark in reference to the state’s engineering graduates has triggered a political firestorm, with opposition leaders and students accusing the government of being disrespectful.
full_text:
Hyderabad: Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy’s “criminal waste” remark in reference to the state’s engineering graduates has triggered a political firestorm, with opposition leaders and students accusing the government of being disrespectful.
The war of words between the chief minister and opposition leaders from the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) and the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) escalated after engineering students rallied around the parties, seeking an apology from the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi.
Student associations and opposition leaders K.T. Rama Rao (KTR) and G. Kishan Reddy called the remarks derogatory and disrespectful, strongly condemning the Congress for failing to provide jobs to young people in the state.
“On every occasion, the Congress has used the youth for political gains. On the one hand, he asked the students to consume ‘Endrin’. On the other hand, it promised to employ 2 lakh graduates within a year of coming to power,” BRS working president KTR said.
“The fact that the Congress government has failed to fulfill the pending youth declaration promises is the real ‘criminal waste’,” he added.
He was referring to the chief minister’s controversial remarks early in July asking police job aspirants to “consume Endrin and die” after they requested an increase in police recruitment. Endrin is a highly toxic insecticide and rodenticide.
The BRS working president wrote a four-page open letter to Rahul Gandhi holding him morally and politically responsible for anointing Revanth Reddy as the state’s chief minister.
Union Minister Kishan Reddy slammed the Congress for outstanding fee reimbursements, alleging that the state government owed around Rs 10,000 crore in fee reimbursement arrears, with more than Rs 5,000 crore due to engineering students.
BJP MP D.K. Aruna also criticised the chief minister for his choice of words, saying such language was disrespectful to parents who spent large sums of money educating their children with the hope of securing government jobs.
‘Telangana Endrin Party’
As the political controversy escalated, unemployed youth in Telangana created a symbolic “Telangana Endrin Party” on social media platform Instagram to protest Revanth Reddy’s handling of job vacancies.
At least two joint action committees (JACs) threatened to form a variant of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) in southern India, saying that the ‘Telangana Endrin Party’ could soon be a reality if the government did not keep its promise to recruit 2 lakh people in various government positions.
Tensions between the Congress party and various joint action committees in the state representing unemployed youth flared after Gaddam Venu, an unemployed young man, attempted suicide on Sunday in Telangana’s Khammam district.
Naming the chief minister and the deputy chief minister, Bhatti Vikramarka, Venu, who is currently undergoing treatment, said he took the extreme step after being unable to secure a job and provide for his disabled mother.
In a detailed letter, he said the delay in job notifications and repeated appeals to government officials that went unheard caused him significant distress.
The fact that the opposition leaders from the BRS and the BJP were not allowed to meet Venu soon after his hospitalisation further enraged tens of thousands of youth already protesting across the state.
The Telangana Police JAC (unemployed) staged dharnas at multiple locations in the state following the chief minister’s Endrin comment. This JAC comprises aspirants who are currently unemployed and awaiting recruitment exams by the state police department.
According to figures from the state Director General of Police, the department has 20,000 vacancies, of which only a little over 5,000 vacancies have been filled.
Durgam Harish, General Secretary of the District Selection Committee (DSC), told ThePrint, “The chief minister said he kept the HRD portfolio to himself to bring about large-scale reforms to the education and employment sectors.”
“With the DSC exams not being held for two years in a row, more than 10,000 jobs are waiting to be filled. How will the 100 new Telangana Residential Schools run if teachers are not appointed?” he asked.
The DSC is the nodal body for conducting recruitment exams across the state to recruit and post teachers in government-run schools.
Telangana has seven recruitment boards for government jobs. Job aspirants can apply when these boards release recruitment notifications annually, each with its own unique eligibility criteria.
Before the 2023 assembly elections, the Telangana Congress invited Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi and made a Youth Declaration.
It included 24 promises to students and unemployed youth. The key promises were filling 2 lakh government vacancies within a year, releasing an annual job calendar, a monthly unemployment allowance of Rs 4,000 for qualified jobless youth, fee reimbursements, and electric scooters for college-going women.
While the Congress says it has filled 60,000 jobs, the BRS says the government has only filled vacancies already notified when the K. Chandrashekar Rao-led government demitted office.
In May this year, the Telangana government raised the upper age limit for direct recruitment in state government jobs to 44 years, an increase of 10 years from the baseline of 34 years.
It issued an order stating that those unemployed at age 40 could be fully eligible for the general category non-uniformed direct recruitment posts overseen by agencies such as the Telangana Public Service Commission.

headline: Tharoor to attend Mumbai event where RSS chief will have ‘session with Gen Z’? He clarifies
full_text:
Tharoor to attend Mumbai event where RSS chief will have ‘session with Gen Z’? He clarifies
Tharoor clarified that the programme was not an RSS event and was instead a student-led initiative involving educationists and thought leaders.
Congress MP Shashi Tharoor will attend the later two days of an event in Mumbai where, on the first day, Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat is scheduled to interact with Gen Z students from over 100 cities on Thursday (August 6).
This Gen-Z outreach by the RSS, parent body of the ruling BJP, comes days after the student protests at Jantar Mantar forced PM Narendra Modi's government onto the backfoot and the education minister had to be changed.
Tharoor, responding to a social media post asking why he was attending an event “organised by RSS”, clarified that the programme was a student-led initiative instead. Tharoor is a board member of the India's International Movement to Unite Nations (IIMUN) that's organising the event, its press release said.
"I believe in freedom of expression and will chair their Board meeting and events on 7th & 8th. Mr Bhagwat will meet them on 6th when I am in Delhi for Parliament," Tharoor wrote on X.
Earlier, Tharoor expressed concern over the lathi charge on Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protesters and questioned the use of force against non-violent protesters. He urged the government to allow discussions on “burning issues” in Parliament.
Event organised by Bhagwat
The interaction between the youth and RSS chief Bhagwat, 75, will take place in Mumbai during an event commemorating the 15th anniversary of IIMUN, according to the press release.
Also read | Shashi Tharoor's son asks for ‘boomers’ to be banned on WhatsApp, Congress MP outwits him
Over 2,000 high school students are expected to be present during the inaugural ceremony of IIMUN's Annual Championship Conference, which will be held at the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre (NMACC). Gen Z and Gen Alpha are demographic groups, segregated according to their birth years — those born from 1997 to 2012 come under the Gen Z umbrella, those from 2013 to 2025 are considered to be Gen Alpha. Gen Z made up a major part of the recent student protests.
The gathering will include the organisation’s Advisory Board, which includes prominent personalities such as Ajay Piramal, Deepak Parekh, Nadir Godrej, Dr Shashi Tharoor, Justice DY Chandrachud, Karan Johar, former Chiefs of the Armed Forces and PT Usha, among others, as per the press release.
Aaditya Thackeray questions Gen Z interaction
Meanwhile, Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray took a jibe at recent Gen Z interactions, questioning the legal action on the student protesters. He further asked why leaders had not “stepped in” during police action and complaints against them in the aftermath.
“Suddenly everyone who wants to interact with Gen Z and Gen Alpha, and some who have taken it on themselves to preach “culture” to them via social media, the simple question to all of them is…Where were you when they were facing AK-47s, lathis with rusted nails, electric shock guns and electric barricades, tear gas and when women were manhandled in the name of “law and order?”” Thackeray asked.
Dialogue with the youth is welcome, but it would be more meaningful if young or Gen Z voices led the conversation, Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke said ahead of an interaction between Mohan Bhagwat and students in Mumbai.
Mohan Bhagwat to address participants between 15-19 years of age
According to the press release, the participants at the event are between 15 and 19 years of age. Bhagwat's address will mark the beginning of flagship Annual Championship Conference under IIMUN, one of the largest youth-led congregations. The inaugural ceremony will be centred around the theme "The Role of Youth in Uniting the World, the Indian Way."
Student participants, representing their schools and colleges, will debate and deliberate on local, national and international issues during the conference.

headline: Govtâs rooftop solar initiative has crossed the 50-lakh household milestone within 29 months
full_text:
Govtâs rooftop solar initiative has crossed the 50-lakh household milestone within 29 months
NEW DELHI: Govtâs rooftop solar initiative, PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, has crossed the 50-lakh household milestone within 29 months of its launch in Feb 2024, achieving half of its target of one crore households by March 2027.According to new and renewable energy ministry, more than five lakh households installed rooftop solar plants in July, the highest monthly addition since the scheme began. Officials said nearly one lakh new households are being added under the scheme every six days, making it one of the fastest-growing clean energy programmes in the world.âThe pace of installation has increased 3.2 times over the last nine months, rising from 5,038 installations a day in Oct 2025 to nearly 16,328 a day in July 2026,â the ministry said in a statement.When the scheme was launched in 2024, the country had fewer than eight lakh rooftop solar installations.Of the schemeâs Rs 75,021-crore outlay, govt has already disbursed Rs 28,024 crore directly to beneficiaries through direct benefit transfer. So far, nearly 19 lakh households have recorded zero electricity bills in at least one billing cycle, significantly reducing their power expenses.The ministry said more than 12 lakh households earned a combined Rs 421 crore by selling surplus electricity to the grid in FY 2024-25, translating into an additional income of around Rs 3,500 a year per household.
Cumulatively, 14.8 GW of rooftop solar capacity has been commissioned under the scheme so far.The ministry said 1.6 lakh installations have been completed for Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana beneficiaries, Below Poverty Line families, and SC/ST households across four states under the utility-led aggregation model. The model enables low-income households to install rooftop solar systems while helping states reduce their power subsidy burden.
Govt has also solarised 25,255 govt buildings with a combined rooftop solar capacity of 872 MW, against 41,542 buildings where installations totalling 1,418 MW are considered feasible. Overall, states have identified around 3.2 lakh govt buildings with an estimated rooftop solar potential of 4,400 MW. Of these, 81,329 buildings with a combined capacity of 1,450 MW have already been solarised, the ministry said.

headline: Arundhati Roy says Cockroach Janta Party protest shook PM Modi's image in 2 weeks
full_text:
Arundhati Roy says Cockroach Janta Party protest shook PM Modi's image in 2 weeks
At her book launch, Arundhati Roy said the Jantar Mantar youth protest dented Narendra Modi's image within two weeks. She called it a political jolt bigger than elections and urged wider democratic unity.
Author Arundhati Roy on Monday said the Cockroach Janta Party-led youth protest at Jantar Mantar had shaken Prime Minister Narendra Modi's public image within two weeks, calling the political impact “in a way, a bigger victory than elections”.
Speaking at the launch of the Hindi translation of her book Mother Mary Comes to Me, titled Meri Maa, Meri Gangster, Roy said the recent mobilisation had demonstrated how narratives built over decades could be challenged in a short span.
She, however, cautioned that the political challenge remained difficult if the government continued to control institutions and the levers of power. Roy also called for opposition parties and civil society to work together, while praising the young protesters at Jantar Mantar for handling their role responsibly.
“What I like the most is that no one knows what will happen to us, the country. The script is being written. And everyone has their own part. People often believed they would have to live under the same conditions for a thousand years, but in two weeks, it was shaken a little, from the roots,” Roy said at a packed event at the India International Centre.
‘COCKROACHES DESTROYED 24-YEAR IMAGE’
Roy said Modi's public image had been built over 24 years with substantial expenditure and without him addressing a press conference.
“The image of 24 years (of PM Modi)... made by spending crores of rupees, not even addressing a press conference, where some call him the incarnation of Vishnu... and in two weeks, cockroaches have destroyed that whole 24 years,” she said.
Roy then described the development as “in a way, a bigger victory than elections”.
She nevertheless warned that challenging a political narrative was not enough if institutional power remained with the government.
“If this government... keeps the institutions or levers of power, then it will be very difficult for us,” she said.
‘THEY PLAYED THEIR ROLE VERY RESPONSIBLY’
Roy urged opposition parties to take lessons from the young protesters at Jantar Mantar, saying they had shown maturity despite possible differences among themselves.
“They played their role very responsibly,” she said.
Using a musical analogy, Roy added, “The bass guitarist can't be the singer, the singer can't be the drummer, the drummer can't be the guitarist... they all have played their roles differently. Now the adults also have to show their maturity.”
ON HER MOTHER AND ‘MERI MAA, MERI GANGSTER’
During the discussion, Roy also spoke about Meri Maa, Meri Gangster, translated into Hindi by Prabhat Singh and published by Rajkamal Prakashan.
Roy said the book was “neither her autobiography nor her mother's biography”, describing it instead as the “biography of a relationship” between two women who happened to be mother and daughter.
The book centres on Roy's difficult relationship with her mother, Mary Roy, an educator and women's rights activist known for the legal battle that secured equal property rights for Kerala's Syrian Christian women in their father's property.
Explaining the book's title, Roy defended her description of her mother as a “gangster”.
“Some people, perhaps in the Hindi-speaking world, get offended because I called my mother a 'gangster'. But both the criticism and the defense miss the point. The critics say, 'How can you call your mother a gangster?' On the other hand, people defending me say, 'She was just very protective'. Both are wrong. She was a gangster,” Roy said.
She added that whenever she faces attacks, she reminds herself: “Do you know who my mother is? Do you know whose daughter I am? What can you possibly do to me”.
‘SOMEONE IS BEING BEATEN IN THE OTHER ROOM’
Roy also reflected on the burden she has felt from being regarded as a successful writer.
She referred to the chapter “Collateral” in the book and recalled a childhood incident in which she pretended to be asleep while her mother woke her brother and beat him with a wooden ruler after he brought home a report card describing him as an “average student”.
The following morning, Roy said, she was hugged after securing top grades.
“Since then, for me, all personal achievement comes with a sense of foreboding. On the occasions when I am toasted or applauded, I always feel that someone else, someone quiet, is being beaten in the other room,” she writes in the book.
Roy said the idea of “the other room” eventually became central to her writing.
“People think I am a successful writer, I am not. They felicitate me, they give me prizes, they give me the Booker... but in the other room, someone is being beaten. The whole of my writing is about that,” she said.
She expanded the metaphor to describe suffering and injustice in different parts of the world, saying “someone is being beaten” everywhere — “in Gaza, at a bus stand, in a village, at Jantar Mantar”.
Roy said her writing had sought to draw attention to people and experiences that often remain unseen.
‘WE WILL NOT BE BEATEN ANYMORE’
Ending the discussion, Roy said the responsibility now lay with citizens to resist the normalisation of injustice.
“Now we have to show that we will not be beaten anymore,” she said.
Her remarks at the book launch brought together her views on the Jantar Mantar protest, political power and democratic institutions with the personal experiences and relationship with her mother that form the core of Meri Maa, Meri Gangster.

headline: Andhra intensifies search for elusive royal bengal tiger ‘Explorer’, livestock attacks
full_text:
Andhra intensifies search for elusive royal bengal tiger ‘Explorer’, livestock attacks
The Andhra Pradesh forest department is tracking a male tiger named Explorer, which has roamed the Godavari region for six months, causing livestock attacks.
The Andhra Pradesh forest department has intensified efforts to track and safely capture an elusive male Royal Bengal tiger named “Explorer”, which has been roaming across the Godavari region for the past six months and triggered panic among villagers following repeated livestock attacks, people familiar with the matter said.
Nearly 100 forest personnel, assisted by wildlife experts, specialised tracking teams, thermal drones, trap cameras and radio-collar monitoring systems, have been deployed across the Eluru, Rajamahendravaram, Kakinada and Chintoor forest divisions surrounding the Papikonda National Park (PNP).
The tiger has been moving through dense forests, hilly terrain and agricultural plantations. Over the past week, the forest department stepped up surveillance following reports of its movement in Gopalapuram mandal of East Godavari district, particularly around Karakapadu, Nandigudem and Tokkireddigudem villages, based on fresh pugmarks.
Also Read | 11 MoUs exchanged on International Tiger Day to promote conservation, wildlife tourism in Maharashtra
On July 30, the tiger entered Mangapathi Devi Peta village in Koyyalagudem mandal of Eluru district, where it allegedly attacked and killed two cows on the outskirts. The incident prompted the forest department to strengthen surveillance and expand monitoring into nearby villages and forest fringes.
Officials said the tiger has also been moving near Jalleru in West Godavari district, where calves were reportedly killed, indicating that it continues to rely on livestock as prey while moving through agricultural landscapes.
“Initially, 60 personnel divided into five specialised teams were deployed to monitor the tiger’s movements using drones, trap cameras and field surveillance. The operation has since been expanded, with nearly 100 forest personnel, wildlife experts from Pune, Maharashtra, and thermal drone teams joining the search as the tiger continued moving across multiple forest divisions,” a senior forest official said.
Also Read | Rethinking human-wildlife conflict
Senior officials, including the chief conservator of forests (Rajamahendravaram) and the divisional forest officer, Eluru, have visited the affected areas to review the operation and coordinate field teams.
According to the forest official, Explorer was first spotted in the Papikondalu area in February. It is believed to have left its native habitat in the Tadoba-Andhari Tiger Reserve in Maharashtra in December 2025 and travelled through Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh and Telangana before entering Andhra Pradesh, covering more than 650 kilometres and eventually adapting to the Godavari landscape.

AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges.
AI is often discussed in terms of chatbots, coding assistants, and workplace productivity. But a quieter transformation is taking shape across India, where AI is increasingly being used to tackle some of the country's most persistent development challenges, from helping farmers cope with climate change to assisting teachers in rural classrooms, improving TB screening and making govt services available in multiple languages.According to MeitY, Indiaâs digital economy contributed Rs 31.6 lakh crore, or 11.7% of the GDP, in 2022-23. By 2030, that share is expected to approach one-fifth of the economy. Increasingly, govts, tech companies, startups, nonprofits and research organisations are working together to deploy AI where it can reach millions of people rather than a handful of users.

Education offers one of the clearest examples. Microsoftâs Shiksha Copilot, developed with the Shikshana Foundation using Azure OpenAI Service, is helping around 1,000 teachers prepare localised lesson plans for nearly 30,000 children across 750 govt schools in Karnataka.What once took teachers hours can now be done in about 10 minutes. The programme is expected to expand to another 8,000 teachers across Karnataka and Telangana. The company has also announced a larger commitment to train 10 million Indians in AI by 2030 after achieving its earlier target of skilling 2 million people ahead of schedule.Agriculture has emerged as another major beneficiary. Farmers increasingly face unpredictable rainfall, pest outbreaks, and rising temperatures, while agricultural extension services remain stretched.
AI-powered advisory platforms help bridge that gap.Farmer.Chat, developed by Digital Green, provides advice through voice, text, images and videos in local languages. It offers recommendations tailored to crops, soils, weather, and local conditions. The platform reportedly expanded from 15,000 to 250,000 Indian users within a year while costing less than$1 per farmer annually. Digital Green also says it has reduced the cost of introducing a new farming practice from $35 to under $1 by using AI-driven advisory systems.Non-profit institute Wadhwani AI uses similar technologies at a larger systems level. Its AI tools are now reported to have reached more than 190 million people. The organisation says its solutions have helped prioritise over 35,000 villages for tuberculosis screening, supported nearly 2.7 lakh teachers, delivered personalised learning support to 7.9 million students and resolved more than 5 million agricultural grievances.Healthcare is seeing practical applications. Startup Qure.ai has developed an AI system that analyses chest X-rays for tuberculosis. A Health Technology Assessment by the Indian Institute of Public Health Gandhinagar reportedly found the technology to be more cost-effective than conventional screening pathways. That could be significant in a country that accounts for nearly 28% of the world's new tuberculosis cases.And, language is a barrier AI is beginning to address. Platforms such as Bhashini aim to make govt services accessible in more than 22 Indian languages. AI-powered translation is already being used for grievance redressal, Aadhaar transliteration, railway enquiries and several citizen services, reducing dependence on English or Hindi and making digital governance more inclusive.
Climate resilience is becoming another area of rapid innovation. SatSure combines AI with satellite imagery to help banks assess agricultural loans, monitor climate risks, and evaluate farms. The company says its systems operate across more than 70,000 villages, reducing loan underwriting time while improving assessments for farmers who often lack formal credit histories.India is also investing heavily in the infrastructure needed to support this ecosystem. Enterprise AI adoption is estimated at 87%, while the IndiaAI Mission has expanded national computing capacity to 38,000 GPUs under an outlay exceeding Rs 10,300 crore. Nearly universal 5G coverage, digital public infrastructure such as AgriStack and a growing climate-tech startup ecosystem are providing the foundations for wider AI deployment.The common thread across these initiatives is not the sophistication of the algorithms but their ability to solve everyday problems at scale.

headline: TVK intimidating Udhayanidhi; doesn’t want him in assembly tomorrow: MK Stalin
full_text:
TVK intimidating Udhayanidhi; doesn’t want him in assembly tomorrow: MK Stalin
“If questioning was the only goal, could it not have been conducted in Chennai? Why take him to Thanjavur?” MK Stalin asked
Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) president MK Stalin on Tuesday attacked Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay accusing him of arresting those who criticise him and the government. The remark came after the Thanjavur police detained Udhayanidhi Stalin on Tuesday morning following an FIR against him over his alleged remarks on Tamil film actor Trisha Krishnan.
“Disregarding his status as the Leader of the Opposition, the TVK [Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam] government arrested him and took him to Thanjavur. By filing cases under various sections, they are trying to intimidate Udhayanidhi,” MK Stalin said.
Soon after police picked up Udhayanidhi Stalin from his Neelankarai residence, MK Stalin along with senior leaders met at Anna Arivalayam, the DMK headquarters in Chennai.
In a statement issued later, MK Stalin said that the protest by DMK in Thanjavur on Monday reflected the rage of all of Tamil Nadu displaying the TVK government’s lack of capability in upholding Tamil Nadu’s rights over the sharing of river Cauvery.
Udhayanidhi led the protest in Thanjavur and criticised the TVK government’s incompetence, MK Stalin said.
“An incompetent CM can neither bring Cauvery water nor speak up to stop the Mekedatu dam. Farmers are shedding tears in agony, but ministers are shedding tears watching the Chief Minister’s movie,” MK Stalin said.
“The assembly is set to convene tomorrow to present the financial budget. The Leader of the Opposition, who holds Cabinet rank, ought to be present in the House. Intending to prevent this, they initiated this action.” MK Stalin alleged.
Also Read:Opposition condemns Udhayanidhi’s arrest ahead of Aug 5 TN assembly session
Responding to the government counsel’s statement in the Madras High Court that there was no intention to arrest, he asked, “If questioning was the only goal, could it not have been conducted in Chennai? Why take him to Thanjavur?”
“Backtracking its stand due to public backlash, the government is now attempting a cover-up. The Madras High Court’s order instructing that ‘Udhayanidhi must be released today itself’ is a blow to TVK’s fascist nature!”, he said.
He continued that the chief minister ever since coming to power, focused solely on arresting those who criticise him, his ministers, and his government.
“The TVK government has suppressed anti-NEET demonstrations by students and youth from assembly and is taking fascism to its peak by completely knocking down Chennai’s Marina beach,” he said.
He claimed that the arrest of Udhayanidhi — who protested and spoke for the farmers—is a continuation of this trend.
MK Stalin said, “Udhayanidhi did not speak anything obscene in his speech, nor did he single anyone out... he is not someone who speaks inappropriately. Even if he were to make a mistake in his speech, he is of the nature to apologise immediately.”
He further demanded the release of the party cadres who were detained across the state for protesting.
Edappadi Palaniswami, the general secretary of All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) recalled his earlier statements and said, “With the budget session commencing tomorrow, this government’s desperation to arrest the opposition leader today raises suspicion among the public that there is a political motive behind this case.”
He criticised the TVK for acting with an intent to stall and conduct the assembly without the person holding that position, which is highly condemnable.

headline: Udhayanidhi's 10-hr detention over 'Trisha remarks': Day-long drama in Tamil Nadu
full_text:
Udhayanidhi's 10-hr detention over 'Trisha remarks': Day-long drama in Tamil Nadu
Stalin was booked under charges of insulting the modesty of a woman, obscenity and criminal intimidation tied to comments made against actor Trisha Krishnan.
Leader of the Opposition in Tamil Nadu Udhayanidhi Stalin was arrested by the police for over 10 hours, taken from Chennai to Thanjavur and booked for insulting the modesty of a woman, obscenity and criminal intimidation, among others, over an obscene remark apparently aimed at actor Trisha Krishnan a day before.
In a day packed with high drama, Udhayanidhi was arrested from his residence in Chennai at 10am and taken to Thanjavur, where he had made the controversial comment at a rally on Monday. The Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) hit the streets and approached the Madras high court, where the state government clarified that Udhayanidhi would be released “today itself”.
A political spar
In the evening, Udhayanidhi was taken to the Sengipatti police station after huge crowds gathered in Thanjavur – roughly 350km from state capital Chennai, he was quizzed for more than an hour.
At around 8pm, he was released on station bail, and returned to Chennai around midnight.
“They arrested me for nothing. I have not said anything wrong. I have not said anything wrong against anybody,” he said. The 49-year-old leader stood atop a vehicle and greeted supporters late into the evening at Sengipatti in a show of strength by the DMK.
“With 3,000 police personnel, they took us by road from Chennai to Thanjavur like a terrorist,” he said, dismissing the allegation that he made offensive comments.
“They cut, copied, and pasted my speech to claim I spoke inappropriately. Some have accused me of using double meaning. I spoke with only a single meaning: the farmers need water. I have absolutely no intention of disrespecting women,” he said.
“Everybody agrees that it was an obscene remark, and that too from a very senior leader. So, definitely the government has a responsibility to ensure that no one can escape the rule of law after committing such a despicable crime. That is why this government has taken very firm action on that,” said Tamil Nadu minister KG Arunraj.
Also Read I ‘Offensive’ remarks to detention: 6 points on Udhayanidhi Stalin's Trisha comments row
The over 10 hours between his morning arrest and evening release represent the first major political face-off in Tamil Nadu since C Joseph Vijay’s shock victory in the assembly elections this summer. The row also saw the DMK, somewhat listless after it lost allies to the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), rally behind the former deputy chief minister. The developments came a day before the budget session of the assembly.
Remarks at a rally
The controversy began on Monday when Udhayanidhi was speaking at a rally meant to press the state government on the Cauvery water sharing – a century-old irritant in relations between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu. As the crowd chanted the name of Trisha – a friend of the chief minister – Udhayanidhi made an obscene remark.
Hours later, Sengipatti police in Thanjavur east registered a case against Udhayanidhi on a complaint filed by local TVK functionary Bairavi.
He was booked under sections 196 (promoting enmity, hatred among two groups), 192 (punishes the act of wantonly or malignantly giving illegal provocation to cause a riot), 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace), 79 (punishes any word gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman), 296 (b) (Penalises singing, reciting or uttering any obscene song in public place), 61(agree to do an illegal act or by illegal methods), 351 (2) (criminal intimidation) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, section 4 of the TN Prohibition of Harassment of Woman (Amendment) Act, 2002 (which specifies the penalty for harassing women), and section 67 (punishes anyone who publishes or transmits obscene material in electronic form) of the Information Technology Act, 2000.
Around 8.30am on Tuesday, senior police officers arrived at his Neelankarai residence in Chennai.
“Did I mention anyone’s name except the CM’s? Then why do you think this is happening? Let the court decide,” he told reporters before being escorted away by the police.
Also Read I TVK intimidating Udhayanidhi; doesn’t want him in assembly tomorrow: MK Stalin
As the news spread, hundreds of DMK workers crowded the road leading to his residence. Senior DMK functionaries reached his residence and tried to prevent the police. At around 10.40am, the police convoy left Chennai for Thanjavur.
“They have arrested me. I am not worried. I am ready to face the consequences. Let us wait and see,” Udhayanidhi said.
Around 10.30am, Udhayanidhi’s legal team approached the high court with an urgent anticipatory bail petition. Justice GK Ilanthiraiyan recorded the submission of advocate general Vijay Narayan that though Udhayanidhi was detained and taken to Thanjavur, the state did not intend to remand him. The AG submitted that the state only intended to question Udhayanidhi and release him on station bail.
“Recording the above submissions made by the learned advocate general, the respondent is directed to release the petitioner, after questioning him, pursuant to the registration of the FIR..today itself. The petitioner is also directed to co-operate with the respondent in the investigation as and when required,” the high court said.
The plea was mentioned for urgent hearing by senior counsel Hasan Mohammed Jinnah on Tuesday morning. Jinnah had sought protection against arrest, saying that there was an apprehension that the police could take coercive action a day before the commencement of the budget session.
When the plea was taken up for hearing at 2.15 pm, the advocates informed the court that Udhayanidhi was already arrested and taken to Thanjavur.
Parties pick corners
DMK chief MK Stalin defended his son. “Udhayanidhi is not someone who speaks inappropriately. Even if he were to make a mistake in his speech, he is of the nature to apologise immediately,” he said.
Also Read I From Sanatana row to alleged remarks against Trisha: The many controversies of Udhayanidhi Stalin
He also criticised the Tamil Nadu government and alleged that the police force arrived at Udhayanidhi’s residence to cover up the government’s failure on the Cauvery issue. “Backtracking its stand due to public backlash, the government is now attempting a cover-up. The Madras high court’s order instructing that ‘Udhayanidhi must be released today itself’ is a blow to TVK’s fascist nature,” Stalin said.
All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK) chief Edapaddi Palaniswami criticised Udhayanidhi. “Unaware of the dignity of the position he holds, his continuous loose talk and derogatory remarks about women are strongly condemnable,” the former CM said.
Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMDK) chief Premalatha Vijayakanth said, “This act of stifling the opposition is condemnable.”
VCK chief Thol Thirumavalavan, an ally of the TVK, termed Udhayanidhi’s comment “unacceptable”. State Congress chief B Manickam Tagore said Udhayanidhi should apologise.
BJP leader Tamilisai Soundararajan attacked the DMK. “We strongly condemn the derogatory words of Udhayanidhi Stalin against womenhood, humiliating women celebrities.”

headline: ‘Never mentioned Trisha’: DMK after Udhayanidhi detained over allegedly offensive remarks

‘Never mentioned Trisha’: DMK after Udhayanidhi detained over allegedly offensive remarks
The DMK trained its guns on the ruling TVK and Tamil Nadu chief minister Vijay and said that Udhayanidhi's detention was based on “false and fabricated” claims.
Leader of Opposition (LoP) in the Tamil Nadu Assembly and DMK leader Udhayanidhi Stalin was detained by police on Tuesday morning. This came after the chief minister Vijay's ruling party TVK filed complaints with the police and the National Commission for Women (NCW) over his alleged offensive remarks directed at actress Trisha Krishnan.
Following Udhayanidhi Stalin's detention, the DMK trained its guns on the ruling TVK and chief minister Vijay.
Also Read | What did Udhayanidhi Stalin say on actor Trisha that led to his detention?
Earlier, DMK spokesperson TKS Elangovan told news agency ANI that in Udhayanidhi's speech, the Tamil Nadu LoP only "listed out the CM's failures," adding that he did not mention Trisha.
"I listened to his entire speech. Nothing was said as people are saying. He only listed out the CM's failures. Nothing was insulting in his speech. He did not even mention the name of the actress (Trisha)," he said.
"He was only attacking the govt. The problem with this govt is that they don't care about the people of Tamil Nadu. They are being used by someone to attack DMK. Their party started only to attack us," he added.
DMK MP Kanimozhi, in a post on X, alleged that detaining Udhayanidhi was to prevent him from participating in the Assembly session.
"If the government wants to personally take revenge against LoP Udhayanidhi Stalin, let it file a case. Let the court deliver its verdict. But, lacking the courage to confront the DMK as an opposition party, for the government to resort to such oppressive tactics is against the law. Arresting the Leader of Opposition in this way, solely to prevent him from participating in the Assembly session starting tomorrow, is blatant cowardice."
DMK MP P Wilson said, "This is one of the atrocious acts of the state government. Yesterday, the DMK party arranged for a statewide agitation because the ruling TVK government has given up and is not working for the rights of the farmers, for the rights of the people of Tamil Nadu... And since Udhayanidhi pointed out that the CM, the TVK leader, is always thinking about suppressing the voices of dissent... Now, the police have registered an FIR against Udhayanidhi Stalin."
“Anyone who has heard a speech will know that no such speech was made. Only to sidetrack the issue of farmers, the government itself has planted this news... There is no truth in such an allegation. It's false and fabricated news about Udhayanidhi Stalin,” the MP added.
DMK MP TR Baalu said, “It is totally wrong... he has not mentioned any word about the particular woman. It is all false. He has not made any reference about the particular woman.”
