Multi-crore fraud scam lured investors via gaming platform, kingpin arrested
The accused, Anurag Arvind Srivastava, was arrested in Nagpur in connection with multiple cyber fraud cases registered across the country, including in Uttar Pradesh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
The Uttar Pradesh Special Task Force (UP STF) has arrested the mastermind of a multi-crore investment fraud, accusing him of duping investors by promising stock market training, IPO opportunities and high returns before diverting them into a fantasy gaming platform to siphon off money.
The accused, Anurag Arvind Srivastava, was arrested in Nagpur in connection with multiple cyber fraud cases registered across the country, including in Uttar Pradesh and the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
According to the STF, Srivastava lured people by offering stock market education and investment guidance.
He then persuaded to invest in stock trading and initial public offerings (IPOs), after which they were convinced to deposit large sums of money into fraudulent schemes.
Investigators said the accused also used a fantasy gaming platform called My Ground 11 Gaming Zone to deceive investors and their acquaintances, making it another channel through which funds were allegedly collected.
During the operation, the STF recovered six cheque books and unsigned cheques with a combined value of around Rs 5.67 crore from the accused.
Police said Srivastava has an extensive criminal record, with 10 cyber fraud cases registered against him at the Cyber Crime Police Station in Lucknow.
Another case has also been registered in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, while investigators suspect his activities may have affected victims in multiple states.

headline: Netaji Subhas Chandra Boseâs grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose resigned from the TMC on Monday, citing personal reasons, months after joining the party ahead of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections.
full_text:
Netaji Subhas Chandra Boseâs grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose resigned from the TMC on Monday, citing personal reasons, months after joining the party ahead of the 2026 West Bengal Assembly elections.
NEW DELHI: Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose's grandnephew Chandra Kumar Bose on Monday resigned from the Trinamool Congress (TMC), saying he was "disillusioned" with mainstream political parties and saw "no difference" between the BJP and the Mamata Banerjee-led party.Bose, who joined the TMC barely four months ago ahead of the West Bengal assembly elections, said he would now mentor a proposed youth-led political platform based on the ideals of Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose."I have been in the Forward Bloc, BJP and TMC. I am disillusioned with the mainstream political parties. They are all the same, just two sides of the same coin," Bose told PTI.He said the proposed platform would seek to offer an alternative to what he described as the politics of polarisation and confrontation."My politics is based on Netaji's ideology. We want to build a new political platform based on his principles of inclusive nationalism, secularism, social justice and development. I will mentor the youth who are coming together to form a party based on Netajiâs ideals," he added.There was no immediate reaction from the TMC to Bose's resignation.His exit marks another political shift for the former BJP state vice-president, who has repeatedly maintained that his politics is rooted in Netaji's ideology rather than party affiliation.
Bose was earlier associated with the Forward Bloc, the party founded by Netaji. He joined the BJP in 2016 as the party expanded its political presence in West Bengal. He was subsequently appointed the party's state vice-president and contested the 2016 Assembly election and the 2019 Lok Sabha polls on a BJP ticket.His ties with the BJP later deteriorated. He was dropped as state vice-president during an organisational reshuffle in 2020 and increasingly voiced differences with the party leadership.Bose quit the BJP in 2023, claiming that the party had not lived up to its promise of advancing the inclusive nationalist ideals championed by Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose and Sarat Chandra Bose.When he joined the TMC in April this year, Bose had criticised his former party over what he described as divisive politics and said the BJP's approach was contrary to the spirit of the Constitution."When I joined the Bharatiya Janata Party, I was made to understand that I could work to promote the ideology of Sarat Chandra Bose and Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose, which is inclusive and secular. India, as per the Constitution, is a sovereign, democratic, socialist, secular republic," he had said while joining the TMC.He had also described his decision to join the BJP as a "mistake" and said he hoped the TMC would provide a platform to uphold constitutional values and inclusive politics.
Monday's resignation signals a similar disenchantment with the TMC, with Bose now seeking to build a political platform centred on Netaji's principles.Bose's political moves have attracted attention because of his family connection to Netaji and his sustained efforts to bring the freedom fighter's political philosophy into contemporary politics. Though he has not emerged as a mass electoral figure, he has consistently advocated what he describes as Netaji's vision of an inclusive India.Outside electoral politics, Bose has also campaigned for the preservation of Netaji's legacy. As spokesperson of the Open Platform for Netaji, he has led efforts seeking the declassification of files relating to the freedom fighter and greater public access to archival records concerning his life and disappearance.

headline: The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has issued a compliance order for all schools in the State to ensure the provision of safe and balanced food. The order applies to all government, aided, and private schools, including those affiliated wit...
full_text:
The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has issued a compliance order for all schools in the State to ensure the provision of safe and balanced food. The order applies to all government, aided, and private schools, including those affiliated with state, CBSE, and ICSE boards, and covers pre-primary to secondary levels, residential schools, hostels, canteens, and food suppliers. It excludes creches and day-care facilities for children up to 22 months.
The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India has specified regulations under the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006. The order, issued by the Maharashtra Food Safety Commissioner, Tukaram Mundhe, directs that all food in schools should align with the dietary guidelines of the National Institute of Nutrition. The order sets a preference for fruits, vegetables, whole grains, pulses, and dairy products. The sale and display of HFSS items, such as chips, fried snacks, and sugary beverages, are prohibited within school premises. The supply of drinking water must meet safety standards.
The order states that school management serves as the primary responsible entity for food safety. Schools must obtain the required FSSAI license or registration, adhere to Schedule 4 hygiene standards, appoint a trained Health and Wellness Ambassador or nodal officer, display warning boards at entrances, and block HFSS advertisements on computers. They must also report any unauthorized sales within a 50-metre radius of the school to the food safety officer and the local self-government body.
The School Education Department acts as the institutional guarantor for the implementation in government and aided schools. Its duties include the registration of PM POSHAN suppliers, joint training, and submission of a compliance report by March 31 every year. State boards, CBSE, ICSE, and other boards must make adherence to the School Food Regulations compulsory for school affiliation and renewal. They are also required to take action against serious violations.
Food safety officers are the primary authorities for field-level implementation. They will inspect each school at least twice a year, collect food samples at least once a year, and take action against unlicensed vendors and violations within the 50-metre zone. Assistant Commissioners (Food) or designated officers handle district-level supervision, issue improvement notices, approve prosecutions, and compile reports. Municipal corporations, municipal councils, district councils, and gram panchayats are tasked with cooperating to prevent HFSS sales within the 50-metre radius.
The order includes a Statewide campaign with the central theme of “safe food - healthy childhood - capable Maharashtra.” The order notes that the changing lifestyle, aggressive marketing, and the easy availability of HFSS items have led to health concerns. The regular consumption of such items is linked to childhood obesity, micronutrient deficiencies, anaemia, reduced concentration, and an increased risk of lifestyle diseases in later life.
Each school is expected to develop a School Nutrition Policy, provide safe drinking water, conduct at least four awareness sessions per year, and set up a healthy canteen model. Parents are expected to monitor their children’s diet and report any violations. Students are expected to make healthy food choices. In case of violations, action includes improvement notices, seizure, suspension or cancellation of licenses, prosecution, and stringent action based on the severity of the offence, all in line with the procedures of the Food Safety and Standards Rules, 2011.
The Food Safety cCommissioner stated that the order is not limited to legal enforcement and that children have a right to safe and balanced food. He said that ensuring the safety of every child’s food is a moral responsibility of society. He stated that the initiative aims to make every school a safe food school and every student a healthy child.
Under the statewide initiative, 4,919 teachers from 3,567 schools have been trained and sensitised on food safety and balanced diet through 42 awareness workshops. The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration has called upon all schools, education boards, local self-government bodies, parents, and food business operators to participate actively in this initiative.

headline: The High Court of Karnataka has said two children, both majors, will have to recover from their father the ₹25 lakh compensation, awarded by a tribunal for their mother’s death in a road accident, as the father’s negligence in driving the motorcycle ...
full_text:
The High Court of Karnataka has said two children, both majors, will have to recover from their father the ₹25 lakh compensation, awarded by a tribunal for their mother’s death in a road accident, as the father’s negligence in driving the motorcycle had caused her death.
Justice Shivashankar Amarannavar passed the order while rejecting the appeals filed by the children seeking directions to the insurance company to pay the compensation to them as was awarded by the tribunal and recover the amount from their father, who owned the two-wheeler which was insured.
The tribunal, which had awarded compensation of ₹25 lakh with 6% interest to the children, had exonerated the insurance company from the liability while holding that the vehicle owner — the father of the claimant-children — must pay the compensation.
Upholding the tribunal’s order, the court noted that the accident occurred owing to the rash and negligent driving by the father. The chargesheet confirmed that he was not holding a valid driving licence at the time of the accident, with offences registered under Sections 279 and 304(A) of the Indian Penal Code.
The court ruled that the “pay and recover” principle cannot be applied in the presence case as the claimants’ own family member is the offender, as he had breached the term of the policy by driving the insured motorcycle without a valid driving licence.
Under the “pay and recover” principle, the insurance company must first pay the compensation amount to an innocent third-party accident victim. Then, the insurance company has the legal right to recover that same money from the vehicle owner or driver who had breached the conditions of the insurance policy.
Since the owner of the vehicle is the father of the claimants, the order of “pay and recovery” could not be applied and hence the tribunal has rightly exonerated the insurer from payment of compensation and asking the claimants to recover the compensation from the owner of the vehicle.

Census phase 2 to begin Aug 17, will capture caste, parentsâ birth details

The Census is also likely to collect passport numbers (where available) and Aadhaar numbers voluntarily.
NEW DELHI: The population enumeration phase of Census 2027 â which will capture caste for the first time since 1931, and most likely also record the date and birthplace of parents, along with the respondentâs passport number (where available) and Aadhaar number (voluntary) â will start in Ladakh and the snow-bound areas, J&K, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand on August 17.A home ministry notification on Monday said the population enumeration exercise in snow-bound areas of the four northern states/UTs will run from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of August 17-30. This means that the questionnaire for Phase 2 of Census will also be notified soon.According to sources, caste will be recorded âas declared by the respondentâ. There will be a drop-down menu for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, while the âcasteâ field will only cater to those in non-SC, non-ST category. The drop-down menu will only show the SC/ST list of the state where the respondent is being enumeratedThe spelling of the declared âcasteâ will be recorded as cited by the respondent. No document or caste certificate is required to be shown to verify oneâs SC, ST or âcasteâ status. An officer said while the self-declaration template followed for the socio-economic caste census (SECC) in 2011 had thrown up over 45,000 castes, making the data unusable, modern digital tools and AI can now surmount compilation and segregation challenges.Census Phase 2, in a first, , will collect the date and place of birth of parents, the key factors that determine citizenship/nationality.
The national population register (NPR) exercise â conducted alongside Census 2011, intended to be repeated with Census 2021 before it was postponed, but now delinked from Census 2027 â had in 2010 collected details of nationality as declared by the respondent, with the rider that it would not confer any right of citizenship.Sources said the respondents will not be asked for proof of birth details of parents and these would be recorded âto the best knowledge of the respondentâ. In fact, where the respondents do not know the exact date of birth of parents but only the year, a default date like January 1 of that year will be accepted.The Phase 2 questionnaire will also log passport details where available. Aadhaar number will be collected on a voluntary basis.âThe purpose of collecting the birth data of parents is to know the total number of people who meet citizenship criteria based on their declaration, even though unverified. It will have no impact on the individual as the Census Act does not allow individual data to be used for âlegal evidence, govt benefits or public disclosure,â said an officer.Self-enumeration option for Phase 2, unlike Phase 1, may allow users to submit partially-filed enumeration forms, provided a minimum number of questions are answered. âThere is a realisation that even if some data fields are self-enumerated, the task of the enumerator becomes easier and less time-consuming,â said an officer.
As per convention, the population enumeration exercise â which records individual data like marital status, religion, SC/ST status, occupation, migration and fertility, besides arriving at the countryâs headcount â is conducted nationwide in February of the census reference year. However, it is advanced in pockets that face extreme cold and inclement weather during this window.

Having covered the Union home ministry, security agencies, Election Commission and the âprimeâ political beat, the Congress, for The Economic Times all these years, she moved to TOI in August 2012. Her repertoire of news stories delves into the whole gamut of issues related to terrorism and internal strife, besides probing strategic affairs in Indiaâs neighbourhood.

headline: ‘Dragged, stabbed within 40 seconds’: Inside Faridabad teacher's brutal murder at school
full_text:
‘Dragged, stabbed within 40 seconds’: Inside Faridabad teacher's brutal murder at school
Police identified the victim as Sandhya Karhana, a resident of Firozpur Kalan, who taught Class 2 at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona.
A 30-year-old teacher was stabbed to death inside a private school in Faridabad on Monday after an alleged stalker dragged her out of a classroom and attacked her in full view of students and staff, police said.
CCTV footage showed the assailant stabbing the woman at least 25 times before fleeing. The accused, 21-year-old Amit, was arrested from Kot village in Faridabad about two hours later, still wearing blood-stained clothes, officers said.
Also Read | Miscreants stab, mow down AAP sarpanch in Hoshiarpur village
What the investigators said
Police identified the victim as Sandhya Karhana, a resident of Firozpur Kalan, who taught Class 2 at Saraswati Senior Secondary School in Sikrona. She is survived by her husband and two children.
Investigators said Karhana reached school around 7:30 am and was teaching a class when the accused, his face covered with a white cloth, entered the campus through the main gate around 9:35 am.
According to police, the security guard was not at the entrance at the time, allowing the stalker to enter unchecked.
An investigator, requesting anonymity, said the accused first approached two students and a staff member, asking them to call Karhana outside on the pretext that her husband had come to meet her. Witnesses told police the man knew her husband’s name.
Police said around 300 to 350 students from Classes 1 to 12 were on campus when the attack took place, with many witnessing it from classroom windows.
A senior police officer said the accused stabbed Karhana at least 25 times in the neck, chest and abdomen in an attack lasting barely 30 to 40 seconds. “The entire incident was captured on CCTV,” the officer said.
School director reacts to the attack
School director Tejpal Sharma, who witnessed the attack, said he rushed out of his office after hearing screams. “I initially thought someone had been electrocuted because of the rain. When I came out, I saw the man repeatedly stabbing Sandhya,” he said.
Sharma said he tried to intervene but the assailant turned on him. “He attempted to stab me as well. I ran inside to get a stick while raising an alarm. By the time I returned, he had escaped,” he said.
Karhana was rushed to Al-Falah Medical College and Hospital, where doctors declared her dead on arrival, Sharma said.
Also Read | 2 Delhi men stab teenager 4 times, throw him in drain; he survives: Police
Case registered
A case under Section 103(1) (murder) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita was registered at Sector 58 police station.
Faridabad police spokesperson Yashpal Yadav said crime branch teams arrested the suspect by 11:30 am.
“He had not even changed the blood-stained clothes he was wearing during the murder. His actions, including stretching himself moments before the attack, indicate that the crime was premeditated,” Yadav said.
Police identified the accused as Amit, who had allegedly known Karhana from when she worked at a private school in his native Kot village two years ago. According to the investigator cited above, he began stalking her after that, prompting her to sever contact and recently warn him that she would approach the police if he continued harassing her.
“The victim’s husband has also alleged that the accused had been stalking and harassing her for several months,” Yadav said.

Police said the accused will be produced before a court on Tuesday to seek custodial remand for further interrogation. Karhana’s body was handed over to her family after the postmortem examination.

headline: FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits.
full_text:
FSSAI has prohibited adding rum or whisky flavour to spirits.
NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has said alcoholic beverage manufacturers cannot add "rum flavour" to rum or "whisky flavour" to whisky and market them as standard products, saying the practice misrepresents the true nature of the beverage and misleads consumers.The regulator said the issue is not the use of permitted flavouring substances, but addition of the flavour of the standardised alcoholic beverage itself, which serves no legitimate purpose. It said the characteristic taste and aroma of products such as rum and whisky should develop naturally through the base ingredients, fermentation, distillation and maturation. However, inspections found that some manufacturers were producing beverages largely from neutral alcohol, which has no characteristic flavour, and then adding identical flavouring substances to recreate the taste and aroma of rum or whisky. Such products, FSSAI said, should be labelled as "rum-flavoured spirit" or "whisky-flavoured spirit", with the front of the pack clearly disclosing their true nature. Laboratory testing of rum and whisky samples from multiple manufacturers found the addition of artificial or nature-identical flavours that masked the products' natural characteristics, rendering them sub-standard under existing regulations, FSSAI said.
Based on findings, it prohibited the sale of products manufactured by units of Mohan Rocky Springwater, United Spirits, INBREW Beverages and Associated Alcohol & Breweries. It also inspected Mandexi Distilleries & Breweries in Goa and issued notices to six producers in Maharashtra.FSSAI also objected to the "7 years old blended" claim on an Old Monk XXX Rum variant, saying the product predominantly contained neutral, unmatured spirit, while matured rum spirit accounted for less than 5% of the blend. It said the issue is not representative of the entire industry, noting that many manufacturers continue to produce beverages in compliance with the prescribed standards.

headline: NEW DELHI: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, crossing the 20,000-mark for the first time and registered a 6.5% increase over the previous year, according to National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisationâs (NOTTO) annual r...

NEW DELHI: India performed a record 20,138 organ transplants in 2025, crossing the 20,000-mark for the first time and registered a 6.5% increase over the previous year, according to National Organ and Tissue Transplant Organisationâs (NOTTO) annual report. The figure marks a fourfold rise from 4,990 transplants in 2013.Delhi-NCR recorded the highest number of transplants in 2025 with 4,564 procedures, followed by Tamil Nadu (2,796), Maharashtra (2,136), Telangana (1,523) and Kerala (1,489). Tamil Nadu topped the country in deceased organ donors with 266, followed by Maharashtra (205), Telangana (198), Karnataka (154) and Kerala (152).India has emerged as the worldâs third-largest country in total organ transplants, after the US and China. Despite the gains, deceased organ donation remains Indiaâs biggest challenge. Deceased donor transplants rose from 837 in 2013 to 3,526 in 2025, but continue to fall far short of demand. âA substantial gap still exists between demand for organs and their availability. Addressing this gap remains a national priority,â MoS for health Anupriya Patel said.
To strengthen the programme, govt launched âJug Jug Jiyo Abhiyaanâ, a year-long awareness campaign, besides rolling out e-Pratyaropan, a digital platform for donor registration, waitlist management and organ allocation, NOTTO mobile app, and new Brain Stem Death Certification and Swap Transplantation guidelines.Govt has also expanded transplant services, with 10 new AIIMS now performing kidney transplants, while AIIMS Bhopal has started heart transplantation and AIIMS Jodhpur, Bhubaneswar, Patna, Rishikesh have launched liver transplant programmes.The report highlights reforms under âOne Nation, One Policyâ initiative, including removal of domicile requirements, the upper age limit and registration fees for patients seeking deceased donor organs. full_text: Chikkamagaluru: The hopes of Chikkamagaluru district securing representation in the Cabinet were dashed once again after Congress leader Gayathri Shanthegowda’s name was dropped from the final list of ministers, despite earlier indications that she would be sworn in..The district Congress unit was optimistic that Gayathri Shanthegowda would take an oath as a minister even before being sworn in as a member of the legislative council (MLC). The excitement was short-lived with the dropping of her name from the second list..Gayathri had contested the 2021 Legislative Council election from the Local Authorities constituency but lost by just six votes. Challenging the inclusion of nominated members in the voting process, she approached both the Karnataka High Court and the Supreme Court.After nearly four-and-a-half years, the High Court set aside the election of M K Pranesh, paving the way for Gayathri’s election to the Legislative Council. Her election was officially announced only three days ago, though she is yet to take the oath as an MLC..Serial number 17.On Monday morning, a list of 20 ministers circulated by the All India Congress Committee included Gayathri Shanthegowda’s name at serial number 17. The document, carrying the signature of AICC General Secretary K C Venugopal, was widely shared, prompting Gayathri to express her happiness before the media. However, within hours, the list was revised, and her name was removed..Reacting to the development, Gayathri said, “The high command has only postponed its decision for now. I am confident that I will be given a ministerial berth in the future.”.Unrealised hope.During previous Congress governments, Chikkamagaluru had witnessed ministers from other districts. With all five Assembly constituencies in the district currently represented by Congress MLAs, party workers had hoped the district would finally secure a Cabinet berth in this expansion. The High Court’s verdict in Gayathri’s favour, delivered just days before the Cabinet expansion, had further strengthened the expectations. Seen as a close associate of former chief minister Siddaramaiah, Gayathri Shanthegowda was widely considered a strong contender..Two-time MLAs T D Rajegowda and G H Srinivas were also among those aspiring for ministerial positions. headline: SC said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women
full_text:
SC said that cruelty does not distinguish between married and unmarried women
NEW DELHI: Saying that "live-in relationships" are a reality particularly in urban areas and the law must adapt itself to serve those who choose this form of relationship and protect them from harassing partners, the Supreme Court Monday brought them under the ambit of Section 498A of the IPC or Section 85 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) where a husband or in-law shall be punished with imprisonment for a term up to three years for subjecting a woman to cruelty.A bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and N K Singh rejected the plea that 498A is confined only to a husband married to a woman in the traditional sense. "Since the provision was aimed at solving a societal issue, it is this larger objective of securing equality for women, stepping away from the superiority of males that is an inheritance from bygone days, that has to inform the understanding in interpretation and implementation of the Section," SC said.It, however, clarified that only those "live-in relationships" which are in the nature of marriage will come within the ambit of Section 498A of IPC or Sec 85 of BNS. "Cruelty does not check at the door whether the house it's entering is that of a married woman or not. Once it enters, its propensity to destroy is aggravated," it said.SC, however, took note of the growing instances of alleged misuse of Section 498A. Describing as worrisome the trend of the section being misused and employed as a means of settling scores and ventilating grievances, SC said its verdict would be applicable to only those 'relationships in the nature of marriage' and the initial burden of proof would be on the female live-in partner seeking protection of the law.
"When the objective of the Section 498A was to provide coverage to those cases where harassment by husband or in-laws through wilful conduct causing mental or physical injury or driving the woman to suicide, then to say that such harassment can only be caused when they are married and not before that, in our considered view, would be a case of over simplification. Whether or not the woman in question is married or not, in the present day, does not have a proximate link to the objective of the section, which is to prevent cruelty in such a household setting," Justice Karol, who penned the verdict, said.The court said the law must respond to changing times, and bringing live-in relations within the ambit of Section 498A is needed. "Marriage was considered to be sacrosanct, which undoubtedly is a changing phenomenon. Living together, prior to marriage, is not unheard of or unacceptable anymore. In the same way, that same-sex relations, once criminalised and deemed to be a mental illness, have now been decriminalised and recognised as naturally occurring.
This is the evolution of societal standards," SC said."Not a single person goes into a relationship knowing or anticipating that cruelty may be meted out to them. When a couple sets out on their journey, it is always, one presumes, with the best of intentions and to bring joyfulness of all forms. With the passage of time, however, some relationships may go down this troublesome path. The law must provide for the same. This distinction between "married" and "live-in relationship in the nature of marriage", in as much as it relates to the protection envisaged by Section 498A, has no rational nexus with the object of preventing domestic violence and is as such offensive to Article 14 of the Constitution," the bench said.

headline: As the State continues to face the threat of flooding amid intense monsoon rains, the social media accounts of District Collectors are being inundated with demands to declare holidays for educational institutions. The public comments, a mix of genuin...
full_text:
As the State continues to face the threat of flooding amid intense monsoon rains, the social media accounts of District Collectors are being inundated with demands to declare holidays for educational institutions. The public comments, a mix of genuine requests, sarcasm and criticism, appear to exert considerable pressure on the decision-making officers, prompting some of them to call out this online behaviour.
District Collectors across the State have faced intense criticism on social media in the past few days, either for not declaring holidays in view of heavy rain or for allegedly delaying the announcements.
“Better late than never,” one user commented after Ernakulam District Collector G. Priyanka announced on Sunday night (August 2) a holiday for educational institutions in the Kothamangalam and Muvattupuzha taluks for Monday (August 3). However, many users in the comments section criticised the decision and demanded a holiday across the district. “Seriously, madam? Do you know the situation in Aluva?” another user asked. By 11.30 p.m., the Collector had declared a holiday for the entire district, drawing another round of criticism over the delay. Similar comments, some harsh in tone, were also seen on the social media accounts of other District Collectors.
Amid the debate, Kozhikode District Collector Madhavikutty M.S. shared a detailed note on social media explaining the challenges involved in deciding whether schools should be closed.
She pointed out that although a school holiday is almost certain when the India Meteorological Department (IMD) issues a red alert, there are no fixed rules for orange or yellow alerts. Such decisions, she explained, are based not only on weather forecasts but also on local assessments of waterlogging, landslide threats, river water levels and road conditions, as well as reports from tahsildars, village officers, Revenue Divisional Officers and local bodies.
Warning against decisions driven by public pressure, Ms. Madhavikutty said opinions expressed on social media were often formed without access to the detailed field reports and Automatic Weather Station (AWS) data available to the administration. “Such public pressure should not influence the decision-making process,” she wrote, clarifying that she was expressing her personal views.
The Collector also highlighted the consequences of unnecessary holidays, noting that students lose valuable academic time while many parents, particularly daily-wage earners, suffer a loss of income. She further pointed out that a significant number of drowning incidents involving children during the monsoon occur on days when schools remain closed, as children may venture near rivers, ponds and flooded areas without adequate supervision.
Another District Collector, on condition of anonymity, said Ms. Madhavikutty’s remarks echoed the sentiments of several Collectors. “The unnecessary online backlash is quite stressful. It also gets abusive sometimes,” the officer said, admitting that Collectors often feel pressured to declare holidays even when their reasoning suggest otherwise.

headline: 'Impermissible' to judge women by clothes: SC panel urges overhaul of language adopted in sexual offence cases
full_text:
'Impermissible' to judge women by clothes: SC panel urges overhaul of language adopted in sexual offence cases
Apart from reforming judicial language, the committee recommended a series of courtroom practices aimed at making the justice system more sensitive.
It is “unpardonable and impermissible in any civilised society” to judge a woman by the clothes she wears or draw conclusions about her virtue, modesty or character, an expert committee constituted pursuant to Supreme Court directions has said, recommending a sweeping overhaul of the language and approach adopted by judges in sexual offence cases to eliminate stereotypes and prevent the secondary victimisation of survivors.
The committee, headed by former Supreme Court judge Justice Aniruddha Bose, has called for the creation of a new “language ecosystem” in the judiciary that replaces patriarchal, moralistic and stigmatising expressions with neutral, survivor-centric terminology.
Also Read | SC may issue sensitivity norms for courts in sexual assault cases
Report after analysing 125 trial court judgments
Its report, “Judgments and Gender: Sensitivity and Compassion in Writing Judgments,” was prepared after analysing 125 trial court judgments from across the country with assistance from State Judicial Academies.
The report is the outcome of the February 10 directions by a bench headed by CJI Surya Kant in a suo motu case to revisit judicial practices in sexual offence cases after controversial observations made by the Allahabad High Court. The committee comprised former Gujarat High Court chief justice Sonia Gokani, former Madhya Pradesh director general of police Anuradha Shankar, Supreme Court advocate Surat Singh and anthropologist Lucy TV Zehol.
The panel said that judicial language is not merely a matter of style but “shapes justice” by influencing how survivors experience the legal process and how society understands sexual violence.
Also Read | Legally Speaking | A look at the Supreme Court's judgment on the right to privacy of adolescents
‘Prosecutrix’, ‘helpless woman’ and other expressions
It urged courts to stop using expressions such as “prosecutrix”, “helpless woman”, “poor helpless minor girl”, “lost her chastity”, “victim of another person’s lust”, “outraged her modesty”, “destroyed her life”, “spoiled her childhood”, “woman in a non-permissive society”, and references to a woman’s “honour”, “shame”, “sanctity” or “bashfulness”.
Instead, it recommended the use of terms such as “victim”, “survivor”, “complainant”, “sexual assault”, “sexual violence”, “violation of bodily autonomy” and “bodily autonomy”, observing that these expressions recognise dignity and constitutional rights instead of reinforcing patriarchal notions.
The committee also advised judges against using words such as “whore”, “fallen woman”, “mistress”, “concubine”, “kept”, “call girl” or “prostitute”, recommending “partner” and “sex worker” wherever appropriate, except where statutory terminology requires otherwise.
Making a strong case against victim blaming, the report underlined that survivors routinely face intrusive questions throughout the criminal justice process about why they were outside at a particular time, why they wore certain clothes, why they delayed reporting the offence or why they were not accompanied by male relatives.
“It is unpardonable and impermissible in any civilized society to judge a woman solely based on her clothing or to draw conclusions about her virtue or modesty,” said the committee, stressing that such assumptions have no place in judicial decision-making. Judicial findings, it said, must be founded on evidence and not on stereotypes or preconceived notions about how a victim of sexual violence is expected to behave.
The report lays down nine broad principles to guide judicial writing in sexual offence cases. These include ensuring that findings are evidence-based; exercising caution while using statutory expressions such as “outraging modesty”; adopting trauma-informed language; using gender-neutral and survivor-centric terminology; referring to victims under the POCSO Act as “children” or “minors”; replacing “prosecutrix” with “victim” or “survivor”; avoiding sensational or moralistic descriptions; focussing on autonomy, consent and child rights; and recognising the enduring psychological and physical trauma suffered by survivors. It reiterates that absence of injuries, delayed reporting or lack of physical resistance cannot be equated with consent.
Apart from reforming judicial language, the committee recommended a series of courtroom practices aimed at making the justice system more sensitive to survivors. It said judges should ensure that victims receive legal aid from the FIR stage, facilitate access to victim compensation schemes, conduct in-camera proceedings wherever required by law, proactively prevent humiliating or irrelevant cross-examination, particularly on a survivor’s sexual history, and ensure strict confidentiality of victims’ identities.
The report also encouraged greater use of video links and screens for vulnerable witnesses, observance of witness protection measures even without formal applications, and a trauma-informed approach to courtroom management. Witnesses, it said, should be treated as “guests” of the court rather than being made to spend long hours waiting to testify, a practice that weakens both the justice delivery system and public confidence in courts.
Calling sensitivity “an ongoing process”, the committee underlined that judicial training should continuously address unconscious bias and gender stereotypes. Quoting the Supreme Court’s observations in SP Gupta Vs Union of India (1981), it said the true independence of a judge lies in overcoming personal prejudices through education, training and humility.

headline: No reason, only disappointment: Ex-Minister after Karnataka cabinet snub
full_text:
No reason, only disappointment: Ex-Minister after Karnataka cabinet snub
The Cabinet reshuffle sparked discontent within the Karnataka Congress, with former state minister Dinesh Gundu Rao questioning his exclusion and seeking an explanation. The expansion also saw last-minute changes, Gayathri Shanthegowda's induction deferred despite approval, protests by disappointed aspirants, and one ministerial berth left vacant.
Former Karnataka minister and senior Congress leader Dinesh Gundu Rao on Monday voiced disappointment after being left out of the first expansion of Chief Minister DK Shivakumar's Cabinet, saying he had not been told why he was excluded despite his long years of service to the party and the state. In a statement issued after the expansion, the six-time MLA said he had stayed committed to the Congress and to the people of Karnataka throughout his political career.
His reaction came as the much-awaited Cabinet expansion was marked by confusion over the final list of inductees, the last-minute postponement of MLC Gayathri Shanthegowda's swearing-in and unhappiness among Congress leaders who did not get ministerial berths.
Gundu Rao, who served as a minister in the previous Siddaramaiah government, was among several senior Congress leaders left out of the expanded Cabinet.
Nineteen legislators took oath as ministers at Lok Bhavan even though the Congress high command had approved 20 names, with Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot administering the oath of office and secrecy.
Taking to X, Gundu Rao said his repeated electoral victories showed the trust that people had placed in him and added that he remained grateful for the chance to have served both as a legislator and as a minister.
He also pointed to his long association with the Congress organisation, saying he had worked in the Youth Congress, the District Congress, the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee and the All India Congress Committee, while remaining loyal to the party and its ideology.
"It is disappointing that after so many years of service to the State and the party, I have not been considered to serve the government in this Cabinet. I am disappointed by decisions taken without being given any reason for my exclusion," he wrote on X.
Despite being left out, Gundu Rao said he would continue to work for the welfare of the people and the development of Karnataka.
Talking to ANI, Dinesh Gundu Rao said he was still searching for an answer as to why he had been dropped from the Cabinet without being given any reason, despite remaining loyal to the party.
"The only thing is that they should have told me the reason. I don't know why I have been dropped. Was I a poor performer as a minister? Do I have any corruption charges? Was I not working well for the party?" he asked.
Gundu Rao also said he was hurt by the lack of communication before he was dropped from the ministry.
"Even in the previous government, when Siddaramaiah was Chief Minister, I voluntarily told him for three years that he should make somebody else a minister because I wanted to work for the party. Becoming a minister is not the end for me. But the disappointment is that they have not given me a proper reason for dropping me. I hope that, at least in the future, they will tell me why I was dropped. A proper reason should be given. That is the only thing I expect," he told ANI.
Several senior leaders from the previous Siddaramaiah government were also kept out of the new Cabinet on Monday, including HC Mahadevappa, HK Patil, K Venkatesh, MC Sudhakar and Laxmi Hebbalkar.
Those inducted into the Cabinet were PM Narendraswamy, Shivaraj Tangadagi, Rudrappa Lamani, KS Basavanthappa, B Nagendra, T Raghumurthy, BZ Zameer Ahmed Khan, Rizwan Arshad, Santosh Lad, Madhu Bangarappa, Putturangashetty, SS Mallikarjun, Ajay Singh, N Chaluvaraya Swamy, KM Shivalinge Gowda, HC Balakrishna, Basvaraj Rayareddi, Vijayanand Kashappanavar and Laxman Savadi.
Earlier on Monday, Congress general secretary KC Venugopal had conveyed the Congress high command's approval of 20 names. However, Gayathri Shanthegowda, whose name was on the approved list, was not sworn in, leaving the Cabinet without a woman minister. No official reason was given, though party circles linked the delay to differences among state leaders over her induction. An earlier list was also revised, with Bhatkal MLA Mankala Vaidya replaced by former minister SS Mallikarjun without any official explanation.
The developments triggered resentment among several ruling party legislators, and supporters of some ministerial aspirants staged protests in different parts of the state.
Indi MLA Yashavantarayagouda V Patil also submitted his resignation from his legislative post after failing to get a place in the ministry. Shivakumar, who was sworn in as Chief Minister on June 3 along with 13 ministers, appealed to disappointed aspirants to remain patient, saying patience had brought him to his present position.
After Monday's expansion, one berth remains vacant in the 34-member Karnataka ministry. The Congress high command also approved GS Patil as Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly, A S Ponnanna as Deputy Speaker, Saleem Ahmed as Chairman of the Legislative Council and Umashree as Deputy Chairperson.

headline: Justice Liberhan, who led Babri demolition probe panel, dies at 87
full_text:
Justice Liberhan, who led Babri demolition probe panel, dies at 87
It took nearly 17 years and 43 extensions for the Liberhan Commission to deliver the report on June 30, 2009.
Justice Manmohan Singh Liberhan, a former chief justice of the Andhra Pradesh and Madras high courts who headed the panel probing the demolition of the Babri Masjid in 1992, died in Chandigarh on Sunday. He was 87.
Born on November 11, 1938, near Chandigarh, justice Liberhan began practising at the Punjab and Haryana high court in 1964 before getting elevated to the bench.
He was cremated on Monday in Chandigarh in the presence of friends, family and colleagues.
“My first appearance in the Punjab and Haryana high court was before him, in August 1992,” said Anu Chatrath, senior additional advocate general for Punjab.
Also read: Airlines report 352 major flight defects till June, Akasa and Air India top list
“He was a highly motivating judge and made others feel at ease. I remember, whenever the atmosphere would become tense in court, he would crack a witty one-liner,” Chatrath added.
Justice Liberhan was elected to the Punjab and Haryana bar council in August, 1970 and served as its member until February 11, 1987. He was appointed chief justice of the Madras high court on July 7, 1997 and chief justice of the Andhra Pradesh high court on February 28, 1998.
But his most-high-profile role came when he was named the head of a one-man inquiry commission into the Babri Masjid demolition on December 16, 1992 – 10 days after the structure was controversially razed by a mob.
Also read: Couple killed in Delhi after roof of house collapses, narrow escape for son
It took nearly 17 years and 43 extensions for the Liberhan Commission to deliver the report on June 30, 2009, making it among independent India’s longest-running judicial inquiries.
In his report, justice Liberhan stated that destruction was premeditated, systematic, and a planned conspiracy executed by multiple individuals, including political figures and others part of right-wing organisations.
“... it stands established beyond doubt that the events of the day were neither spontaneous nor unplanned nor an unforeseen overflowing of the people’s emotion, nor the result of a foreign conspiracy as some overly imaginative people have tried to suggest,” the 1,029-page report said.
Also read: Paper leaks, caste factors: What led to BJP loss in Bankipur and Datia?
To be sure, everyone accused in the conspiracy to demolish the mosque was later acquitted.
“While the structure or the methods of the Sangh Parivar for aggregating a substantial public base may neither be illegal nor strictly objectionable, the use of this gargantuan whole for the purpose of the Ayodhya campaign was clearly against the letter and spirit of Indian law and ethos,” the report said.

headline: Marine researchers claimed to have solved a 150-year-old taxonomic confusion regarding the identity of the thorny seahorse, Hippocampus histrix.
full_text:
Marine researchers claimed to have solved a 150-year-old taxonomic confusion regarding the identity of the thorny seahorse, Hippocampus histrix.
Scientific studies have identified a new species, Hippocampus amandavincentae, which was previously misidentified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.
Earlier, researchers had described Hippocampus jayakari, a lesser-known one, which was also previously wrongly identified as Hippocampus histrix, they said.
The new species, which was named after noted marine biologist Amanda Vincent, was collected from the fish bycatch at the Tuticorin fisheries harbour by Shalu Kannan, the lead author of the paper.
The species was described in a recently released research paper, according to the team of researchers from Kerala University of Fisheries and Ocean Studies (Kufos).
This is also the fifth known seahorse species from the Kerala coast, they said.
The study published in the taxonomy journal Zootaxa demonstrated that the thorny seahorse (Hippocampus histrix), historically believed to be widespread from the Red Sea and East Africa across the Indian Ocean to the western Pacific, was three distinct species, they claimed.
“Many museum specimens and online biodiversity records of spiny seahorses in the Indian Ocean have been assigned to Hippocampus histrix for decades,“ said Rajeev Raghavan, Assistant Professor at Kufos and a senior author of the study.
The new species was photographed alive during a survey held as part of the Ecomarine project at around 15-metre depth on the rocky reefs off Anchuthengu, said Kufos Vice-Chancellor A. Biju Kumar.

The government aims to increase nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047, with an intermediate target of 22 GW by 2031-32. This expansion will involve multiple stakeholders and the introduction of new legislation.
NEW DELHI: In a milestone for Indiaâs clean energy production, Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) has cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of nuclear electricity.NPCIL said Tuesday, âSince commencement of commercial operation, NPCILâs nuclear power plants have cumulatively generated over 1,000 billion units of clean electricity, thereby avoiding over 860 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent emissions into the environment.ââThis milestone reflects NPCILâs steadfast commitment to deliver safe, reliable and sustainable nuclear power, strengthening Indiaâs energy security while supporting the nationâs clean energy transition and climate goals,â it said on XTo give the scale of how much carbon emission is avoided, a typical passenger vehicle emits about 4.6 metric tonnes of CO2 per year. Avoiding 860 million tonnes is equal to taking roughly 187 million gasoline-powered cars going off the road for an entire year. At least 860 million tonnes is roughly equivalent to the total annual greenhouse gas emissions of a major industrial country like Germany or Japan for a full year.Govt has drawn up a roadmap for reaching the 100 GW nuclear power capacity in the next two decades by 2047, as announced in the Nuclear Energy Mission in the Budget 2025-26, thereby increasing the share of reliable, low-carbon base-load nuclear energy in the countryâs energy mix and reaching the goal of net zero carbon emissions by 2070.
The present nuclear power capacity of 8.78 GW is expected to reach about 22 GW by 2031-32 on progressive completion of projects presently at various stages of implementation. Another 32 GW of nuclear power capacity is envisaged to be set up beyond 2032 by NPCIL under the administrative control of the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE).
This will comprise indigenous pressurised heavy water reactors (PHWRs) and light water reactors (LWRs) planned to be set up by 2047, taking NPCILâs nuclear power capacity to 54 GW.The balance of 46 GW comprising reactors of different technologies, is expected to be set up by other public sector enterprises, private sector and joint ventures in different business models. With the govt enacting the SHANTI Act (Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India Act, 2025) last year, the new law provides the legal framework that makes this 46 GW expansion possible.

headline: Haryana’s dominance at the recently concluded Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow has sparked a fresh demand from sportspersons and political leaders across party lines to make the State a co-host of the 2030 CWG scheduled to be held in Ahmedabad.
full_text:
Haryana’s dominance at the recently concluded Commonwealth Games (CWG) in Glasgow has sparked a fresh demand from sportspersons and political leaders across party lines to make the State a co-host of the 2030 CWG scheduled to be held in Ahmedabad.
Sportspersons from the agrarian State bagged seven of India’s 13 gold medals and 11 medals overall. Five of the seven golds in boxing came from Bhiwani alone, four of them won by women.
The performance has fuelled calls that the “Mini Cuba” of India, a tribute to the Caribbean island nation that has produced many famed boxers, deserves more than praise.
Bhiwani Boxing Club founder Jagdish Singh, who has trained several world-class boxers, said the demand is legitimate.
‘Strong claim’
“Haryana certainly has a strong claim; after all, we win the highest number of medals. The government renamed the existing stadium in Gujarat after Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and the facilities there are excellent. In terms of infrastructure, that venue is indeed deserving, but Haryana has a stronger claim in terms of performance on the ground,” he said.
Olympic bronze medallist boxer Vijender Singh, a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader, said while the final call rests with the government, “it would be good if they were held in Haryana”.
Will speak to PM: BJP MP
Bharatiya Janata Party’s (BJP) Bhiwani-Mahendragarh MP Dharambir Singh said, “It is valid to say that boxing events — or at least some CWG events — should be held in Bhiwani. It is a hub for boxing in India.”
Mr. Singh said he would seek an appointment with Prime Minister Narendra Modi and raise the issue.
BJP leader and Olympic bronze medallist boxer Vijender Singh said while the final call rests with the government, “it would be good if the games are held in Haryana”. Former BJP Rajya Sabha member Kiran Choudhry said “If that happens, it would not only benefit budding sportspersons in Bhiwani but also those in neighbouring Hisar and Rohtak,” Ms. Choudhry said, adding she would take up the matter with the Prime Minister and Chief Minister Nayab Singh Saini.
On Monday (Auust 3, 2026), Congress’s Haryana MPs — Deepender Hooda, Jai Prakash, Varun Mulana, Satpal Brahmachari, and Karmbir Baudh — staged a protest at the Parliament complex demanding that Haryana be made the host or a co-host for the 2030 games.
‘Centre shut the door’
Mr. Hooda alleged the Centre had already shut the door by announcing the Games would be held exclusively in Ahmedabad and that the 2036 Olympics bid was also being submitted only for Gujarat. He asked why Haryana, which wins 50% of the country’s medals at the CWG, Asian Games and Olympics with just 2% of India’s population, continues to face neglect. “Investments worth lakhs of crores of rupees for the games will now flow into Ahmedabad, where sports infrastructure will be developed. Had Haryana been made a co-host, this massive expenditure would have taken place in Haryana as well,” he said.
The Congress leader attacked the State government for not submitting a proposal to host the games and demanded that it immediately send a bid and that the Central government consider it seriously.

headline: The flood doesn't end with the rain: What I witnessed in Kerala's worst-hit areas
full_text:
The flood doesn't end with the rain: What I witnessed in Kerala's worst-hit areas
The rain may have eased by the time we left Kerala's flood-hit Pathanamthitta, but for thousands of families, the ordeal was far from over. Homes had been inundated, businesses destroyed, roads swallowed by floodwaters and entire neighbourhoods emptied as residents sought refuge in relief camps.
"Chechi?" I called out to a woman standing outside her house along the road leading to the famed Aranmula Temple. We had reached the area to report on the severe waterlogging that had submerged the temple approach road and large parts of the premises, bringing movement to a standstill. I was desperately thirsty. Every shop nearby was shut because of the flooding.
"Yes?" she replied, stepping outside. I asked if I could have a glass of water. She smiled, said "of course" and invited me inside. I hesitated because I was drenched from hours of reporting in the rain, but she insisted.
Her house stood on slightly higher ground, with a sloping entrance. Looking at it, I assumed it had escaped the flooding. "The water wouldn't have entered this house, right?" I asked while drinking the water. "It did. Yesterday." Her answer caught me completely off guard. She pointed to the sofa where I was sitting. "In 2018, the water had reached this level."
For her family, this was the first time since Kerala's devastating floods of 2018 that floodwater had entered their home. Then she pointed towards the house opposite. "That belongs to our relatives. They've shifted to a relief camp. The water there rose to the level of the dining table."
As I stepped out, I turned around for one last look at the living room where I had just been sitting. I tried to picture muddy floodwater filling the space, swallowing the furniture and everything around it.
That's the strange thing about covering floods. You can stand waist-deep in water all day and still fail to comprehend what it means for those who live there. The real devastation begins inside people's homes.
From Aranmula, we headed to Ranni, one of the worst-hit towns after overnight torrential rain. I had seen drone footage before arriving, but nothing prepared me for the scene on the ground.
Police had barricaded the road leading into the flooded locality. Beyond the barricades, I waded through water that rose above my waist to report from the heart of the inundated neighbourhood.
A little further ahead, I saw a family taking shelter on the upper floor of their house. The ground floor had disappeared beneath murky floodwater.
"We don't want to leave everything behind and move to a relief camp," an elderly woman called out from upstairs. "Once the rain stops for a while, the water will go down."
It is a dilemma we encounter repeatedly while covering floods. Many residents hesitate to leave because they fear returning to find their homes looted or further damaged. Others simply cannot imagine abandoning everything they own.
For families living in Kerala's flood-prone low-lying areas, relief camps have become an unfortunate annual reality rather than an emergency measure.
Then came one of the most frightening moments I have experienced while reporting.
As I made my way back through the flooded street, I suddenly spotted a live snake cutting swiftly through the current just a few feet away. For a split second, I froze. Then instinct took over. I hurried through the water as fast as I could while keeping an eye on the snake. Thankfully, it slithered onto the gate of a nearby house before disappearing inside the compound.
Despite years of covering floods, this was the first time I had come face-to-face with a snake in floodwater. The fear is always there whenever you step into submerged streets. That day, it became real.
The neighbourhood itself was unnervingly silent. Every house was locked. Every family had left. With floodwater stretching across deserted lanes, the area felt abandoned.
A short distance away, I found a man hurriedly carrying goods to the first floor of a commercial building. He ran a business on the ground floor. "The stock downstairs is soaked. Most of it is damaged," he said without pausing. "We didn't get any warning or proper directions. Had we known earlier, we could have shifted everything to a safer place."
Like many others, he wasn't just counting financial losses. He was trying to salvage whatever little remained before the water claimed that too.
About two kilometres away, a relief camp had been set up at MS Higher Secondary School. Inside, families who had fled their homes just hours earlier were trying to settle into temporary lives. "We are 10 families, around 25 people, staying here," said Mini, who had arrived from a nearby apartment complex.
"We got a call from our panchayat member saying the water level was rising and asking us to leave immediately. We informed all our neighbours and rushed here. We came wearing only the clothes we had on. There wasn't even time to collect our belongings."
For Mini, displacement has become painfully familiar. "This happens almost every year," she said.
Then came the sentence that stayed with me long after we left. "I just hope there is a permanent solution. Going back, cleaning and making life normal again is a task."
That, perhaps, is the part of a flood most people never see.
Television cameras capture swollen rivers, submerged roads and dramatic rescues. But when the rain stops, another battle begins – scrubbing layers of mud from homes, salvaging damaged possessions, reopening shuttered shops and trying to rebuild routines that the water washes away every monsoon.
By the time we drove out of Ranni, the downpour had finally eased, and the floodwaters had begun to recede in parts. For us, the assignment was ending. For the people of Pathanamthitta, it was only the beginning. Their next few days would not be about surviving the flood, but about reclaiming their homes, their livelihoods and, somehow, a sense of normalcy.

headline: As many as 152 recruits of the 10th batch of the commando wing passed out after completing training at the India Reserve Battalion (IRB) at Pandikkad in Malappuram on Tuesday (August 4).
full_text:
As many as 152 recruits of the 10th batch of the commando wing passed out after completing training at the India Reserve Battalion (IRB) at Pandikkad in Malappuram on Tuesday (August 4).
State Police Chief (SPC) Ravada A. Chandrasekhar reviewed the passing-out parade and urged the newly inducted commandos to uphold the Constitution, discipline, and professionalism in the line of duty.
Addressing the recruits, he said physical fitness and combat skills alone do not define a commando. “Unwavering loyalty to the Constitution, moral courage, and composure during crises are the hallmarks of a true commando,” he said.
The SPC said the Kerala Police commandos are called upon when the State faces extraordinary situations. They should be ready to tackle terror threats, protect vital installations, and serve as the first responders during natural disasters and other emergencies, he said.
“You are the shield that protects our peace and democratic system. Uphold the pride and discipline of the Kerala Police. Perform your duties with precision, confidence, and responsibility,” he told them.
The passing-out parade was followed by mock operational exercises by the newly trained commandos. They demonstrated anti-terror operations inside a hospital, the rescue of passengers from a hijacked bus, joint operations against militants hiding in a forest, VIP protection drills, and close combat techniques. The commandos also showcased their proficiency in handling modern firearms used by the Kerala Police.
The regular wing (Scorpion) commandos underwent an 18-month training programme, comprising nine months of basic training followed by nine months of advanced training at institutions including the Border Security Force in Manipur. The recruits were trained in handling a wide variety of guns.
Among those present were M. Rahmathullah, MLA; Usha Vijayan, MLA; Armed Police Battalion Commandant K.E. Baiju; India Reserve Battalion Commandant P. Wahid; Additional Director General of Police (Armed Police Battalion) Balram Kumar Upadhyay; and District Police Chief Chaithra Teresa John.

headline: A sense of insecurity and lack of support system faced by the elderly population emerged as a predominant concern during a sitting held by the Kerala State Elderly Commission (KSEC) at the district collectorate here on Tuesday.
full_text:
A sense of insecurity and lack of support system faced by the elderly population emerged as a predominant concern during a sitting held by the Kerala State Elderly Commission (KSEC) at the district collectorate here on Tuesday.
The complaints lodged by senior citizens with the Commission pertained to a variety of issues including alleged neglect of elderly parents by adult children, financial cheating, and trouble from neighbours, officials said.
The Commission received seven complaints during the sitting, five from individuals and two from organisations involved in issues of the elder community.
“A common complaint we receive is about the alleged neglect of parents by children after getting their properties transferred to the latter’s name. Today also there were a couple of such complaints. There were also complaints about troubles from neighbours, including an allegation that improper maintenance of pets in neighbourhood was causing health issues to the complainant,” KSEC Chairperson K. Somaprasad said.
He added that the complainants approached the Commission alleging inaction by the authorities they had approached earlier. One of the complaints was from a retired government employee who had accused a non-banking financial company based in Aluva of cheating him of ₹85 lakh by promising higher returns on investment. The complainant knocked on the Commission’s door alleging that the local police were not keen to investigate the complaint.
A similar complaint alleged that a lender was not returning a 1.25-acre property mortgaged by an elderly person despite repaying the private loan.
Mr. Somaprasad said the Commission would seek report from the departments or agencies concerned on the complaints and summon the parties involved for hearing accordingly. Though two complaints received earlier were scheduled to be heard on Tuesday, neither of the opposing parties in one case turned up. Only the complainant appeared before the panel in the second case.
The Commission is scheduled to conduct similar hearing in other districts in the coming days. It has received around 300 complaints from across the State in the past nine months and nearly 50 of them have been disposed of.

headline: Amid PM Modi video row, Meta’s global executives to meet MeitY officials today
full_text:
Amid PM Modi video row, Meta’s global executives to meet MeitY officials today
MeitY summoned the tech giant after a Facebook reel by the PM addressing nationwide protests over the NEET paper leak was removed from the platform.
Senior global executives from Meta, the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, will meet officials from the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY) on August 5 and 6 following the temporary takedown of a video posted by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, a government official said on Tuesday.
MeitY summoned the tech giant after a Facebook reel by the Prime Minister addressing nationwide protests over the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET-UG) paper leak was removed from the platform for about five hours on July 28.
Speaking on the sidelines of an event in New Delhi, MeitY secretary S Krishnan said the discussions will cover non-compliance with Indian laws, Child Sexual Abuse Material (CSAM), synthetically generated content, and safeguards for verified accounts, alongside the video removal.
Also Read | 'Stop them immediately': Centre orders Meta to remove Instagram ads promoting child sex abuse content
“There will be a range of issues…We know that the CSAM issue was raised…what measures have been taken regarding that? Synthetically generated information…to what extent that is being looked at? For prominent personalities, they have verified accounts. When content gets taken down, there have to be safeguards. We would like to understand from them as to why some of these things have not been working the way they are supposed to work and what are their challenges. After all, these are some of the world’s leading technology companies and they should have technology to make this work,” Krishnan said.
The August 5-6 meeting was convened after the ministry expressed disappointment with Meta’s India policy team, which it felt was not adequately conveying government concerns to the company’s US leadership, Hindustan Times reported earlier.
The secretary did not disclose the names of the executive delegation visiting India. Meta’s global public policy and global affairs leadership is headed by Joel Kaplan, chief global affairs officer, and Kevin Martin, vice-president and head of global policy. An emailed query sent to Meta seeking comment did not receive a response.
The upcoming meeting follows demands from Nishikant Dubey, chairperson of the parliamentary standing committee on Information Technology and Communications, for an apology from Meta chief executive officer and co-founder Mark Zuckerberg over the video removal.
Dubey stated that failure to issue an apology could result in Meta losing its safe harbour protection under Section 79 of the Information Technology Act. Section 79 grants online intermediaries immunity from liability for third-party content hosted on their platforms, contingent upon compliance with due diligence requirements and lawful government directions.
However, legal protection under safe harbour is statutory and cannot be revoked unilaterally by the government. An intermediary’s entitlement to immunity remains a legal matter for determination by courts based on compliance with conditions specified under Section 79.
During the parliamentary committee meeting, a Meta executive apologised for the removal of the Prime Minister’s video, attributing the incident to an algorithmic error, according to people present at the meeting who spoke to Hindustan Times. The executive assured the panel that Meta would amend its algorithm to prevent recurrence.
A separate query sent to Meta regarding the committee chairperson’s demand for Zuckerberg’s apology also went unanswered.

headline: NEW DELHI: If a food label says "100% pure", "100% natural" or "100% purity guaranteed", consumers may still need to read it with caution. In one of its strongest actions against misleading food labels, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (F...
full_text:
NEW DELHI: If a food label says "100% pure", "100% natural" or "100% purity guaranteed", consumers may still need to read it with caution. In one of its strongest actions against misleading food labels, Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has ordered Dabur India to stop selling a range of products carrying such claims, saying they violated food labelling regulations and could mislead buyers.The order covers products that include organic honey, apple cider vinegar, virgin coconut oil, sesame oil, cow ghee, coconut water and coconut milk, marketed with claims such as "100% juice", "100% purity" and "100% original".According to FSSAI, the company had made unauthorised organic claims, creating an impression of regulatory endorsement.The regulator also found that some claims on the labels were not permitted under Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.FSSAI has directed the company to immediately stop the sale of the identified products, recall products already in the market within 15 days and submit a compliance report.In a statement, Dabur said it believes the declarations on its product labels comply with the prevailing legal and regulatory framework and are consistent with long-standing industry practices. It said it stands by the purity and quality of its products and has never made misleading claims.
Dabur said that it had begun removing the "100%" claims from product labels, advertisements and its website, in keeping with FSSAI's observations, adding that many products have already been updated while others are in the process of transition.It said that it is responding to the regulator, and will continue to engage constructively to resolve the matter.
Anuja Jaiswal is a Senior Assistant Editor at The Times of India, with an impressive 18-year career in narrative journalism. She specializes in health and heritage reporting, expertly simplifying complex health information to make it engaging and understandable for readers. Her deep dives into heritage topics are well-researched, resulting in captivating narratives that resonate with her audience. Over the years, she has worked in Chandigarh, Chhattisgarh and West UP, gaining diverse on-ground experience that shapes her storytelling.

headline: India's youth is among the best, Sonam Wangchuk says in a video message
full_text:
India's youth is among the best, Sonam Wangchuk says in a video message
Sonam Wangchuk thanked supporters after ending his hunger strike and returning to his village. He said the protest renewed his faith in India's youth, democracy and the people.
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk has shared an emotional message of gratitude nearly two weeks after ending his indefinite hunger strike, thanking supporters for standing by him and saying they had restored his faith in India's youth, democracy and the nation.
In a 4-minute, 34-second video posted on X, Wangchuk said it had been 12 days since he ended his fast and five days since he returned to his remote village.
"It's five days since I'm back in my remote village and 12 days since I broke my fast. I've regained six of the 11 kilos I lost. Thank you all for restoring my faith and hope in the youth, in the nation, and in democracy again," he wrote alongside the video.
Wangchuk said he had lost around 11 kg during the hunger strike but had already regained 6 kg and expected to return to his normal routine within a few weeks.
JANTAR MANTRA MEMORIES STAY WITH ME
Although he has returned home, Wangchuk said the memories of the protest at Delhi's Jantar Mantar remain fresh.
"Whenever I close my eyes, the scenes from Jantar Mantar come back to me," he said. He praised Generation Z, saying the protest had disproved the perception that young people are lazy or self-centred.
"I have always believed that if young people are given respect and responsibility, there is no one better than them. What I witnessed at Jantar Mantar proved me right," he said.
According to Wangchuk, students and volunteers consistently put others before themselves, supported one another through difficult moments and showed extraordinary commitment during the protest.
INDIA'S YOUTH'S AMONG THE WORLD'S BEST
Drawing on his travels around the world, Wangchuk said India's young people were among the best he had encountered.
"I have travelled to many countries and met people from around the world. I can say with confidence that India's youth is among the best in the world," he said.
He added, however, that the country's real challenge lay with the older generation, particularly political leaders, saying he would speak about that at another time.
THANKS VOLUNTEERS, DOCTORS AND SUPPORTERS
Wangchuk thanked CJP volunteers, core committee members, doctors who monitored his health, student unions, donors, gurdwaras that provided accommodation and food, political parties, farmer organisations, media outlets, content creators, police personnel and government officials who supported or facilitated the protest.
He reserved special thanks for the people of India.
"You have shown that in a democracy, it is ultimately the people who hold the power," he said.
Reflecting on his role in public movements, Wangchuk said he saw himself as someone who gives a stalled vehicle an initial push before it starts moving on its own.
"I was with you until your vehicle started moving. Now I will probably help another movement," he said.
He ended his message on a hopeful note.
"We will meet again somewhere along the way. Wherever I am, I will never be far from you. Stay connected. Thank you once again. Jai Hind."
Earlier during the CJP protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi, Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day indefinite hunger strike after weeks of negotiations with the Centre, breaking the fast in the presence of Union Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh. Wangchuk had launched the strike in support of students protesting irregularities in competitive examinations and demanding accountability for paper leaks.
During the fast, he was shifted to a hospital after doctors advised close monitoring of his health. The Centre assured him that the issue of accountability for paper leaks across India would be discussed by all political parties in Parliament.

headline: Three persons were killed in separate road accidents near Katpadi in Vellore on Tuesday.
full_text:
Three persons were killed in separate road accidents near Katpadi in Vellore on Tuesday.
