headline: New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology...
full_text:
New government schemes will offer significant financial support to Indian private space companies. These initiatives aim to boost domestic launch capabilities and global competitiveness for businesses. Subsidies will cover launch services, technology transfer, and access to ISRO facilities. The programs are designed to lower entry barriers and accelerate private sector growth. This support will make satellite data and infrastructure more affordable for Indian entities.
BENGALURU: Indian private space companies and non-government entities will receive govt support ranging from 30% to 100% on everything from launch services and technology transfer to satellite data and access to Isro facilities under two new schemes of the Department of Space (DoS).The incentives â Launch Services Price-support Scheme (LSPS) and the Price Support Scheme â being implemented by Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) are aimed at lowering entry barriers, making Indian space businesses globally competitive and accelerating private participation across the sector.The larger of the two initiatives is the Launch Services Price-support Scheme, with a budget of Rs 800 crore over five years until June 2031. The scheme seeks to boost domestic commercial launch operations and strengthen India's position as a global launch hub.IN-SPACe chairman Pawan Goenka told TOI: âThe idea is to make the launches competitive. Therefore, we are trying to defray the cost of launch, thereby making the launch cost globally competitive. The ultimate beneficiary will be the satellite launch.âUnder Category A, eligible entities can receive up to 50% support for using Isro and DoS launch facilities.
The benefit extends to NGEs, government entities and launch vehicle providers.Category B offers a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower, for Indian small launch vehicles carrying satellites, experiments or payloads weighing up to 500 kg. The support is available to satellite owners and operators.The subsidy would apply to launches by Indian private entities from Indian soil too. âIt will be applicable to [Skyrootâs] Vikram also. Any satellite launch by an Indian company... from Indian soil... we will directly pay the satellite guys $3,000 per kg,â Goenka said. He added that the policy is focused on promoting small launch vehicles where private sector participation is growing.Category C provides the highest level of support, offering 100% funding for repurposed upper-stage platforms carrying payloads of up to 120 kg. The funding is capped at $13,000 per kg and limited to four missions. The category is aimed at NGEs, govt entities and launch vehicle providers.Category D extends launch incentives to satellites weighing up to 100 kg launched aboard PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 missions. Beneficiaries will receive a 30% subsidy on contractual launch costs, or up to $3,000 per kg, whichever is lower.Complementing the launch incentives is a separate Price Support Scheme for Indian entities, which will run for three years until Feb 2029. The programme is intended to reduce the cost of accessing Indiaâs space infrastructure, technologies and data.The scheme has three components. The first provides up to 50% support for the utilisation of DoS and In-SPACe facilities, along with technical expertise.
The second offers a 30% subsidy on Technology Transfer Fees (TTF) for technologies licensed from Isro, lowering the cost for companies seeking to commercialise govt-developed technologies.The third provides a 50% subsidy on standard Earth Observation data and data products, making satellite imagery and geospatial datasets more affordable for Indian companies developing applications in agriculture, urban planning, disaster management, climate services and other downstream sectors.
Chethan Kumar is a Senior Assistant Editor with the Times of India. Aside from specialising in Space & Science, he has reported extensively on varied topics, with special focus on defence, policy and data stories. He has covered multiple elections, too. As a young democracy grows out of adolescence, Chethan feels, there are reels of tales emerging which need to be captured. headline: Heatwaves, lightning now a natural calamity in NDRF protocol, says Centre
full_text:
Heatwaves, lightning now a natural calamity in NDRF protocol, says Centre
The latest inclusion will ensure states can use the SDRF fund for providing relief and assistance to people affected by heatwaves and lightning.
Heatwave and lightning have been included in the list of notified natural calamities under the operational guidelines for the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF) and National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), the Union home ministry informed the Lok Sabha on Tuesday, adding that at least 20 heat stroke deaths have been reported in the country between March 1 and July 26 this year.
“The 16th Finance Commission, in its recommendations for the award period 2026-31, recommended inclusion of heatwaves and lightning in the list of notified natural calamities, considering the increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events arising from climate change,” minister of state for home Nityanand Rai told the Lower House in response to a set of questions from fellow BJP MP Anoop Pradhan Valmiki.
Also read: Madhya Pradesh air ambulances served 159 people since 2024, 32 had BJP links
Based on these recommendations, the ministry of home affairs has “included heatwaves and lightning in the list of notified natural calamities” under the operational guidelines for administration of the SDRF and NDRF for the award period 2026-31, Rai said.
4,853 heat stroke cases between March and July 2026
The minister added that a policy framework for providing relief assistance through SDRF/ NDRF is now in place.
Rai also informed that there were 4,853 heat stroke cases between March 1 and July 26, 2026, while the confirmed heatstroke deaths were 20 in the country during the period.
Most heat stroke cases were reported from Telangana (915 cases), followed by West Bengal (733) and Chhattisgarh (660).
Also read: Complaint against Noida teen who ‘abused’ PM Modi at NEET protest dropped
The current list of notified disasters has 12 entries: cyclone, drought, earthquake, fire, flood, tsunami, hailstorm, landslides, avalanches, cloudburst, pest attack, and frost and cold waves.
The latest inclusion will ensure states can use the SDRF fund for providing relief and assistance to people affected by heatwaves and lightning.
Welcoming the move, Anjal Prakash, a climate expert and an IPCC (Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change) author, called it a significant policy shift.
“It’s an important step, given India’s rising exposure and fragmented response to it. By including these as notified calamities, states can now take central support for relief, which was previously hard to justify under the disaster finance tools,” he said.
“The 16th finance commission has also cited an increasing frequency and intensity of extreme weather events due to climate change. This brings India’s fiscal architecture closer to observed and projected risk, especially for urban and Agrarian population. Cities can also move away from ad-hoc solutions, to proper measures now,” Prakash further said.

The Gujarat health department has organised 6,868 medical camps, deployed more than 18,000 surveillance teams and administered preventive medicines to over 7.61 lakh people in flood-affected districts as part of an extensive drive to avert disease outbreaks following last week’s heavy rains, officials said on Tuesday (August 4, 2026).
According to officials, over 1.74 lakh people were examined and treated at the medical camps, while surveillance teams conducted daily door-to-door visits, distributing more than 1.05 crore chlorine tablets and 10.29 lakh ORS packets in affected areas.
The State government said a comprehensive Monsoon Action Plan had been implemented across all 34 districts and eight municipal corporations before and during the rainy season, helping prevent any major public health emergency despite widespread flooding.
Health authorities also conducted regular health check-ups in relief camps and shifted 675 pregnant women from vulnerable areas to healthcare facilities in advance, where 272 deliveries were carried out safely.
Round-the-clock health control rooms were established in all districts and municipal corporations, with each district receiving five additional emergency medical teams along with dedicated vehicles and staff. As many as 1,496 ambulances under the 108 Emergency Service and 816 ambulances attached to primary and community health centres have also been kept on standby.
The department said all government healthcare institutions have been stocked with more than 1.5 crore chlorine tablets, over 60 lakh ORS packets and 1,38,234 anti-snake venom injections.
Following the receding of floodwaters, preventive medicines against leptospirosis were administered to more than 7.61 lakh high-risk residents in 562 villages across Surat, Tapi, Valsad and Navsari districts. Additionally, 497 extra vector control teams were deployed in south and central Gujarat to undertake anti-larval measures and create public awareness against vector-borne diseases.
Torrential rain lashed several parts of south and central Gujarat on August 1, prompting authorities to evacuate around 27,000 people and rescue 53 others, particularly in Surat and Navsari districts, where flood-like conditions cut off several villages.

headline: The doctor certified her 90% disabled, but a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability
full_text:
The doctor certified her 90% disabled, but a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability
NEW DELHI: Holding that functional disability faced by a road accident victim should be the deciding factor for granting compensation and not doctor-certified medical disability, SC has granted compensation of Rs 83.3 lakh to a minor who met with an accident when she was just six months old and is now suffering from severe spinal cord and neurological injuries.Though the doctor certified her 90% disabled, a bench held that she was suffering from 100% functional disability and quantified the compensation on that basis."...In the given facts of a case, a lesser physical disability may result in a much higher functional disability and in an appropriate case, even amount to complete loss of earning capacity," the bench said, adding it would be reasonable to assume that functional incapacity resulting out of a particular bodily injury may be higher and greater than what may be medically perceived."The present case concerns a child who has suffered permanent disability at a tender age and whose future stands altered on account of the injuries sustained in the accident. In such circumstances, the court is required to adopt an approach which is realistic, humane and consistent with the settled principles governing award of compensation under the MV Act," the bench said while increasing the amount of compensation to over Rs 83 lakh.
"Cases involving child victims suffering permanent or near total disability constitute a distinct and special category within the law relating to motor accident compensation. A child, by reason of age, vulnerability and complete dependence upon others, stands on an altogether different footing from an adult claimant. The consequences of a catastrophic injury suffered during childhood are not confined merely to the immediate physical impairment caused by the accident.
Such injuries alter the entire course of the child's existence and affect every subsequent stage of her life. The law, therefore, cannot evaluate claims involving injured children through the same lens that may ordinarily be applied in cases involving adults," it said.

Meanwhile, Yemen’s internationally recognised government also condemned what it called a “Houthi terrorist attack”, saying the Indian-flagged ship was targeted by “an explosives-laden boat” off the country's western coast.

A total of 10 Indian seafarers are among the 16 Indians who have died so far in the West Asia conflict, the MEA informed Parliament. It also said that another 5 Indian seafarers were killed in recent attacks on merchant ships in the Black Sea involving Russia and Ukraine.

“The Ministry reaffirms the solidarity of the Republic of Yemen with the friendly Republic of India and its continued coordination with the relevant Indian authorities, while extending all necessary support and facilitation to the vessel’s crew members,” it added.

headline: Karnataka Council chair row: Basavaraj Horatti says Shivakumar asked him to resign
full_text:
Karnataka Council chair row: Basavaraj Horatti says Shivakumar asked him to resign
Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti said Chief Minister D K Shivakumar asked him to resign. He said only the House can decide the post, sharpening a fresh constitutional row.
Karnataka Legislative Council Chairman Basavaraj Horatti on Tuesday said Chief Minister D K Shivakumar had called him and asked him to resign from the post. Horatti said he would discuss the matter with BJP and JD(S) leaders before taking a decision.
He also said the chairman of the Legislative Council and the Speaker of the Assembly can be chosen only by the House, and not by the high command of a political party. His remarks came after the Congress high command approved Saleem Ahmed as its nominee for chairman of the state Legislative Council and Umashree for deputy chairperson.
The approvals were conveyed in a letter sent to Shivakumar on Monday, along with the list of ministers who were sworn in the same day. The party also cleared the names of G S Patil as its nominee for the post of Speaker of the Karnataka Legislative Assembly and A S Ponnanna for deputy speaker.
"The chief minister called me and requested that I resign and cooperate to prevent embarrassment, as the party has sent the name (for the new chairman).... I will discuss this with opposition leaders and decide," Horatti told reporters. Horatti, an eight-time MLC, has his current term till July 2028.
Questioning the announcement by the party, Horatti said, "This is probably for the first time I have seen a party declaring the chairperson of the legislative council. I'm not sure how they are doing it. It is not good in democracy." He said the chairman of the council and the speaker of the assembly could only be elected by the House.
Explaining the process for his removal, Horatti said, "To remove the chairman, ten members must give 14 days' advance notice, to move the no-confidence motion. Based on the discussion in the House the matter will be decided," and added that the decision of the House was supreme in the matter.
He also said no chairperson had been made to resign since 1956 and that all had completed their terms. According to Horatti, there were no grounds to remove him.
In the 75-member Legislative Council, the Congress has 38 members, the BJP 24 and the JD(S) 6. There is one Independent member and one chairman, while five seats are vacant. The row over Horatti's continuation has come after the Congress named its candidates for the top posts in both Houses.

headline: Man accused of kidnapping, raping schoolgirl lynched by mob in Jharkhand
full_text:
Man accused of kidnapping, raping schoolgirl lynched by mob in Jharkhand
Eight people were arrested in Jharkhand after an angry mob fatally beat a man who held a schoolgirl captive and raped her for two days.
A 32-year-old man accused of kidnapping and raping a girl died after being severely beaten by an angry mob in Jharkhand's Chatra district, police said, adding that eight people have been arrested in connection with the lynching.
According to locals, the man, Md Emroz, had kidnapped a schoolgirl and held her hostage inside his residence for two days.
The girl's family had been frantically searching for her but was unable to find any trace of her whereabouts. The situation reached a boiling point early Tuesday morning when the minor finally returned home. She recounted her ordeal to her family, alleging that she had been held captive by Emroz, who also threatened to kill her.
Enraged by the girl's statement, a large crowd of villagers gathered and surrounded the accused's house, subsequently launching an attack on him.
Police, who reached the scene, managed to rescue a critically injured Emroz from the crowd and transported him to a local hospital. After receiving primary treatment, he was referred to a higher medical facility, where he died during treatment.
Emroz's father, Sultan Miyan, also sustained injuries during the mob's attack.
Authorities have placed the girl under protection and initiated the mandatory medical examination process. The police have also recorded formal statements from the family members of the man.
Local villagers claim that this was not Emroz's first offence, alleging that he had a previous rape case registered against him and had served time in jail in 2023.
Police have confirmed that the allegations regarding the minor are being thoroughly investigated under due legal process. They added that further efforts are currently underway to identify and arrest other individuals involved in the mob violence.

headline: An engine failure left a roll-on roll-off (Ro-Ro) ferry adrift towards the open sea off Kochi on Tuesday evening, before a timely rescue operation brought its passengers and vehicles safely back to shore, according to a communication.

An engine failure left a roll-on roll-off (Ro-Ro) ferry adrift towards the open sea off Kochi on Tuesday evening, before a timely rescue operation brought its passengers and vehicles safely back to shore, according to a communication.
The Kerala Shipping and Inland Navigation Corporation-operated ferry, conducting service on the Vypeen-Fort Kochi route, developed a technical snag around 6 p.m. while on its way to Fort Kochi from Vypeen. With its engine rendered inoperative, the vessel drifted along the ship channel towards the sea, triggering concerns over the safety of those on board.
A major mishap was averted following the swift intervention of the Fisheries Marine Enforcement wing at Vypeen. A Fisheries patrol boat and the enforcement team pursued the drifting ferry, secured it with towing lines, and safely towed it back to the shore, the communication said.
The ferry was carrying nine cars, a traveller van, around 50 motorcycles, and nearly 50 passengers at the time of the incident. All those on board were evacuated safely, and no injuries were reported.

headline: A 12-year-old tribal girl from Mancheeri hamlet in Karulai forest range of Nilambur sustained a thumb injury after she was allegedly beaten with a stick by her mathematics teacher at school. The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights ...
full_text:
A 12-year-old tribal girl from Mancheeri hamlet in Karulai forest range of Nilambur sustained a thumb injury after she was allegedly beaten with a stick by her mathematics teacher at school. The Kerala State Commission for Protection of Child Rights has registered a case.
The Class VI student of S.V. Higher Secondary School, Palemadu, suffered swelling on her thumb after the alleged assault on July 21. The student is among the 16 Cholanaikan children from the Mancheeri tribal settlement studying at the school. She stays at a hostel run by Mahila Samakhya at Palemadu. According to sources, the teacher punished students for scoring poor marks in the examination.
Cholanaikans are a particularly vulnerable tribal group (PVTG) living deep inside the forests of Nilambur in Malappuram district. Traditionally, they lived in natural rock shelters and caves and are often described as among the last surviving cave-dwelling indigenous communities in Asia.
The child’s father Mani was killed in an elephant attack on January 4, 2025, while returning on foot to the hamlet after dropping his children at the hostel.
Mahila Samakhya district programme coordinator M. Rajeena took the child to a private clinic, where she was given a pain-relief injection. She was later taken to Eranad Hospital, Edakkara, where an X-ray ruled out a fracture.
Ms. Rajeena said the student entered school only in Class IV, without any primary education. “She is in Class VI now, but the learning gap still affects her studies,” she said.
Ms. Rajeena said she met the headmaster and teachers after the incident and warned them about the consequences of corporal punishment. She also reported the matter to her higher authorities.
According to sources, the school management informed the teacher that she would be held responsible for any consequences arising from the incident.
Representatives of Child Helpline (formerly Childline) visited the hostel on Monday and spoke to the girl. Child Rights Commission member Shajesh Bhaskar told The Hindu that a suo motu case was registered after seeing the video of the girl in sling, and a notice served on the school.

headline: VIT Chennai has launched a dedicated centre to revive traditional Tamil knowledge and scientifically investigate the impact of traditional Tamil games and select teachings from traditional scriptures on cognitive abilities.

VIT Chennai has launched a dedicated centre to revive traditional Tamil knowledge and scientifically investigate the impact of traditional Tamil games and select teachings from traditional scriptures on cognitive abilities.
The centre seeks to explore how traditional games such as Pallanguzhi, Thayam, Adupuli Attam, Paramapadham, and Aindhu Kal and select teachings of Thirukkural and Thirumandhiram can help improve concentration, memory, problem-solving skills, visuo-spatial ability, cognitive flexibility, and emotional regulation, a press release stated.
The centre has been developed under the Indian Knowledge Systems division of the Union Ministry of Education.
According to Vijayabanu U., Associate Professor of Psychology and the Co-Principal Investigator, the centre will examine specific cognitive abilities associated with different traditional games. Aindhu Kal will be studied in relation to visuo-spatial ability, Pallanguzhi with metacognition, Thayam with problem-solving skills and strategic thinking, Adupuli Attam with memory and cognitive skills, and Paramapatham to face life challenges.
Instead of assuming that ancient practices are beneficial simply because they are traditional, the researchers propose to test their effects using measurable scientific parameters, which makes the initiative quite unique, according to Ganesh N., Professor of Computer Science Engineering and the Principal Investigator.
The centre seeks to bring these traditional practices back into the lives of younger generations as knowledge systems whose potential benefits can help them, according to G.V. Selvam, Vice President, VIT.

headline: Fifth pellet gun victim says he knows of a sixth protester who was shot in Delhi
full_text:
Fifth pellet gun victim says he knows of a sixth protester who was shot in Delhi
Painter Prashant Kumar Singh says RAF firing during the Chalo Sansad march on July 20 left metal pellets lodged in his arm and chest. The 28-year-old, who will have to live the rest of his life with some of the pellets in his body, says he knows of a sixth protester who was shot. The sixth person hasn't been documented yet.
Prashant Kumar Singh, a painter trained in pastel, watercolour, oil and visual arts, started documenting the Gen Z protest at New Delhi's Jantar Mantar visually, through his art, from day one. He was also among the protesters who, on July 20, marched towards Parliament. A painter who has spent years using his right hand to create strokes on canvas, now lives with metallic pellets lodged in it after he was hit when the Rapid Action Force (RAF) opened fire at the protesters.
Until now, there were five documented people who sustained pellet injuries during the New Delhi protests. But Prashant says there was at least one more. He told India Today Digital that another injured protester arrived at Lady Hardinge Hospital around the same time he did — around 4.30 pm on July 20 — suggesting the number of those hit may be higher than previously documented. Prashant has seen the images of the four other documented pellet victims, and says the sixth person isn't the one whose name has surfaced in media.
Today, Prashant can feel the pellets when he presses against the flesh of his right arm and chest. Doctors have told him that removing the remaining ones would require cutting tendons and muscle. The risk, they said, is lasting damage. "If they operate, many muscles will be damaged and that will affect me in future," he told India Today Digital.
Some of the pellets extracted on the day of the firing were discarded as medical waste. He never saw them. But the rest remain with him, possibly for life.
India Today Digital has accessed his medico-legal certificate from Lady Hardinge Medical College and Hospital, which records "pellet" injury. His X-ray report from Holy Family Hospital, done on July 29 (Wednesday), shows at least 10 pellets still lodged in his arm and chest area.
THE MARCH TO PARLIAMENT THAT CHANGED PRASHANT'S LIFE
Prashant was not a first-time protester. An artist based in Delhi's Mayur Vihar, originally from Bihar, he had been following the agitation from its first day.
He went to the site on alternate days, sketching the unfolding moments. "I was documenting through my sketches that a particular moment is happening," he said. His toolkit — pastels, watercolours, paper — stayed with him even on July 20, the day of the Chalo Sansad March.
That afternoon he was near the last barricade, roughly 50 metres from Parliament. Chandrashekhar Azad of the Azad Samaj Party had just finished addressing the crowd and said he would return in 15-20 minutes. Prashant was at the front. The atmosphere, he insisted, was not violent. People were standing, listening. Then the Rapid Action Force (RAF) and Delhi Police began pushing the crowd back towards Connaught Place, into the inner circle near Mahatma Gandhi Road.
Tear-gas shells, which he described as "bomb shells", came first. Prashant referred to them as such as they sounded like bombs. Then, lathi charges followed. "They were really brutal," he said. "Within a few minutes, the force opened fire with shotguns on the crowd," he said.
No clear warning that live pellets would be used, he claimed. "In the beginning, they were warning us that do not come closer. They didn't want us to cross the barricade. The crowd wasn't going to cross," he said.
Then came the shotgun burst, hitting him, and one more person near him. The warning, in his account, never explicitly signalled metal pellets.
Prashant fell. Pellets struck his right arm and chest. Around him, others went down too because of tear gas, and possibly, shotgun wounds.
One man, whose name Prashant never learned, was hit at the same time. The two reached Lady Hardinge Hospital together, he told India Today Digital. Media reports have spoken of five pellet victims, including Prashant. Prashant believes there is a sixth, who isn't among the victims documented by the media. Of the known pellet gun victims, one is a woman and four are men.
A source later shared a photograph of another injured man with India Today Digital, who appears to have been treated at the same hospital that day. However, there is no confirmation on his identity and whereabouts so far. The photograph of the "sixth victim" shared with India Today Digital is different from the four other male pellet gun victims.
METAL, NOT PLASTIC, PELLETS USED AGAINST PROTESTERS
The Rapid Action Force (RAF) has maintained that it used plastic or rubber pellets.
But Prashant's X-ray and the feel of hard objects still under his skin tell a different story.
"I got an X-ray done a few days ago and the film shows that there are metal pieces still in my body," he said.
Doctors at Lady Hardinge hospital treated only the surface wounds, removed some metal fragments, and discharged Prashant the same day. Subsequent visits to Lok Nayak Hospital and then Holy Family hospital confirmed more pellets remained lodged deep in the muscle of his right arm.
OTHER JANTAR MANTAR PROTESTERS WHO WERE HIT WITH PELLET GUN
So far, there have been five documented pellet victims from the Chalo Sansad protest.
India Today Digital earlier reported exclusively on a man in his twenties shot in the back and arm; his identity is being concealed as per his request.
Sahil Lochab, whose injuries were reported by The Hindu and who appeared on camera with Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi, faces possible permanent damage to his eyesight.
Shaikh Irshad Mansoori's account was carried by both The Indian Express and The Hindu.
The fifth is Nutan, a 32-year-old woman from Ranchi working with a private firm in Gurugram. She told The Hindu that she sustained "gunshot" injuries during the students' protest at Jantar Mantar on July 20. According to her discharge summary from Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, she suffered "trauma to right ear by gunshot". She said her ear had "practically been torn off" and required stitches. She has since returned to her hometown, Ranchi.
Prashant's testimony now suggests that there's a sixth pellet gun victim who was treated the same day at Lady Hardinge.
DELHI POLICE'S DENIAL VS DIARY ENTRY THAT TELLS ANOTHER STORY
Delhi Police initially denied that pellet guns had been used against protesters. The claim did not hold.
An RAF general diary entry registered at Parliament Street police station in the early hours of 22 July — soon after The Hindu reported pellet injuries — recorded the use of the weapons. Delhi Police had authorised pellet-gun deployment on July 20. After the incident, the RAF withdrew pump-action guns (PAGs), electric shields, anti-riot guns and shock batons from personnel deployed at Jantar Mantar.
Prashant does not believe that the crowd couldn't have done anything to have prevented the firing. "They [forces] got the orders, and they fired," he said.
He said that the tension had escalated and the personnel seemed angrier than the protestors. "If I weren't hit, someone else would have definitely been hit," he said.
The pellets that remain are not abstract. Prashant can still feel them. He presses the skin and the hard points speak much more than both the Delhi Police, and the RAF's clarifications. An artist who went to the protest at Jantar Mantar with a sketchbook and pastel colours now carries metal under his skin.

Less than a year before the Punjab Assembly election, Congress leader Charanjit Singh Channi finds himself in a difficult position after locking horns with the party leadership over the recent organisation overhaul. With the party leadership clearly in no mood to relent, Mr. Channi’s options seem to have narrowed to two alternatives — accept a diminished role within the party or seek a political future elsewhere — neither of which may be favourable for him.
The discord was triggered by the All India Congress Committee’s organisational overhaul on July 1. While Amrinder Singh Raja Warring was retained as the State unit chief, Mr. Channi, Punjab’s first Dalit Chief Minister, was appointed chairman of the State poll campaign panel.
On July 3, the Lok Sabha member from Jalandhar and Congress’s most prominent Dalit face in the State convened a meeting of supporters at his Morinda residence, followed by another gathering in Mohali, in a clear show of strength aimed at persuading the high command to revisit its decision.
He was conspicuous by his absence from an event last week, where Congress general secretary for Punjab Bhupesh Baghel kicked off a nine-day mass mobilisation programme. He has stayed away from party events so far.
While Mr. Baghel has repeatedly ruled out replacing Mr. Warring as the Punjab Congress president, the faction led by the former CM has shown little sign of backing down.
Disruptions during the party’s ‘Har Booth Mazboot’ events in Patiala, Samana and Bathinda, where sections of workers were seen raising slogans in Mr. Channi’s support, have publicly exposed the fault lines. Mr. Baghel’s warning — urging party workers to stay alert against “traitors within the party who could cause serious damage” — seems to have had little effect in calming tempers.
Along with Mr. Channi, leaders such as Sukhjinder Singh Randhawa and Rana Gurjit are also believed to be upset with the revamp of the party unit, even as veteran leader Partap Singh Bajwa, the Leader of the Opposition in the State, is pushing for party unity to wrest power from the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP).
Weighing options
“It appears that Congress factions are weighing their options and trying to outwit each other to gain a political edge. No faction can afford to go it alone. That would be self-destructive. But, if the situation fails to improve, I believe Channi could contest the election separately with leaders from his camp,” said Kehar Singh, former head of the Department of Political Science at Punjabi University.
While Punjab Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) chief Kewal Dhillon has said he would welcome the Jalandhar MP into the party, Mr. Kehar feels the chances of disgruntled leaders switching to the BJP are slim.
In January, Mr. Channi, who was also the party’s chief ministerial face in the previous poll in which the Congress suffered a crushing defeat, called for “greater Dalit representation” in the party, adding that the community is “not getting due representation”.
Dalit representation
His remark, which brought the internal discord within the Congress into public, assumed significance given that Dalits constitute nearly 32% of Punjab’s population — the highest proportion among Indian States — making them a decisive electoral constituency.
For the Congress, which had been emerging as a serious contender for the 2027 election, the continuing drama could result in loss of momentum. The infighting has, at least for now, shifted attention from its campaign against AAP towards its own infighting.

headline: Congress's shock Datia bypoll victory triggers BJP overhaul, district chief fired
full_text:
Congress's shock Datia bypoll victory triggers BJP overhaul, district chief fired
The BJP dissolved its entire Datia district organisation after losing the Assembly bypoll to Congress. The move followed a review of the defeat and revived tensions over Narottam Mishra's denied ticket.
The BJP has dissolved its entire district organisation in Madhya Pradesh's Datia after the party's defeat in the July 30 by-election, acting on the recommendation of a probe committee constituted to examine the setback.
Tuesday's action came a day after the Congress retained the Datia Assembly seat, with its candidate Ghanshyam Singh defeating his BJP rival Ashutosh Tiwari by 6,016 votes.
Singh secured 66,757 votes, while Tiwari polled 60,741. Azad Samaj Party candidate Damodar Yadav finished third with 22,527 votes.
In an order issued by BJP state office secretary Shyam Mahajan, the party announced the immediate dissolution of the entire Datia district unit.
District president Raghuveer Singh Kushwaha was removed from his post along with the entire district executive.
The order also dissolved all organisational divisions, fronts, cells, projects and departmental units operating in the district.
Earlier in the day, Chief Minister Mohan Yadav held a review meeting with senior BJP leaders from both the organisation and the government to assess the reasons behind the bypoll defeat.
Following the meeting, the party constituted a two-member committee to investigate the loss.
According to an official party statement, BJP State General Secretary Gaurav Randive and senior leader Ambaram Karada have been appointed to the panel.
The committee has been tasked with interacting with party office-bearers and senior leaders associated with the election, analysing the factors that led to the defeat and submitting its report to state BJP president Hemant Khandelwal.
The Datia by-election had already generated controversy within the BJP after the party replaced six-time MLA and senior leader Narottam Mishra with Ashutosh Tiwari as its candidate.
The decision to deny Mishra a ticket had triggered strong protests by party workers and supporters in his home district ahead of the bypoll.

headline: Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) said he would discuss with the Centre the issue of mining in Nagaland as one of the causes of the devastating flood that has killed 87 people so far.
full_text:
Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) said he would discuss with the Centre the issue of mining in Nagaland as one of the causes of the devastating flood that has killed 87 people so far.
A majority of the people died in three districts adjoining Nagaland — Sivasagar, Charaideo, and Jorhat. These districts hardly have a history of a major flood.
Touring the flood-hit districts, Mr. Sarma said the State government will begin assessing the damage to the houses from August 9 to fast-track relief and rehabilitation of the affected families.
He also addressed concerns about mining activities in Nagaland having contributed to the unprecedented flooding in the three districts, specifically Charaideo and Sivasagar. “I cannot stop mining in Nagaland. I will raise the issue with the Centre. We need a scientific study to determine the actual cause of the problem,” he said, insisting there was no illegal mining in Assam.
Many in the affected districts, including Sibsagar MLA Akhil Gogoi, have blamed illegal sand, stone, and coal mining along the foothills of Nagaland for the flood in Assam. They said such activities, along with rampant felling of trees, removed natural resistance to the floodwaters that rushed down the hills of Nagaland after bouts of extremely heavy rain.
Nagaland-based organisations, however, trashed “theories” that activities there were responsible for Assam’s flood.
Mr. Sarma said the government would drain out the floodwaters as quickly as possible, apart from rebuilding the houses under the government’s rehabilitation programme.
He said the highways obstructed the natural flow of floodwater in certain areas. “I will ask the National Highways Infrastructure Development Corporation Limited to construct additional cross-drainage structures,” he said.
He further said embankments would be constructed in vulnerable areas to prevent flood damage in future.
Higher compensation
Mr. Sarma concurred with Mr. Gogoi’s suggestion that the compensation to flood victims should be increased.
Donations have been pouring in from individuals, organisations, political parties, and social media influencers.
Many have touched hearts with ‘shram daan’ or voluntary labour. They include a group of Sikhs who have been cleaning up flooded namghars (prayer halls), temples, and other places of worship besides serving meals.
A group of daily wagers from western Assam, mostly Bengali Muslims and Koch-Rajbongshis, has been clearing silt from farmlands and house compounds, or removing livestock carcasses.
Members of a barbers’ association have been providing free haircuts to the flood-affected people. At the same time, car mechanics from other parts of Assam have pitched in to repair vehicles free of charge. “Visuals of hundreds of upturned, half-buried two-, three-, and four-wheelers made us reach out to the people. We do not have cash to spare, but decided we can make a difference by trying to restore these vehicles without any labour charge,” a mechanic from Nagaon said.

headline: In the first phase of the census â involving housing and houselisting operations â those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields
full_text:
In the first phase of the census â involving housing and houselisting operations â those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields
NEW DELHI: Census authorities are considering allowing persons self-enumerating for the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 to submit a partially filled form online.In the first phase of the census - involving housing and houselisting operations - those opting for self-enumeration were not able to submit the form with blank fields. If any field was left blank - either accidentally or intentionally due to lack of clarity - the user could not advance to the submission window.Sources said that it was felt during discussions among census teams that this feature forced many to opt out of self-enumeration and rely on the enumerator's visit to record their replies to the questionnaire.There is now a realisation that even a partially filled form, provided a minimum number of questions are answered, would help in easing the task of the enumerator. Besides, self-declared data tends to be more accurate and reliable."Internal deliberations focused on why the self-enumeration option should not be made flexible, given that the data is to be entered digitally either by the respondent or the enumerator.
The census application anyway allows the enumerator to access the filled-up form and change any wrongly entered data. So why can't he access a partially filled-up form and fill in the few remaining fields during the house visit, saving time and effort?" an officer told TOI.The population enumeration exercise is set to be conducted nationwide in Feb 2027. However, the exercise, as per convention, is advanced for select states/UTs like Ladakh, J&K, HP and Uttarakhand that become wholly or partially snow-bound in Feb. These areas will witness population enumeration from Sept 1 to 30, preceded by a self-enumeration window of Aug 17-30.

TNN / Aug 05, 2026, 04:40 IST

NEW DELHI: Govt is likely to allow a levy of 0.25% to 0.4% as merchant discount rate (MDR) or charges on UPI payments above Rs 2,000 made to businesses, while keeping payments made by one person to another outside the ambit.The Taxation and Other Laws (Amendment) Bill, moved by FM Nirmala Sitharaman on Tuesday, has sought to remove the bar on banks and payment service providers to levy MDR on notified electronic payment modes. Govt officials said there is no decision on when the proposal will be implemented.Official estimates show that the Rs 2,000 floor will cover 5% of all UPI transactions, but those transactions account for 65% of the total transaction value, and is unlikely to impact daily purchases such as milk, vegetables and groceries or even payments for auto or taxi use. In July, there were 23.7 billion transactions, whose combined value was pegged at Rs 29.9 lakh crore."Even if implemented, 95% of the transactions will not face the merchant discount rate. Besides, not all businesses are going to pass on the fees, which will be a small amount," an official said.
Industry persons said govt may likely impose a ceiling on the absolute amount that is charged. "Unlike credit cards, there is no funding cost involved so it makes sense to have a ceiling once the costs are covered," said an industry source.
At present, credit and debit cards come with MDR, but most merchants do not pass it on to consumers. In the case of credit card MDR, where the fee is not regulated, it can be as high as 3% of the transaction value. For debit card transactions up to Rs 20 lakh, there is a cap of 0.4%, and for higher value it is 0.9%.

This statement comes amid heightened rhetoric from Pakistan's military, and experts suggest it serves as a strategic narrative amidst rising tensions.

The hate-filled speech comes on the heels of Lt General Ahmed Sharif Chaudhry, the official spokesperson of Pakistan armed forces (DG-ISPR), and the son of a US-designated terrorist peddling similar extremist views on a video while alleging that Afghans were not Muslims.
Security experts saw these speeches as a face-saving narrative building exercise. The escalation in sectarian rhetoric comes as Islamabad faces mounting public unrest in Pakistan-Occupied Kashmir, where violent state crackdowns against anti-govt protesters at Rawalakot, in particular, and other places have drawn severe criticism while denting Pakistan's narrative about it being the champion of Kashmiris and their right to self-determination.Pakistan defence minister Khawaja Asif also labelled anti-govt demonstrators in POK as "enemies" comparable to India and ruled out any dialogue with them while defending the violent attacks on protesters.

headline: Have undertaken comprehensive overhaul to eliminate NEET paper leaks: Centre tells SC
full_text:
Have undertaken comprehensive overhaul to eliminate NEET paper leaks: Centre tells SC
New Delhi, The Centre has told the Supreme Court that it has undertaken a comprehensive overhaul of the conduct of the National Eligibility-cum-Entrance Test to eliminate paper leaks and systemic failures.
In a compliance affidavit filed before a bench headed by Justice P S Narasimha, the Ministry of Education said the reforms are aimed at creating a robust and institutionalised system that preserves institutional memory, strengthens examination security and prevents future incidents of paper leaks or other malpractices.
The affidavit was filed in response to the apex court's May 29 direction asking the Union government to explain how future NEET examinations would be conducted and how regulatory authorities would build and retain institutional memory to improve examination processes over successive years.
The government said that while the Ministry of Education oversees the National Testing Agency, NEET is conducted by the NTA on behalf of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, the test-indenting agency.
It also said that the affidavit does not comment on the merits of the ongoing CBI investigation into the NEET-UG 2026 paper leak.
The Centre said Parliament has further strengthened the legal framework against examination fraud through the Public Examinations Amendment Act, 2026, building on the 2024 law that criminalised question paper leaks, impersonation, tampering with computer systems and other examination-related offences.
According to the affidavit, the amendments reflect the government's resolve to impose even stricter penalties against those compromising the integrity of public examinations.
The government also informed the court that it has constituted a High-Powered Task Force on Examination Reforms to recommend structural improvements in the conduct of public examinations and to modernise examination systems.
The government said the reforms are intended to create a stronger institutional framework capable of learning from previous examination cycles through systematic use of experience, data and information, thereby reducing vulnerabilities and improving oversight.
It said the HPTF set up on July 27 is headed by Infosys co-founder and Aadhaar architect Nandan Nilekani.
The task force is mandated to submit recommendations within three months on end-to-end reforms, focusing on leveraging AI and Blockchain to secure examination conduction, it said.
To prevent a repeat of earlier issues, the affidavit said, the NTA has implemented a 10-stage security protocol described by officials as a "fortress" model.
To prevent leaks at the translation stage, the government is using "air-gapped" AI systems for initial drafting, followed by limited human verification, it said.
Every question paper and OMR sheet now carries a unique serial number tied to a specific candidate, it said.
Papers are housed in six layers of tamper-evident packaging, including steel trunks with one-time-use locks that can only be cut open, it said.
The affidavit highlighted that the Public Examinations Amendment Act, 2026, now provides for up to 10 years of imprisonment and fines up to ₹1 crore.
On May 12, the NTA cancelled the NEET exam held on May 3 amid allegations of paper leak. A re-exam was held on June 21.
After the questions of NEET-UG were allegedly leaked in 2024, the top court had refused to cancel the test but passed various directions aimed at tackling paper leaks and also a criterion for cancelling public exams.
Hearing the pleas on May 25, the top court observed that it was sad that the NTA had not learnt lessons from the earlier NEET paper leak.
It had sought the response of the Centre, NTA and CBI on pleas for the replacement of the testing agency with a robust and autonomous body to conduct the medical entrance exam.
The top court had issued notice on the pleas, including one filed by the Federation of All India Medical Association through lawyer Tanvi Dubey.

headline: SC has raised alarm on the uninsured vehicles operating on road
full_text:
SC has raised alarm on the uninsured vehicles operating on road
NEW DELHI: If your vehicle is not insured, you may not be able to get fuel from petrol pumps in the near future. Supreme Court Tuesday suggested this as one of the measures to tackle the problem of uninsured vehicles plying on roads and also directed that cameras deployed on highways and roads be used to identify such vehicles and send challans to owners.Expressing shock that nearly 56% of vehicles plying on Indian roads remain uninsured (most of them two-wheelers), a bench of Justices Sanjay Karol and Prashant Kumar Mishra said the purpose behind mandatory insurance under Section 146 of the Motor Vehicles Act gets defeated, resulting in victims of road accidents being forced into prolonged litigation to get compensation. In absolute terms, the stark figure of uninsured vehicles stands at 16.5 crore vehicles out of a total of 30.4 crore registered vehicles. As per govt data, 22% of road accidents involve uninsured vehicles.As per the MV Act, those who drive or allow an uninsured vehicle to be driven without valid motor third-party insurance are liable to be punished, including imprisonment, for violation of the law. In the case of a first offence, the punishment is imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of Rs 2,000 or both; and for a subsequent offence, imprisonment for up to three months, or a fine of Rs 4,000 or both are provided.
"The Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority, in consultation with the road transport ministry, to deliberate and evolve a pilot project whereby fuel for vehicles to be linked with valid insurance status. In the absence thereof, the vehicle concerned would be refused fuel at petrol pumps until such time valid insurance is obtained. The benefit therein is two-fold - first, it will assist in identification of uninsured or unregistered vehicles. Secondly, it will prompt the owners of these vehicles to ensure that they have valid insurance status. Such projects would ensure ground-level compliance with the statutory mandate of Section 146 of the MVA. This may be done through the use of cameras. The ministry of petroleum and natural gas, has in principle, no objection to the same," the bench said.The bench said that there should be strict implementation of law and directed that state traffic police should be given handheld devices or downloadable apps, linked with the data from Insurance Information Bureau and VAHAN portal to verify insurance status on the ground. "ANPR cameras deployed on highways and roads are equipped with a mechanism to catch and penalise road safety violations such as high speed, red light jumping, driving on the wrong side of the road, etc. Carrying this forward and as already deployed by the MoRTH in certain states, ANPR cameras are to be integrated with data from the Insurance Information Bureau and the VAHAN portal for issuance of automatic e-challans to uninsured vehicles," the bench said.
The result of vehicles remaining uninsured is that accident victims and their families have no recourse to adequate compensation within a reasonable time period.In 2018, the apex court had directed mandatory buying of third-party insurance for three years for new cars and five years for two-wheelers at the time of buy/registration of new vehicles. Noting that a large number of vehicles remain uninsured, the bench increased the period by one year and directed that henceforth, a buyer has to buy third-party insurance for four years for new cars and six years for new two-wheelers.

headline: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Chhattisgarh on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) announced that the committee formed to prepare the framework for the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) implementation in the State has invited suggestions and opinions on ...
full_text:
The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government in Chhattisgarh on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) announced that the committee formed to prepare the framework for the Uniform Civil Code (UCC) implementation in the State has invited suggestions and opinions on the proposed law from citizens, organisations and other stakeholders.
According to an official statement, the last date has been set as October 15 by the five five-member high-level committee. Last month, Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai had said that the UCC will be introduced in the Assembly in the upcoming Winter Session.
Since 2024, Uttarakhand, Gujarat, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh have implemented the UCC that largely regulates areas of personal law such as marriage, divorce, succession and inheritance, and live-in relationships.
“The committee is studying the legal, social and administrative aspects of implementing the UCC. Its mandate includes examining the State’s existing legal framework and preparing practical recommendations on matters such as marriage, divorce, maintenance, inheritance and adoption. It will also study UCC models adopted by other States, consider suggestions received from the citizens, legal experts, social organisations and other stakeholders, and prepare a comprehensive draft along with legislative and administrative recommendations,” the statement added.
The committee had appealed to government and non-government organisations, social groups, religious institutions, communities, political parties and citizens to submit their views and suggestions by October 15 this year, the statement said.
“Suggestions can be submitted by email at ucc-chhattisgarh@cg.gov.in, through the web portal https://ucc.cgstate.gov.in/, or by post to the Office of the Uniform Civil Code Committee, New Circuit House, Civil Lines, Room No. 202, Raipur, Chhattisgarh – 492001,” said the official.
While the government statement asserted that the objective of the proposed law was to bring all citizens under a common constitutional framework in place of religion-based personal laws, the Opposition has been long demanding that such a legislation proposed should provide exemptions for tribal communities. It demands that the centuries-old conservative traditions, marriage systems, and social systems of tribal communities should be excluded from the scope of the UCC to ensure that their specific rights are not violated.
In July, the Madhya Pradesh Assembly passed a UCC Bill with provisions to ban polygamy and make the registration of live-in relationships mandatory, while excluding the tribal community from its scope.
The committee headed by Justice Desai was examining the need for a Uniform Civil Code in Chhattisgarh, preparing its framework and undertaking a comprehensive review of the existing laws governing personal civil matters, the official added.

headline: Ghaziabad women taking pregnant cow home thrashed over smuggling suspicion
full_text:
Ghaziabad women taking pregnant cow home thrashed over smuggling suspicion
A woman and her mother, who said they were taking a pregnant stray cow home after residents requested them to look after it, were assaulted by a group on suspicion of cow smuggling.
A mother and daughter were assaulted by a group of women on suspicion of cow smuggling while taking a pregnant stray cow home in Uttar Pradesh's Ghaziabad, prompting police to register an FIR after a video of the incident surfaced on social media.
The incident took place in Modinagar on August 3. A viral video of the incident shows three women sitting on the ground as a woman repeatedly slaps and confronts them while a crowd looks on. The two other unidentified women named in the FIR are not visible in the assault footage.
According to the FIR, Deepa and her mother, Suman, and a friend were taking the cow when they were stopped by Sapna Aggarwal and two unidentified persons. Deepa told police that the trio accused them of cow smuggling, abused them, repeatedly slapped them and threatened to kill them if they were seen in the area again. Both the mother and her daughter sustained injuries in the assault.
Deepa, while explaining the events that led to the incident, said the cow had been wandering in the locality for several days without anyone caring for it. As the animal was pregnant and could give birth at any time, local residents, aware that the family had been rearing cattle for years, asked them to take it home and look after it.
Based on a complaint filed by one of the victims, Deepa, police registered an FIR in the early hours of Tuesday under Sections 115(2), 352 and 351(3) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS).
Some of the women named in the case are being claimed to be associated with a Hindu organisation, though police have not officially confirmed the claim.
Police said they have taken cognisance of the viral video and are verifying its authenticity, reconstructing the sequence of events and identifying those seen in the footage. They said further legal action would be taken based on the findings of the investigation.
Officials also said no individual would be allowed to take the law into their own hands and assured that the case would be investigated impartially, with action taken on the basis of evidence.

headline: The balance of research and development funding has shifted, with government and private industry now investing nearly the same amount. In recent years, private sector contributions to research have seen a notable rise. Government spending is concent...
full_text:
The balance of research and development funding has shifted, with government and private industry now investing nearly the same amount. In recent years, private sector contributions to research have seen a notable rise. Government spending is concentrated on sectors deemed strategic and beneficial to the public. Additionally, multinational corporations are increasingly influential in shaping India's research environment, although the overall research intensity still lags behind other major economies.
BENGALURU: For every Rs 100 spent on R&D, the govt contributes about Rs 48 while private industry accounts for Rs 45, latest data from R&D Statistics At a Glance 2025-26 by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), shows.The remaining Rs 7 comes from scientific and industrial research organisations (SIROs) and private higher education institutions.Indiaâs Gross Expenditure on Research and Development (GERD) breached Rs 2.4-lakh crore in 2023-24, more than three times the Rs 79,356 crore recorded a decade ago. However, overall R&D spend is still under 1% of the GDP, touching 0.8%, as per the latest figures.Private industryâs share in GERD increased from 39.7% in 2020-21 to 45.2% in 2023-24 in just three years. During the same period, govt share declined from 54.5% to 48.2%, although it continues to remain the countryâs single largest contributor to research spending.The report notes that private R&D expenditure has been growing at an average annual rate of around 20% over the last three years.While the DST reportâs detailed analysis is up to 2023-24, it has projected overall trends for two more years: âThe upward [spending] trend is expected to continue, with GERD projected to reach nearly Rs 2.8-lakh-crore by 2024-25 and more than Rs 3.1-lakh-crore crore by 2025â26,â it reads.
Govt spending continues to be concentrated in strategic and public-interest sectors. Among the Centreâs scientific agencies, DRDO accounted for 32.7%, followed by the Department of Space (15%), Department of Atomic Energy (14.4%), Indian Council of Agricultural Research (13.1%) and Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (8.7%). Together, 12 major scientific agencies accounted for 76% of govt R&D spend.Transportation emerged as the biggest destination for industrial R&D, accounting for 32.6% of private sector expenditure, followed by pharmaceuticals (21.4%), biotechnology (8.6%), IT (7.9%) and electrical and electronics (5.9%).The report also highlights the growing role of MNCs in Indiaâs research landscape. Their share in business R&D expenditure has increased from 49.9% in 2020-21 to 71.3% in 2023-24. According to the report, the growth rate of R&D expenditure has outpaced GDP growth after 2021-22, except in 2022-23, reflecting the increasing priority accorded to research and innovation.Despite the encouraging trends, India continues to trail many major economies in research intensity. At 0.8% of GDP, the country's R&D expenditure remains below that of China (2.6%), Brazil (1.2%) and several advanced economies that invest more than 2% of their GDP in research.
Nevertheless, the latest figures point to a maturing innovation ecosystem where the burden of financing research is gradually shifting from being overwhelmingly government-led to one in which private enterprise is emerging as an almost equal partner.
Chethan Kumar is a Senior Assistant Editor with the Times of India. Aside from specialising in Space & Science, he has reported extensively on varied topics, with special focus on defence, policy and data stories. He has covered multiple elections, too. As a young democracy grows out of adolescence, Chethan feels, there are reels of tales emerging which need to be captured. To do this, he alternates between the mundane goings-on of the Common Man and the wonder-filled worlds of scientists and scamsters, politicians and soldiers. In a career spanning nearly 18 years, he has reported from multiple datelines â Houston, Florida, Kochi, Hyderabad, Chennai, Sriharikota (AP), NH-1 (J&K Highway), New Delhi, Ahmedabad, Raichur, Bhatkal, Mysuru, Chamarajanagar, to name a few â but is based out of Bengaluru, Indiaâs science capital that also hosts the ISRO HQ.

headline: The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) passed a resolution urging the Centre to review and suspend the mandatory rollout of E20 ethanol blended fuel for vehicles until all concerns are comprehensively addressed.
full_text:
The Punjab Assembly on Tuesday (August 4, 2026) passed a resolution urging the Centre to review and suspend the mandatory rollout of E20 ethanol blended fuel for vehicles until all concerns are comprehensively addressed.
The AAP government moved the resolution on a day party chief Arvind Kejriwal marched towards the Prime Minister's residence in the national capital with over 2.30 lakh petitions against E20 petrol but was stopped by Delhi Police and later held a sit-in on Firoz Shah Road as part of the agitation against the blended fuel policy.
On the second day of the Monsoon session of the Punjab Assembly in Chandigarh, Finance Minister Harpal Singh Cheema moved the resolution and e criticised the mandatory implementation of 20% ethanol blending (E20 petrol) from April 2026.
Mr. Cheema also questioned why the implementation of the E20 fuel policy has been advanced as against the earlier target of implementing it in 2030.
Highlighting that the U.S. produces 60% of the world's ethanol while India produces only 5%, Mr. Cheema accused the BJP-led central government of surrendering to the United States at the cost of Indian consumers and vehicle owners.
In its resolution, the House expressed serious concern over the decision of the Centre to mandate the nationwide supply of E20 fuel "without adequately safeguarding the interests of consumers, vehicle owners and the states".
"This House notes that while the objectives of reducing crude oil imports, enhancing energy security and promoting cleaner fuels are important national priorities, such policies must be implemented in a manner that is transparent, scientifically validated and sensitive to the concerns of citizens and state governments," it said.
The compulsory use of E20 raises legitimate concerns regarding engine compatibility, accelerated wear and tear of fuel system components, reduced fuel efficiency and mileage, increased maintenance costs, possible warranty disputes and diminished resale value, read the resolution.
It expressed concern that the increased operating and transportation costs would inevitably raise the cost of cultivation, movement of goods and essential commodities, thereby adding to the financial burden of ordinary citizens.
Through the resolution, the Union government was urged to review and suspend the compulsory nationwide rollout of E20 petrol for vehicles not originally designed or certified for E20 fuel until all concerns relating to vehicle compatibility, consumer protection, scientific evaluation and State-specific impacts are comprehensively addressed.
Consumers should be given the option to choose between ethanol-free petrol and E20 petrol, and owners of vehicles not originally designed or certified for E20 fuel should not be compelled, directly or indirectly, to use E20 until their vehicles are demonstrably certified as fully compatible with higher ethanol blends, it said.
The Centre should constitute an independent committee comprising automobile engineers, petroleum experts, environmental scientists, consumer organisations and representatives of state governments to undertake a comprehensive assessment of vehicle compatibility, fuel efficiency, maintenance costs, etc, and place its findings in the public domain, stated the resolution.
Cheema, while referring to "damage" to vehicles due to E20 fuel, said repairing such a car costs between ₹25,000 and ₹50,000.
He criticised the petroleum ministry for failing to provide alternative options for citizens with older vehicles, warning that delivery boys and small business owners risk losing their livelihoods if their vehicles break down every few months.
He claimed even Union Minister Nitin Gadkari admitted in Parliament to a 6% drop in fuel mileage, though actual efficiency losses are much higher.
"The unilateral imposition of policies without consulting domestic scientists, manufacturers, parliamentarians, or the general public is condemnable. The policy is selling out the country to corporate interests," he alleged.
Ethanol production consumes massive amounts of water, which poses a grave threat to Punjab's already depleted groundwater table, claimed Mr. Cheema.

To comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp is piloting new privacy-focused age verification methods for Indian users. This initiative is completely voluntary, allowing users to choose their participation. With the new law's emphasis on stricter regulations for children's personal data, WhatsApp is taking care to safeguard user privacy during this important verification process.
NEW DELHI: In a bid to comply with the upcoming Digital Personal Data Protection Act, WhatsApp has begun testing optional age verification methods for users in India. The Meta-owned messaging service said the pilot is designed to verify a user's age in a privacy-protective manner and that participation in the test is voluntary."To comply with upcoming laws in India like Digital Personal Data Protection Act (DPDP), we are testing privacy-protective ways for people to confirm their age. This doesn't change how WhatsApp works or your experience. We understand that information about someone's age is private and it won't be shared with other WhatsApp users," a WhatsApp spokesperson said.
The company clarified that users do not have to confirm their age to continue using WhatsApp during the test.The development comes as digital platforms prepare for the implementation of the DPDP framework, which introduces stricter obligations for companies handling children's personal data. Under the law, a child is defined as anyone below the age of 18, and companies processing children's personal data are required to obtain verifiable parental consent and put in place safeguards to protect young users.WhatsApp has not disclosed how long the pilot will run or the specific methods being evaluated for age verification. The company said the exercise is aimed at ensuring compliance while preserving user privacy.

headline: Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay virtually inaugurated five health sub centres, mostly in tribal areas, and additional buildings for colleges and university in Vellore, Tiruvannamalai, and Tirupattur districts on Tuesday.
full_text:
Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay virtually inaugurated five health sub centres, mostly in tribal areas, and additional buildings for colleges and university in Vellore, Tiruvannamalai, and Tirupattur districts on Tuesday.
Health officials said that the existing health centres in tribal areas atop hillocks in the district were built more than three decades ago. Most of the structures were damaged and dilapidated.
The buildings of identified health centres, which were certified as unfit for use by the Public Works Department, were demolished. “Permanent buildings for identified health sub centres in tribal and remote areas in the district were opened. It will help provide basic health care to tribals in the hills. Adequate medicines can be stored safely in the new building,” N. Kalu Sivalingam, Deputy Director of Health Services (DDHS), Tirupattur, told The Hindu.
Accompanied by health officials, Tirupattur Collector G. Ravikumar inspected these buildings. The new permanent buildings for health centres are located in tribal villages such as Nayakkeneri, Nilavoor, Chinna Motor, Naikanur, and Nethiji Nagar. These villages come under Jolarpet, Alangayam, and Madhanur Panchayat Unions in the district.
Residents said that a permanent building for health centres was a long-standing demand. At present, residents of Nayankeneri and Nilavoor trek 8-10 km to reach Ambur and Jolarpet, the nearest towns that have government hospitals. “We have to walk through the forests from the hills to government hospitals in the plains. The new permanent buildings for health centres will help provide better medicines and ensure the presence of a Village Health Nurse in the hills,” said B. Perumal, a resident.
The health sub centre has two beds for in-patients, an out-patients block, a separate cabin for a Village Health Nurse, a common visitors hall, laboratory facilities, a pharmacy with adequate stocks.
Adequate parking space for ambulances and other vehicles will also be provided. Each health centre, on an average, was built at a cost of ₹45 lakh under 15th Finance Commission.
Health officials said that sub health centres have to focus on the health of expectant mothers, children, immunization programmes, and other government health schemes in remote villages. The Village Health Nurse was also trained to treat minor illnesses like fever and cold. The health centre will work between 8 a.m and 3 p.m on all days, except on Sundays.
In Vellore, Collector P.S. Leela Alex inspected 18 classrooms in three new buildings at Thiruvalluvar University near Katpadi after it was virtually inaugurated. Additional buildings at Thanthai Periyar Government Institute of Technology were also opened for use. The entire work costs ₹22.36 crore.
After many years, a permanent building for Government Polytechnic College at Nagapadi village on the Polur-Chengam Road in Tiruvannamalai was also opened at a cost of ₹6.25 crore.

Hauz Rani grapples with the aftermath of a fatal fire, highlighting the pervasive danger of tangled overhead wires and inadequate infrastructure. Residents voice concerns about authorities only acting after tragedies, leaving them to rely on themselves in emergencies. The constant threat of electrical hazards is a grim reality locals have learned to endure.

Residents allege unchecked expansion and ignored safety concerns, with one hotel reportedly growing from two-and-a-half to five floors without approval. Bajaj allegedly admitted to illegal expansion, stating 'Delhi mein sab chalta hai'.
A family's journey to be with an ailing patriarch tragically ended in a devastating fire at a Delhi hotel, claiming the lives of eight members. The Aggarwal family, including three generations, perished in the blaze. Their abandoned Mercedes outside the gutted building stands as a silent testament to the unimaginable loss.
Affordable hospitality hubs in Delhi, like Mahipalpur and Paharganj, are rife with fire safety violations, including sealed windows and inadequate firefighting equipment. These conditions mirror those that led to a fatal blaze in Hauz Rani, raising concerns about potential catastrophes due to poor ventilation, narrow access, and delayed emergency responses.
The owner of a Malviya Nagar hotel where a fire killed 21 people was previously arrested in 2025 for allegedly facilitating the illegal stay of Bangladeshi nationals. Police are now investigating his role in the deadly hotel fire.
